articleTitle: Deep Learning Modeling of Power Delay Profile in Motherboard Desktop Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based THz channel model for line of sight propagation in a motherboard desktop environment. A six layer decoder-like MLP network was designed and trained with augmented measured data. The power delay profiles predicted by the MLP model match the relevant signal structures closely while uncovering hidden structure not explained by conventional ray-tracing models. The validity of our model’s predictions is demonstrated by comparing with a baseline of the measured data at different transceiver heights.

articleTitle: Beam Reconfigurable Cylindrical Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A radiation beam reconfigurable cylindrical antenna is investigated in this paper. The structure consists of a coaxial collinear (CoCo) antenna located at the center acting as a radiating element and surrounded by four strips of reconfigurable parasitic elements. The radiation beam of the antenna can be electronically steered to eight directions over the azimuthal plane or can be degenerated to form an omni-directional pattern. The design of associated switching circuits and dc bias lines are discussed. Three reference designs for different operating frequencies are also provided.

articleTitle: Small Antenna with High Inter-port Isolation for In-Band Full-Duplex at HF Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Antenna elements fitting within a 3 m radius sphere (ka = 1 at 15.9 MHz) are arranged in a 4-element circular array for operation in HF band. High inter-port isolation with the same polarization and similar radiation patterns in both transmit (Tx) and receive (Rx) modes simultaneously operating at the same frequency is achieved. The high isolation between Tx and Rx ports is achieved through the intrinsic self-interference cancellation capabilities of the employed modified Butler matrix beam-forming network consisting of one 90° and three 180° couplers fed in circular modes 0 and 1. The proposed antenna system is realized with smaller physical and electrical footprint and all near-field coupling affects are directly accounted for.

articleTitle: A building block element (BBE) that realizes a functional reconfiguration between antenna and filter with the aid of liquid dielectric
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a block of microwave hardware, termed building block element (BBE), which realizes the functional change between antenna and filter mode with the aid of a permittivity changeable substrate. The BBE is composed of an antenna on the and a filter located on different sides of the substrate. Both the antenna and the filter are fed by coplanar waveguide (CPW). When the permittivity of the substrate is 2 the antenna will operate, while the filter will not operate. When the permittivity of the substrate is 15, the filter will operate, while the antenna will not operate. The height of substrate is 4mm, which means that microfluidic channels can be inserted into the substrate and liquid dielectric can be applied to change the permittivity of the substrate.

articleTitle: A Novel Compact Broadband Dual-Polarization Antenna for 2/3/4/5G Base Station
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact broadband dual-polarized base station antenna for 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G base station applications. In this design, the radiation structure is made up of a dipole antenna with rectangle slots and circular trimming. The two pair of dipoles are printed on the bottom of the FR4 substrate ( ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> =4.4) with the thickness of 0.8mm, where the cross feeding-lines are also printed on the top of the substrate. A pair of coax feeds connected to the center of top substrate. The stacked metallic disks are connected by Nylon cylinders. The simulation results by the commercial software HFSS show that the proposed antenna achieves a high port isolation (>-22 dB) and a bandwidth (85.8%) covering 1.71~4.2 GHz (VSWR<2). Moreover, the dual-polarized antenna has an average gain of 6.8dBi. In addition, the overall antenna architecture is simple and easy to fabricate in base stations that can be used in 2G/3G/4G/5G mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: Scale-model based MIMO Shannon capacity estimation using visible light
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: There are two approaches to estimate MIMO channel capacity on wireless communication systems: simulation and experiment. As a novel experimental approach, we propose a MIMO capacity estimation method based on a scale model using visible light, which is a further extension of the method for estimating radio wave propagation characteristics. In this paper, we have actually conducted experiments using a system configuration that scales target environment by 1/20 and consist a laser and cameras. Also, we clarify the effectiveness of the proposed method from the results.

articleTitle: Parabolic Equation-Based Channel Model for Direction of Arrival Estimation in Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The estimation of direction of arrival (DOA) is of fundamental importance to a variety of applications such as channel estimation, tracking, and indoor positioning. The parabolic equation (PE) method has been widely applied to model radio wave propagation in large-scale propagation scenarios (e.g., tunnels, sea surfaces, indoor environments). However, there is a lack of research on the performance of PE-based channel models for DOA estimation. In this paper, the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm is utilized to obtain the DOA information from signals generated using PE-based channel models, and the performance is investigated in an indoor corridor.

articleTitle: Applied Superconductivity and Graphene THz Photonics: S. (Ali) Safavi-Naeini’s Contributions and Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Prof. Safieddin (Ali) Safavi-Naeini as a brilliant intellect, great mentor, a singular colleague and a dominant researcher in electromagnetics is no longer among us but his legacy continues to live and shine through the lives of his family, students and colleagues. This paper briefly introduces two dimensions in Ali’s multi-dimensional and non-orthogonal research space.

articleTitle: Single-Channel Monopulse Tracking Receiver with Time Modulation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel single-channel monopulse tracking receiver is proposed and verified with time modulation. The output signals of the monopulse tracking antenna are selected to the single RF chain by a single-pole three-throw (SP3T) switch periodically, including the sum signal, the elevation difference signal and the azimuth difference signal. Then in digital domain, three signals are separated from generated harmonic components, though they have the same carrier frequency. Compared to existing single-channel monopulse receivers, the proposed receiver has a simpler structure and more concise signal processing. Numeric simulations are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed idea.

articleTitle: Infinite Array Approach for Distributed Subarray Configuration
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a design and analysis of distributed subarray configurations with the subarray units being large finite arrays. Each large subarray pattern has been computed using the infinite array approach of Antenna Toolbox, while the total array pattern is obtained using pattern superposition. The proposed technique can be useful in reducing the overall computational load of simulating large subarray units, thereby impacting the design optimization of such arrays over a wide scanning angle.

articleTitle: Inverse Hilbert Fractal- Metamaterial Rings for Microstrip Antennas and Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A Novel Metamaterial (MTM) property is obtained using a fractal pattern known as Inverse Hilbert. The Mu-negative(MNG) characteristics have been recovered by adopting NRW method. This MTM characteristic is studied for 2.45 GHz using FR4 epoxy as substrate. The dimension of the substrate is 30mm× 36mm × 1.6mm. This fractal metamaterial structure can be amalgamated with an optimized Microstrip antenna (MSA) for improvement in antenna parameters and can be used for RF energy harvesting.

articleTitle: Simulation of Radiated Interference of Cables in Electric Vehicles Using 3D FDTD Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Aim of this study is to explore a method of simulating vehicle radiated interference based on 3D FDTD (Three-Dimensional Finite-Difference Time-Domain) model, which is better suitable for the situation that the full band spectrum needs to be solved. In this study, the model of motor drive system is established by Simulink tool and the current waveform of its power cable is extracted as the interference source. Combined with the field circuit coupling, the electric vehicle and cable model are established in the three-dimensional 3D FDTD model. The time domain results of the radiation field in the simulation space are obtained. Through Fourier transform, the full frequency spectrum can be obtained. Under the same conditions, the solution of 0-100MHZ in CST is obtained to verify its reliability and superiority. The results show that FDTD algorithm is more efficient than traditional commercial software. Its model modification is more flexible and the requirements for computer configuration are not strict.

articleTitle: Capacity Analysis of Ship-to-Shore HF MIMO Systems Employing a Single-Hop Ionospheric Channel
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We examine the capacity of a ship-to-shore high-frequency (HF) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication system that uses a single-hop ionospheric channel between the transmitter and the receiver. Our operating hypothesis is that using platform-based HF antennas in such systems allows for exploiting both polarization and spatial diversity in HF MIMO systems. An analytic model is presented and used to calculate the single-hop MIMO channel capacity. The model takes into account the polarization and spatial diversity, the characteristics of the transmit and receive antennas, as well as the statistical behavior of the ionosphere in response to the ordinary and extraordinary modes of propagation through the ionosphere. The possibility of using the characteristic modes of the platform as radiating elements of such a MIMO system is explored and a procedure for designing platform-based antennas that maximize the HF MIMO channel capacity is presented.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Application For Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the application of Machine Learning (ML) methods in Electromagnetics (EM) design through an illustrative example. Particularly, we show how ML techniques can significantly reduce the need for costly and resource hungry consuming full wave EM simulations by calculating accurate surrogate models using manageable count of EM full wave simulations. Three machine learning methods that are more suitable for antenna and EM applications, i.e., modified linear regression, Gaussian process and Support Vector Regression are applied to a particular problem and accurate models with only few percent prediction error are obtained using a small dataset. More interestingly, we show the surrogate models can successfully predict for the unseen data with only few percent degradation in accuracy.

articleTitle: Expansion in Exponential Sums with Application to Discrete Complex Image Theory
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Expansion of functions in terms of exponential sums is a technique that has been used in the past for applications in applied mathematics such as number theory. However, the technique also has interesting applications in the field of engineering. In this paper we present a novel approach to deriving an expansion of a function as an exponential sum and show how this expansion can be applied to the Sommerfeld Integral to give a novel Discrete Complex Image representation.

articleTitle: Nonreciprocal Concentric Metasurface Cloak
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We introduce here a nonreciprocal (NR) cloak, based on multiple circular concentric metasurfaces, where the curved metasurfaces bend the electromagnetic energy around a cloaked region similar to a conventional reciprocal cloak. On the other hand, we replace one of the reciprocal metasurfaces by a proper nonreciprocal one such that a source placed inside the cloaked region can effectively send signals to the outside. The simulation results confirm the perfect cloak performance and capability of the NR cloak as a transmitter.

articleTitle: Reduced Height Segmented Parabolic Reflector
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Parabolic reflector antennas often require a large volume and are often difficult to package onto a spacecraft. Here, we propose a reduced height segmented parabolic reflector with a lower vertical profile while maintaining good gain performance.

articleTitle: Noise Resistant Time-domain Inversion via Cascaded Network for Human Tissues
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a cascaded deep learning network consisting of an unsupervised U-net and a supervised EfficientNet is proposed to reconstruct the permittivity and conductivities of human tissues from time-domain measurements under high noise environments. The proposed framework has demonstrated superior computational efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. Compared to traditional approaches, a fully trained framework can avoid cumbersome iterations and retrieve the required electromagnetic parameters simultaneously. It is believed that the proposed architecture can be widely applied in real-time medical imaging scenarios.

articleTitle: A Loop Antenna Array with Enlarged Axial-Ratio Bandwidth and Reduced Cross-Polarized Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We analyze a novel dual-loop antenna with parallel wires using the moment method. The antenna is modified with a sequential rotation (SR), and a 3 dB axial-ratio bandwidth is evaluated versus loop height above the ground plane. It is found that the bandwidth with SR reaches 22%, which is 3.5 times as wide as that without SR. Subsequently, we design a decoupling array of two modified antennas to reduce the cross-polarized radiation. It is revealed that the maximum cross-polarization level in the radiation pattern is reduced to −15 dB without deterioration in the axial ratio bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Study of Reliable Short-Range Communication Systems for THz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The evolution of the terahertz (THz) era will be considered as a standard in the upcoming sixth generation mobile communications 6G. Although THz communications are quite auspicious even with the expected rising number of connected devices in future, the detriments such as additional losses and dispersive behaviour owing to the higher free space path loss are quite challenging when compared with lower frequencies. Hence, the aspect of a reliable coverage inside a room is the object of interest for THz systems. In this paper, a distributed antenna system (DAS) and a centralized antenna system (CAS) operating at 300 GHz carrier frequency each is presented in an indoor office scenario, with an isotropic antenna as reference. Furthermore, the antenna element positions and numbers in these DAS and CAS configurations are varied to mimick the isotropic antenna in terms of covering receiver-grids (RX-grids) at 0.75 m and 1.5 m heights as described by the line-of-sight (LOS) coverage probability requirements. Ray-tracing simulations reveal upon comparison with reference antenna that DAS configuration improves LOS coverage to 85.7%.

articleTitle: Compound Reconfigurable Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Agile Polarization and Pattern Diversity
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with probe feeds for both agile polarization and pattern diversity is proposed. Polarization reconfiguration is achieved by select phase shift paths for two side feed ports, while pattern diversity is achieved by exciting omnidirectional TM mode or broadside HEM mode with central or side feeds. For demonstration, here only one DRA at 2.45 GHz is used to obtain polarization and radiation pattern reconfigurable capacity. As expect, different states were obtained, and reasonable S-parameter, axial ratio and gain were achieved.

articleTitle: A Broadband A-Φ Formulation Solver Based on Discrete Exterior Calculus
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The A-Φ formulation of electromagnetics is immune to low-frequency breakdown, thanks to the additional gauge term in the formulation that removes the null space of the double curl operator, which makes the A-Φ formulation ideal for broadband and multiscale electromagnetic analysis. In this paper, a broadband A-Φ formulation solver based on discrete exterior calculus (DEC) is proposed. Implementation details of the DEC A-Φ formulation solver are provided in this paper, as well as numerical examples validate the proposed method and its broadband nature.

articleTitle: Glass-mounted Hidden SXM Antenna for Vehicular Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A glass-mounted hidden Sirius-XM (SXM) vehicular antenna is presented. In an effort to improve the aesthetics and visual profile of the vehicle exterior, a LHCP truncated corner patch antenna was designed to directly mount to the vehicle glass. Taking advantage of the dielectric loading of the glass material, the design is able to be manufactured using standard, less-expensive material, maintain performance, and remain in the interior of the vehicle. A superstrate structure applied to the design mitigates the potential de-tuning effects of installation tolerances near the glass.

articleTitle: Influence of Water Coupling Medium on Wearable Microwave Neurodegenerative Monitoring Device
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Microwave imaging is emerging as a non-intrusive, safe, and convenient modality for monitoring neurodegenerative diseases. This paper examines the effects of using water as a coupling medium on a wearable microwave neurodegenerative monitoring device. The device comprises six antennas that are integrated into a hat. The antennas are textile-based microstrip structures and are confocal to the hat. A water bag acting as a coupling medium is placed between the antennas and an under-testing head model. Experiments using a vector network analyzer (VNA) are performed to capture reflection coefficients (S11). The captured S11 indicates improved energy coupling between the device and the head model with the aid of water coupling medium. Subsequent experiments will be conducted to capture data from different angles around the head model and verify the device's suitability for monitoring neurodegenerative diseases.

articleTitle: Analysis of Partially Reflective Surface Antenna with Different Reflection Magnitudes Using Ray-tracing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: It has been shown that a partially reflective surface (PRS) antenna with a larger reflection magnitude has a higher antenna gain, based on practical design examples. In this paper, PRS antennas with different reflection magnitudes are analyzed using an intuitive ray-tracing model. It is derived that the larger reflection magnitude enables a smaller phase delay and a more uniform magnitude distribution across the PRS, which leads to a superior gain. The antennas with different reflection magnitudes were simulated in a full-wave solver to verify the derivation. The simulated phase and magnitude distributions of the PRS antennas agree with the predicted trends from ray-tracing.

articleTitle: A Ka-band Multilayer Filtering Array Antenna with Distributed Coupled-resonator Topology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper we present a new multilayer filtering antenna (Filtenna) array by using distributed coupled-resonator topology. The main purpose is to integrate both antenna and filter into a single module with multiple functions. The PCB-based multilayer substrate integrated cavity (SIC) resonators are effectively adopted to achieve a low profile, compact and high performance antenna array with filtering functionality. The cavity-backed patch antennas and SIC resonators are utilized to implement a 2 × 2-array antenna with a Chebeshev filtering response. For demonstration, a Ka-band Filtenna with fourth-degree selectivity response suitable for 5G communication links and phased array systems is designed and fabricated. The fabricated Filtenna consists of three separate PCB-layers, which is enabling a cost-effective and fast manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Trimmed Multilevel Fast Multipole Algorithm for D-Type Volume Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a trimming scheme for the multilevel tree structure of multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA), which is applied on D-type volume integral equations. With this approach, the number of iterations and the durations of matrix-vector multiplications are significantly reduced for the solution of multi-scale volumetric problems. The trimming operation is performed on rows and columns of the impedance matrix. In order to eliminate the matrix columns, the current coefficients are estimated via machine learning techniques. The implementation particularly provides significant acceleration for the iterative solutions of electrically large volumetric problems.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Energy Harvesting Metasurface with Polarization-Independent and Wide-Angle Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an energy harvesting metasurface with polarization-independent and wide-angle for 2.45GHz and 5.8GHz is proposed. The top layer on the F4B substrate is composed of metal patch etched with a centrosymmetric closed-ring cross. Four loads are located at four corners of the cross with metallic vias to connect the patch and the ground. The simulation results demonstrate that the metasurface can harvest more than 80% of dual band electromagnetic energy at an incident angle of 0 to 60 degrees, taking into consideration the slight offset of the resonant frequency.

articleTitle: Characteristic Modes as the Basis for Control of Serrated Patch Antenna Frequency Behavior
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Thin form factor antennas are widely used in communication systems. As the antennas become thinner, their bandwidths and radiation characteristics degrade considerably. Edge treatment in the form of serrations can help improve the bandwidth of extremely thin microstrip patch antennas. The theory of characteristic modes is used to analyze edge-treated square microstrip patch antennas. The effect of serrations on the resonant frequencies of characteristic modes is presented. Based on the characteristic mode analysis, guidelines for achieving multiband behavior and improving the bandwidth of thin square patch antennas are presented in this article.

articleTitle: Improvement of Wireless Power Transmission Efficiency to Implantable Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper we examine the advantages of incorporating three orthogonal coils in the implantable receiving unit to improve the power efficiency under device rotation within the human body. The wireless power transmission system incorporates a realistic multi-layered tissue model and the power transfer process is simulated using High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) software. The results show that the external and implantable devices can be optimized with improved power transfer efficiency under the effects of rotation within the human body.

articleTitle: Adaptive Beamforming with Omni-Directional Sensitivity Pattern
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: According to a widely used rule of thumb, an MVDR adaptive beamformer achieves output SINR within 3 dB of the theoretical optimum value, on average, when the number of data snapshots K is approximately twice the number of array elements, 2M. Real applications depend on the performance of individual updates rather than averages, however, and we show that an omni-directional quiescent array pattern is particularly poorly matched to a desired incoming plane wave signal. This results in unstable performance with a small number of snapshots. Many more than 2M snapshots are needed to achieve stable operation and good SINR in this case.

articleTitle: Enhanced Analytical Model for Multibeam Antenna Arrays in Conformal Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the H-plane radiation pattern analysis of a class of patch arrays will be presented with a new analytical modeling technique which employs precision modeling of individual radiators and a newly developed generalized array equation. As will be shown, this technique yields highly accurate overall H-plane radiation pattern prediction of microstrip patch antenna arrays of any conformal shapes.

articleTitle: Compact, Low-profile, Low-mass, UHF, Folded Shorted Dipole Antenna Array with Dual Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This article focuses on the design and simulation of a dual circularly polarized antenna centered in 400 MHz comprised of an array of four folded-shorted dipoles using sequential rotation over a ground plane. By altering the relative phase difference between the feedings of each element, both circular polarization senses are achieved for the same frequency. This antenna offers a comparable performance to other similar designs, like folded-shorted patches, while minimizing size and weight.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Matching Network between UTC Photodiode and 5G mmWave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A Dual-band matching network is proposed be-tween Uni-travelling Carrier photodiode (UTC-PD) and a 50 Ω transmission line using high-impedance transmission lines and planar spiral inductor. The proposed matching network achieved complex conjugate matching at 28 and 38 GHz bands. Furthermore, filtering response is achieved, which mitigates the nonlinearity of the PD.

articleTitle: A Planar True Time Delay 2D Beamformer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Full dimensional mm-Wave beamforming is essential for the successful deployment of 5G. Towards this end, in this work, a fully planar true-time-delay multibeam network based on the Blass matrix topology, is presented, as an alternative to bulky lens-based beamformers. To our knowledge, this is the first planar true-time-delay 2D beamformer. As a proof of concept a 2 × 2 Blass matrix design is designed to operate at 24 − 31 GHz bandwidth. Our proposed design has a footprint of 4.5λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×3.6λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, whereas state-of-the-art true-time-delay 2D beamformers occupy space of 14λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 4λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 4λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>.

articleTitle: Reflections on the Zenneck Wave
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this presentation we review the basic properties of the Zenneck surface wave, and compare and contrast this type of wave with the surface plasmon polariton (SPP) type of surface wave. Although both types of surface waves propagate on the interface between two half-spaces of material, their physical properties are very different. For example, a simple vertical electric dipole source will never excite a field that looks like the Zenneck wave on the interface, while the SPP field can be a dom-inant part of the total dipole field. The issue of "pole vs. zero" of the reflection coefficient for these waves is also clarified, and a relationship between a Zenneck wave and a leaky wave is shown.

articleTitle: A Wide Angle Scanning Spherical Luneburg Lens Antenna Employing Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel design method for employing metamaterial to construct lightweight and high-efficiency spherical Luneburg lens (LL) antennas with a broad scanning range is presented. Based on the method, a spherical LL antenna with a diameter of 4.7λ at 3.5 GHz has been fabricated and tested with dual-linearly polarized square waveguide feeds. The prototype lens antenna performs well with full scan range in the azimuth plane and 60° field of view in the elevation plane across the band between 3.3 and 3.8 GHz. The peak gain is 22.8 dBi with less than 0.5 dB scanning loss, and the cross-polarization level is less than 25 dB for the vertical, horizontal, and slant incident polarization. Simulated and measured results agree well.

articleTitle: WPT Enabled Autonomous RFID Tag for Enhanced Range and Accuracy Localization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The paper presents a compact UHF tag dipole conjugately matched to an active IC chip that enables the read range enhancement, and can also allow higher localization accuracy, when the proposed RIFD tag is used with localization systems based on received signal strength. For the DC voltage supply of the RFID IC, an ISM rectenna with a power management unit circuit are integrated on the RFID tag board to implement a WPT enabled autonomous RFID tag. For the tag, the NXP’s UCODE G2iM+ series transponder IC is used which offers very high chip sensitivity (-27.5 dBm) when it is supplied with 1.8V. The required dc voltage is supplied from the e-peas AEM30940 power management unit IC, which features a cold start from 380 mV. The PMU can be activated for input power at the designed ISM band rectifier as low as -11.5 dBm. Compared to the use of the IC chip in its passive mode, the active mode read range, is enhanced from 2m to 5m.

articleTitle: Automatic Power Control of Uplink Transmission for Sub-6 GHz Backhaul Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In a multi-user environment, a large number of users share the same radio resources. The limited availability of radio channels in the network is that the same channel has to be assigned to many users. A user with very good quality may consider using low power and still have acceptable quality. The advantage is that it will disturb other users less, thereby improving their quality. Power control is essential to do the same thing but in a controlled manner. This paper focuses on the downlink in a cellular OFDM-based network model, suitable for LTE, LTE +, and 5G networks. We consider permanent uplink traffic where each HM module (eNB) has persistent traffic towards its RBMs.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetically Coupled Circularly Polarized Antenna for ISM Application at 2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a single-point feed patch antenna for operation at 2.45 GHz. The antenna consists of patch element, enhanced by two pairs of parasitic elements. The first pair comprises two coplanar circular ring section elements. The second parasite is a stacked patch, analogous to the active one, placed at an optimal distance. Both parasites are aimed to enhance the antenna gain, despite the low-cost and low-performance substrate exploited.The best resulting structure exhibits a gain of 7.5dB from 2.3GHz to 2.6GHz, with a maximum gain of 8.0 at 2.45 hence suitable for application in the ISM band.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Analysis of Screening Effects on Terahertz Photoconductive Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Output saturation observed for high power levels of input optical pump is a well-known bottleneck in the operation of terahertz photoconductive devices (PCDs). This saturation is a result of various screening effects that stem from the interactions between electromagnetic fields and semiconductor charge carriers. To simulate these effects, this work uses a time-domain multiphysics approach that solves a coupled system of the Maxwell and the drift-diffusion equations to rigorously take into account the two-way nonlinear coupling between fields and carriers. Furthermore, an optical absorption-based model is used to correctly compute the carrier generation rate. The resulting multiphysics solver is used to simulate realistic PCDs, and excellent agreement is observed between the simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Body-Proximity Effects on the Input Impedance of a Complex-Conjugate SWIPT Textile Rectenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: While a range of Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) rectennas were proposed for wearables, the human-proximity effects on a complex-conjugate matching network-free rectenna remain mostly unknown. This paper reports for the first time the impact of human proximity on a complex conjugate rectenna’s impedance. The impedance of a dual-mode SWIPT microstrip/dipole rectenna is measured experimentally for varying separation from the body and on different body positions. The measured input impedance is used to simulate the rectifier’s RF-to-DC efficiency using a non-linear model showing the effects of the power level, load, and frequency on the DC output for different on-body impedances.

articleTitle: Prediction of Radiofrequency-induced Heating of Spinal Fixation System using Mesh-based Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a convolutional neural network (CNN) model is proposed to predict the RF-induced heating of Spinal Fixation System (SFS). Device mesh information is combined with the incident electric field information as the input for the network model. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is performed to estimate the appropriate number of training data. 1500 SFS models are created and 296 of thoseare used as training data. Results show good convergence for network training. The R2 score of rod and screw RF-induced heating prediction all reaches above 0.95.

articleTitle: Single Sideband Suppressed Carrier Modulator for C-Band Multiple Access FSO Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A Design procedure to realize a single sideband suppressed carrier (SSB-SC) modulator for free space optical (FSO) communication is theoretically presented. The operating principle relies on introducing spatiotemporal modulation into an indium-tin-oxide integrated plasmonic metasurface to obtain a time-varying output signal that is characterized by a sawtooth phase profile spanning on 2π and a constant amplitude. It is demonstrated that such spatiotemporal modulator transfers the incident signal into the first-order up-modulated sideband with more than 99% frequency conversion efficiency. The optical carrier suppression and undesired sideband rejection of 44 dB and 39 dB are calculated for the SSB-SC modulator, respectively. The application of the high-performance elements for multichannel multibeam scanning over a space-time shared-aperture platform is investigated. Thanks to the strong suppression of all undesired mixing products, the crosstalk between the channels with the same operating wavelength is significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Additively-Manufactured Coaxial Resonator-Based Filtennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new class of highly-miniaturized coaxial cavity-resonator-based filtennas is proposed alongside a monolithic integration approach using digital additive manufacturing. The proposed filtenna concept is based on the EM co-design of a coaxial cavity resonator and an annular slot antenna that exhibit the function of a radiating resonating node within a coupled-resonator-based bandpass filter (BPF). A stereolithography apparatus (SLA) monolithic integration concept is proposed for size compactness and reduced weight. For proof of concept validation purposes, a second-order filtenna was analyzed, manufactured, and tested. It exhibited second-order frequency-selective gain response with the following characteristics: center frequency: 4.75 GHz, fractional bandwidth: 7.4 %, realized gain: 4.4 dBi and radiation efficiency: 80%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Benchmark Biconical Antenna with RWG Method of Moments for IEEE P2816 Project
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents numerical results for electromagnetic analysis of biconical antenna performed via Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) Method of Moments (MoM) solution of the Electric Field Integral Equation (EFIE) in the mixed-potential form. The study is done as part of the IEEE P2816 Project entitled "Recommended Practice for Computational Elec-tromagnetics Applied to Modeling and Simulation of Antennas". Numerical results obtained with in-house RWG MoM code are compared against those generated using FEKO commercial MoM solver as well as analytic solution available for the biconical antenna. It is shown that upon δ-gap excitation mechanism at the port of the antenna the mesh density near the port effects the extracted input impedance of the antenna especially at high frequencies. Effect on the numerically extracted input impedance associated with the closeness of the computational model to the model of the ideal antenna is studied.

articleTitle: Innovative Mm-Wave and Non-Mm-Wave Antenna Integrations for Cell Phones: AiPiA and AiAiP
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper informatively presents the retrospect and comparisons on two innovative, interesting, and inspiring millimeter-Wave (mm-Wave) and non-mm-Wave antenna integrations for cell phones, that is, the mm-Wave antennas-in-package integrating non-mm-Wave antennas (AiPiA) and the mm-Wave antennas in non-mm-Wave antennas integrating a package (AiAiP), from diverse perspectives to enable promising benefits and enlightenments for future developments.

articleTitle: Qualitative inverse scattering from three-dimensional limited apertures using phase-delay frequency variation regularization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present an imaging study of the linear sampling method (LSM) from 3D limited apertures using a phase-delay frequency variation (PDFV) formulation. The aim for the PDFV regularization is to improve range discrimination in the LSM by linking the solutions across frequency according to a propagation-based phase constraint. We demonstrate improved imaging performance using simulated data from a conducting target.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Bandpass Filter Based on a Quarter-Mode Comb Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An X-band bandpass filter based on quarter-mode comb substrate integrated waveguide (QMCSIW) is proposed in this paper. In order to reduce the size and realize the miniaturization for the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter, the comb substrate integrated waveguide (CSIW) and quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) are effectively combined together. At the same time, the capacitive loading is added to the resonator so that the resonant frequency can be reduced while its volume can be kept unchanged. Simulation results show that the filter has a bandwidth of 7.46−10.18 GHz with a center frequency of 9.0 GHz, and its size has been reduced by 71.97% relative to the full-mode SIW.

articleTitle: A Compact, Injection-Moldable, Broadband Waveguide Polarizer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A compact and broadband waveguide polarizer for single-circular polarization is presented. As currently optimized, the novel development offers up to 45% of continuous bandwidth while enabling diverse manufacturing such as injection molding or conventional machining. Manufacturing diversity is achieved through the use of robust ridges in the waveguide which run flush to the polarizer backwall. The ridges also facilitate a joint optimization of amplitude difference, phase difference and internal reflections which gives rise to a multiplicity of axial ratio nulls. The developed feed cavity contains no undercuts and readily accepts draft angles up to three degrees without significant performance degradation. Furthermore, the performance offered exceeds that of traditional corrugated polarizers or loaded septum polarizers while accomplishing order-of-magnitude cost reduction when feed quantities are high.

articleTitle: An Antenna for 5G Communication: Mirrored Pair Array of Modified Half Microstrip Patches for Near Endfire Operation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Development of a very low-profile planar antenna that can radiate in the near endfire direction over a wide bandwidth is of great interest for application to 5G communication systems. This paper presents a shorted trapezoidal microstrip patch antenna element with near endfire radiation and a null in the boresight direction for use in a beam-steerable endfire array. The antenna is matched over 10% bandwidth centered at 31.2 GHz. Maximum gain of 8 dBi occurs around θ = 60°, ϕ = 90°. The difference between radiation in the endfire direction and broadside direction is nearly 35 dB. Simulation results are presented.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced Global Optimization for Microwave Brain Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An innovative biomedical inverse scattering (IS) technique is proposed for microwave brain imaging. It leverages on a customized System-by-Design (SbD) methodology enabling an effective and computationally-efficient solution of the differential scattering problem thanks to (i) a "smart" definition of the problem unknowns and (ii) the artificial-intelligence (AI)-driven integration of a global optimizer with a fast digital twin (DT) of the data mismatch cost function.

articleTitle: Focused microwave radiation for the localized curing of polymer resins
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The recent development of optical volumetric additive manufacturing (VAM) technology has enabled rapid 3-D printing of optically transparent resins. However, there is growing interest in employing other materials that extend the design space of this technology. Here we leverage focused microwave radiation to expand VAM to a much broader family of resins, including those which are opaque. We use an X-band microwave applicator array coupled to a beam-steering algorithm to focus microwave energy into liquid resins. We performed numerical simulations to demonstrate this microwave energy localization, and will present supporting experimental results.

articleTitle: Subsurface survey capability demonstration through a drone-borne tri-band SAR
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This article reports two scenarios to demonstrate the subsurface survey capability for high resolution tomographic survey through a drone-borne tri-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR). In the first scenario, a linear flight survey was carried out for the identification of a leaf-cutting ant nest. A reflectivity reduction of up to 8 dB was obtained in the nest area, demonstrating the penetration capability of the SAR system. Additionally, electromagnetic simulations were carried out to better understand nest effects in SAR survey and also presented the same reduction. The second scenario verified the theoretical λ/4 resolution obtained by circular flight surveys. In this case, a quad-corner reflector was analyzed by performing a helical flight, where results very close to the theoretical one were obtained.

articleTitle: Highly One-Way Electromagnetic Wave Transmission Based on Outcoupling of Surface Plasmon Polaritons to Radiation Modes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Unidirectional transmission of electromagnetic waves has attracted great interest due to its wide modern optical applications. This study theoretically demonstrates a one-way transmissive optical device with a high-contrast forward-to-backward ratio at the near-infrared region. The polarization-independent optical diode-like mechanism is designed using a metasurface diffraction grating configuration with symmetry breaking property along the wave propagation in which the working principle is based on the excitation of surface plasmon modes at the interfaces of thin metallic interlayer and their coupling to the radiation modes.

Author Keywords: long- and short-range surface plasmon polaritons

articleTitle: An Eigen Decomposition Method for Finite Element Analysis of Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Finite element method (FEM) is flexible in modeling complex geometries and material compositions and accurate in numerical simulations of a wide range of electromagnetic problems. However, it suffers from the poor convergence when solved iteratively. In this paper, an eigen decomposition method is proposed by removing the null-space of the FEM matrix to speed up the iterative convergence of the FEM solution. The scattering analysis of a large resonant cavity is performed to demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Casing and Hand Effects on a Compact Robust Pattern Reconfigurable Sub-GHz IoT Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The performance of a compact pattern reconfigurable IoT antenna at 868 MHz under environmental effects is assessed experimentally. The reconfigurability reduced the antenna sensitivity to environmental effects sharply. The slot radiators achieved less sensitivity due to hand effects, and they show almost zero sensitivity to 3D-printed plastic casing. On the other hand, the monopole antenna is sensitive to the plastic casing.

articleTitle: Bi-static Radar Cross Section Simulation for a Wind Farm at Short-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper we investigate the bi-static RCS (radar cross section) of wind farms by means of simulations. The study addresses short-wave frequencies which are used for global broadcasting and global communication, as well as for over the horizon radar. Wind farms are of concern because they grow rapidly in number and size. Depending on scenario and application, effects on wave propagation, like signal blocking and strong multi path, due to nearby wind farms may cause service impairments. In literature, we find studies for bi-static RCS mostly at higher frequencies or only mono-static RCS observations of both wind farms and wind turbines. The respective findings may lead to wrong assumptions at lower frequencies when discussing possible impacts of such a wind farm. We show that bi-static scenarios lead to much higher RCS values than the mono-static observation and RCS values increase further with the number of wind turbines of a wind farm.

articleTitle: Eigenfunction Analysis of Cylindrical Metasurfaces with Complete Tensorial Surface Susceptibilities
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A rigorous semi-analytical method to compute the scattered fields off a zero-thickness cylindrical metasurface (MS) is presented, which is described using complete tensorial surface susceptibilities, including both tangential and normal components. Exploiting the angular periodicities of the susceptibilities and the scattered fields in the Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTC), the scattered fields can be efficiently computed. Two examples of a purely reflective cylinder and a finite-sized arc are shown to demonstrate the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Unstructured Mesh Transformation FDTD Method for the TM Mode Equations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We introduce a new finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method for solving the TM (transverse magnetic) mode reduction of Maxwell’s equations with complicated material interfaces. The method uses an unstructured quadrilateral mesh intended to conform to the complicated geometry of material interfaces. Using a quadrilateral to unit-square local coordinate transformation, we remap all the field components from the physical grid to a computational grid consisting of unit-squares. On the computational grid of unit-squares we update the fields in time using the usual FDTD field updates. The local coordinate remap, however, changes a scalar material on the physical space to an anisotropic material on computational space; we handle the mixed components of the anisotropic material by interpolating the non-colocated field components. Finally, we resolve material parameter jumps across interfaces using a harmonic-mean. By testing our method on the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,1</inf> mode in partially filled infinite cylindrical cavity, we verify that the method converges, is second order accurate, and maintains stability.

articleTitle: Development of Unified GPU Parallel Framework Based on High Order DGM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Based on high order DGM and parallel framework, we done some further research on unified GPU parallel framework. First, high order DGM have been successfully implemented and integrated into the unified GPU parallel framework. Second, we further optimized the entire unified GPU parallel framework. The accuracy and stability of the framework have been further improved while ensuring computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Absorber Based on a Frequency Selective Surface Built on FR4 Substrate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A frequency selective surface consisting of a periodic copper pattern, built on a grounded FR4 substrate is introduced. The structure operates as an absorber for waves at 2.46 GHz, up to an incidence angle of 60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>. Variation of the geometrical parameters allows for the modification of the working frequency, as also demonstrated by the parametric studies reported in the paper. Properties of the structure have been assessed by full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Plasmonic Metasurfaces as Efficient Entangled Single-Photon Pair Quantum Sources
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC) is a quantum optical process where a photon spontaneously splits into a pair of lower energy entangled single-photons. Here, we demonstrate that the quantum effect of SPDC can be substantially boosted at room temperature by utilizing nonlinear plasmonic metasurfaces. The presented plasmonic metasurface design is composed of silver nanostripes grown on a bulk lithium niobate (LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) crystal terminated by a silver substrate. The quantum-classical correspondence principle is used to compute the SPDC entangled photon pair generation rate by the classical sum frequency generation (SFG) nonlinear optical process. The generated signal and idler frequencies are matched to the metasurface fundamental and higher order resonances leading to substantially boosted SFG efficiency and, consequently, significantly enhanced SPDC generation rate. The quantum SPDC process is at the heart of many quantum optical emerging apparatuses, since efficient single-photon generation at room temperature is required in a plethora of applications in quantum communications, cryptography, and sensing.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Implantable Antenna for ISM band Biomedical Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an implantable antenna with two co-centric rectangular complementary split-ring elements with slots added between the rings are proposed. The slots, on the other hand, are utilized to fine-tune the frequency. This antenna design works at 2.4 GHz ISM band. Moreover, a shorting pin is used between the radiating patch and the ground plane of the antenna to lower the resonant frequency. In comparison to other current antennas, this one can work in all areas of the human body, as simulated by various body phantoms. It can even be operated with high input power due its lower specific absorption rate (SAR). The presented antenna is compact and has good radiation properties. Implantable antennas in other frequency bands can also be designed using the proposed antenna method.

articleTitle: Planar Ultra-Wideband Modular Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A planar ultra-wideband transmitarray of tightly-coupled dipoles based on a novel modular unit-cell is proposed. Specifically, modularity is achieved by using capacitive coupling to connect the dipoles with the true-time-delay lines. Therefore, this modular design does not require physical connection between the receive/transmit dipole-layers and the true-time-delay lines, thereby enabling the realization of the first (to our knowledge) planar ultra-wideband transmitarray. Also, our design reduces significantly the fabrication cost of ultra-wideband transmitar-rays. As a proof-of-concept, a 12×12 element transmitarray is designed for broadside operation, and provides a 5:1 frequency bandwidth with an active VSWR < 3 from 3 to 15 GHz.

articleTitle: Control of Characteristic Mode Excitation for Wideband and Dual-Band Circularly Polarized U-Slot Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A method of controlling mode excitation by feeding selection is proposed for the designs of wideband and dual-band circularly polarized (CP) U-slot patch antennas. For both types of antennas, two CP modes are excited by combing three orthogonal linearly polarized (LP) modes. The sense of rotation is determined by controlling the feeding position hence different weightings of the LP modes, leading to a wideband CP design and a dual-band dual-CP design. The method is validated by experiments, which agrees well with the simulation. The measured CP bandwidth is 27.5% for the wideband CP antenna, a significant improvement compared conventional CP patch antennas. For the dual-band dual-CP patch antennas, the measured CP bandwidths are 2.7% and 4.4% respectively.

articleTitle: 100-200 MHz sdr-based radio telescope focused on the cosmological study of the Epoch of Reionization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Radio astronomy as an observational technique used in Astronomy allows experimental validation of theoretical models based on the study of electromagnetic cosmic waves. Technically speaking, uses dedicated instrumentation (radio telescopes) to acquire such signals. The study, base on the emission of 21-cm of neutral hydrogen at frequencies between 100 and 200 MHz, permits to cover a scientific case of open study called Epoch of Reionization (EoR) in which we seek to compare physics models with experimental measurements. This paper presents simulations and measurements of the sub-systems of a 100-200 MHz radiotelescope to establish the feseability to use Software Defined Radio (SDR) technology devices as receptors for low frequency radio telescopes.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Radio Transmission Through a Collisional Plasma: Theory and Simulation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: High-speed flight above Mach 5 leads to the formation of a thin plasma layer surrounding the vehicle. Transmission through this plasma layer is currently not possible when the frequency of the source is below the electron plasma frequency. In this paper, we show that introducing finite electron-neutral collisions in the plasma increases transmission. We first discuss the relevant theory. We then present results from a frequency dependent FDTD plasma dielectric model. Good agreement between theory and simulation is demonstrated with both methods demonstrating that transmission increases at larger collision frequencies and lower source frequencies.

articleTitle: Computationally-Efficient and Reliable Antenna Design within the System-by-Design ML-Based Framework
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electromagnetic (EM) devices requires advanced solution strategies to reduce the computational burden of the synthesis process. In this work, the machine learning (ML)-based System-by-Design (SbD) framework is exploited to address the design of antennas in a reliable and computationally-efficient fashion. The SbD scheme is based on a "divide-et-impera" paradigm which aims at decomposing the problem at hand into smaller sub-tasks that are addressed by specific interconnected functional blocks. Hence, the overall computational cost can be reduced by choosing and integrating the proper functional blocks, including global optimization techniques and learning-by-examples (LBE) approaches. The effectiveness of the SbD paradigm is shown with an illustrative example concerning the design of a mm-wave slotted substrate integrated wave-guide (SSIW) antenna for 77 GHz automotive radar systems.

articleTitle: Space-time coherence processing of electromagnetic fields in complex media
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work deals with the analysis of the degree of coherence of electromagnetic fields propagated through structured or reverberant media. The study focuses on space-time transfer matrices associated with the excitation of spatially localized and temporally coherent waves within such type of environment. It is proposed to associate numerical techniques allowing the decomposition of the propagated fields into a set of subspaces ordered according to their degree of coherence. Finally, we show that the components associated with the propagation regimes most favorable to any practical needs can be identified to either mitigate or enhance the effect of the complex media under consideration.

articleTitle: A New Hybrid DGTD/FDTD Method for 3-D Multiscale Simulations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a simple scheme to hybridize the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) and the standard finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods for modeling multiscale structures, such as metasurface unit cells. We use an unstructured tetrahedral mesh to model curvilinear and sub-wavelength geo-metrical details in the DGTD region, while keeping a structured FDTD mesh for other areas, including the perfectly matched layer (PML). We present a simple scheme to connect the two regions in a stable manner. The proposed method leads to significant computational savings combined with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized MIMO Antenna with Side-Lobe Suppression
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a three-port circularly polarized (CP) self-complementary Multiple-Input-Multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system with pattern diversity is proposed for sub–6 GHz 5G applications. The open end of the cylindrical cavity can be equivalent to a magnetic dipole. An equivalent electric dipole is introduced by etching two antipodal notches for each element at the top and bottom of the cavity. The field components produced by the two equivalent dipoles are orthogonal, and circular polarization is realized by adjusting their amplitude and phase difference. Then, a pair of metal walls is introduced to suppress the side lobe for each antenna. This antenna offers features including high radiation efficiency, low side lobes, good matching and high isolation.

articleTitle: Sidelobe Reductions in Rectangular-Lattice Planar Arrays with Reconfigurable Element Spacing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The transformative approach to sidelobe reductions using the electronically displaced phase enter antenna technique is investigated in a planar array configuration in this paper. A physically periodic rectangular-lattice array is electronically reconfigured into an aperiodic planar array to lower the sidelobe levels without any physical displacement while maintaining the same array size. The sidelobe reduction capability of the E-DPCA technique is further bolstered by combining it with the array thinning method to achieve about 8.6 dB reduction in a 7×7 planar physically-periodic rectangular array without any mechanical movement.

articleTitle: A Circular Dipole Antenna Array Design for RF Energy Harvesting in Wireless Communication Technologies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Antenna design for wireless communication technology applications has become a subject of interest in recent years. In this study, firstly, a single element circular dipole antenna is proposed and investigated with the help of electromagnetic software Ansys HFSS. The circular dipole antenna is recommended for RF harvesting in the study; it has been optimized due to the proper adjustment of many parameters such as shape, radius, and feeding range. To improve the power and direction characteristics of the antenna, the circular dipole antenna is made into a two-component rectenna array with an interconnection method. It has been demonstrated that the proposed circular dipole can be utilized to build a broadband antenna array for applications such as 5G technologies, wireless power transmission, and RF energy harvesting.

articleTitle: Wideband Wide-Angle Beam-Scanning SIW Cavity-Backed Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wideband patch antenna backed by substrate-integrated waveguide cavity is proposed and presented. An impedance bandwidth of 24.3 % with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf><-10 dB is achieved. The antenna features a compact size, which is then applied to the development of a planar patch array. To this end, an H-plane array antenna of 9 elements is studied in this work. Simulated result shows that a wide scanning range can be achieved. The main beam can scan from -70° to +70° with 1.1 dB gain fluctuation when f=12.5 GHz, and from -75° to +75° with 1.1 dB gain fluctuation when f=15 GHz. The TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> surface wave mode supported by a thick grounded substrate is critical for radiation enhancement at the ground plane direction.

articleTitle: Detection of Weak Electromagnetic Pulse Signal Based on Fractional Fourier Transform
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the electromagnetic pulse signal is difficult to detect due to the weakening of the signal strength after passing through the ionosphere, a weak electromagnetic pulse signal detection method based on Fractional Fourier transform (FRFT) is studied. Simulation results show that the method has good detection performance even in complex working backgrounds.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work illustrates an improved and well-designed dielectric resonator antenna that provides multiple frequency bands for wireless/ITS applications. The proposed antenna consists of an 1×2 even power splitter with a modified slotted ground made up of a star rectangular slot with an inner slotted ring and an outer partially slotted ring to excite a HEM mode inside the dual resonating CDRA’s. Four circular slots at the corners have been used to enhance the reflection coefficient. The proposed antenna operates at 2.62 GHz, 4.465 GHz, 6 GHz and 8.25 GHz and can achieve a peak gain of 3.66 dB with a maximum efficiency of 85 %.

articleTitle: Metasurfaces for Increasing the Power Level Harvested by Rectenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel concept to enhance the power level of rectenna systems based on focusing metasurfaces. A focusing metasurface is designed and fabricated based on the hyperboloidal profile of the generalized law of reflection at 900 MHz. Measurements have been carried on alongside an existing commercial off-the-shelf rectenna harvesting system. The novel concept has shown significant performance enhancement of the harvested power of the rectenna device: a linear gain of 5 is obtained when implemented along side the focusing metasurface.

articleTitle: A Ka-band Planar Integrated Circularly Polarized Magneto-electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a Ka-band planar integrated circularly polarized magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is proposed. The circularly polarized wave is generated by the metal via perpendicular to the ground and the rotationally symmetrical rectangular patches on the top layer. The antenna is fed by the slot coupling, and four parasitic patches effectively improve the axial ratio performance. The proposed antenna achieves 50.6% impedance bandwidth (23.3-39.1GHz) with S11<-10dB and 32.5% (26.5-36.8GHz) 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth.

articleTitle: Polarization Diversity via Aperture Sharing Between Orthogonal Sub-arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Polarization diversity is becoming the need of the hour as more and more wireless applications use electromagnetic bandwidth. The recently deployed 5G and upcoming 6G communications will require multiple polarization antennas. Polarization diversity of an antenna adds to the stability of the connections, channel capacity, increased bandwidth and can be used as various channels. In this paper, a shared-aperture orthogonally polarized array is presented that can produce multiple linear and circular polarization without inboard switches or additional hardware. The polarization diversity is achieved through orthogonal aperture sharing. The array is designed at 11.5 GHz frequency and has a 3-dB bandwidth of 17%, peak directivity of more than 15 dB, cross-pol isolation of -40 dB, and 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth 10%.

articleTitle: Entangled Quantum Imaging in Nikishov Underwater Turbulence Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Combined with the theory of statistical optics and underwater optical properties, this paper proposes a quantum imaging method for entangled photons in the Nikishov ocean environment targeting the problems of low imaging resolution of entangled photons in seawater and low probability of underwater photon capture. Specifically, we first design the optical path for underwater quantum imaging with the entangled light. Then based on the Nikishov ocean turbulence model, an underwater correlation algorithm is proposed according to the Rytov approximation. We set up an experimental optical path and test the effect of different seawater characteristic parameters on the imaging resolution to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method and system.

articleTitle: Integrated Gaussian Filtering and Wavelet Transform Based Coincidence Count Filtering for Quantum Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: To improve the quality of quantum imaging, this paper proposes a coincidence count filtering method based on integrated Gaussian filtering and wavelet transform for quantum imaging. Firstly, the photon information is collected to obtain coincident count values, and then Gaussian filtering is applied to smooth coincident count values. Secondly, discrete wavelet transform is performed on coincident count values to obtain wavelet coefficients, and Gaussian filtering is conducted on high-frequency coefficients. Finally, inverse wavelet transform is used to obtain the optimized coincidence count result, and then the target is imaged by linear mapping. Both simulation and actual tests verify that the proposed method can achieve high-quality imaging.

articleTitle: A Parasitic Loaded Rectenna for Energy Harvesting Applications for the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper a compact patch antenna suitable for Internet of Things applications at 5.8 GHz is presented. The antenna is printed on a commercial substrate and optimized for obtaining the maximum gain as well as the optimum input impedance for controlling a RF to DC module for energy harvesting applications.Simulation predicts a maximum gain of 7.00 dB at 5.8 GHz, with a return loss exceeding 33.0.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Software Development. Legacy of Prof. Tapan K. Sarkar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The impact of Prof. Tapan K. Sarkar on the research and professional career of the authors of this paper has proved to be tremendous. Specifically, this paper presents relatively recent achievements related to the computational electromagnetics field in the form of commercial (or pre-commercial) software which authors have participated in and, in one way or the other, are part of the legacy of Prof. Tapan K. Sarkar.

articleTitle: High-Gain Wire-Patch Based Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A Wire Patch Antenna (WPA) based Electronically Steerable Parasitic Array Radiators (ESPAR) System is proposed for an endfire pattern reconfiguration. The proposed system is characterized by 6 reconfigurable directive beams that combined can cover all 360°over the azimuth plane. Its low profile, high-gain (7.22 dBi) and low side lobe level (-6.3 dB) makes this antenna system suitable for long-range portable devices in IoT environments.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized LTCC Feeding Circuit for a 4-Port Wideband Wide Axial Ratio and Beam Width Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper reports on the design, fabrication and measurement of an compact, wideband 4-port circularly polarized antenna based on a dielectric resonator (DR) and a quad-phase power dividing network realized in LTCC technology. The choice of the DR antenna is motivated by its high radiation efficiency, wideband response and miniaturization possibility with a high dielectic constant material. The LTCC technology was selected to build a miniaturized 4-port feeding circuit necessary for generating the circular polarization in providing equal amplitude and 90° phase difference between the ports. The antenna is specifically designed to meet the requirement for GNSS applications, for fixed or mobile platforms, in terms of operating frequency and radiating characteristics while obtaining a compact design.

articleTitle: A Multilayer Circularly Polarized Ka-Band Phased Array Module using Sequential Rotation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new circularly polarized 4x4 antenna array with beamforming capabilities. The antenna is integrated in a multilayer PCB ready to combine with the remaining RF frontend in a vertical stacking and it can be scaled to fit applications such as new space satellite communications. By using the sequential rotation (SR) technique, it is possible to achieve wide scan angles, both LHCP/RHCP, while maintaining the axial ratio (AR) below 3 dB between 27.5-30 GHz, with a maximum gain of 14 dBi.

articleTitle: Minimization Formulation for Neural Network Based Solution of Maxwell’s Equations in Frequency Domain
