The simulation results on the nonuniform mesh grids achieve a much better accuracy and a lower overall computational cost.

articleTitle: UAV-assisted 5G Networks for Optimised Coverage Under Dynamic Traffic Load
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Cellular communication researchers and engineers are both interested in the potential use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as aerial base stations. In comparison to terrestrial communications or systems based on high-altitude networks, on-demand wireless systems using low-altitude UAVs can be deployed faster, can be reconfigured more easily, and will likely have better communication channels due to short-range line of sight links. The goal of this paper is to evaluate the use of UAVs in next-generation wireless networks, specifically as a flying base station. Ray-tracing simulations are used to simulate the coverage of a UAV-aided base station (UAV-BS) in a scenario with a fixed base station at the University of Glasgow, UK. The results imply that the UAV-BS will be of tremendous benefit to 5G network communication, such as capacity expansion in metropolitan regions, better coverage in rural areas, and network densification.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Microstrip Patch Antenna for 28 GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this article, the design of a rectangular patch antenna in the millimeter-wave range is presented. The antenna is placed on a Rogers TC600 substrate with a dielectric constant of 6.15. The antenna resonance is kept around 28 GHz. The proposed work enhances the gain by placing a superstrate at a specific distance from the radiator equal to 0.5 λ, which reflects the electromagnetic wave between the two substrates and, consequently, enhances the gain. As a result, the proposed method enhances the gain by approximately 2.27 dB, which suitable for automotive applications at mm-wave band.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Acoustics Promoted Low Frequency Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A dual-band bulk acoustic wave (BAW)-mediated multiferroic antenna is proposed, modeled and simulated, which is mainly composed of two multiferroic materials, namely, ZnO and FeGaB. As the devised antenna is implemented with acoustic resonance, the size of low frequency antenna can be reduced compared with conventional low frequency antenna. In this case, the entire length of antenna is 2000 μm and its thickness is about 20 μm. A two-dimensional antenna model is created using commercial software COMSOL MULTIPHYSICS based on finite element. As a result, the antenna has two frequency bands operating at 251MHz and 528MHz. The imulation results show that the antenna provides good resonance at the desired working bands, and the stress generated by the resonance is smoothly transferred from the piezoelectric layer to the magnetostrictive layer, realizing the conversion of electric-magnetic converting.

articleTitle: Near-Field Antenna for Noninvasive Human Head Microwave Thermometry
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Microwave radiometry is an emerging technology for noninvasive measurement of internal body temperature. This technique relies on the use of a near-field antenna placed on the skin that receives black body radiation from the tissues under it. Even for a well-matched antenna, mismatch is introduced from variations in the tissue layer properties and/or imperfect characterization of the dielectrics used for antenna assembly. This work demonstrates a design of a receiving antenna element for a human head-specific tissue stack, and a tuning procedure to improve impedance match. Measurements of a fabricated antenna against the forehead indicate that inaccurate characterization of the materials used for antenna assembly more significantly contribute to antenna mismatch than variations in the tissue properties of the forehead. Therefore, proper modeling of assembly materials, in addition to reasonably accurate tissue stack modeling, is crucial for near-field antenna design.

articleTitle: The Theory of Chee that Transformed Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) into Scientific TCM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) has been practiced in China since 2700 BC; yet not recognized as a modern science. This paper reports that a theory of Chee has been created to transform TCM to a Scientific TCM (STCM). The approach was to latch TCM onto the newly discovered human organ called Interstitium, then distil and synthesize TCM to conform to modern sciences. The theory of Chee was then formulated following the path Stratton took to create macroscopic electromagnetic theory published in 1941. This paper also shows that the theory of Chee not only transforms TCM to STCM, but also likely leads to new scientific discovery as well as new diagnostic and therapeutic instrumentation and procedures with robotic and even supernatural potentials.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Phased Array Performance with Uniaxial Anisotropic Metamaterial Radome
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The effects of metamaterial radome with uniaxial anisotropic layers are evaluated on a mm-Wave patch array. The longitudinal and transverse permittivity and permeability parameters of the meta-radome uniaxial layers provide additional degrees of freedom to obtain a radome design that can improve some intrinsic limitations of the phased arrays. A 3×7 element 2D mm-Wave array performance is evaluated while it is loaded with a meta-radome at a distance much smaller than a wavelength. It is found that the thick meta-radome with the meticulously tuned uniaxial layer parameters decreases the inter-element coupling of the array elements in the H- and D-planes.

articleTitle: Lossless Planar Metasurface for Wide-Angle Anomalous Refraction Based on an Efficient Surface Field Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a numerically efficient surface field optimization is used to design a locally lossless and passive metasurface (MTS) performing anomalous refraction. The MTS consists of the cascade of three patterned metallic layers, modeled through homogenized impedance sheets. A certain number of evanescent Floquet modes are introduced through an optimization procedure aiming at minimizing the real part of the sheets surface impedance. Numerical results show a near-perfect anomalous refraction without reflection for arbitrary incidence and refraction angles.

articleTitle: Wideband Millimeter-Wave Switched-Beam Lens Antenna with a Planar Array Feed
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wideband switched-beam gradient index lens antenna system is proposed for millimeter-wave applications. A modified Luneburg lens with a flat focal plane is designed based on the quasi-conformal transformation optics technique. This lens design facilitates the use of a planar array feed and enables wide-angle beam scanning. The proposed lens feed is a 9×9 magneto-electric dipole array operating over 24-40GHz. The proposed lens antenna features a large scanning coverage of ±58° with peak directivity > 19dBi while maintaining excellent pattern integrity and acceptable beam crossover levels over the band.

articleTitle: Direction of Arrival Estimation Using an Array of Stacked 2D Luneburg Lenses
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present the design and simulation of a DOA system composed by a novel 2D stacked Luneburg lens and an antenna array. The non-resonant lens is composed of 7 layers of a dual-diameter structure. The variation in the refraction index is achieved by adding cylindrical air inclusions in a dielectric base material. The results demonstrate that the design is suitable in direction finding applications.

articleTitle: A Genetic-Algorithm-Based Sparse Planar Array Optimization Method for 77 GHz High-Resolution Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a sparse planar array optimization method based on genetic algorithm is proposed for 77 GHz high-resolution imaging. The large scale half-wavelength uniform planar array is divided into multiple symmetric sparse subarrays, and the 2-D sidelobe of the sparse subarray is suppressed by the genetic based optimization approach, which reduces the number of array elements while remains the desired azimuth resolution and elevation resolution. The performance of the proposed method is verified by several simulation experiments. The results show that the optimized arrays can achieve an azimuth resolution of 0.7° and an elevation resolution of 2.3° in a field of view (±45°, ±45°), while the normalized sidelobe magnitudes in these sparse array radiation patterns are below -10 dB, which is suitable for high-resolution, wide field of view, and low-cost 77 GHz radar imaging applications.

articleTitle: New reconfigurable SIW phase shifter with transverse CPW-based stubs and PIN Diodes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a new electrically reconfigurable substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) phase shifter is proposed. The proposed structure uses a single PCB layer and does not require wire bounding for the bias circuit. Its principle consists in the integration, in the SIW, of several transverse CPW lines, each one is connecting a post, a PIN diode and a radial stub. Numerical results are presented to validate this concept. With the proposed design, for the two states of the PIN diodes (ON and OFF), broadband matching is obtained and a relatively constant phase difference is achieved in a broad frequency band.

articleTitle: A High Gain Circularly Polarized Pin Loaded Microstrip Patch Antenna with DNG Metamaterial as Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A high gain Double Negative (DNG) metamaterial superstrate based Circularly Polarized (CP) microstrip patch antenna for Ka band satellite communication is represented in this article. The rectangular patch antenna is developed with shorting pins along the two orthogonal diagonals. Pairs of shorted pins are placed to generate two different modes for obtaining CP. A simple coaxial probe-feeding is used to excite the patch antenna at Ka band. A 4x4 array of rectangular-shaped slotted ring patches which exhibits the characteristics of negative dielectric permittivity and permeability at Ka band has been used as superstrate. The implementation of this DNG metamaterial-based superstrate enhances the right hand CP gain from 10.2 dB to 12.2 dB, which makes the overall antenna height to be 0.58 times of the free space wavelength (λ0). The proposed design shows minimum axial ratio of 1.42 dB near the magnetic resonance of 28.5 GHz which makes the structure suitable for satellite applications.

articleTitle: A Compact Metamaterial based High Isolation MIMO Antenna for 5.8 GHz WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact metamaterial-based MIMO antenna for 5.8 GHz WLAN applications. The proposed antenna consists of two rectangular patches placed on a low-cost FR4 substrate. A series of metamaterial absorber unit cells are integrated between the two antenna elements to attain a high isolation level of 50 dB. The total size of the proposed MIMO antenna is only 32 x 60 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a mutual coupling level of less than -50 dB, thus making it an ideal candidate for 5.8 GHz WLAN-MIMO applications.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Ultrawideband Combined TEM-Horn Loop Antenna for Use at HF Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wideband combined TEM-horn loop antenna is miniaturized such that ka=0.126 at the lowest operating frequency and total efficiencies of 10% and 78% are realized when ka=0.5 and 1, respectively. The antenna instantaneously covers the full HF band (2-30 MHz). Miniaturization primarily stems from fuller utilization of the minimum enclosing sphere to push as much of the currents to the outer surface as possible, as according to electrically small antenna theory. Further modification involves combining the termination of the loop into one port to enable a 50 Ω system impedance. Simulations at HF and with a scaled model designed for manufacture (DFM) are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: On the Sensitivity of RCS to the Wall Conductivity of Highly-Conductive Structures with Voids
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: One of the recently introduced camera-box benchmarks is used to investigate the sensitivity of radar cross section (RCS) to the wall conductivity of highly-conductive structures with voids. Simulation results show that the effect of wall conductivity varies with look angle and frequency: The object’s monostatic RCS, a function of both the housing and the void, is insensitive to the wall conductivity at angles blind to the void or frequencies where the modes in the void are below cut off. The RCS is sensitive to wall conductivity up to remarkably high values, however, at angles aware of the void and frequencies where the void supports modes; e.g., distinct differences in patterns are observed at void-aware angles at 10.24 GHz until conductivity is higher than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> S/m. The study indicates that simulations that use the perfect-electric-conductor simplification may not accurately compute scattering from platforms containing even highly-conductive structures with voids.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Reflective Polarization Converter MSF for mm Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The conducted work focuses on the design of a reconfigurable reflection-based polarization converting metasurface for 5G communication applications (i.e. avoiding indoor/outdoor obstacles and allowing wireless quasi-line of sight path communication). The proposed design consists of an I-shaped resonator linked with two parallel biasing lines and an inverted butterfly shaped structure, integrated with voltage-controlled PIN diodes within the unit cell. The novel approach ensures the provision of electronically controlled, ultra-wide band (UWB) reflective circular polarization in one state and cross-polarization in the other. The reconfigurable MSF operates in K and Ku bands. The simulated results demonstrate that with zero biasing voltage the metasurface presents circular polarization ranging from 19 GHz to 40 GHz. This state can be reconfigured to cross polarization ranging from 30 GHz to 42 GHz through a global switching of the PIN diodes in every cell.

articleTitle: Power Pattern to Planar Dipole Array Synthesis Using a Text-to-Image Transformer Based Model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Based on a neural network architecture for text-to-image synthesis, we develop a neural network algorithm for far-field (FF) power pattern to planar dipole array synthesis. To this end, the desired FF power pattern (two perpendicular cuts) is compressed into the so-called FF tokens. The FF tokens are then translated to array tokens. Once the array tokens are obtained, they are decompressed to yield the planar dipole array design.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Intelligent Frequency Selective Surface Unit Cell For Future Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable dual-band unit cell based on frequency selective surfaces (RDBFSS) for 6G applications is presented. The proposed design consists of two patches mounted on a substrate. The patches are composed of hollows, and connected through two PIN diodes to achieve a dual-band operation with high isolation. The proposed design reconfigures its functional characteristic operations between the stop and pass bands at frequencies 5.8GHz and 28GHz, by changing the biasing of the PIN diodes. The transmission/reflection characteristics of the incident waves are investigated by changing the state of the pin diode, where the patches are responsible to generate the reflection/transmission at frequency 5.8 GHz, while the notches are responsible for generating the reflection/transmission at frequency 28GHz. The proposed unit cell is simulated, where good results are achieved.

articleTitle: S-Band Circularly Polarized Wideband Loaded Slot Antenna for CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: With the recent proliferation of CubeSat missions, there is a critical need for space-ready antennas with a desired set of characteristics. In this paper, a wideband, circularly polarized (CP), S-band loaded slot antenna with a co-planar waveguide (CPW) feed is proposed for CubeSat applications. The antenna geometry is presented, and its performance is validated through extensive numerical electromagnetic simulations and measurements. The proposed antenna is shown to achieve fractional impedance bandwidth of 37.1% centered around 3.5 GHz, axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) of 18.75%, and 7-8 dBi gain all while being lower profile and constructed on space-qualified substrate (i.e., Rogers RO4350B).

articleTitle: A PIFA Design with WLAN and Wi-Fi 6E Band for Laptop Computer Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A small-size (18.2×5×0.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) design working across the WLAN band (2.4 / 5 GHz) and Wi-Fi 6E band (5.925–7.125 GHz) is proposed for laptop computer applications. By modifying the PIFA structure (with bending and slot-loading), it can excite two resonant modes at 2.4 and 5.5 GHz, which can cover the entire WLAN frequency bands (2.4/5 GHz). To further cover the Wi-Fi 6E (5.925–7.125 GHz) band without affecting the original PIFA performances, a U-shaped parasitic element is printed behind the PIFA structure so that an additional resonant mode at 6.5 GHz is excited.

articleTitle: Developing an Electromagnetic Vortex Beam Structure Based on Advanced Plasma Transmit-array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) vortex waves in microwave regime offer a great venue for new communication links. Comparatively to multi-band and multi-antenna mechanisms, they can provide greater channel diversity and capacity. A plasma transmitting surface is proposed based on EM scattering wave theory to produce vortex beams. As a complex medium, plasma can be modeled by the Drude dispersive dielectric model. Plasma cells are to be housed in a multilayered medium and covered in glass. In the lower K frequency band, a 360-degree circle of transmission phase is achieved using plasma advanced structures. Physical parameters of the plasma can be tailored to alter the phase front of an incident wave. The analytical proposal for the plasma phase engineering surface is verified with full wave simulations. Using the proposed transmit-array, several vortex beams (0, ±1, ±2, …) can be generated with a single structure without any blockage of the modes. Plasma arrays with reconfigurable designs can be used in future generations of mobile networks.

articleTitle: Printed Planar Antenna for 28GHz 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a printed planar antenna for 28GHz 5G millimeter wave (mmWave) applications is presented. The proposed antenna is designed using substrate material Rogers Ultralam 1250, having dimensions of 20mm × 20mm × 0.79mm. The design evolution has been discussed and optimized design parameters have been presents. Results shown that it exhibits wide bandwidth of 5.2GHz covering frequency range from 26.4 – 31.6 GHz, high gain up to 8dBi and radiation efficiency greater than 80% for the entire band. The proposed antenna is compared against existing literature, and is compact in size, low profile, simple in geometry and is suitable for 5G mmWave applications.

articleTitle: A Gain Enhancement Study on a Vivaldi Antenna for Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an exponential flared Vivaldi type antenna in two different modifications that achieved high bandwidth and gain. The proposed antenna has been designed and optimized, considering the integration feasibility of the phased array system. The proposed antenna has been obtained with the bandwidth 5.12-16.34 GHz by optimizing a standard exponential flared Vivaldi antenna topology on CuClad substrate with dielectric constant ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 2.5. Including a half-circle as a hat notch and slots improve the antenna's directivity. The parametric study on notch elements is provided. The outcome of the parametric investigation is that those notch elements affect the directivity of the radiation characteristic without changing the S parameters due to its symmetrical characteristics.

articleTitle: Fully 3D-Printed Lightweight Combination of a Circularly Polarized Transmitarray and a Feed Horn
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The growing demand for high gain and beam steerable antennas onboard small satellites has motivated research on lightweight antenna technologies. We present a lightweight transmitarray antenna system including a 19-GHz, circularly polarized (CP), three-layer transmitarray, and a K-band CP feed horn with a built-in septum polarizer. Both the transmitarray and the horn are fully 3D-printed using the novel charge-programmed multi-material 3D printing process. The total weight of the printed horn and the 12-cm diameter transmitarray is only 17 g, which is about an order of magnitude lower than a conventional transmitarray system of this size in K-band. The transmitarray uses the horn as feed and achieves a measured directivity of 24.1 dB at 19 GHz, corresponding to 45.1% aperture efficiency.

articleTitle: Spacing Analysis of a Dual-Element Dipole
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A spacing study is performed on a dual-element dipole. Two distinct modes of operation are found: dipole mode and Yagi mode. It is found to achieve a high realized gain (6.3 dBi) at dipole bandwidth combination (Yagi mode). The antenna also maintains around 2 dBi realized gain within the -10-dB Impedance bandwidth outside of the combination (dipole mode). A -10-dB Impedance Bandwidth of 16.7% is reported.

articleTitle: A Variational Auto-Encoder and Transformer Based Approach for Metasurface Unit Cell Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Inspired by the similarity between the text-to-image synthesis problem and the scattering parameters to metasurface unit cell synthesis problem, we utilize a variational auto-encoder and transformer based approach to synthesize three-layer dog-bone unit cells from the knowledge of two-port scattering parameters in the X band.

articleTitle: Systematic Design of Metasurface Angular Filters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a systematic methodology for synthesizing metasurface (MS) angular filters, which are beneficial for improving antenna radiation patterns: by deriving a convenient rational-function form for the reflection coefficient, we facilitate efficient and flexible design of such devices. We validate our framework via full-wave simulations by devising all-pass angular filters with tunable phase featuring rigorously designed physical MS inclusions. Our results pave the path towards complete control over the angular response of MSs, from theory to practice.

articleTitle: Low Power Broadband Rectifier with Wide Dynamic Input Power Range for RF-Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We proposes a broadband rectifier with wide dynamic input power range, which is mainly used for low input power RF-recycling. As for the proposed structure, a broadband impedance matching network consisting of a two-stage microstrip line is adopted to cancel mismatch and achieve high power conversion efficiency （PCE） over the operating range. A prototype of the proposed rectifier is fabricated and tested for verify its performance. The tested results agree well with the simulated ones, which show the effectiveness of the numerical results. With an input power range of -1 – 10 dBm and a bandwidth of 1.8 – 2.8 GHz (fractional bandwidth of 43.4%), the PCE is greater than 50%. Besides, a peak PCE of 76.4% is obtained at an input power of 10 dBm.

articleTitle: Multiple Folding Array Antenna aboard a CubeSat and the Effects of the Element Arrangement to the Radiation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Multiple folding array antennas are deployed with the steps remaining between panels. It is possible to fold a large antenna in a small space and to deploy in two-dimension with simple mechanical structure. The array antennas that can be packed in a volume of 3U are investigated in this paper. The effects of the square and triangular element arrangements are compered. Radiation patterns are well expressed by two-dimensional diagram of contour.

articleTitle: Dielectric Characterization of Small Breast Biopsy Via Miniaturized Open-Ended Coaxial Probe
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The classification between normal and malignant tissues based on the use of an open-ended coaxial probe reveals an advantageous rapid support to traditional biopsy. The present work proposes an assessment of small biopsy breast dielectric characterization with our custom-designed open-ended coaxial probe. To this end, this study was accomplished by means of numerical simulations; results were confirmed by experimental measurements, performed at the University Hospital in Toledo.

articleTitle: Comparison of subsampling strategies for UAV-mounted subsurface radar imaging systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper compares two subsampling strategies for UAV-mounted subsurface radar imaging systems, which feature non-uniform acquisitions that have an impact on the quality of the resulting radar image. The first method is based on selecting those samples that meet four conditions related to the UAV flight speed and stability. In contrast, the second relies on dividing the observation domain in a grid of cells, and selecting only a maximum of a given number of samples within each cell. The impact of both techniques on the image quality is assessed by means of measurements.

articleTitle: Comparing Power Scattered by RIS with Natural Scatter around Urban Corners
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Reflective Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) are considered promising in improving coverage in Non-Line of sight (NLOS) wireless links, especially at mm wave bands. Coverage provided by RIS is here compared to coverage from such ambient propagation mechanisms as scattering from street poles, rough building walls and corner diffraction. It is found that such background scatter provides signal levels around an urban street corner comparable to that of an ideal 0.3m x 0.3 m RIS at 28 GHz. Larger area RIS is thus required to deliver substantial gain in such a scenario.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Two Port Antenna With Dual Polarization Based on Liquid Metal Switching Device
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this article, we present a novel reconfigurable two port antenna with dual polarization based on liquid metal switching device. Two microfluidic channels are embedded on the antenna feedline. First, liquid metal connects the port 1 to main patch that covers application frequency bands (2.7-4.4 GHz). In the second step, liquid metal connects the port 2 to main patch that covers application frequency bands (2.6-5.6 GHz) with dual polarization is proposed. The simulated results show the two polarizations (linear & circular) at 3 GHz in two modes of proposed antenna that is suitable for wireless systems. The proposed antenna has a simple configuration and compact size of 27 × 30 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and control of liquid metal is performed electrochemically on the microfluidic channel.

articleTitle: Beam Steering Performance of Horn Antenna with Risley Prism and Integrated Parabolic Phase Correcting Surface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A two element Risley prism (RP) design with integrated parabolic phase correcting surface (PCS) for beam steering application is presented. The proposed RP is illuminated by a triple mode circular waveguide horn. Use of the parabolic PCS along with typical RP has improved gain and pattern quality of the steered beams. Results for other quadratic surfaces as PCS will be presented during the symposium.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section (RCS) Technique For Antennas Characterisation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a non-contact radar technique for antennas characterisation. Both monostatic and bistatic radar configurations are used. By analysing the physical phenomena of the antenna backscatter with available terminal impedances, the re-radiation mode (transmission-mode) can be extracted. The calibration process eliminates contributions of both the antenna structure mode and measurement environment. In normal incidence, the transmission-mode data leads to the calculation of the antenna gain in the frequency domain. In bistatic mode, it is possible to reconstruct the far field radiation pattern of the antenna. The consistency of the results is based on the comparison of the reconstructed gain and radiation patterns based on the radar and conventional techniques obtained jointly by CST Microwave Studio numerical simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: Microwave Single Layer Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: a single-layer, low profile metamaterial absorber is designed and experimentally characterized in the microwave region. The unit-cell of the metamaterial structure is composed of a rectangular shape split ring resonator (SRR) placed around four square patches of different sizes. All are etched on a 1.6 mm dielectric FR4 substrate baked by a continuous metallic ground-plane. Full wave’s simulation and measurement show multi-distinctive near-perfect absorption peaks at several frequencies from 3.75 GHz to 16 GHz. A large continuous bandwidth is achieved from 8.7- to 11 GHz (absorption > 90%). The designed monolayer absorber would be a promising candidate in radar X-band and imaging applications.

articleTitle: A Benchmark Airplane Model with Ducts
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A recently introduced full-size airplane model is upgraded to encourage and support advances in computational electromagnetics. To increase the complexity of scattering problems defined using the model, surfaces covering the intake and exhaust entrances are removed and curved ducts are defined. The ducts are terminated at simple surfaces to reduce requirements on geometric tolerances, support additive manufacturing of scale models, and increase reproducibility of measurements and simulations. To facilitate the benchmarking of as many computational methods as possible, data are shared on a version-controlled online repository to include: (1) exterior surface (outer mold line) of the CAD model, including precise duct definitions, (2) triangular surface meshes of various resolutions, and (3) measured and predicted radar-cross-section data of scale models approximated as perfect electric conductors.

articleTitle: Metal-Only Reflectarray Generating Two Independent Beams with Orthogonal Linear Polarizations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Metal-Only reflectarray antenna generating two independent beams with orthogonal linear polarizations. Such reflecctarray is based on a dual polarized cell that allows to control the reflection phase of incident waves independently in both polarizations. The simulated gains of the two beams at 25 GHz are 30.77 dBi and 30.14 dBi respectively.

articleTitle: Design of a Circular Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Vehicle-to-Everything Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Advanced vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication is expected to require very large data rates, ultra high reliability, and low latency. This motivates the design of antennas able to operate in the mmWave spectrum with sufficient bandwidth and high gain. In this paper, candidate antennas are investigated and Dielectric Resonator Antennas (DRAs) are found to be an effective solution. An aperture-coupled circular DRA made from Rogers 6010 substrate is designed and simulated. The simulated peak gain and impedance bandwidth are 6.4 dBi and 2.51 GHz, respectively. The designed antenna shows potential for use in mmWave vehicular communication.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensing based on Variable Axial Ratio
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we report a novel wireless technique to remotely interrogate passive sensors and wirelessly estimate a physical or chemical quantity of interest. The technique consists in making the axial ratio of the sensor antenna dependent on a complex impedance itself related to the physical quantity to be measured. We numerically illustrate the principle with a single-port patch antenna loaded by a variable resistor. A constant axial ratio sensitivity of -0.2 dB/Ohm is obtained within the resistance range and we achieve a bijective axial ratio variation as a function of the loaded resistance.

articleTitle: Multi-layer Butler Matrix Beamformer using LTCC technology for 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized Butler matrix design method using folded structure is introduced. The Butler matrix was fabricated in multi-layer using Low temperature cofired ceramics (LTCC) and designed to operate at 28 GHz. The conventional one-layer Butler matrix has a disadvantage in that the length has to be increased inevitably and the volume of the system is increased. By using the proposed folded structure, the length can be reduced by more than 2 times compared to the general one-layer Butler matrix. In order to minimize the loss, it was designed in a stripline structure by forming a ground plane on the upper and lower surfaces of each layer. A signal is transmitted between layers through via holes.

articleTitle: An Accurate Link Budget Estimation of UAV Considering the Degradation of Antenna Patterns
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The operating environment introduces distortions on the antenna patterns, that are not considered in the classical application of the link budget formula that approximates the gain values of the antennas with their maximum value. The proposed method considers the antenna patterns modified by the environment as well as the flight conditions of UAV by means of full-wave or ray tracing simulations. The comparison between measurement and simulation shows that the proposed model is accurate and suitable for the design of the radio system of UAV.

articleTitle: Focused Metasurface with Multiple Near-Field Nulls
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a novel design of the near-field focused metasurface, which transforms a linearly polarized planar wave into a near-field focused wave with a focus and multiple nulls on its focal plane. The transmitting coefficients distribution on the metasurface for specified focus and nulls may be derived by calculating the pseudo-inverse matrix of its propagating channel matrix, and the focused metasurface is designed using a three-layer particle structure. A focused metasurface operating at 10 GHz with a focal distance of 100 mm and two specified nulls on its focal plane is designed and full-wave simulated. The simulating results show that the E-fields at the nulls are more than 30 dB lower than that at its focus on the focal plane.

articleTitle: A Multi-band Monopole Antenna for the 5G Wireless Communication Systems Operating at Sub-6G Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact multi-band printed monopole antenna for the 5G wireless communication operating at the Sub-6G frequency band. The proposed antenna consists of three resonators that operate at 1.9, 3.5, and the range of 4.6 to 7GHz for possible GSM1900, LTE, LTE-Advanced, and 5G applications. The antenna is built on RT/Duroid 5880 high-frequency laminate with a finite ground plane on the other side of the substrate. Simulation results show that the antenna has good performance in all frequency bands of operation, where a matching level is below -10 dB at the aforementioned bands.

articleTitle: Analysis of Penetration Depth and Average SAR in Double-Ridge Open-Ended Waveguide Antennas for Skin Cancer Detection at Millimeter-Wave Regime
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the assessment of penetration depth and average specific absorption rate (SAR) in ultra-wideband double-ridge open-ended waveguide antennas (OE-WAs) for skin cancer detection at millimeter-wave (mm-wave) regime. Specifically, two double-ridge OEWAs with 15–40-GHz and 40–110-GHz bandwidths are designed and fabricated. Each antenna demonstrates |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|<–10 dB and stable and symmetric radiation patterns across 15–40 GHz and 40–110 GHz with aperture sizes of 9.47×5.79 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 3.78×2.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. To understand how the electric field affects the subcutaneous layers, a 3D realistic biological model consisting of skin, fat, and muscle is adopted. The findings suggest that the proposed antennas can detect early-stage skin cancer even in the worst-case situation of very thick skin, i.e., when cancer begins to grow at a depth of roughly 0.2mm, which corresponds to the bottom layer of epidermis. Additionally, the average SAR values are well within the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) safety standard.

articleTitle: Robustness Optimization of Nanophotonic Devices Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Realizing state-of-the-art metasurfaces depends on meeting strict geometric tolerances due to their inherent sensitivity to structural variations. A design may have extremely good performance in simulation which is lost when undergoing fabrication. We present how a Deep Learning-augmented multiobjective optimization method can be used for designing metasurfaces which are robust to a common type of manufacturing defect, namely erosion and dilation.

articleTitle: Chip-scale Beamforming with Magnetostatic Spin-wave Transducer Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a magnetostatic spin-wave (MSW) phased array which provides control over the angular distribution of spin-wave propagation in a magnetic film. A description of the array and magnetostatic simulation model is provided. Beamwidth scaling and beamscanning are shown to be well-predicted by classical antenna array theory. The proposed transducer array can be used to reduce diffraction loss for efficient spin-wave devices and also enables new applications for chip-scale analog signal processing directly at radio frequencies.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-wave Wideband Dual Circularly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wideband dual circularly polarized antenna working in millimeter-wave band is proposed in this paper. The antenna is composed of three substrate layers, a round radiation patch on the top of the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> substrate layer, a three-stub 3-dB directional coupler planted between the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> and 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> substrate layers, and two capacitive disks in the air layer between the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> substrate layers connected to the coupler through two probes. The proposed antenna has both wide impedance bandwidth of 25.6-34.1 GHz (30%) and wide 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 24.1-34.1 GHz (33.3%) simultaneously, with the isolation between two input ports better than 15 dB within the operating band. The proposed antenna is able to achieve left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) or right-hand (RHCP) in a wide bandwidth of about 26-34 GHz (26.7%) and can be used as the units for an antenna array.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Scattering Contribution by RCS Feature Extraction Using Point Scatterer Modeling with Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper has been presented the point scatterer modeling technique to extract the radar cross section (RCS) properties for each parts of the radar object. Back-scattered electric field is formulated in matrix form by combination of the effects of scattering sources and phase correction term, and complex-valued point scatterers are computed by using iterative solver based on basis pursuit denoising (BPDN) algorithm, a kind of compressive sensing (CS). Applying the proposed method to the numerical example, simple missile model, the RCSs caused by head, leading edges, and tail wings are retrieved, and it has been verified that the proposed method can be applied to scattering factor analysis by the comparison of three components for contributions to overall RCS level.

articleTitle: Planar Strip for Decoupling Between Tightly Spaced Patch Antennas and Radiation Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A planar metal is proposed to decouple and correct the radiation pattern of two closely spaced patches separated by λ0⁄20 in the H-plane. The metal is close enough to the patch edges to induce the near-field power, and the length is about one effective wavelength λ of 5.80 GHz. As a result, the isolation at 5.80 GHz is improved from 7.30 to 16.34 dB. In addition, the realized gain of E-plane is enhanced by 2.85 dB, and the maximum radiation in the H-plane is almost corrected to be in the broadside direction, where the beamwidth is broadened to be 50° with only 0.2 dB fluctuation and the realized gain is almost no decrease comparing with those of no-decoupling structure.

articleTitle: Dual-Differential SIW-Fed Leaky-wave Antenna with Dual-Polarization for Full-Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized leaky-wave antenna (LWA) for full-duplex (FD) communication applications. The design is based on slots fed by substrate integrated waveguides (SIWs) with differential feeding. This SIW feeding and slot arrangement, which realizes two orthogonal and linear polarizations in the far field, is then used to excite leaky-wave (LW) fields on a superstrate constituted by a printed partially reflective surface (PRS). The LWA provides -10 dB impedance matching from 24 to 28 GHz (more than 15%), with isolation levels greater than 50 dB and with realized gains of 16 dBi. The proposed LWA is also compact, low profile, wideband, and offers a convenient feeding approach making the design useful for FD communications, dual-polarization, and 5G systems.

articleTitle: On the Use of Quantum Fourier Transform for Array Antenna Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The analysis of the power pattern of linear phased arrays (PAs) is addressed by exploiting advantages offered by the Quantum Computing (QC) framework. The proposed approach is described in its mathematical formulation and the parallel between the classical Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) algorithm is discussed in the context of the power pattern analysis. The proposed QFT-based method is validated by means of proof-of-concept results, in order to show the peculiarity of the quantum method in terms of accuracy and computational cost.

articleTitle: Knitted Antenna Design for UHF RFID and Wearable IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presented a knitted antenna design for ultra-high frequency (UHF) radiofrequency identification (RFID) and wearable internet of things (IoT) applications. The proposed antenna consists of a dual slot-match structure that provides a good impedance match with RFID microchip on high permittivity surfaces such as the human body. The slot-match structure is designed and optimized using characteristic mode analysis (CMA). The slot-match structure poses a very high inductive impedance and very low real impedance in free space. However, this impedance behavior helps in countering high capacitive effects caused by the human body and other high permittivity materials. The proposed antenna is fabricated by knitting using conductive thread. This antenna design features a read range of 2.4 m measured using an RFID reader setup after placing the tag on the human body abdomen. Moreover, the proposed antennas can be used as a sensor for vital signs or breath monitoring as its stretched state provide less read range as compared to the unstretched state. Therefore, the proposed antenna design can be used for UHF RFID, sensing, and wearable IoT applications.

articleTitle: A Flexible SS-SIE to Model Three-Dimensional Composite Objects With Nonconformal Meshes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A three-dimensional single-source surface integral equation (SS-SIE) formulation is proposed to solve the electromagnetic problems including multiple composite objects. By carefully considering boundary conditions and incorporating the surface equivalent theorem, an equivalent model with only the electric current density is constructed. Since boundary conditions between different regions are automatically satisfied, nonconformal meshes are intrinsically supported and troublesome treatments of boundary conditions at the shared interfaces or junctions are not required. It is extremely flexible to model complex composite objects. Numerical examples are carried out to validate its accuracy, efficiency and flexibility.

articleTitle: Design of Sub-6 GHz and Millimeter-Wave 5G Embedded Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a design of dual-band dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) for both sub-6 GHz and Millimeter-Wave (mm-wave) 5G applications is presented. Two-Cylinder Dielectric Resonators (CDRs) are embedded for generating two different operating resonances. The small CDR with relative permittivity of 10 is fed by a rectangular slot on the ground plane, while a 50Ω coaxial cable feeds the large CDR with relative permittivity of 6.15. The proposed antenna is simulated, where the structure resonates at two different frequencies. The first resonance results from the large CDR at 2.4 GHz with a realized gain of 6.3 dBi. On the other hand, the small CDRA resonates at 28 GHz, achieving a realized gain of 12.1 dBi.

articleTitle: Design of Compact L/Ka-Band Shared-Aperture Patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Design of a L/Ka-band shared-aperture patch antenna array is investigated. Compared with previously reported dual-band antenna architectures with wide frequency separation utilizing a multilayer structure, the current configuration presents a compact dual-band design over a single substrate. The L-band and Ka-band antennas consist of 2×2 and 14×10 microstrip patch antenna arrays respectively. The L/Ka-band patch arrays are excited through microstrip corporate feed networks. The design is optimized to achieve adequate impedance match for the array at L and Ka-bands. Antenna gains of 7.74 dBi and 26.20 dBi are obtained at the corresponding resonant frequencies at the L and Ka-bands respectively.

articleTitle: An Efficient DGTD Method for Computing Non-Local Electromagnetic Effects
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The nonlocal effects play an important role as the size of nano-plasmonic get much smaller than the wavelength of electromagnetic. In this paper, we introduce an efficient discontinuous Galerkin time-domain method (DGTD) for the numerical analysis of nonlocal electromagnetic effects in nano-plasmonic. We first adopt nonlocal hydrodynamic Drude model (NHD) to time domain Maxwell’s equations. Then the DGTD method is employed for the solution of nonlocal electromagnetic effects based on NHD model. The local time stepping algorithm is further introduced to improve the computational efficient. Finally, numerical example is presented to show the availability and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Polarization Insensitive Tunable AFSS with Wide Tuning Range
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A simple wide tuning active frequency selective surface (AFSS) architecture with a broad tuning frequency spectrum is presented in this work. The structure uses four varactor diodes to achieve this characteristic. Secondly, the biasing complexity of the AFSS is simplified and the unit-cells are isolated from each other using inductors. The AFSS operates in 2.2-8.7 GHz and 15.0-24.1 GHz bands in both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) modes. To obtain the desired operating characteristics, the topology evolution steps have been discussed.

articleTitle: Impact of Cross Terms on Pattern Multiplication in Receiving Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The performance of a receiving antenna array can be substantially improved by multiplying the outputs of two co-located receiving arrays. Compared to the performance of the two individual arrays, such multiplication can increase directivity, increase the number of nulls, and reduce sidelobe levels. However, in the multiplication process undesirable cross terms appear which may reduce the potential performance gains. Here, the detrimental impact of correlation between a desired signal and an interfering signal on the cross terms is investigated, as well as the impact of the signal-to-interference ratio on the cross terms.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable 3-D Printed HoneyComb Puzzle Piece Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A 3-D printed reconfigurable HoneyComb puzzle piece antenna designed to operate at S-band is presented. Utilizing fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3-D printing, hexagonal-shaped substrates with patch antenna elements are incorporated into a puzzle allowing for the series connection of two antenna elements. This design can easily be expanded to larger, more complex arrays with more than one frequency of operation.

articleTitle: Experimentally Validated, Compact, Highly-Integrated Differential-Fed, Dual-Band, Diplex Filtennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Compact, highly-integrated, differentially-fed, dual-band, diplex filtennas are presented. Our innovative designs make use of a rectangular dual-mode patch that operates in both its TM10 mode and a reshaped TM30 mode to realize two passbands. The first design is a compact, wideband, differential dual-band filtenna with strong frequency selectivity and high cross-polarization discrimination. Moreover, it shows a stable in-band realized gain at its broadside direction, and excellent stop-band suppression characteristics for both frequency bands. The second design is a highly-integrated, compact differential diplex filtenna that operates over the 2.4G and 5.8G WLAN bands. It has highly symmetric realized gain patterns and high port-isolation over both of its passbands. Prototypes of each design were simulated, optimized and tested. The experimental results, in agreement with their simulated values, verify that they both have attractive dual-band bandpass performance characteristics.

articleTitle: On the Contrast between Healthy and Cancer Tissues at Millimeter-Wave Regime for Skin Cancer Detection Using Reflectometry
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper evaluates the contrast between healthy and cancer tissues at millimeter-wave (mm-wave) regime using open-ended waveguide antennas (OEWAs) for skin cancer detection based on reflectometry. Two double-ridge OEWAs with 15–40-GHz and 40–110-GHz bandwidths are designed and fabricated. Each antenna demonstrates |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| <–10 dB and stable and symmetric radiation patterns a cross 15–40 GHz and 40–110 GHz with aperture sizes of 9.47×5.79 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 3.78×2.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. The minimum and maximum contrasts were obtained as 1.1% and 21.55% at 15.9 GHz and 109 GHz, respectively. The study provides valuable insight into the design of open-ended waveguide antennas for highly sensitive skin cancer detection systems at the mm-wave regime.

articleTitle: Wideband Bandpass Filter Based on Flag Shaped Central Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel wideband bandpass filter based on flag shaped central resonator with super-wide upper out band skirt rejection and a high selectivity factor. Bottom layer aperture with two stages based on three edge-coupled lines with centrally loaded flag resonator and lower stepped circular resonator contributes to the performance enhancement of the developed filter. The suggested bandpass filter has a fractional bandwidth of 103.5 % with a centre frequency of 5.8 GHz. The filter construction is optimized using the simulation software IE3D. The filter is made from a low-cost FR4 substrate with a thickness of 0.8 mm and a dielectric constant of 4.4. The centrally loaded flag resonator generates two transmission zeros, giving the filter structure an abrupt roll-off. The exceptionally wide upper stopband performance with greater than 30 dB suppression level is extended up to 22.3 GHz.

articleTitle: Light quantum positioning method based on integrated coincidence counting and adaptive light source selection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the dynamic change of the scattering environment affects the propagation distance estimation performance by different light sources, resulting in low positioning accuracy and poor robustness, a light quantum positioning method based on integrated coincidence counting and adaptive light source selection is proposed. Specifically, the method considers the dynamic changes of the scattering environment to group the entangled light time pulse sequences, calculates the signal propagation distance of each light source under each group based on the coincidence count, and takes the relative error of each light source under each group as the basis to dynamically select different light sources for positioning. The experimental results show that the proposed method has higher positioning accuracy and stronger positioning robustness.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Sum-Difference Beampatterns Using the Quadratic U Distribution
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work examines the quadratic U distribution, a unique convex quadratic function for the application of distributed antenna arrays. The analysis applies a fitting phase coefficient for the elements, such that the radiated signal power of each element is coherently added in the far-field region of a specified target direction with net destructive interference occurring in all other regions to suppress sidelobe behavior. The analysis also applies characteristic modal solutions in which element radiators are used independently to deliver both sum and difference beams. Sum-difference radiation patterns are generated and analyzed for suitability in applications such as amplitude monopulse scanning, the direction of arrival estimation, and target tracking. We observe that the inherent randomness of the antenna array distribution alleviates typical half-wavelength spacing requirements for grating-lobe-free scanning. Tapering of the pattern is accomplished by confining the distribution to a quadratic U or convex probability topology.

articleTitle: Intelligent Remote Powering System With PTE Auto-Balancing For a Wireless and Batteryless EEG Cap
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a fully battery-less and wireless (untethered) EEG readout cap. The powering system is equipped with a highly efficient and compact power transmitter mosaicked by an array of 8×11 Tx resonators in a certain pattern operating at the lowest ISM band of 6.78 MHz. The front-end’s power receiver block Rx includes multi-resonators mounted all-around an EEG cap that can be worn by a subject. Furthermore, considering the subject’s head which could assume different positions, a well-designed positioning system and an intelligent feeding setup are developed to balance the efficiency drop due to misalignment and to involve the most associated resonators with the powering scenario with the potential of switching off the extraneous resonators that are not engaged with Transmit and Receive (Tx-Rx) power.

articleTitle: Limiting Co-location Effects of Antennas using Engineered Electromagnetic Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An application of engineered materials to control electromagnetic waves and shield devices to maintain antenna parameters in a highly scattering multiple-antenna environment is shown. In a multiple-antenna environment, where each antenna operates at different frequencies, the scattering effects can be significantly reduced by enclosing an individual antenna with an engineered electromagnetic structure operating at a wavelength higher than the source. Numerical simulations are performed in COMSOL Multiphysics to demonstrate the success of the proposed shielding technique involving two 2D line-dipole antennas and a cylindrical enclosure of engineered EM materials at microwave frequencies.

articleTitle: Single Layer Frequency Selective Surface with Three Transmission Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a single layer frequency selective surface(FSS) with three transmission bands is realized with substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. The super unit cell of the proposed FSS consists of four small unit cells, in which the square slots with two different dimensions are embedded. The full-wave simulation results are investigated to illustrate the performance and operation principle of the proposed device. The tri-band FSS exhibits excellent angular stability up to an oblique incident angle of 40 degree.

articleTitle: Design and Manufacturing of C-Band FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A practical and educational design of a frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar operating at 5.8 GHz is showcased. Solutions to design challenges are noted and completed hardware is described. A simple test of radar performance, demonstrating the capability of the system, is presented.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Investigation into all Possible Reasons Causing Cross-polarized Radiations in Microstrip Antennas and Predictable Solutions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work addresses possible reasons behind the cross-polarized radiations commonly occurring from a microstrip antenna. A detail analysis of the surface conduction current has been presented in identifying the same. Necessary correction of the source current has also been examined as the means of removing the unwanted cross-polarized fields. A representative design is presented in C-band circular patch. The experimental studies with a prototype promises a considerable improvement in XP value by about 10 dB over a diagonal plane (φ = 45°) and 11 dB in the H-plane (φ = 90°). This study would enlighten the engineers in dealing with XP issues in several microstrip antenna designs.

articleTitle: Dispersion Characteristics of Accelerated Spacetime-Modulated Media
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper opens up the field of nonuniform-velocity SpaceTime-Modulated (STM) metamaterials, with the canonical example of an STM metamaterial of constant proper acceleration or, equivalently, hyperpolic acceleration. Combining tools of General Relativity and Classical Electrodynamics, it derives the dispersion relation of this exotic medium and reports its fundamental physics, whose most striking feature is the bending of light in the direction opposite to the direction of the modulation.

articleTitle: PIN Diode-Enabled Reflector/Absorber with Out-of-Band Transmission
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A PIN diode-enabled reflector/absorber with out-of-band transmission is proposed. First, an equivalent circuit model is developed to provide insight into the physical operation. Using the circuit model, a parametric study is provided demonstrating a tradeoff between reflector/absorber bandwidth and insertion loss in the transmission bands. Next, the desired response is demonstrated with a simulation model of a two-layer frequency selective surface. Transmission line theory is employed so that each layer can be initially modeled individually and fine-tuned by hand. Finally, the dynamic resistance of the PIN diode is leveraged to achieve the desired attenuation in the absorbing state. This approach provides electronic control of the attenuation level and simplifies the design by avoiding additional lumped resistors or lossy films.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Shared Aperture Antenna for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Shared Aperture Antenna (SAA) where two circularly polarized (CP) patch antennas operating at GPS L1 (1.575 GHz) and X-band frequency are combined into a single antenna for small satellite communication applications, e.g., CubeSats. The GPS slotted-patch antenna is designed and optimized in a manner that it can accommodate the X-band antenna inside one of its slots. The X-band antenna is a Fabry-Perot Resonator Cavity Antenna (FPRA) with a partial reflective surface which increases its gain significantly. Simulation results show that both antennas have good impedance and Axial Ratio (AR) bandwidth and CP gain. The antenna has a small dimension (65×65×18 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) which makes it suitable for placing it on any of the CubeSat sides. The antenna can simultaneously operate at multiple frequencies and replace multiple antennas required for GPS, uplink, downlink, and crosslink communications in CubeSats, saving space and volume, and reducing design complexity.

articleTitle: Compact Circular Polarized Fractal Antenna Array for Vehicle Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) fractal antenna array was designed and presented in this work focused on applications in vehicular communication systems in the 5.85–5.925 GHz frequency range, the array was developed based on the IEEE802.11p standard. The new geometry used as element array was generated in MATLAB™, using Koch fractal transformation in the complex plane. The transmission line antenna was fed by a connected to a underneath each fractal rotated truncated rectangular patch element of the array to generate circular polarization. The bandwidth the circularly polarized array is equal 72.5 MHz at 5.88 GHz, with on axial ratio of 0.22 dB. The compact dimensions of the array were optimized for applications in road units RSUs. Double layer dielectric substrate with a permittivity of 10.20 and a thickness of 1.27 mm was used on the design. The first results were obtained using ANSYS Designer™ full wave simulation software.

articleTitle: Radiation Control Using Dipole-type Antenna for PCB Handset Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the radiation features of typical Printed Circuit Board (PCB) antennas combined with a dipole-type structure. Driven by the application request, a pattern-reconfigured is proposed and experimentally verified. By taking advantage of PCB antenna radiation feature and working principle of the dipole element, we are showing that a simple antenna structure change could redirect the radiation pattern. The antenna is designed on 1.6 mm FR4 board at 2.4 GHz aiming for Internet of Thing (IOT) applications. The modified antenna remains good radiation performance in terms of efficiency and bandwidth, while antenna pattern or polarization have been well tailored to meet to specified application request.

articleTitle: Application of Adaptive Moment Estimation For Solving Scattering Problems with PE Basis Function
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper studies the feasibility of using the adaptive momentum estimation (Adam) to solve matrix equations generated by the phase-extracted (PE) basis function in method of moments (MoM). PE-MoM has the advantage of modeling large and smooth scatters with less unknowns, but the matrix equation usually has a large condition number and hard to solve with iterative solvers. Here we use the technique of stochastic row samples to accelerate the solution process. Numerical examples verifies the performance of this scheme.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed mmWave Dual Dielectric Lens Antenna for Series-Fed Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a 3D-printred dual lens structure that is used to enhance the gain of mmWave radar systems with series-fed antenna arrays. The design is based on a hyperbolic lens structure that is modified to accommodate the series-fed array with frequency dependent beam direction. The goal of the design is to focus the main beam of the antenna in one direction through the whole 77GHz band while providing gain enhancement. The design was created and simulated using Ansys HFSS and then 3D-printed using Raise3D Pro2 printer with a PLA filament. The lens performance was verified using TI AWR2243 radar board for a remote material characterization application.

articleTitle: A Bandstop Filter Based on Inverted Microstrip Gap Waveguide for Millimeter-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Based on the inverted microstrip gap waveguide (IMGW) technology and U-shaped resonant element, a narrow bandstop filter for millimeter-wave V-band is proposed in this paper. Firstly, we analyze the two-dimensional dispersion relationship of the high impedance surface periodic structure and simulate the transmission characteristics of the IMGW in the V-band. The return loss of the IMGW is less than 30 dB in the frequency band of 55 − 65 GHz. By using the −coupled U-shaped resonator structure on the inverted microstrip line, the filter with bandstop characteristics is designed. Finally, the narrow bandstop filter with a center frequency of 60 GHz is optimized by the well-known HFSS software. The insertion loss of the bandstop filter is up to 18 dB and the bandwidth is 0.57 GHz.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Analysis of Millimeter-wave Series Patch Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, characteristic mode analysis is used to gain insight into the operation of millimeter-wave series patch array. It is shown that the series patch array (broadside) mode has lower modal bandwidth and higher resonant frequency than the corresponding mode of a constituting patch element, whereas the other dominant orthogonal (broadside) mode is identical between the array and the single element. Moreover, it is found that unlike the use of shorting vias, non-shorted microvias along the array direction can help to decrease the resonant frequency of the series array mode. A parametric study is performed to show the effect of the length and position of the microvias on the series array mode.

articleTitle: Multi-Band Single-Layer Reflectarray Using Arbitrarily-Shaped Elements for Dual Polarization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes arbitrary-shaped elements for a multi-band single-layer reflectarray antenna. These elements generated by optimizations based on the genetic algorithm provide various reflection phase properties desired for multi bands. As a design example, we present a reflectarray operating at 14 GHz, 20 GHz and 30 GHz bands and verify its usefulness numerically.

articleTitle: Enlarged Metaloop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A conventional natural loop antenna does not radiate a circularly polarized (CP) broadside beam when the perimeter is greater than one free-space wavelength (1λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>). To overcome such a restriction, this paper investigates a planar loop antenna based on c-type metaatoms, referred to as a metaloop antenna. The investigation is performed by letting the loop perimeter be greater than 1λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. When the operating frequency is within the fast wave region of the negative propagation phase constant, the antenna, whose height is on the order of λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/100, radiates a CP broadside beam. The gain for the CP broadside radiation is also clarified.

articleTitle: Revisiting the Eiffel Tower Antenna of 1911
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The history of the Eiffel tower and the attached transmitting antenna in the 1898-1911 era is reviewed with particular attention to technical details involving antenna and tower dimensions, transmitter circuits, and observed performance. Using a scaled drawing constructed from available elevations of the tower and a ball chain simulation, a working model for analysis is shown along with an impedance sweep of the antenna. The resonant frequency is determined along with the capacitance, inductance, and radiation resistance. By comparing these results with those measured at the time, a clearer picture of the antenna is presented.

articleTitle: Revisiting End-to-End Communication Model for Realistic Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS), a planar intelligent structure made of a large number of reflecting elements, is a potential smart radio technology that enables the intelligent construction of reconfigurable wireless environments. More precisely, each element of the RIS changes the reflection of the incident signal according to its own set of specifications. As a result, wireless environment becomes smart based on multiple design goals. The radio map of RIS assisted environment can be generated using end-to-end (E2E) analytical communication model reported in literature where all unit cells of RIS are assumed as metallic cylindrical thin wires and the mutual coupling effects of them are calculated analytically. While such simplistic analytical modelling applies only to simple structures and is based on several assumptions, the more accurate full wave computational electromagnetic (EM) modelling has its own limitations and drawbacks like computational complexity and storage requirements.
