In order to study the realistic RIS assisted wireless environment, we employ a hybrid approach where the effective impedance of unit cells are calculated using full wave EM simulation and are employed in the analytical E2E communication model. We also investigated the influence of a) the placement of RISs, b) the number of RIS reflecting elements, and c) multi-RIS environments using both analytical and hybrid approaches. It is shown that the proposed approach can be leveraged for efficient modeling, analysis, and optimization of RIS-assisted communications.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Small Aperture Horn Antenna by Three Dimensional Printable Prototype
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The three dimensional printable antenna prototype is proposed for smaller aperture feed horn source. It shows an improvement of about 3 dBi in directivity and gain of feed source which is able to decrease SLL to -17.2 dB at design frequency of 12 GHz. The dimensions of considered horn feed is 2.6λ×1.6λ×4λ, where the designed proposed prototype is of 3λ×3λ×1.5λ. The distance between feed horn aperture and proposed prototype is 12.5 mm (0.5λ), which is able to correct the phase variation from 170.41° to 20.47° where the former phase value is for horn source only and later is the phase value as obtained after the placement of proposed prototype above the feed horn that is noted at 5 mm (0.2λ) above the upper surface of designed prototype. The 3dB angular width is decreased from 30.9° to 17.7° after keeping the designed prototype above the feed horn source.

articleTitle: Conical and Broadside Beam Switching Micromachined Antenna at 26GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A pattern switchable micromachined antenna operating at 26 GHz is proposed. The antenna consists of a microstrip circular patch and a ring antenna placed concentrically. The antenna can switch between conical and broadside radiation patterns by exciting TM21 mode of the ring and TM11 mode of the circular patch, respectively. The ring is excited by two ports and the patch is excited parasitically. Two different techniques are proposed to switch between these patterns. In the first approach in phase and out of phase feeding of the antenna is employed whereas in the second approach both ports are fed in phase and the beam control is achieved by inserting two slots to the ring. The absence or presence of the slot can be controlled by placing a switch at the center of each slot. Hence, switches control pattern selection in this configuration.

articleTitle: Validation of Physics-Based Circuit Model For Multiport Microstrip Antennas Using DCIM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The previously proposed circuit model for general planar antennas of arbitrary geometry is extended to antennas over microstrip substrates. Using discrete complex image method (DCIM) together with matrix pencil technique, the microstrip dyadic green’s function is modeled analytically and used for characteristic mode analysis (CMA) and field calculation of arbitrary microstrip antennas. The characteristic modal responses are then used as the basis to expand antenna input responses at arbitrary feed positions. A 2-port antenna system is numerically investigated to validate the extended circuit model, and illustrate its utility for antenna feed placement and input parameter visualization.

articleTitle: Design of Conformal Sparse Metasurfaces using Green’s Function
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, numerical calculation of Green’s functions is employed to design arbitrarily-shaped sparse meta-surfaces composed of few elements for wavefronts tailoring. Several metasurfaces are designed in the microwave domain for beamforming and scattering reduction functionalities.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Evaluation of Passive Wireless Neurosensing Recorder for Biopotentials Recognition
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Neuropotentials monitoring can help individuals to significantly enhance their physical and mental well-being. We present an evaluation of a multichannel, passive and fully implantable wireless neurosensing system (WiNS). WiNS employs radiofrequency and optical communications to address the need for non-battery-operated systems. In this study, we will present a new automated technique to identify signal segments eliminating the difficulty of manual classification of evoked biopotentials. In addition, machine learning algorithms are adopted to evaluate signal quality from WiNS and compare it with a commercially available wired system. Somatosensory evoked potential data measured from wired and our wireless systems shows < 6% deviation in machine learning testing accuracy, indicating successful detection of biopotential signal as low as μV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf>. These results support the concept that real-time machine interface for wireless and passive acquisition of biopotentials is indeed feasible translating to several uses for future clinical research.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Reconfigurable Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton (SPP) Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A switchable binary patterned surface plasmon polariton (SPP) leaky-wave antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna consists of an ultra-thin corrugated metallic structure on 2mm thick substrate which supports highly confined spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs). The antenna is fed by a coplanar waveguide (CPW) structure. To achieve a smooth conversion from the spatial mode in the CPW to the flat mode in the spoof surface plasmon (SPP) structure, two sector-like transition sections are introduced to suppress the return loss. Two varactors are integrated inside the SSP unit-cells to enable a reconfigurable surface impedance pattern. By actively modulating the surface impedance, a switching mechanism between the guided transmission mode and the leaky wave mode is achieved with a high degree of robustness. Furthermore, multi-directional beam steering from the broadside to endfire can be synthesized with this antenna with high efficiency. A highly directional pattern with a maximum realized gain that varies from 6 dBi to 8 dBi is demonstrated at 6 GHz.

articleTitle: Polarization Reconfigurable Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper reports a simple design method for wideband polarization reconfigurable magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna and array. By only adopting two biasing voltages, the polarization can be switched among four polarizations, e.g., two orthogonal linearly polarized (LP) and two orthogonal circularly polarized (CP). This quad-polarization diversity is realized by systematically integrating a wideband reconfigurable feeding network and a ME dipole with two orthogonal feeding ports. By controlling the states of the switchable feeding network, two orthogonal LP mode corresponding to the two ports can be excited with specific phase difference, thereby generating four different polarizations. Moreover, the reconfigurable feeding network can be extended to array application without increasing any p-i-n diode. For proof of the concept, a 1 × 4 array is designed, fabricated and tested. The measured results confirm the array’s capability for four reconfigurable polarizations. Moreover, the array also exhibits exceptional advantages as wide bandwidth and a simple switching topology.

articleTitle: Analysis of Microwave Absorbers for Electromagnetic Coupling Reduction Using Waveguide Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, analysis of broadband absorbers for reducing the electromagnetic interference (EMI) is carried out in the frequency range from 6 to 14 GHz (i.e., X-band). Two different resistive FSS-based absorbers are designed using efficient equivalent circuit model. To analyze the utility of the designed absorbers for the EMI application, transmission coefficient (S21) of the transverse EM wave is evaluated by using the waveguide method through accurate full wave simulations. Besides absorption, computed S21 for the different configurations are compared to assess the resistive FSSs capability also in the EMI reduction.

articleTitle: Metasurface Reflective Polarization Converter Based Dual-Band Circularly and Linearly Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A dual-band circularly (at 0.78GHz) and linearly (at 2.45GHz) polarized antenna is proposed for radio frequency identification (RFID) and WIFI indoor positionings. The relevant standard for 779-787 MHz RFID is newly used in China, whereas the standard for 2.45 GHz RFID is ISO/IEC 18000-4. The antenna consists of microstrip-fed solt antenna (MFSA) and reflective polarization converter. This converter can transform a linearly polarized (LP) incident electromagnetic (EM) wave into its orthogonal LP reflection wave. The MFSA can achieve dual-band linearly polarized radiation. After loading the reflector, 3dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidths of 0.78–0.82 GHz is achieved.

articleTitle: Tumor Margin Identidication Based on Contrast Values in Millimeter-wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work proposes a novel method for tumor margin identification in millimeter-wave imaging in which a priori information about the statistical distribution of the dielectric properties of tissues is employed. In prior work, we presented a new millimeter-wave imaging modality that visualizes tumor profiles with high contrasts through the depth of skin with low cost. In this paper, we add the capability of estimating the margin of the tumor based on the contrast in millimeter-wave images. We propose a novel level set method in which the image function takes only two constant values. A learning-based method is employed to estimate the level set and corresponding reflectivity profile. Synthetic data are generated for objects within a 3-D imaging cavity and used for model training and testing. Furthermore, the method is tested on a numerical phantom. The reconstructed image indicates that the method can produce accurate estimates of object location, shape, and size while recovering the contrast with an error less than 5%.

articleTitle: Sustainable X-Band Absorber using Iron-Catalyzed Laser-Induced Graphitization on Wood
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A fully sustainable two-layer X-band absorber based on resistive patterns engraved on wood veneers is presented. The resistive structures are produced using an innovative laser-induced graphitization procedure based on a sustainable iron-containing ink. Simulations and measurements show that the absorber is realizable in practice and works for incident angles up to 45° off broadside.

articleTitle: Watt-Level Low-SAR Near-Field Wearable Wireless Power Transfer using an All-Textile Receiver
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Near-field radiative Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) has the advantage of high-power WPT. In this paper, an all-textile high-power WPT receiver is realized for the first time, using an embroidered coil and a printed tuning capacitor on a textile substrate. The proposed coil is demonstrated receiving over 3 W DC power at 6.78 MHz with a 23% end-to-end efficiency. A low Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) of 0.37 W/kg is observed, through full-wave simulation, for up to 10 W high-frequency input to the on-body coil, demonstrating its suitability for wearable applications.

articleTitle: A Process for Developing Additively Manufactured Interposers for Use in Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Additive manufacturing has seen much growth in the past few years due to many advantages it provides. Although much progress has been made in the field so far, there is still more optimization that needs to be done before it can be used for mass production. Utilizing the strengths of both manufacturing methods, a hybrid approach is discussed in this paper. An additively manufactured interposer is placed inside of a traditionally manufactured printed circuit board (PCB). The interposer connects the board to circuit components via conformally printed interconnects. Due to the low-loss characteristics of the interposer material in the X-Band, they can be used in multi-stack boards with RF components.

articleTitle: Open-set Classification of Small Complex Targets with ISAR Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In target recognition systems, it is necessary for the system to handle observations of both known and unknown targets. In this work, the ability of a neural network to classify synthetic ISAR images representing both known and unknown targets is investigated.

articleTitle: Second-harmonic Generation from Asymmetric Lithium Niobate Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we study the second-harmonic generation (SHG) in lithium niobite (LN) based asymmetric metasurfaces. The numerical results show that high Q-factor resonances linked to quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs) can give rise to highly efficient SHG from LN metasurfaces. Our work reveals the potential application of conventional nonlinear crystals in nonlinear metadevices.

articleTitle: A Method for Estimating User Equipment Orientation Using the Ratio of Received Power due to IRS Reflection Pattern Switching
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: High frequencies, such as in the millimeter-wave band, which have been available since 5G, are likely to cause insensitivity areas where blocking reduces the received power and communication quality cannot be guaranteed. As a solution to this problem, research on intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRSs) has become active. As a method of orientation estimation for appropriately directing the reflection pattern to the user equipment (UE), a method of narrowing down the orientation by switching the beam width of the reflection pattern in a hierarchical manner has been proposed, but it requires many steps (number of times to switch the reflection pattern) and takes a long time to complete. In this paper, we propose a UE orientation estimation method that solves this problem by reducing the number of switching times by using the ratio of received power when the reflection pattern is switched. We evaluated the accuracy of the orientation estimation and the number of times to switch the reflection pattern before the orientation can be estimated correctly, and showed that the UE orientation can be estimated more quickly than the conventional method when the received power fluctuation due to shadow fading is small.

articleTitle: Bounds on Substructure Dielectric Resonator Antennas Using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a recent development on the fundamental limits of substructure dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs). Specifically, the substructure DRAs are found to have higher resonance frequencies than the superstructure DRA, and a bounding relation on Q factor is also obtained. Numerical examples based on a ring DRA and a cylindrical DRA is examined here to demonstrate the bounding relations.

articleTitle: A Compact 2-D Conformal FDFD Method with Non-uniform Mesh for Waveguide Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A compact two-dimensional (2-D) conformal finite difference frequency domain (FDFD) method with non-uniform mesh is proposed for the analysis of dispersion characteristics of a general guided wave structure. The use of conformal and non-uniform meshes in complex waveguides that contain curved boundaries or local features of fine geometry can significantly reduce the size of computational matrix. Additionally, the newly proposed method reduces the error caused by stepped approximation at a curved boundary. Less computational cost are required as compared to the original compact 2-D FDFD method. Numerical results of some typical guided wave structures are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of this method.

articleTitle: A Reflectarray Element with Low Reflection Loss and Excellent Amplitude Stability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a reflectarray element that is capable of continuously tuning the phase of reflected wave is proposed. It consists a single dielectric layer with metallic structures on both sides. The upper metallic layer includes one meandering-line ring and a square ring with open slots. The lower metallic layer acts as the ground plane. The varactor diodes are placed between the square ring and the meandering-line patches. The phase of reflected wave can be continuously tuned by varying the capacitance of the diodes while a low reflection loss and excellent amplitude stability are achieved during this process. Full-wave simulation results demonstrate an overall phase tuning range of 258 degrees and low reflection loss below -0.35 dB.

articleTitle: Flexible Liquid-Metal-Tuned Absorber
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A flexible, low-profile, and polarization-insensitive absorber with a tunable absorption band is presented in this paper. The proposed metasurface absorber consists of a resonant liquid metal frequency selective surface (FSS) layer embedded in a thin (0.044λ) slab of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). By pneumatically controlling the position of liquid metal dipoles inside PDMS channels, continuous tuning of the absorption frequency is achieved over a 1.6 GHz (16 %) bandwidth in the X-band.

articleTitle: Empirical modeling of diffuse scattering at millimeter wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Propagation channel models based on ray-tracing techniques can estimate the specular multipath components (MPCs) reaching the receiver antenna, but have difficulties to estimate the diffuse components. In this work, an empirical model to include the diffuse scattering in ray-tracing channel models, or channel simulators, is presented. The diffuse scattering model has been developed from channel measurements at millimeter wave (mmWave) frequencies collected from 25 to 40 GHz in the frequency domain in an office environment.

articleTitle: Novel Approach Improving Quality Factor of Miniature Slotted Resonators in Near-Field WPTs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new simple method to enhance the quality factor (Q) of small-size slotted resonators applicable for wireless power transfer (WPT) systems. The employed spiral-type slots were thoroughly analyzed to determine their optimum parameters for the high Q achievement. It was also revealed that integrating a metal streak into the resonator structure positively affects the overall performance. In particular, the aptly implemented modification resulted in a 17.8% increase in Q compared to the initial resonator. Finally, these newly designed resonators were used in the development of near-field WPT.

articleTitle: Wide Beam Steering by Leaky Wave Antenna with Liquid Crystal-based Phasing Structure and Metamaterial-based Radiating Apertures in Ku Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wide beam steering leaky-wave antenna (LWA) based on a liquid crystal (LC) phasing structure and metamaterial apertures is presented and simulated. The antenna continuously steers its beam from −48° to +44° at the fixed frequency of 13.6 GHz (Ku band) by biasing the embedded LC. As a result, the beam steering angle is 64% wider than the state-of-the-art LC-based LWAs in the Ku band to the best of our knowledge. This improvement is obtained by the design of a meander-line phasing structure as revealed from an analysis based on the array factor. The antenna design also offers compactness, lightweight, low-cost, simple beam steering mechanism, and design with much-reduced bias lines and control circuits, low bias power consumption, good power handling, good realized gain, and low sidelobes.

articleTitle: Analysis of EM reflections in a undergound mine for the CBRS band of Private mobile networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The bandwidths, as well as the frequencies used in the new communication systems, are constantly increasing. Their behaves in the underground mines are not really known. The use of models and/or simulation software requires knowing the nature of this environment as well as their propagation characteristics. Indeed, this environment has rough walls with irregular reliefs. In this paper we will evaluate, with a measurement set-up, the reflection coefficient of the walls. This reflection coefficient will be used in propagation simulation software to predict propagation in this environment and thus ensure optimal and efficient use of new communications systems.

articleTitle: Low-Profile GAP-Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna for Millimeter-wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, for the first time in gap waveguide (GW) technology, the radiation and feed sections are implemented in only one substrate. Hence, a low-profile antenna structure is achieved. To verify the operation of this concept, a cavity-backed slot antenna is designed in the millimeter-wave frequency band. Specifically, the cavity section and the feed line are embedded on two sides of a substrate. This low-profile structure can be a good candidate for 5G wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Dielectric Flat Lens for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a dielectric flat lens for gain enhancement. The proposed lens consists of a set of concentric rings with different refractive index values for each. The proposed lens is based on the graded steps of the effective refractive index of the semi-spherical lens. The radius of the designed lens is 6λ, and the thickness is optimized based on a tradeoff between the gain and the side lope levels. A horn antenna is used to examine the performance of the designed lens at 28 GHz frequency in terms of the maximum gain, and side lobe level.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam 1.6m Ka-band Deployable Mesh Reflector Antenna concept for INCUS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A multi-beam Ka-band deployable mesh reflector designed for the NASA’s Earth Ventures Mission named INCUS (Investigation of Convective Updrafts) is presented. It is a 1.6m diameter mesh reflector offset-fed by an array of five small horns. The 4 off-nadir horns are arranged in two rows in order to achieve the desired cross-track overlap at the 3-dB point of the antenna pattern. This solution takes advantage of the platform motion to achieve the desired scan pattern with a simple switched-horn solution. The optimization of the antenna feed location to achieve the 3dB beamwidth overlap is described and the overall reflector antenna performance is presented.

articleTitle: Generation and Manipulation of Lower Out-of-Band Rejections of Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a strategy to create and control the lower cut-off frequency of the spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) transmission lines (TLs). Pairs of short-circuited shunt stubs are employed to introduce and flexibly control the lower cut-off frequency. The proposed strategy is validated by numerical simulations. A cut-off frequency can be found in the lower rejection band. The 3-dB fractional bandwidth is about 128.1% covering a frequency range from 1.19 to 5.43 GHz. This work paves the way for the development of novel SSPP-based microwave devices.

articleTitle: Planar SIW-Based Dual-Polarized Filtering Antenna with High Port Isolation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel planar dual-polarized filtering antenna is proposed in this work. When the vias on the edges of a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) dual-mode cavity become sparse, the electromagnetic (EM) wave leaks out while maintaining the original dual-mode filtering response. Four orthogonal quarter-wavelength patches act as the radiators in conjunction with the SIW cavity. Through common-mode (CM) and differential-mode (DM) signal excitation, TE201 and TE102 mode are generated inside the SIW cavity. The radiation patches are directly fed by the leaky EM wave. Two orthogonal polarizations along the x-axis and y-axis are obtained, respectively. A 180° hybrid was vertically integrated to provide CM and DM signals. A folded structure is applied to reduce the aperture size forming an un-split radiation beam, which also improves the boresight gain. A prototype with a height of 0.058λ0 has been implemented. Measured results are well consistent with the simulation, demonstrating dual-polarized radiation with high port isolation and good filtering performance.

articleTitle: Estimating effective contact resistance of resonant cavity joints using near-field scanning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The possibility of estimating the effective resistance at contact points along a seam in a cylindrical vessel is investigated. The vessel is formed from two top-hat structures bolted together at a flange. Aluminum shims at the bolt locations ensure a nearly constant 5-mil gap or slot between the flanges. Cavity modes are excited with a short monopole antenna inside the structure, and external near fields 5 mm away from the slot are probed around the vessel circumference. Comparison of CST and FDTD simulations with measurements reveals that the shape of the field-vs-angle curve is strongly dependent on the contact resistance, indicating that meaningful estimates can be extracted.

articleTitle: My Considerations on the Legacy of Professor Tapan Sarkar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: I’ll present a short consideration on the legacy and impact of the work of Professor Tapan Sarkar. This reflection is mediated by numerous exchanges, conversations, and discussions I had with him about three different but deeply interconnected subjects.

articleTitle: Dielectric Breast Phantom by A Conditional GAN
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Synthetic dielectric breast phantoms are generated by conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN) in this paper. Phantoms produced by the generative neural network are 128 by 128 pixels for frequency 3 GHz. The generated phantoms can be used in electromagnetic simulations for microwave breast imaging (MBI) research and can serve as the training data to develop machine learning algorithms for MBI research.

articleTitle: Conjugate Match Algorithm-Based Synthesis of RCS Reduction Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, the Conjugate Match Algorithm (CMA) is employed for the first time to synthesize RCS reduction metasurfaces. CMA is applied to estimate the phase distribution of the metasurface that would result in a 10 dB RCS reduction of flat metal targets at normal incidence. The metasurface considered for the synthesis is of size 300 mm × 300mm with an inter-element spacing of λ/2 at 10 GHz. The phase distribution thus estimated is realized using crossed dipole elements. A MATLAB code uses these data to generate the metasurface CST file for simulation. On simulation, the synthesized metasurface provides a bandwidth of 49% over the frequency range 5.7 GHz– 9.4 GHz.

articleTitle: An Angularly Stable Linear to Linear Polarization Conversion Metasurface for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A highly compact single-layered polarization convertor with high angular stability for X-band applications is proposed in this work. The unit cell is based on a square loop with two additional split square loops attached to the diagonal vertices. The cell is backed with a solid ground plane and realized on FR4 substrate. The proposed design converts x- or y- polarized incident wave into their orthogonal counterpart. The design also exhibits stable frequency response at oblique angles of incidence up to 45°. A finite prototype with overall dimensions of 210 × 290mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is fabricated and tested. The measured results validate the simulated ones. The proposed PCM can be used in polarization converters and RCS reduction applications that employ the passive phase cancellation technique.

articleTitle: A Radio-Frequency Detection System for Biomedical Imaging with Magnetic Contrast
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a biomedical imaging system suited for malignant inclusion detection, employing magnetic nanoparticles as contrast medium, is presented. In particular, the proposed system, working at 3 MHz, comprises two identical sensors, symmetrically separated by the biological phantom. Each sensor is made up by an internal coil, resonating at the chosen operative frequency through an opportune capacitive load, inductively coupled to an external, unloaded concentric probe. The inclusion detection and localization are achieved by measuring the two sensors input impedances and their mutual coupling. We performed preliminary numerical simulations, obtaining promising results and demonstrating the possibility to correctly localize 10 mm diameter inclusions inside the investigated tissue, despite the significantly low frequency. The main advantages of the proposed system, beside the relatively low-complexity instrumentation, also include the possibility to reducing the invasiveness for the patient since safe, non-ionizing radiations are employed. Therefore, the proposed imaging system can be potentially a good candidate as a non-invasive, low-frequency and contactless near-field device, encouraging further analysis.

articleTitle: Glue-free Technology for Hybrid Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) and Array Designs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the design of a glue-free hybrid DRA array which utilizes an unconventional radiating mode HEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12δ</inf>. Special care has been exercised to realize the above mode in a cylindrical DRA to ensure a relatively higher gain over a wide bandwidth. A robust mechanism has also been investigated for mounting a 2×2 hybrid DRA array, which attains a gain of nearly 14 dBi together with a 10% operating bandwidth. Experimental validation of the proposed design has been included.

articleTitle: Efficient DGTD-GSTC Modeling of Arbitrarily Curved Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We propose a discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method based on the generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) to analyze arbitrarily curved metasurfaces. The discontinuities in the electromagnetic field near the metasurface are simulated by placing virtual edges on both sides of the metasurface. The GSTC approach is incorporated in the update equations in standard DGTD algorithm. Furthermore, we have extended the method to arbitrarily curved metasurfaces, which has been proposed and verified for the first time. This is also the first time that the DGTD scheme is extended to include the GSTCs for metasurfaces. Two examples are simulated to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Novel On-chip True Time Delay Engine using Frozen Modes for mm-Wave Beamforming and Optical Networking
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a simple all-dielectric photonic waveguide structure based on Silicon-on-Insulator platform that exhibits 3rd-order degeneracy enabling frozen modes. Such degenerate propagation modes with vanishing group velocity is realized by introducing coupling among 3 neighboring Si ridge waveguides to design a stationary inflection point in the dispersion diagram, leading to the frozen mode and a true time delay device capable of 0.5 THz ultra-wide-band beamforming for millimeter wave phased arrays. For a 1 Tbit/s optical transmission system, the device is capable of data buffer or synchronization of up to 14 bits. The 600x slowing down of light compared to free space optics could be utilized for applications like biosensors and optical coherence tomography, in addition to ultra-wideband beamforming of phased arrays.

articleTitle: Analysis on Power Transfer Efficiency Using Near Field Plates
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Two wireless power transfer system using Near Field Plates (NFP) loop antennas, which are designed to operate close to the ISM band between 886 and 906 MHz are proposed in this paper. It has been shown that an NFP using a set of eight loaded loops has better performances in terms of the the magnetic field and the current intensities on the receiver when compared to NFP using four loaded loops. The Wireless Power Transfer Efficiency (PTE) is examined while displacing the NFP in various positions between two coupled resonant loops in order to uncover the position that provides the highest PTE.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Modeling and Radiation Analysis of a Micro-Coaxial Collinear Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a super-miniaturized Ka-band coaxial collinear (COCO) antenna based on a micro-coaxial transmission line is designed and analyzed. An equivalent circuit model of this micro-coaxial collinear antenna is established to explain the impedance characteristics of the antenna. In addition, a radiation model of the antenna is built, based on simulation data, to analyze its radiation characteristics. The above models can help explain the working mechanism of the COCO antenna and provide guidance on the design of such an antenna.

articleTitle: Fast Null Placement in an Adaptive Planar Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Unwanted interference signals have been a bottle-neck for many radar applications and satellite communications. Most of these interfering signals are usually from undesirable sources. A Schelkunoff polynomial nulling technique incorporated with a genetic algorithm is proposed in this paper, in order to place multiple nulls at the undesired directions where the interference signals are radiated. The genetic algorithm is employed to steer the radiation patterns nulls at the undesired directions and simultaneously optimizing a reduced number of the array elements excitations. This results in relaxing the complexity of the problem. The proposed technique has been validated by reducing the processing time by about 90% compared to the conventional optimization process with almost no effect on the required pattern specifications.

articleTitle: RF Ionization and Multipaction Breakdown Prediction for High Power Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes system-level simulations for high-power RF antennas from full-wave electromagnetics to RF breakdown in a harsh environment (under vacuum as well as high pressure) for arbitrary 3D structures. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations can be performed in HFSS using the modal or terminal solution, the time-domain simulation then takes over to predict the onset of corona discharge and multipaction breakdown. The entire simulation can be executed in a single run for antenna analysis and the prediction of RF breakdown. The accuracy and robustness of the simulation have been guaranteed through the FEM unstructured mesh. Particle-in-cell simulation for tracking multipaction electrons in an unstructured FEM mesh is a key success. A comprehensive visualization user interface helps to explain the detailed physics.

articleTitle: Advanced Feature of a Circular Patch Realized as a Mode Specific Metaelement and Further Improvement by Ground Plane Engineering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work proposes an interesting idea by incorporating a mode filtering feature in a standard circular patch. This indeed extends a newly proposed concept from a recent publication by the same authors. It weakens TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> mode and hence reduces the cross-pol (XP) level over the H-plane leaving the diagonal plane (D-plane) values almost unaltered. A considerable improvement in the D-planes has been achieved by introducing a ground plane (GP) engineering. Three types of such configurations are proposed in S-band and their comparative results are presented. The final one achieves up to 8dB XP suppression in the D-plane along with nearly 9dB in the H-plane.

articleTitle: A Novel 3D Kriging-Aided Path Loss Model for Indoor Corridors Considering 28 GHz Measurements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: While fast-growing, telecommunication students, researchers and engineers have to consider innovative approaches to continuously address user demands and provide progressive involvement in technology development, as well as its usefulness and support capabilities for indoor consumers. Through an outstanding and specialized narrowband sounder, this research employed three-dimensional (3D) radio measurements in indoor corridors at 28 GHz, where complete coverage of 360-degree scans at each measured location were assessed. Based on the experimental measurements, when Kriging was included, path loss predictions were more accurate, reducing the RMSE by more than 50%, suggesting a reliable path loss model for planning and deployment of wireless communication systems in indoor corridors.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Flat Panal 4-Arm Curl Antenna Array for Emergency GEO Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A 1x3 array consist of 4-arm curl antenna elements is presented in this paper. This array is capable of beam steering to θ = 70° in all azimuth directions. The proposed 4-arm curl antenna array has been designed for L-Band (1.518 - 1.675 GHz) with a RHCP radiation to primarily target the Inmarsat BGAN. An HIS has been implemented to reduce the height of the antenna by > 50% over previous designs. Compared to a traditional patch antenna array system, the proposed 1x3 array system can reduce the number of feeding network components by 40%. This compact, low-cost array design will allow for an affordable mass deployable system for emergency services and other areas where communication in all locations is vital.

articleTitle: 2-D Sub-Diffraction Focusing with Concentric Circular Arrays in the Microwave Regime
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: To our knowledge, this work introduces the first method to generate a two dimensional (2-D) circularly symmetric sub-diffraction focus in the microwave regime with concentric circular arrays based on superoscillations. It is demonstrated that an arbitrarily small focus can be theoretically achieved by appropriately exciting two or more concentric circular arrays. Here, two concentric circular arrays are used as a proof-of-concept. Full-wave simulations show that by appropriately exciting the arrays, a focus with 50% the spatial width of the diffraction limited sinc pulse is achieved. The proposed methodology for breaking the diffraction limit in the microwave regime is expected to have important applications, such as, remote sensing and imaging.

articleTitle: Package Thickness Investigation of the U-Slot Patch Antenna for Beyond-5G Antenna-in-Package Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The U-slot patch antenna is explored as broadband antenna solution for a multi-layer interconnect antenna-in-package (AiP) technology for beyond-5G and 6G phased array applications. An initial design method is used to investigate the bandwidth response of the U-slot patch antenna for different package thicknesses. Simulation results show that a bandwidth larger than 30% can be achieved for package thicknesses between 0.06λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and 0.10λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> with relative permittivity of 2.81 at a center frequency of 28 GHz. A decreased package thickness below 0.06λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and restrictions on the line spacing of the package technology results in decreased bandwidth due to the increase of the Q-factor of the antenna and a smaller separation of the resonance peaks.

articleTitle: Estimation Technique of RCS using LSTM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: RCS measurement is a factor that helps design communication systems, antenna systems, and aircraft where scattering and reflection of electromagnetic waves are important. However, RCS measurements of time and cost are particularly related to large items such as aircraft and ships. Accordingly, this study provided a long-short-term memory (LSTM) strategy to solve the above difficulty and increase RCS measurement efficiency. RCS was evaluated using computer simulation, and after learning based on the observed data, RCS prediction data not measured within tolerance was calculated. The estimated data used RMSE to determine the error, and the estimated value indicates the result along the trend line of the observed value.

articleTitle: An Aperture-Sharing Antenna-in-Package exhibiting Endfire and Broadside Radiation Selection for Enhanced Beam Coverage of mmWave Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a new class of aperture-shared, phased array antenna-in-package (AiP) which exhibits endfire and broadside radiation while featuring compact profile. The shared aperture cavity slot antenna (SACSA) is proposed and demonstrated as single and 1×4 phased array architecture at mmWave spectrum and is exemplified for mmWave mobile devices. Experimental studies verify the SACSA can steer up to ± 45° beam scanning angle in both endfire and broadside modes while maintaining under -15 dB of cross-polarization and reflection coefficients less than – 10 dB at 28 GHz band.

articleTitle: Beam Shape Reconfigurability of Wide-Scan Focal Plane Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution we investigate the flexibility of wide-scan focal plane array antennas at mmWave. Based on measurement data, it is shown that highly directive beams can be generated, as well as wide beams with increased transmission power which are useful in stormy conditions where the rain attenuates the signal and the antenna tower twists and sways due to the wind. In addition, it is shown that sum and difference beams can be generated which can be used for radar sensing applications. The directivity is between 31.4dBi and 37.2dBi depending on the beam type, with a relative transmission power between 10.5dB and 18.1dB, compared to the maximum transmission power of a single antenna element.

articleTitle: Degenerated Integral Kernel Function Algorithm for Generating the Nested Representation of Stratton-Chu Formulas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the nested representation of Stratton-Chu formulas, which is generated by developing the degenerated integral kernel function algorithm, is applied to model the low frequency eddy current problems. With the nested approximation framework, only the low rank approximation matrices at leaf level in the far blocks of each submatrices need to be stored, while those at higher levels don’t. The transfer matrices are expressed in a closed form with the help of the Lagrange interpolations to ensure the good performance of the proposed nested kernel degeneration (NKD) algorithm. The accuracy and efficiency of the NKD algorithm are demonstrated and verified by conducting the numerical experiment.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Radio Transmission Through a Collisional Plasma via Antenna Impedance Matching
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Radio communication through a layer of plasma is a common requirement in several applications, particularly for high-speed vehicles traveling in the Earth’s atmosphere. Plasma sheaths generally act as a shield that blocks radio frequencies below the plasma frequency. We show that a finite collision rate in the plasma results in a higher degree of transmission for low frequency signals that would have otherwise been shielded. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that reflections at the air-plasma interface can be minimized by utilizing the near-field impedance properties of an antenna. The transmission coefficient through a homogenous plasma slab is evaluated analytically for an incident plane wave and for a small loop antenna that is placed close to the plasma. It is shown that at frequencies considerably below the plasma frequency, the fields from a loop antenna can transmit through the plasma several orders of magnitude more efficiently than a plane wave. The results suggest that an antenna’s near-field impedance properties can thus be exploited to enhance low frequency radio communications through collisional plasma sheaths.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of a Broadband High-Gain Omnidirectional Printed Antenna for Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wide-band high-gain omnidirectional printed antenna model, which can realize antenna multiplexing of multiple mobile communication bands, is proposed in this paper. The antenna is composed of two sub-arrays and two types of antenna structures. It operates from 1.46 GHz to 2.35 GHz, and the horizontal omnidirectional gain is 4.9 dBi and 3.6 dBi at 1.75 GHz and 1.8 GHz, which are two typical mobile communication frequencies of the internal digital cellular system (1710 MHz-1880 MHz). The out-of-roundness on the xoy plane is less than 3 dB. An equivalent current radiation model is used to analyze the radiation mechanism. The proposed antenna has the characteristics of wide bandwidth, high gain, and good omnidirectivity. It can be printed on a circuit board, and widely used in mobile communication equipment terminals.

articleTitle: Toward Hyper-Compact Rotman Lenses: A Meta-Transmission Line Wave-space Design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a novel approach for miniaturization of Rotman lenses used for versatile beamforming applications in satellite, radar, and unmanned aerial vehicle systems. Since these systems usually operate at very-/ultra-high frequencies (VHF/UHF), conventional techniques for Rotman lens design become impractical as they lead to bulky solutions ( > 5 − 6 λ long). To address this challenge, herein, we propose a modified lumped element transmission line (TL) model by introducing a mutual inductance term between the first nearest neighbors. Such a TL called the meta-transmission line can be used to extend the linearity of the dispersion diagram and reduce the overall size of the Rotman lens. A proof-of-concept 1D meta-TL is designed and analyzed to demonstrate the improvement in the linearity of the dispersion diagram by ~ 36%.

articleTitle: Real World Considerations for Into-Body Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We previously proposed the Bio-Matched Antenna (BMA), a new class of broadband, high gain antennas for into-body radiation with improved transmission through biological tissues. BMAs have many desirable characteristics for telemetry, imaging, and sensing applications, but the design exhibits limitations for real-world implementation. Notably, fabrication is time-consuming and tedious, the materials are unstable over time (e.g., performance of the antenna was found to significantly degrade after Day 1 of fabrication), and the connector is not reliable. In this paper, we determine the fundamental limitations with BMAs and propose possible solutions to address them. The discussions in this paper will facilitate robust, stable into-body design and fabrication for real-world applications in the future.

articleTitle: Measurement of Electromagnetic Property Parameters of Penetrable Materials Based on Partially-Filled Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An experimental device based on a rectangular waveguide is proposed to measure electromagnetic (EM) property parameters of lossy penetrable materials. The frequency band of measurement is 8.2 – 12.5 GHz and the parameters like effective dielectric constant and loss tangent can be measured through a mode-matching method and numerical analysis with a partially-filled waveguide. With the obtained mode and field distribution in the filled materials, the EM property parameters of the material can be inverted. Measurement simulations for typical materials show that the designed device can effectively measure the EM property parameters of penetrable materials and the measurement error of 0.2% can be achieved.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancing Compact GRIN Lens
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: GRadient INdex (GRIN) lenses are spatially inhomogeneous dielectric lenses that can significantly improve the gain of an antenna. However, traditional lens designs are too bulky to be used on aircraft or in space applications especially for frequencies at or below L-band. To overcome these size limitations, an additively manufactured ceramic compact GRIN lens with a diameter of 1.3 wavelengths at the smallest frequency of interest was fabricated and demonstrates over 4 dB gain improvement compared to the no lens case. This significant improvement is possible because of the coherent interaction of the radiation through the inside and, importantly, around the outside of the GRIN lens.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave High Gain Hybrid ME-DRD Antenna Fed by PRGW Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a high gain and wideband magneto-electric dielectric-resonator dipole antenna operating at millimeter-wave (mm-wave) bands around 30 GHz. The proposed antenna is implemented by combining two multi-resonant modes, namely, a magneto-electric (ME) dipole and stacked dielectric resonator dipole (DRD) antennas fed by printed ridge gap waveguide technology (PRGW) to present a wideband antenna. In addition, a perforated dielectric substrate lens located in the broadside direction of the antenna as a gain enhancement technique is used to increase the gain by an average of 3 dB over the entire operating bandwidth. The simulated results demonstrate a reflection coefficient better than −14 dB of 42.4% over 26–40 GHz, while the realized gain of the designed ME-DRA antenna is more than 9 dBi over the frequency band with a peak gain of 13.5 dBi at 37.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Traveling-Wave Slotted Array Antenna Based on SIW at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, based on substrate integrated wave-guide (SIW), a 2×10 slotted waveguide antenna with six split ring resonators (SSR) is designed and simulated at Ka-Band to validate the slotted antenna. A series of 2×10 longitudinal slots etched on the top layer of SIW are employed as radiating elements at the Ku-band, while the SSRs etched on the bottom layer of the SIW are employed to filet electromagnetic wave. A one-to-two Wilkinson power divider feeds the antenna, which simplifies and compacts this antenna structure. The simulated results show that the bandwidth of the designed antenna for voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) ＜2 is 2.5GHz at the center frequency of 32 GHz, and the side-lobe level is controlled lower than -18dB, and the realized gain is better than 14dBi. Due to its compact size, low side-lobe level and easy manufacturing, this proposed antenna may be applied to a Ka-band radar and communication system.

articleTitle: Effects of Array Interpolation on DOA Estimation with OMP
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Reconstruction of compressively sampled (CS) signals can be accomplished using Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP). The same technique can be used to estimate the arrival angles of signals impinging on an antenna array. The array can be uniform, nonuniform, linear, or circular. Array interpolation has long been used as a technique that transforms a non-uniformly spaced array (circular or linear) into a uniformly spaced linear array thus permitting DOA estimation using methods such as the MUSIC algorithm. The question addressed in this paper is whether array interpolation enhances the performance of DOA estimation when using CS-based techniques such as OMP. This paper explores scenarios involving non-uniform circular or linear arrays and assuming signals are correlated or uncorrelated.

articleTitle: A MIMO Antenna Array with an Integrated Bandstop Filter at W Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) RADAR provides the advantage of streaming multiple datasets at a time. Concurrently, operating such a system at millimeter-wave (mm-wave) implies a significant reduction in the size of RF circuitry. A major drawback is mutual coupling between antenna elements. In this paper, we present a mm-wave MIMO system operating at 78GHz with integrated bandstop filter (BSF) to improve isolation between antenna elements. Simulations show that the addition of the filter leads to a 27dB reduction in mutual coupling without impacting the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Deep Learning based Power Delay Profile Trend Generation: A 60 GHz Intra-Vehicle Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this article we have utilized deep learning (DL) for channel sounding application in the millimeter wave (mmWave) band. Using data from a channel sounding campaign for studying intra-vehicle wireless channels operating over the 55-65 GHz mmWave band, we have trained an artificial neural network (ANN) model, which is used to simulate power-delay-profile (PDP) trends. The required simulation inputs form a minimal set, only comprising the frequency points, the transmitter-receiver distance and the presence of passengers inside car. The simulated PDP trend shows good match with the measured PDP and can be used for constructing tapped-delay-line (TDL) based channel models.

articleTitle: Design and Manufacturing of a Compact and Broadband DWG Transition-Antenna using 3D Printing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, a transition-antenna is introduced, which enables the symmetric radiation of dielectric waveguides in the mmWave range. Design considerations as well as the split-block manufacturing technique that utilizes 3D printing and a two step metalization process are presented. Finally, simulation and measurement results, which reveal the component’s performance, are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Wideband Monocone with Integrated Coaxial Bandpass Filter for UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Wideband monocone antenna integrated with a curved coaxial bandpass filter and operating from around 1 to 5.5 GHz is discussed. The RF ground is modified to represent a conical skirt. To reduce the volume, the bandpass filter recta-coaxial line used for feeding the antenna is curved within the volume of the grounding. The proposed RF front-end is designed for monolithic fabrication using additive techniques and seamless integration at the back end of unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Design of Modulated Dielectric Metasurfaces for Antenna Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Metasurfaces can be engineered to taper the electromagnetic fields and realize radiated beams. In this paper, we present an optimization framework to design metasurfaces comprising a thickness-modulated dielectric layer above a ground plane. By taking into account all mutual coupling effects, farfield radiation patterns with high accuracy can be obtained. An example of dual-beam generation with an embedded source is demonstrated showing the potential of beamforming with lowloss and low-profile dielectric metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Resonance Behavior of a Conducting Wire Object Above a Halfspace
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Successful extraction of the resonant modes embedded in the transient target signature is vital to resonance-based radar target recognition. For targets in free space, although these resonant modes are theoretically aspect independent, the corresponding residues are known to be aspect dependent. When the target is located above a halfspace, the interface will electromagnetically interact with the target and alter the residue. Within the context of resonance-based target recognition, the influence from an interface to the residues, to the best of our knowledge, has not been well studied. In this paper, we study this problem through a wire target. Our results show that the residues of the mode follow a similar behavior as the dielectric properties of the halfspace vary.

articleTitle: A Scalar Impedance Surface Antenna for Generating Focusing Radial Vortex Beam
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This letter presents a low-profile broadband scalar impedance surface antenna to achieve focusing radial orbital angular momentum (OAM) waves at the 17GHz. A good surface impedance of the 3x3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> square unit is obtained at the operating frequency. The antenna is designed using the holographic method with the square unit to realize a focused radial scalar vortex beam of +1 and +2 OAM mode, and the radial vortex beam is focused near z=100 mm. The whole size of the surface antenna is 117x117 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna satisfies |S11|<-10dB at 14.1-21.9 GHz. Theoretical, simulated results are presented.

articleTitle: Ray Tracing Prediction of Path Loss for 5G Wireless Communications within Hospital Patient Room
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Millimeter (mm)-waves band has become a promising option for fifth-generation (5G) near-infinite data rate and ultra-low latency communications. Despite all recent achievements, engineers are still facing technical challenges for the assessment of indoor propagation mechanisms at extremely short wavelengths. In this paper, a mathematical-based deterministic Ray-Tracing Model (RTM) has been derived for the prediction of Path Loss (PL) within a hospital patient room while ensuring users freedom of mobility. Directional, and omnidirectional radiation patterns have been considered at both transmitting and receiving ends of the channel, respectively. For the RTM validation, broadband propagation measurements have been conducted under Line-Of-Sight (LOS) condition. The predicted and measured channel responses are found to be in a good match for all R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf> positions throughout the room. Furthermore, both predicted and measured path loss exponents (n) are found to be about 1.55. The predicted n agrees with the values reported in the literature.

articleTitle: An Improved Direction of Arrival Technique Based on Nullforming and Steering Theory
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new technique is introduced for finding direction of arrival (DoA) of an incident signal based on the nullforming and steering theory. On the contrary to the operation of beamforming, the proposed method creates a deep and precise null that is then steered toward all the possible directions to estimate the minimum power that indicates the direction of the incident signal. Additionally, this new method can outperform conventional beamforming as the resulted null is much narrower than conventional beams. The proposed null-forming and steering theory has been proven successfully by both analytical and simulation validation using MATLAB Simulink model and an integrated software defined radio USRP N200.

articleTitle: Sub-Millimeter Melanoma Skin Cancer Detection: Differentiating Between Healthy and Malignant Tissues Based on Local Specific Absorption Rate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the local specific absorption rate (SAR) of ultra-wideband millimeter-wave (mm-wave) double-ridge open-ended waveguide antennas (OEWA) for early-stage skin cancer detection. Specifically, an OEWA with a 15– 40-GHz bandwidth is designed and fabricated. The proposed antenna demonstrates |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|<–10 dB and stable and symmetric radiation patterns across 15–40 GHz with aperture sizes of 9.47×5.79 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A 3D realistic biological model consisting of skin, subcutaneous fat, and muscle is developed to evaluate the SAR in healthy and malignant lesions. The permittivity of the cancerous tissue was modeled according to a Debye function that took into account the higher water content of this tissue with respect to healthy skin.

articleTitle: Compact UWB Cellular Antenna Integrated Into Vehicle Spoiler
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A common way of integrating high frequency antennas into an automotive vehicle is a shark-fin module on the roof of the vehicle. However, increasing the size of shark-fin modules in order to accommodate a growing number of wireless communication services is undesirable from both aesthetic and aerodynamic performance points of view. The antenna integration will become more challenging as the trend of integrating more antennas and sensors continues with the emergence of autonomous vehicles. This paper proposes to integrate the antennas inside a spoiler of a vehicle to address the integration challenge and presents an integration of a cellular antenna in a rear spoiler of a vehicle. The proposed ultra wide-band (UWB) antenna operates from 617 MHz to 5 GHz supporting most of cellular bands including sub-6 GHz 5G. The antenna has a compact size of 0.14λ × 0.13λ × 0.04λ at the lowest operating frequency. The simulated results agree well with the measured results.

articleTitle: 2.4/5 GHz Dual-Band Multilayer Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel antenna design to realize high antenna gain in dual bands (2.4/5 GHz) by arraying slot antenna elements and a multilayer structure. A 5 GHz slot array antenna is placed on the top metal, and the floating metal is attached on the backside to realize the one-sided directional radiation. A 2.4 GHz slot array antenna is placed on the upper side of the 5 GHz antenna. The RF signal is fed into each antenna element with the same power and phase branched coplanar waveguides (CPW). The antenna was fabricated on FR-4 substrate with top and bottom metals. The final dual-band antenna size was 161 mm x 116 mm x 28.2 mm. The measured +z-axis directional gain was 11.1 dBi at 2.50 GHz and 12.8 dBi at 5.57 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a 10-Port MIMO Antenna for 5G/WiFi Indoor Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A 10-port wide-band cavity-backed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna with decagonal shape is presented for 5G/WiFi indoor base stations applications. For the design of the antenna a methodology based on sector unit cells is employed dividing the whole design in 10 equivalent sectors and only analyzing two cells for the prediction of the whole design performance. The proposed antenna has a total size of π×228.85<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>×37.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (π×1.63<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>×0.49λ, at central frequency f=f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>=3.9 GHz). The antenna is composed by 10 independent ports with 15 dB of minimum isolation and an impedance bandwidth (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> < −10 dB) of 130% (1.37-6.5 GHz). Simulated results show unidirectional radiation pattern, a total efficiency higher than 86% and low envelope correlation coefficient (ECC).

articleTitle: Towards Wearable Wireless Power Harvesting using Clothing-Integrated Beamforming Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: High-gain wide-beam off-body wearable antennas are essential for efficient wearable RF energy harvesting (RFEH). Here, we report a 5.8-GHz reflector-backed Yagi-inspired antenna with over 2 dB gain and efficiency improvement over a conventional Yagi. Using the reflector, the end-fire patterns are re-directed in the broadside off-body direction while maintaining a simulated 76% efficiency. To demonstrate the feasibility of high-gain RFEH, a beam-forming Rotman lens is designed with a relatively low insertion loss based on conventional fabrics with conductive surfaces designed to be implemented via the automated embroidery of conductive threads. This work is a stepping stone to clothing-integrated low-profile beamforming for sub-6 GHz 5G/6G applications.

articleTitle: Reflection-less Lens Based on Miniaturized-Element Frequency Selective Surfaces at Millimeter-Wave Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A reflection-less lens antenna based on miniaturized element frequency selective surfaces (MEFSS) arranged in a quasi-periodic structure is investigated to provide not only a collimated beam but also a very low reflection towards its feed. This antenna is a key component in a sensitive, high resolution instrumentation polarimetric radar designed for phenomenological radar studies of traffic scenes in the 77 GHz band. The incident wave phase correction is accomplished locally on the surface of the lens through a spatial filter that makes use of only shunt elements. To achieve 0-360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> phase shift, the lens includes three MEFSS layers using gold deposited on top, bottom, and in the middle of two glass wafers. As an air-gap between the glass wafers can affect the performance significantly, very smooth glass wafers are fused in a high temperature furnace after patterning the MEFSS layers with careful alignment. The lens has F/D~2 and is fed by a dual-polarized horn antenna with 7 dB field drop at the edges.

articleTitle: Training of Deep Neural Networks With up to 10 Million Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We summarize the results of using deep neural network for modeling the forward gain of Yagi-Uda antenna. The training datasets of antenna are generated using custom highly parallelized method of moments code. The used datasets have up to 10 million antenna samples generated randomly over the design space. The training is done using TensorFlow library.

articleTitle: Conductive Fabric-Based Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are positioned to be a key enabling technology for next-generation wireless systems. However, for RIS to become pervasive in future systems will require new technologies to unobtrusively integrate them in everyday objects (e.g., carpets, drapes, upholstery) rather than exclusive use of printed circuit boards (PCBs). In this paper, we presented a proof of concept prototype of a fabric-based RIS for internet of thing (IoT) applications. The proposed RIS is a two-dimensional surface with 6 × 9 conductive fabric elements placed on a non-conductive fabric to operate at 2.4 GHz. Each element acts as a radio frequency (RF) switch to either let the signal through (i.e., "lens") or reflect it (i.e., "mirror") to, for example, enable a legitimate link or impair an eavesdropping link. This concept of the RIS is validated in an indoor test, where the proposed fabric RIS prototype provides a 16 dB decrease in received power when the elements in adjacent columns are electrically connected to reflect the incident waves as compared to the case where the elements are electrically isolated to allow signal transmission.

articleTitle: Calderón Preconditioners for the TD-EFIE discretized with Convolution Quadratures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work focuses on the preconditioning and DC stabilization of the time domain electric field integral equation discretized in time with the convolution quadrature method. The standard formulation of the equation suffers from severe ill- conditioning for large time steps and refined meshes, in addition to DC instabilities plaguing standard solutions for late time steps. This work addresses all these issues by preconditioning the TD- EFIE operator matrices with a Calderon approach. Numerical results will corroborate the theory, showing the practical relevance of the proposed advancements.

articleTitle: A Novel Cavity Resonator with TM010 Mode and 8.5-GHz Frequency for Complex Permittivity Measurement
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Perturbation method is one of main methods to measure the complex permittivity of materials since the method is easy and simple to implement. In this paper, we propose a novel design of cavity resonator with a TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">010</inf> mode at the 8.5-GHz frequency based on the perturbation method. Using the cavity, we perform a series of measurement simulations for typical low-loss materials based on the well-known HFSS. The relative errors of measured values for the real part and loss tangent of permittivity are within 0.8% and 8.0%, respectively. The measured results by simulations validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the cavity method.

articleTitle: Numerical modelling of video transmission range for an unmanned aerial vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an approach to compute the range and data rate of video signals from an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) is presented. The UAV is flown on a pre-defined flight path in an urban environment and the throughput of the video signals is computed using a Dominant Path Model. A truncated patch antenna operating at 5.8 GHz with a bandwidth of 128 MHz is designed and integrated with the UAV to transmit the video signals to the base station. The effects of the UAV structure on the antenna characteristics are presented along with an example of virtual flight test computation that achieves a minimum throughput of 28 mbps over a specific area.

articleTitle: A Stable Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain Method for Simulation of Thin Conductive Layers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A conductive layer that is much thinner than the skin depth is often incorporated into electromagnetic solvers as a resistive boundary condition (RBC) to avoid fine meshes (and consequently small time steps for time-domain methods). When the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method, which relies on an explicit Runge-Kutta (RK) scheme for time integration, is used in a simulation involving an RBC surface with high conductivity, the solution becomes unstable. In this work, to circumvent this bottleneck, a locally-implicit time marching scheme is developed. The proposed method uses implicit Euler backward and explicit Euler forward schemes to discretize the time derivatives in local DG equations associated with the elements that "touch" and do not "touch" the RBC surface, respectively. This yields a locally-implicit Euler (LIME) time marching scheme that maintains its stability in the presence of a highly conductive layer. Indeed, numerical results demonstrate that LIME-DGTD is more stable than RK-DGTD for a transmission problem involving a thin metal sheet.
