articleTitle: Heart Rate Extraction of Doppler Radar Systems Using Grey Wolf Optimization for Multiple Targets
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel algorithm is presented for heart rate extraction under multi-target environments using a single antenna pair. A grey wolf optimization (GWO) algorithm is utilized to estimate the frequency component of breathing as well as breathing harmonics to reconstruct the heartbeat signals. Then, empirical mode decomposition is introduced to cancel the frequency components of respiration and clutters by selecting an intrinsic mode function. While measuring the two people case, there are error rates of 4.92% and 3.11% respectively.

articleTitle: On the Implementation of Fourier Neural Operator in Solving Electromagentics Problems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In the paper, we launch Fourier Neural Operators (FNOs) to solve the 2D electrostatic Poisson equation. FNOs are data-driven models that directly learn the mapping from parametric dependence to the solution from the training dataset with finite difference method (FDM) simulations. Thus they learn an entire family of Poisson equations, in contrast to classical methods which solve one instance of the equation. We apply a neural network with FNOs to predict the electric potential with different permittivity distribution in 2D models. The neural network is tested by 2D Poisson equations in a domain with a line source and PECs. The neural network with FNOs shows state-of-the-art accuracy and a speedup factor of over 1000 compared to traditional FDM, which demonstrates its great future potential in solving time-variant Maxwell equations.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Augmentation of Wideband Spectrum Sensors for Polarimetry
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A cascaded neural network architecture is discussed to classify the polarization of a signal that is incident on a dual-polarized log periodic antenna. The antenna system is designed for spectrum sensing but retrofitted to add polarimetry through the use of machine learning. The cross-polarized contamination in the system causes raw estimation to barely exceed 13% classification accuracy, as opposed to 25% accuracy with blind guessing. However, the use of machine learning enables over 90% accuracy when classifying. Three neural networks are deployed. The first separates linear from circular, followed by specialized networks to discriminate between horizontal and vertical as well as left- and right-hand circular polarizations.

articleTitle: Fast Solution of Volume Integral Equations with Dielectric-Magnetic Media
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Some materials like mineral substances are both dielectric and magnetic and also may be fully inhomogeneous in nature, and full volume integral equations (VIEs) are needed to describe their interaction with electromagnetic (EM) wave in the integral equation approach. When the problem is large, a fast algorithm is needed to accelerate the solution of VIEs. To simplify and speed up numerical solutions, the Nyström method is used to discretize the VIEs and then the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is incorporated to accelerate. A numerical example is provided to demonstrate the approach and good results have been achieved.

articleTitle: Reducing the Computational Expense of Uncertainty Quantification in Computational Electromagnetics: A Goal-Oriented Perspective
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We summarize several challenges in uncertainty quantification involving simulations of electromagnetic scattering. While the finite element method (FEM) provides an excellent means of producing approximate solutions to partial differential equations (PDEs), the computational expense mandated by full model solves complicates the application of the standard Monte Carlo method, which converges slowly, albeit independently of the dimension of the parameter space (i.e., the number of uncertain variables). As a result, alternative techniques must be employed to quantify uncertain without incurring inordinate computational costs, both in time and computing power. We summarize one such approach based on the higher order parameter sampling (HOPS) method, which constructs a deterministic response that may be applied for accelerating uncertainty quantification, with the underlying goal-oriented framework supported by applications in error estimation and adaptive refinement that may precede objectives in uncertainty quantification.

articleTitle: Proposal of an Array Antenna with Radially Arranged Linear Arrays and its Equivalence to an Aperture Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An array antenna that composed of linear arrays in radial arrangement is proposed in this paper. Its equivalence to an aperture antenna is deduced so that the excitation of the linear array elements is designed to obtain a desired radiation pattern. Its validity is shown by simulation, and the radiation pattern is well illustrated in a two-dimensional diagram of contour.

articleTitle: Multiplicative Frequency Diverse Image Formation in Active Incoherent Millimeter-Wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Active incoherent millimeter-wave imaging systems reduce the bandwidth requirements of passive systems by increasing the signal-to-noise ratio using incoherent signal illumination and therefore mitigating high sensitivity requirements on the receiver. As a result, active incoherent millimeter-wave imaging systems can operate with much narrower instantaneous bandwidths than passive imaging systems. However, narrow bandwidths can pose problems in terms of target interference that can impact image formation. In this work, we present a frequency diverse active incoherent millimeter-wave imaging array that uses a frequency hopping scheme to control the electromagnetic radiation. By changing the frequency, wavelength-dependent interference issues are reduced. We employ a multiplicative processing approach that reconstructs images at each frequency and multiplies the reconstructed images. The concept is demonstrated using an active incoherent millimeter-wave imager operating with a signal bandwidth of 50 MHz at 1-GHz frequency steps between 36-40 GHz. We demonstrate reconstruction of a reflecting object with multiple scattering points, showing that the multiplicative frequency diverse approach obtains better images than individual frequency images.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Design of Printed Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a focused and comprehensive method to predict the resonant frequency of a patch antenna using machine learning. By using a dataset with 20480 full-wave simulated samples, first, a binary classification model could provide 97.9% accuracy on the question of whether the specific antenna configuration has valid resonance or not, then a regression model could predict the resonant frequency with accuracy score of 0.926. Taking the well-trained models, designers can predict the antenna performance based on these configurations without additional simulation in the frequency band from 3 to 15 GHz, which saves a lot of time and computational resources in the antenna optimization process.

articleTitle: 8x8 Millimeter-Wave Series-Fed Patch Antenna Array for Anti-collision Automotive Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, 8x8 series-fed patch antenna arrays for automotive radar phased arrays at 77 GHz are introduced. The proposed planar array antenna is composed of eight patch antennas with a series feed configuration, which are fed by a 1-to-8 feeding network. The designed array configurations operate over an impedance bandwidth of 75-80 GHz. All simulations are carried out using the CST Microwave Studio™ full-wave software program, and the validation of the reflection coefficient is performed with Ansys HFSS. The developed arrays exhibit a directive broadside radiation pattern with a high gain of more than 20 dBi at 77 GHz. The proposed array's performance is suitable for phased array anti-collision automotive radar applications at 77 GHz.

articleTitle: Efficiency Improvements in Compressing H2 Matrices for Translationally Invariant Kernels
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> matrices provide efficient representations for compressible kernels such as those encountered in low-frequency electromagnetic modeling applications. It has recently been observed that H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> matrices obtained using matrix sampling techniques can be rendered translationally invariant using an iterative procedure. For some applications the computational costs associated with the previously reported procedure are high. This presentation will report strategies to reduce these costs for the kernels encountered in low-frequency electromagnetic modeling applications.

articleTitle: A New Refinement-Free Preconditioner for the Symmetric Formulation in Electroencephalography
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Widely employed for the accurate solution of the electroencephalography forward problem, the symmetric formulation gives rise to a first kind, ill-conditioned operator illsuited for complex modelling scenarios. This work presents a novel preconditioning strategy based on an accurate spectral analysis of the operators involved which, differently from other Calderón-based approaches, does not necessitate the barycentric refinement of the primal mesh (i.e., no dual matrix is required). The discretization of the new formulation gives rise to a well-conditioned, symmetric, positive-definite system matrix, which can be efficiently solved via fast iterative techniques. Numerical results for both canonical and realistic head models validate the effectiveness of the proposed formulation.

articleTitle: Compact Wide-band Gysel Power Divider
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A compact and wideband Gysel power divider is proposed in this study. The design steps on a widely available low-cost FR-4 substrate are presented. The design is simulated with a Method-of-Moments based 2.5D EM simulator and verified with measurement results. The power divider supports an operating bandwidth of 1.5 GHz between 1.94 GHz and 3.44 GHz. The measurements show an insertion loss of 4.5 dB and return loss better than 15 dB which agrees with simulations. The fabricated circuit has at least three-fold wider bandwidth (with %56 fractional bandwidth) and four-fold smaller size (3.6 cm x 4.3 cm) than similar designs in the recent literature.

articleTitle: A compact three-way Wilkinson divider with reduced central line length
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper a compact three-way Wilkinson divider is attained by artificially shortening the central quarter wavelength line by resorting to reactive loading. As opposed to a conventional designs, with a meandered central line, the proposed design is much shorter, hence allowing a tighter integration.Design is carried out at 2.45 GHz, on a commercial FR408 substrate, characterization of the prototype shows a very good behavior with return loss and isolation better than 10 dB over a 60% band, with a device which is almost 30% shorter than a standard three-way divider.

articleTitle: UTC Photodiode Model for mmWave Photonic Integrated Antennas at 5G Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The equivalent circuit of two UTC photodiodes (UTC-PDs) are modelled using microwave and semiconductor-device simulations. The models are achieved without the need to measure the S-parameters of a photodiode (PD). Hence, low-cost and accurate models are generated, from which PD S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf> are obtained in the frequency range from 1 to 141 GHz. Thanks to the accurate PDs’ models, a matching network between the PDs and millimeter-wave circuits can be designed.

articleTitle: New Fourier Transform Approach to the Synthesis of Shaped Patterns by Linear Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new Fourier Transform (NFT) approach is developed for the synthesis of shaped patterns radiated by linear antenna arrays. The proposed method exploits in an innovative way the FT relation between the source distribution and the radiated pattern. Precisely, the finite dimension of real sources is firstly taken into account by using the sampling theorem to approximate the desired pattern as a band-limited function. It is this step that allows one to obtain an important performance improvement. Then, a continuous source is evaluated from the approximate desired pattern to finally obtain the element excitations. Numerical examples validate the method.

articleTitle: Wide-Band, Multi-Beam, High Isolation, Multi-Mode Radial Vivaldi Antenna for Direction Finding
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and experimental verification of a low-cost, wideband, multi-mode antenna intended as a reflector feed for direction finding applications. The design consists of dual concentric radial arrays of interleaved Vivaldi elements, with a tilt and orientation optimized for use in an Axially Displaced Ellipse (ADE) dual-reflector antenna system. The central main array provides four wide-band, high efficiency beams (sum and difference right and left-handed polarizations), whereas the outer array provides an isolated, second set of independent beams. An advantage of the radial array is that it can be optimized to achieve a wide range of near-constant directivity and beamwidth values over a wide bandwidth, permitting its use as a feed to a reflector system where a wide range of F/D values can be accommodated. The linearly polarized Vivaldi elements are optimized to cover Ka-band, and they provide a very high frontend efficiency. The optimized feed is then integrated into a 70cm ADE deployable mesh reflector, where good agreement between modeled to measured primary feed and secondary patterns are reported.

articleTitle: Wideband Decoupling for Bandwidth Enhanced Dielectric Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wideband decoupling method for dielectric patch (DP) antenna (DPA) is proposed in this paper. The air tunnel can not only incorporate TM10 and antiphase TM20 modes to expand the antenna bandwidth, but also make the port-to-port isolation (S21) flat in broadband. Furthermore, the two pairs of metal strips on the DPA help to achieve a balance between the mutual capacitive and inductive coupling, further improving wideband isolation. Meanwhile, it is worth noting that the radiation pattern can be stabilized during the decoupling process. Finally, the simulation result exhibits that the impedance bandwidth is 18.4% (4.97GHz-5.98GHz) and the in-band isolation is enhanced to more than 20dB.

articleTitle: A hybrid CNN-NGBoost model for probabilistic image-driven path loss prediction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We propose a hybrid model for probabilistic path loss prediction, based on the footprint of the urban built-up area. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is being deployed in order to extract information regarding the built-up area in the form of a feature vector. The extracted features are then processed from a Natural Gradient Boosting (NGBoost) regressor, who is inherently capable of performing probabilistic prediction. That is, along with point estimations of the received path loss value, the CNN-NGBoost model additionally calculates the prediction interval which covers a user-defined percentage of the prediction distribution. The proposed model can therefore assist network engineers in calculating the risk of their decisions about network coverage.

articleTitle: Design of a High Gain Broadband Balanced Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna with 3D Dielectric Lens
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A high gain and broadband Balanced Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna (BAVA) was designed in conjunction with a 3D dielectric lens. The antenna exhibits a broad bandwidth of 4.5 GHz to over 55 GHz, covering the 5G New Radio (5G–NR) bands starting from n79 (4.7 GHz) of Frequency Range 1 (FR1) to n262 (47GHz) of Frequency Range 2 (FR2). Adding a 3D teardrop-shaped dielectric lens at the aperture of the BAVA helps facilitate an ever-increasing gain profile with increasing frequency. Between 4.5 GHz and 55 GHz, the inclusion of the lens resulted in a steady increase in gain values from 7 dBi to 24 dBi. This is a significant improvement compared to the 3.5 dBi to 11.67 dBi gain range of the BAVA without lens.

articleTitle: The Sphere as a Reference in Direction Finding Antenna Development Using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The feasibility of the sphere as an idealized multi-mode multi-port direction finding antenna is investigated. Constraints for port implementations on the sphere are derived from group theory, based on the symmetry properties of the sphere. An example excitation setup is compared to a similar one on a cube. It is found that a spherical antenna has the potential to treat different polarizations equally.

articleTitle: All-Metal Patch Circular Polarized Fan-Beam Antennas for Potential Europa Lander
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: All metal patch circularly polarized X-band antennas are under development at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory for a potential Europa Lander. The dual-band antenna is proposed to be used as a secondary telecommunication antenna and the single band antenna is proposed to be used as a communication antenna for the Deorbit, Descent, and Landing (DDL) stage. Both the antennas would establish a Direct-to-Earth (DTE) link without relying on an Orbiter. Antenna arrays with fan-beam radiation have been designed for wide beam circular polarization for longer coverage while surviving the harsh environmental conditions at Europa, including, cryogenic temperature, high radiation and electrostatic discharge (ESD) levels.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Measurement of LT-GaAs Photoconductive THz Broadband Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents fabrication and experimental measurements of broadband terahertz (THz) photoconductive antennas (PCAs), based on the conventional low temperature gallium arsenide (LT-GaAs) material. Various antenna electrode geometries, that were previously designed through computer simulations, are fabricated using the electron beam lithography (EBL). The generated time domain pulse is measured using a time domain spectroscopy system (TDS). The bandwidth of each emitting device is obtained using the fast Fourier transform of the generated electric field pulse.

articleTitle: Polarization Agility Using A Microfluidically Reconfigurable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a microfluidically reconfigurable metasurface for polarization switching. A 5 × 5 unit cells metasurface array acts as a superstrate layer on the top of a circularly polarized antenna. The square split ring resonator with cross-shaped microfluidic channels can be reconfigured by pneumatically injecting or removing liquid metal alloy into 3D printed channels in two orthogonal directions. The incoming circular polarized (CP) wave can be either converted into a linearly polarized (LP) wave or transmitted without any effect as a CP wave. The simulated return loss plots for CP-CP and CP-LP conversion exhibit good impedance matching from 4.5 – 4.9 GHz, which represents a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 8.5%. The far-field realized peak gain for both states remains greater than 6 dBi. The common bandwidth of CP-CP and CP-LP conversion is 4.5 –4.7 GHz resulting in FBW of 4.3%. The proposed metasurface antenna can be used in MIMO systems and biomedical applications to reduce polarization mismatches and multipath fading.

articleTitle: A Thin Paper UHF Antenna on Nanocelloluse Based Substrate for Battery-free Geolocation Tags
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and characterisation of an antenna on a paper-based substrate. The antenna is designed on a nanocellulose foil optimised with a highly conductive ink based on silver nanoparticles. The electrical and dielectric properties of the materials were characterised prior to the antenna simulation. The antenna is designed to operate at the ISM 868 MHz frequency band and has a maximum gain of +1.7 dBi. Its development is part of the first step in the implementation of a flexible battery-free geolocation tag, remotely powered by UHF Energy sources in the European RFID spectrum between 865.6 MHz and 867.6 MHz. An accurate characterisation procedure was carried out and the results show good agreement with the simulations.

articleTitle: Antenna Array Optimization via Deep Learning For Breast Cancer Microwave Hyperthermia Application: Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Microwave hyperthermia (MH) requires the effective calibration of the antenna for selective focusing of the microwave energy at the target region with a nominal effect on the surrounding tissue. Many different antenna calibration methods such as optimization techniques and lookup tables have been proposed. In this paper, we present the preliminary results of a CNN based phase and power optimization approach. To create the necessary dataset, we used the superposition method to combine the information from the individual antennas. The results of the CNN model are compared with lookup table results. The proposed approach is promising as it shows less hot spots in heating potential distributions.

articleTitle: A High-efficiency Polarization Conversion Cell for Generating Broadband Vortex Beams
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, it is proposed a ultra-wideband polarization conversion cell for metasurface which is based on the concept of Pancharatnam-Berry(PB) phase. By optimizing the parameters of the cell, a near-ideal 180 reflection phase difference is obtained, which can achieve high-efficiency co-polarization conversion in 9.26GHz-19.84GHz, and the polarization conversion efficiency of this cell is as high as 0.98. Based on the same principle, the unit reflection phase is arranged, and the high purity vortex beam metasurface in the band that listed above is designed, which proves the effectiveness of the proposed cell.

articleTitle: Battery-free Mechanically-Tunable Wireless Sensors for Railroad Track Ballast Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a battery-free, mechanically tunable and narrowband wireless sensor that can be used to detect railroad track ballast fault conditions, along with an interrogator. The sensor consists of receive (operating at f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) and transmit (operating at 2f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) antennas and a diode for frequency doubling. The experimental and simulated results reveal that the sensor operates with high conversion efficiency at micro-Watt power levels. This performance indicates that the sensor can work effectively if it is buried under the railroad track for fault detection. Frequency tunability is achieved by adjusting dielectric loading on input and output matching networks.

articleTitle: Fast Source Reconstruction of Large Reflector Antennas for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a method for diagnostics of large reflector antennas for space applications is presented. By using a Calderón projection together with a Higher-Order (HO) Method of Moments (MoM) discretization, the inverse electromagnetic scattering problem is solved in an efficient manner, allowing for diagnostics based on the equivalent currents. This method is referred to as the Calderón method and is shown to be well suited for use in antenna diagnostics applications. Two reflector antenna cases have been analysed and significant reductions in computation time and memory allocation requirements are observed in comparison to other state-of-the-art solvers.

articleTitle: A Novel FSS Absorber for 5 GHz WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This article investigates the design of a cascade absorber FSS based on open trapezoid rings geometry. Numerical analysis was performed using Ansys Electronics Desktop, thus, an FSS with a conductive and resistive layer arranged in a cascade was designed in order to verify the effectiveness of the structure for 5 GHz WLAN applications. An absorption up to 90% and an angular stability up to 40° were achieved with the proposed design.

articleTitle: Characterization and Sensing of Milk Fat% in the Low GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper studies the dielectric properties of commercially available milk products of varying butterfat 0.1 – 3.25% in the low spectrum 1 – 10 GHz using an open-ended coaxial probe kit. Extracted properties have indicated an appreciably dielectric contrast between tested milks with a negative linear relationship between the dispersive complex permittivity and the fat content. A resonant sensor was developed to operate in one sensitive region to allow for non-invasive milk fat detection by monitoring changes in the resonance profile of the transmission coefficient S21.

articleTitle: Method to Estimate in-band Scattering Cross Section of Vivaldi Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The in-band scattering of the antenna is the superposition of the antenna mode scattering and structural mode scattering. In this paper, the scattering, resulted from the scattering sources on the edges of the array, is proved to be the main contribution to the structural mode scattering. Moreover, the antenna mode scattering of the array can be estimated through the radiation of the antenna element. Therefore, the in-band scattering cross section (SCS) can be estimated by the superposition of the estimated antenna mode and structural mode scattering. The X-band Vivaldi array antenna is fabricated and measured. The measured monostatic SCS results are in an agreement with the simulations, showing the correctness of the analysis and the effectiveness of the estimation method.

articleTitle: Dual Band and Dual Polarization Reflectarray Enabling Reflection to Two-dimensional Direction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents dual band and dual polarization reflectarray for two-dimensional reflection. The reflectarray is designed by the supercell structure which is equal phase difference among the unit cells. In this paper, the unit cell configuration operating at 28 and 39 GHz to realize two-dimensional reflection for supercell structure is proposed. The unit cell configuration is swastika and patch structure. The simulated reflection angle is obtained for θ = φ = 45 degree.

articleTitle: Experimental Implementation of Microwave Multi-Objective Linear Constrained Minimum Power Beamforming in the Near Field
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We explore the use of a linear constrained minimum power (LCMP) algorithm for near-field beamforming and null forming for distributed phased arrays. Distributed array systems used in future microwave and millimeter-wave wireless communications, distributed sensing, and biomedical applications will necessitate the ability to focus energy and steer nulls in the near field of the array. We apply the traditional quiescent pattern constraint, which is a specialized form of the LCMP process for distortionless focusing at multiple desired locations or for simultaneous focusing and nulling. Experimental results demonstrate the ability to steer multiple beams or nulls to targets at 2.5 GHz using software-defined radios.

articleTitle: A High Gain Flexible Antenna for Full Duplex System at 5.8 GHz with Defected Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel high gain full duplex flexible antenna using PET paper and foam is presented for 5.8 GHz. Two rectangular patches are placed on top layer whereas bottom layer has defected ground structure printed on it. Patches are fed with inset line feeding. This antenna works effectively from 5.75GHz to 5.81 GHz for full duplex purpose while maintaining a radiation efficiency of 98.6% and peak gain of 8.78 dB at 5.8 GHz. This antenna is believed to be first proposed antenna which is flexible and full duplex with such high gain while working at 5.8 GHz. It also has simple structure, low cost, light weight along with good isolation and gain, which eventually makes it a good candidate for 5.8 GHz full duplex applications.

articleTitle: De-embedding a Low-Cost Partial-Data Electromagnetic Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A method for de-embedding the data acquisition electronics of a low-cost Electromagnetic Imaging system applied to grain storage bins is presented. Unlike standard de-embedding schemes, the proposed approach requires only S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> data; the remaining S-parameters are estimated. De-embedding results for a commercial imaging system are consistent compared to traditional techniques using complete 2-port measurements of all components. This new approach suggests that imaging hardware costs can be reduced, which increases their commercial appeal.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized 1-D Antenna-on-Display (AoD) for Millimeter-wave 5G NR Signals over 24-40 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an unprecedented antenna-on-display (AoD) topology featuring dual-polarization and multi-band properties for the first time in literature. The proposed phased-array AoD component achieves a realized gain of more than 7 dBi in the entire n257/n258/n260 (24.25-29.5 GHz and 37-40 GHz) spectrum. The measured results confirmed that the fabricated proof-of-concept model featuring 5G beamformer IC generates the beamforming radiation patterns at 28 GHz and 39 GHz with good correlation between simulation and measurement results.

articleTitle: A Probability Density Tapering Approach With Fitness Function Model for Linear ArrayThinning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new approach for the synthesis of thinned periodic linear arrays featuring a minimum sidelobe level is presented. The approach is mainly based on the probability tapering iterative Fourier technique (PTIFT) with a fitness function model to determine element distributions for large linear array thinning, which is denoted as FPTIFT here. Namely, the fitness function is used to initialize the starting parameters of the position of the elements. Then, a probability density taper is adopted to model the element distributions across the aperture. Compared with the traditional methods, the proposed FPTIFT acquires a minimum sidelobe level and avoids the problem of local optimum. The efficiency of the FPTIFT method was validated by two representative examples of array thinning with minimum peak sidelobe level. This demonstrates that the FPTIFT inherits PTIFT ad-vantages, and results in high efficiency in reducing the side lobes. Therefore, this proposed FPTIFT can be applied in synthesis and optimization of large-scale antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Broadband High Gain Helical Antenna for Satellite Comunication Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wideband helical antenna is developed for GPS satellite communication applications. The proposed antenna constructed from a thick copper conducting wire with diameter of 4 mm and ground plane diameter is 300 mm. The proposed antenna reflection coefficient is matched over a wider bandwidth using dielectric material of an optimized dimensions. The reflection coefficient parameter is less than -10 dB over a band from 1.1 GHz to 1.9 GHz. The antenna is encapsulated inside a radome designed using Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) material. The reflection coefficient and gain parameters of the proposed antenna with and without radome are calculated and compared. Moreover, a parametric study on various types of impedance matching transformer is conducted using multiple electromagnetic simulations. Results indicate the presented antenna exhibit very good performance in terms of impedance matching, coverage, gain and axial ratio over the entire GPS communication range and it is promising for the satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Experimental Detection of Pipeline Leaks with a 3-D Subsurface Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Pipeline leaks detection is an important problem in water transport systems maintenance. Bistatic subsurface synthetic aperture (SAR) radar is a promising tool that could be used to detect leaks due to the radar’s ability to illuminate the underground from multiple directions. However, a major obstacle preventing leak detection is the dominance of the scattered signal from the pipeline compared to the leak signal. Utilizing the different scattering mechanisms exhibited by the pipeline and the leak, this paper proposes a technique that identifies the pipeline part in the radar signal and eliminates it leading to better leak detection. The radar response of water leaks out of metallic as well as plastic (PVC) pipes is measured with a pair of ENVELOP antennas designed for subsurface radar and a por table Vector-Network-Analyzer (VNA). Processing the measurements using the proposed technique shows a significant improvement in leak detection for both the metallic and the PVC pipe cases.

articleTitle: Broadband low radar cross section circularly polarized Fabry-Perot antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In the article, we proposed a novel polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) structure, which is characterized by broadband radar cross section (RCS) and gain enhancement for Fabry-Perot (FP) antenna. The structure consists of two layers, the top layer forms metamaterial absorber (MA) to realize the RCS reduction, and the bottom layer is a linear-to-circular metasurface which can transmit a circular polarized (CP) wave. Simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth (IBW) of the antenna is 9.51-10.47 GHz (9.6%), and the axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) is 9.63 -11.09 GHz (13.7%). In addition, the gain of the proposed FP antenna can be improved by about 3.1 dB at 10 GHz, and the RCS can be reduced significantly over a wideband ranging from 7-13 GHz for both polarizations, compared with the conventional patch antenna.

articleTitle: An Efficient Transmitarray Element using Diagonal Double-Headed Arrows with Vias
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a double-layer transmitarray element operating at 10 GHz. The element consists of two crossed double-headed arrow-shaped patches printed on both surfaces of a dielectric substrate and four identical conductive vias connecting patches through the substrate. The performance of the design is simulated via HFSS and CST software packages. A full 360° transmission phase range is achieved with less than 1.8 dB transmission magnitude loss at the design frequency with normally incident source wave. The proposed element is a promising candidate for high-gain transmitarray antenna designs at X-band applications with its high performance, and structural simplicity.

articleTitle: On the Smallness of Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper explores the notion of current limits of the smallness of the small antennas. Our current activities focus on High Frequency (2-30 MHz) and Very High Frequency (30-90 MHz) bands for both long-range communication and jammer applications. In both cases, the antenna size together with their installation on relevant vehicle platforms often exceeds the maximum authorized height. Hence, we question ourselves about the real smallness of the small antennas that we can design based on the current theories. This contribution provides an extensive review with some simulations to verify the preliminary ideas and arouse the curiosity of a wider electromagnetic community to discuss the extreme limit of antenna miniaturization.

articleTitle: A77GHz Quasi-Optical Mirrors Systems for Space Routing of Lens Antenna’s Feed
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a system of two mirrors is used to shift the focal length of 3D printed lens antenna in space at millimeter wave band. The 3D-printed mirrors are sections of convex parabolic reflectors used to guide the radiated power of the lens feed antenna to a longer distance of 15cm for compact feed system design. This routing mirrors system shift allows for compact feed system design as a significantly low loss in millimeter-wave radar applications. The radiation patterns of two different feed antennas are reconstructed at 77GHz with less than 1dB reduction in the overall antenna gain.

articleTitle: Novel Contactless Sensing Technique for Real-time Human Activity Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Recent research has looked to implement real-time contactless sensing within a healthcare application which can pro-vide monitoring of vulnerable people living at home. Currently systems make use of wearable devices to achieve this but this requires users to always be wearing devices. This paper presents a real-time contactless system which makes use of radio frequency signal propagation to determine if a person is sitting or standing. This is achieved by observing incoming channel state information to detect movements and passing detected movements to an AI model that can predict sitting or standing motions from changes the signal amplitude described in the channel state information. The system is able to make accurate real-time classifications in multiple environments.

articleTitle: Energy Conserving Finite Elements for the Maxwell System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution a novel finite element method for the system of first order Maxwell equations in the time domain is introduced. It is based on both a primal and a dual set of finite elements. The resulting discrete curl operators are equivalent to those from basis free methods such as the finite integration method, the discrete exterior calculus, and the Yee-cell method. Using a finite element approach leads to a natural discretisation of the permittivity and permeability operators. Because of the symmetry of the resulting linear system and the particular choice of discretisation, this method, when used in conjunction with a Crank-Nicholson time stepping scheme, conserves the electromagnetic energy exactly.

articleTitle: Resistance Compression Network Integrated Dual-Port Radiator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A resistance compression network (RCN)-integrated dual-port radiator at 2.4 GHz is proposed in this article. The architecture implements the resistance compression and power division along with radiation, making the structure conveniently compact and low profile. The radiator structure is analysed in the 3D EM solver and a gain of 5.64 dBi is observed at the boresight direction. The differential in-phase feed architecture facilitates ease-in-integration with differential rectifier circuits and thus acts as a reliable choice for energy harvesting (EH) and wireless power transfer (WPT) applications.

articleTitle: UHF/VHF Tightly Coupled Dipole Array for CubeSat Constellations Based on Synthetic Aperture Concepts
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A deployable, two-layer Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA) is presented for CubeSat constellations based on Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) concepts. The proposed SAR system will perform a coherent integration along the constellation of CubeSats to synthesize a large array. The synthetic aperture offers finer resolution and drastically reduces cost as compared to existing airborne platforms. Our goal is to achieve 1m slant range and along-track resolutions using a large, and wideband effective aperture. In this perspective, we propose accordion-like foldable sub-arrays that operate across 130 MHz to 550 MHz with VSWR < 3. The entire antenna array is folded across the two sides of a 6U CubeSat chassis for minimal space usage. This design also introduces a ground plane that fits within the 6U CubeSat’s standard height, providing a 16 dB front-to-back gain ratio in both E- and H- planes.

articleTitle: On the Fast Analysis of Finite Printed Arrays Supporting Eigenmodes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate that the Array Scanning Method-Macro Basis Function approach, named as ASM-MBF method remains very accurate for the analysis of printed arrays in the presence of eigenmodes. The eigenmode condition occurs for the phase shifts in "spectral domain" where determinant of the Method-of-Moments (MoM) impedance matrix vanishes. Under this condition, at least one of the eigenvalues of the infinite-array impedance matrix vanishes and the corresponding eigenvector represents the eigenmode current distribution in terms of elementary basis functions. The resulting set of MBFs are used to analyse the specific array condition supporting the eigenmodes in terms of the port currents.

articleTitle: Far Field Pattern Calculation for Antenna Array with Displacement and Rotation of Elements Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In practice, mechanical errors of the array antenna affect its radiation performance. This paper proposes a method of calculating distorted array antenna radiation pattern based on the theory of characteristic mode (TCM). This method simultaneously considers the translation error and posture deflection error of array elements. A 9*5 array antenna is taken as example to verify the correctness of this method.

articleTitle: An Experimentally Validated Multi-Physics Simulation of Microwave-Induced Thermoacoustics under Microwave Heating
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Microwave-induced thermoacoustic imaging is a promising method for monitoring microwave ablation in real-time. We investigate the impact of a dynamic temperature environment on thermacoustic signal characteristics. First, we experimentally validate the simulation model using spatially uniform temperature profiles. Then, we investigate the evolution of TA signal characteristics within the spatially nonuniform temperature profiles that arise during microwave heating. We find that thermoacoustic signal characteristics are highly temperature-dependent and thus change significantly within an environment where temperature varies through space and time.

articleTitle: Pattern-reconfigurable antenna with beam switching in elevation and azimuth planes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A pattern-reconfigurable quasi-Yagi antenna with beam switching in both elevation and azimuth planes at 5.2 GHz is proposed. The antenna consists of three layers, where four quasi-Yagi antenna elements and eight pin diodes as switches are inserted in the middle layer. The top and bottom layers include parasitic elements. By controlling the pin diodes in the middle layer, the antenna can realize beam switching in the azimuth plane in four directions. Moreover, beam tilting in the elevation plane is also achieved by activating the pin diodes on the top and bottom layers to reconfigure the length of the parasitic elements.

articleTitle: Multi-trace Single Source Equations for the Modelling of Partially Coated Composite Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Multi-trace boundary element methods have become a robust and relatively easy to implement technique for the modelling of scattering and transmission by composite targets. To counteract the doubling of unknowns inherent to multiple-trace methods, the central idea of inserting a gap at the interface between domains can be applied to the single source equations (as opposed to the PMCHWT equation). In this contribution, a well-conditioned multi-trace single source method is introduced for the modelling of scattering by composite devices that may include perfectly conducting regions and perfectly conducting coatings.

articleTitle: Aperture-Coupled Patch Antennas for UWB Indoor Localization Systems in the 4 and 6 GHz Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Ultra-wideband- (UWB-) based localization systems are becoming increasingly popular, particularly for indoor navigation of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). Both the typical indoor channel properties as well as the specific requirements for UWB localization via time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) pose special and difficult requirements on the antennas. As shown with two specific anchor antenna designs, aperture-coupled patch antennas provide the required bandwidth and visible range, exhibit little dispersion, and their radiation characteristic helps mitigate multipath issues. Beyond that, it is observed that they also show low angular dependency of the transfer characteristics — a key requirement for precise UWB localization applications.

articleTitle: Alternative Ways to Feed the Arecibo Observatory Spherical Reflector
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The Arecibo Observatory 1000 ft spherical dish has been used for many years for astronomy, planetary radar, atmospheric radar, and other research. However due to unfortunate and unforeseen events, the usage of such a monumental research instrument came to a halt as the whole feeding mechanism fell in December of 2020. The old feeding mechanism consisted of a Gregorian dome and a linefeed. Even though the original feed worked wonderfully for many years, it had its issues, it was incredibly heavy and especially hard to maintain. While there is currently no clear indication on what the future holds for the Arecibo telescope, however it is interesting to explore alternative ways to feed the Arecibo spherical reflector if it is to be rebuilt in the future. In this paper, two alternative options of feeding the reflector are introduced. Both methods are modeled in the electromagnetic modeling software FEKO which utilized numerical methods to approximate the solution. The methods introduced are just preliminary results of simple concepts that could be built and put up in a quick manner to potentially get the Arecibo radio telescope running again. The goal is not to compete with the old linefeed but rather to come close to its overall results in a simpler manner.

articleTitle: D-Track: Towards Accurate Tracking Using a Single Access Point
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work proposes an indoor tracking model that establishes the correlation between the target motion and the direct path’s channel parameters, including the angle of arrival (AoA) and angle of departure (AoD). Based on this correlation, we can formulate the tracking problem as the state transition with the observations. Due to the nonlinear observation equation, D-Track resorts to particle filters to solve the problem accurately. D-Track solves the problem of discontinuous tracking due to the lack of available reflection paths when using multipath geometry for indoor tracking. Finally, we validate the proposed system using Wireless Insite software. Experimental results show that D-Track’s performance is comparable to previous state-of-the-art systems.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized All-Metal Orbital Angular Momentum Beam Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an all-metal, dual-circularly polarized OAM beam reflectarray antenna operating at 30 GHz. A 15λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×15λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> OAM reflectarray having F/D ratio of 0.6 is designed to produce Bessel beam with mode number, l = 1, and cone angle of 15°. The reflectarray consists of a low-loss square-shaped metallic unit cell independent of the polarization of the incident waves. The dual-circular polarization is achieved using a pyramidal feed horn antenna with a square septum polarizer. The feed offers polarization diversity by switching between the two input ports of the septum polarizer.

articleTitle: Dual Beam Steering LC-based Holographic Antenna with Coupling Considered Modulation Scheme utilizing Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A holographic antenna capable of dual-beam-steering is proposed. Coupling between adjacent cells in the holographic antenna is presented with a simple mathematical model. Utilizing this model, current flow on patches of each cell can be calculated for any given state sequence by simple matrix operations without full wave simulation. This capability is combined with particle warm optimization technique to find the optimal state sequence which radiates similar power for both directions in dual-beam-steering. The optimal state sequences are tested in full wave simulation and it is confirmed that gain difference between both directions was improved to less than 1dB. This antenna and methodology present the possibility of creating any desired beam patterns for various applications, not only for dual-beam-steering by elaborating the mathematical model and activating various states in each cell.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Linearly Polarized Patch Antenna at Millimetrewaves
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Phased array antenna capable of providing wider scanning range of beam radiation. The conventional phased array antenna mostly covered a single polarization of beam radiation. Therefore, by improving the phased array antenna design by implementing dual polarization will enhance the capacity of beam radiation to radiate at wide angular angle. A dual linearly polarized phased array antenna slanted at ±45° has been designed to operate at frequency of 28 GHz by using CST tool. Based on the simulation performance, the reflection coefficient (S11) and radiation pattern of both single and array antenna shows a good performance. The S11 value for both single and array antenna are -11.36 dB, and -20.17 dB, respectively. The gain of single slanted -45°, single slanted +45°, and 1x2 ±45° array patch antenna are 7.48 dB, 7.47 dB, and 7.08 dB.

articleTitle: Coupled Line Waves in Parallel-Plate Waveguides Formed by Metasurface Junctions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We study parallel-plate waveguides formed by two planar metasurface junctions. In particular, we focus on certain parameter regimes wherein each junction supports a line wave, and we investigate their coupling effects as the waveguide thickness varies, in both purely reactive and non-Hermitian (gain/loss) scenarios. Preliminary results indicate the possibility to attain strongly confined, quasi-one-dimensional modes that are of potential interest for flat-optics applications.

articleTitle: Wearable Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Array for Millimeter-Wave Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wearable magneto-electric dipole antenna array with compact size, high gain, and wide impedance bandwidth is proposed for millimeter-wave body area networks (BANs). The proposed antenna array consists of two magneto-electric dipole antenna elements and a two-way power divider. Based on a three-layer human tissue model, the body-antenna coupling effects are investigated and the results of negligible coupling effects are obtained. Therefore, the proposed magneto-electric dipole antenna array is well suited for wearable applications. The working frequencies of the proposed antenna array can cover the whole W band from 75 to 110 GHz and the realized peak gain is 13.1 dBi at 100 GHz.

articleTitle: Massive MIMO Channel Delay Spread Characteristics in Underground Mine Environment at 3.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the delay spread characteristics of a wideband Massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system in an underground gold mine is presented and analyzed. The analysis is based on the results of a measurement campaign performed at a center frequency of 3.5 GHz with a bandwidth of 400 MHz. Both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation scenarios are considered. The resulting propagation characteristics differ from those frequently encountered in more typical indoor environments such as offices and corridors. Indeed, the RMS delay spread shows little or practically no dependence on propagation distance. Therefore, 3.5 GHz band could be a good candidate for 5G communications in underground mine.

articleTitle: Wearable Microwave Imaging System for Brain Stroke Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the experimental validation of the detection capabilities of a low complexity wearable system designed for the imaging-based detection of brain stroke. The system approaches the electromagnetic inverse problem via a 3-D imaging algorithm based on the Born approximation and the Truncated Singular Value Decomposition (TSVD). For testing, flexible antennas with custom-made coupling-medium are prototyped and assessed in mimicked hemorrhagic and ischemic stroke conditions. The experiment emulates the clinical scenario using a single-tissue anthropomorphic head phantom and strokes with both 20 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and 60 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> ellipsoid targets. The imaging kernel is computed via full-wave simulation of a virtual twin model. The results demonstrate the capabilities for detecting and estimating the stroke-affected area.

articleTitle: A Scalable Aperiodic RFIC Phased-Array Topology for the mmWave Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The millimeter wave (mmWave) spectrum promises improved communications, but comes with the challenge of developing steerable, highly directive antennas which are operable over wide bandwidths. For mmWave systems, engineers often employ RF integrated circuit (RFIC) technologies for which scalable architectures are highly desirable. Periodic arrays, easily scaled to large apertures, are nevertheless hindered by grating lobes and inter-element coupling, which necessarily limit the operating bandwidth. Therefore, we present in this work a new aperiodic array topology which is supported by an underlying periodic feeding layer. Antenna element aperiodicity renders grating lobes virtually non-existent at wide steering angles, while feed point periodicity maintains RFIC scalability. Furthermore, this new topology is shown to be rapidly optimized with modern algorithms and verified by analytical formulations.

articleTitle: Tri-Polarization Reconfigurable Patch Antenna for ISM Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable antennas have seen increasing interest in recent years, due to their ability to dynamically change their operating frequency or radiation characteristics. Polarization reconfigurable antennas are of use in diversity schemes, where multiple differently polarized antennas can be replaced by a single reconfigurable antenna. We present the design and analysis of a wideband tri-polarized reconfigurable antenna. The antenna is capable of producing left-handed, right- handed, and linearly polarized radiation. A biasing scheme is proposed to allow for a pair of PIN diodes to switch the antenna radiation states. The circularly polarized state has a broad band match of ~17% bandwidth, with an overlapping match in the linearly polarized state in the 5.8GHz ISM band.

articleTitle: Accurate Solutions of Scattering Parameters of Multi-conductor Transmission Lines Based on Transfinite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an accurate analysis method of scattering parameter (S-parameters) of multi-conductor transmission lines (MTL) based on transfinite element method (TFEM). Combining the finite element method (FEM) and transfinite-element boundary truncation of the ports, the modal S-parameters can be obtained directly and accurately, and then the nodal S-parameters can be transformed by the modal S-parameters and the electric field on the ports. Compared with the results of HFSS, the numerical results prove the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Modal analysis of Electrically Small Antennas in Lossy Medium Using Eigenmode Expansion Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel numerical approach to evaluate the performances of Electrically Small Antennas (ESAs) in lossy medium is proposed. It is based on the eigenmode expansion of currents and on a multi-layer lossy dielectric model. The lossy medium as 2D dielectric multi-layer structure while the metallic antenna can be 3-dimensional. Elementary sources as well as non-resonant dipole and loop are considered in both horizontal and vertical orientations. A full physical behavior on the radiation phenomena is provided based on the modal analysis Eigenmode Expansion Method (EEM).

articleTitle: Metamaterials of conducting obstacles: An investigation of effective permeability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Lorentz theory for metamaterial constructed with conducting obstacles yields electric and magnetic polarizabilities, that effectively modify the permittivity and permeability from that of the host medium. However, the Floquet eigenmodal analysis shows while the permittivity tensor generally concurs with the Lorentz model, but the permeability tensor has no effect on the perfectly conducting obstacles. Interestingly, numerical results of metamaterial-slabs support the Floquet model. The source for the inaccuracy in Lorentz theory is examined and discussed.

articleTitle: Flexible Antenna Arrays based on Graphene For High-speed THz Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a hybrid antenna design for terahertz (THz) communication. The proposed antenna operates in the frequency range of 0.35-0.45 THz. Simulations show that the combination of graphene material and gold improves the antenna efficiency up to 80% in the desired frequency band. The proposed hybrid design can be used in high-speed wireless communications in the future.

articleTitle: DR Based Compact MIMO Antenna with Resistor-loaded DGS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This article presents a two-element-based four-port compact MIMO structure. The single antenna element is energized by two diverse feeding techniques: coaxial probe and conformal strip. Resistor-loaded defected ground structure and orthogonal mode generation technique is used simultaneously to obtain good isolation between adjacent ports (|S21|>18dB). The design operates at 4.9-5.5GHz, covering the entire WLAN band. Furthermore, several MIMO performance parameters like envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and diversity gain (DG) are evaluated and found within the desired levels, signifying good diversity performance.

articleTitle: Publication of the Antenna Measurement Standard IEEE Std™ 149
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: IEEE Standard 149, Standard Test Procedures for Antennas, was last revised in 1979 [1]. Over the past several years, the standard has been rewritten and updated to account for state-of-the-art facilities and modern measurement practices [3],[4]. In this paper, we describe and comment on the changes to the document.

articleTitle: Estimation of Time Delay using Super Resolution Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In signal processing, sonar, radar, seismic waves, and radio waves, time delay estimation (TDE) has long been studied. This work employs the Matrix Pencil Method to recover super-resolution Time Delay Estimation (TDE) of signals in multi-path situations (MPM). To test the novel strategy, errors were measured and compared to the classical Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) and cross-correlation approaches. TDE performance in a multi-channel context is examined using numerical simulations that demonstrate varied values of mean square errors versus signal to noise ratio with separation. . The suggested super-resolution MPM methodology improves earlier approaches by precisely identifying and measuring all components to their resolution limits and addressing closely spaced frequencies.

articleTitle: Quasi-Reflectionless Tunable Bandstop Filter Using Patch Antenna as Dissipation Element
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a patch antenna is designed as a dissipation node of a tunable quasi-reflectionless bandstop filter. This frequency reconfigurable device consists of a radiating patch antenna and a reflective microstrip bandstop filter (BSF) connected in a complementary-duplexer fashion. With a properly designed duplexing common structure of the filter and the antenna, a tunable reflectionless bandstop filter can be obtained by setting up the antenna as a dissipation resistor. The working principle is summarized. For verification, a circuit prototype is fabricated and measured. The measurement agrees well with the simulation. The filter exhibits a fractional bandwidth of 3.2 % and a tuning range from 3.6 GHz to 4.1 GHz. This BSF alleviates the heat dissipation of the resistor in reflectionless design and provides access to high power handling.

articleTitle: Efficient Higher Order VIE Method with Taylor Series Expansion for Wideband Frequency EM Scattering Analysis of Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient volume integral equation (VIE) method with Taylor series expansion (TSE) and higher order hierarchical vector (HOHV) basis functions is developed for fast electromagnetic scattering analysis over a wideband frequency of dielectric objects. In this VIE, the impedance matrix elements can be divided into the frequency dependent item (FDT) and geometric structure dependent term (GSDT), where only GSDT is required to be calculated and stored in advance. Then, during frequency sweeping process, the impedance matrix can be generated by combining the precomputed matrices GSDT and FDT. Besides, due to the hierarchy of the HOHV bases, only one coarse mesh corresponding to the lowest frequency of the given frequency band is generated, and the pre-computed matrices corresponding to the highest order basis are need to be computed. Based on those, the EM scattering corresponding into high frequency point can be calculated simply by adjusting the order of the HOHV bases. This saves much work in geometrical modeling and further improves computational efficiency. In contrast to the conventional scheme for fast EM scattering analysis over a wideband frequency, this HO-TSE-VIE method requires much less computational time while the accuracy remains at the same level. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate its accuracy and efficiency.

Author Keywords: Higher order hierarchical vector (HOHV) basis functions

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Antenna With Low-cost Paddle-controlled Circuit for Flexible Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with paddle-controlled circuit is proposed for flexible beam steering. The dielectric resonator antenna is fed by a monopole and a patch for alternative modes. A sliding paddle is used to control the input phase between two modes to achieve the flexible beam steering over the horizontal plane. The steering beam is tilted to the z-axis with an angle of 45 degrees to achieve indoor coverage. Compared with the traditional beam switching antenna, the proposed DRA is low-cost by avoiding the switching circuit with discrete state. The DRA is fabricated and measured with its center frequency of 2.95 GHz, high gain (5dBi) and high efficiency (86.1%). The measured results are in good agreement with the simulation results and will be demonstrated in the conference. The proposed DRA can be applied to the indoor wireless systems with flexible beam Steering requirement.

articleTitle: All-Fabric Bandage Antenna for RF Information and Power Transfer in Healthcare Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the first antenna invisibly concealed in an all-fabric bandage, with an ultra-low profile (0.001 the wavelength) for sub-1 GHz applications. Antenna parameters, such as the reflection coefficients, mutual coupling, radiation patterns, radiation efficiency, and the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR), were investigated in free space as well as in the presence of human tissue. The antenna’s channel gain over a 60 cm link with a standard RFID antenna is at least −37 dB and −23.6 dB, in the presence and absence of the body, respectively, which indicates the antenna’s suitability for communication and wireless power transfer applications. The all-fabric dipole antenna exhibits the attractive features of being flexible, low-profile, lightweight, easily to fabricate, and conformable to the body and therefore, can be used for designing wireless and battery-free smart bandage for wound healing applications.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Based Antenna Beam Coefficient Generation for Planar Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel design approach on optimizing the complex feeding coefficients of an antenna array to achieve a desired beam pattern. The approach uses a convolutional neural network which takes an image representation of a desired radiation pattern and generates the corresponding phase gradient over the array aperture. To demonstrate the performance of the approach, an 8×8 planar array has been used. The results show the potential for machine learning to optimize antenna parameters in more complicated antenna systems, where an efficient way of developing antenna pattern codebooks by using a trained neural network is used.

articleTitle: A Gain Enhancing Mesh (GEM) in Front of Horn Arrays to Improve Aperture Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The realizable aperture efficiency of electronically steered horn arrays is restricted by the thickness of the horn walls. The minimum thickness is driven by manufacturing limitations. Introducing a metal grid structure over the horn array can appreciably increase aperture efficiency [1]. This gain enhancing mesh (GEM) may be integrated into a radome, dust cover, or meander-line polarizer. An improvement in aperture efficiency of over 0.4 dB at the EHF band has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulations of Quantum Plasmonic Hong-Ou-Mandel Effects
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The new Langevin noise (LN) formalism, proposed in [1], [2], is promising for studying quantum electromagnetic phenomena involving in both open boundary and media with ohmic losses. We incorporate computational electromagnetic methods into the new LN formalism so that one can study practical quantum optics problems in the developed numerical framework. Particularly, we present a test numerical simulation result on Hong-Ou-Mandel effects on a plasmonic platform to verify the quantum statistical behaviors of surface plasmon polaritons.

articleTitle: Respiration detection of sedentary person using ubiquitous WiFi signals
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A sedentary lifestyle significantly influences the health of people. Accordingly, to avoid the risks of sudden respiratory illness, a continuous, effective, and inexpensive sensing system is vital. In this paper, we leverage commercial WiFi devices to deploy a respiration detection system for sedentary scenarios. Our results showed a median error, for one and two human subjects’ breathing detection, of 0.7 bpm and 1 bpm respectively.

articleTitle: On the Effectiveness of Quasi-Helmholtz Projectors in Preconditioning Problems with Junctions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The electric field integral equation (EFIE) is known to suffer from ill-conditioning and numerical instabilities at low frequencies (low-frequency breakdown). A common approach to solve this problem is to rely on the loop and star decomposition of the unknowns. Unfortunatelly, building the loops is challenging in many applications, especially in the presence of junctions. In this work, we investigate the effectiveness of quasi-Helmholtz projector approaches in problems containing junctions for curing the low-frequency breakdown without detecting the global loops. Our study suggests that the performance of the algorithms required to obtain the projectors in the presence of junctions are maintained while keeping constant the number of sheets per junction. Finally, with a sequence of numerical tests, this work shows the practical impact of the technique and its applicability to real case scenarios.

articleTitle: Continuous Beam-Scanning Leaky-Wave Antenna With Circular Polarization Based on Modified Half-Mode SIW
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A compact half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) leaky-wave antenna (LWA) with circular polarization (CP) is proposed in this paper. The LWA is periodically loaded with series interdigital capacitors and additional shunt branch lines as grounded stubs. This novel design is able to provide continuous beam scanning with CP by sweeping the frequency. Within the operating frequency region from 4.08 GHz to 5.16 GHz, the LWA steers CP beam ranging from -22 deg to 36 deg in the measurement.

articleTitle: Wearable 2.4 GHz Bluetooth Antenna for Respiration Monitoring and Contact Tracing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A 2.4 GHz on-body Bluetooth antenna (BLEpatch) is proposed for respiration monitoring and contact tracing applications. Due to its patch structure, the antenna performance is robust at body proximity. The introduction of a compressible foam substrate allows it to periodically compress and relax in response to abdominal pressure due to respiration. The antenna is simulated both in free space and on a human body model. The antenna passband is 2.36 - 2.57 GHz with a maximum gain of 8.2 dBi in the relaxed state.

articleTitle: Antenna Array Beam Steering Based on a Parasitic Layer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication and characterization of a 4x1 antenna array operating in fifth generation new radio (5G NR) sub-6 GHz band of 3.4 – 3.6 GHz. This array uses a parasitic layer placed in its near-field region in performing beamforming as opposed to using phase shifters and thus enables reducing the number of power hungry RF chains of massive MIMO systems. To demonstrate this new beamforming technology, a proof-of-concept 4x1 array prototype was designed, fabricated and characterized, where simulated and measured beam steering performances agreed well.

articleTitle: Low Band Directivity Enhancement of DETSA Using Characteristic Modes Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
