abstract: This paper presents a characteristic modes approach to optimize the low band directivity of a Double Exponentially Tapered Slot Antenna (DETSA). By integrating discrete loads at specific positions inside the antenna structure, the radiated characteristic fields can be manipulated to improve its directivity. The study examines the influence of the loading position on the optimization results. With the proposed loading configuration, the directivity of the DETSA reaches 6.5 dBi in the lower part of the band ~150 MHz rather than 2.5 dBi for the classical unloaded case. Geometrical modifications and additional loads are then introduced to enhance the radiation performance of the proposed DETSA over a wideband.

articleTitle: Substrate-integrated antenna system for microwave and millimeter wave applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a substrate-integrated antenna system for ultrawideband (UWB) applications and millimeter-wave for 5G applications is presented. An ultra-wideband antenna is designed by using the uniplanar nature of coplanar waveguide to create two tapered slots. On the same substrate, a millimeter-wave antenna is incorporated where the surface current is the lowest. The UWB and millimeter-wave antennas provide respectively, a bandwidth going from 3 to 11 GHz and 26.1 GHz to 30.3 GHz (4.3 GHz), while keeping an acceptable isolation.

articleTitle: A Wideband Filtering Patch Antenna with Muti-mode Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This communication presents a wideband filtering patch antenna with three mode radiation in the passband. The proposed antenna is constructed by two layers of substrates and three metal layers, with its entire height being 0.06λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. A rectangular patch and four square parasitic patches support two desired patch modes. A slot etched on the floor is designed to excite the patch modes and introduce a slot mode. Eventually, one slot mode and two patch modes radiate in the passband, and there are no modes radiate out-of the passband. Hence, the filtering and radiation performance are both achieved. In addition, a metal probe is introduced to improve the roll-of-rate at the lower band-edge. Simulated results shows a wide passband of 38% (3.09 GHz - 4.55 GHz) and a maximum gain of 10.3dBi. The out-of-band suppression levels are more than 21 dB.

articleTitle: On the Customized Construction of Periodic Basis Functions: Towards Designing Maximally-locallized Wannier Functions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Periodic and Phased-periodic Boundary Value Problems (P-BVPs and PP-BVPs) occupy a prominent position in computational electromagnetics. Many BVPs in photonics involving the coupled system of Maxwell’s equations, and materials engineering problems utilizing the time-independent Schrödinger equation, lead to PP-BVPs. Bloch waves and the Floquet Theorem, when hybridized with other traditional numerical techniques are classical tools for solving P-BVPs and PP-BVPs. One important feature of the eigenfunctions for PP-BVPs is that they can be linearly combined to obtain localized and maximally-localized solutions of the underlying problems, leading to the so-called Wannier functions associated with the PP-BVPs. This paper scrutinizes the foundation of the governing equations and provides the first general recipe for the customized construction of periodic basis functions. It is hoped that the proposed procedure will further facilitate rigorous modeling of void and defects, in otherwise periodic structures.

articleTitle: GNU Radio based Spectrum Occupancy Measurement Tool
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a prototype of a lower cost tool that allows to measure the channel occupancy and signal levels on a wide range of the electromagnetic spectrum, this tool scan the radio channels of each radio service to establish if there are available as white spaces for cognitive radio or used by a primary or licensed operator in a certain portion of the spectrum. The architecture of the prototype is presented, the hardware components such as the RTL-SDR, the development of the software based on GNU Radio, and finally some results of measurements for frequencies between 470 to 900 MHz are presented.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of 1-D Leaky-Wave Antennas based on Partially Reflecting Sheets
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The properties of one-dimensional (1-D) unidirectional leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) based on partially reflecting sheets (PRS) are analyzed here. In particular, we derive conditions for maximizing the gain and provide analytical formulas to determine the pattern bandwidth. Design equations are finally obtained to optimize the gain of a practical PRS-based 1-D unidirectional LWA propagating a TE mode.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Antennas with Minimal Broadband Radio Frequency Threat Coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Electrically small antennas (ESAs) are known for being tuned and loaded to optimize their broadband capability. This is because ESA systems have a high quality factor (Q). While high-Q systems are undesirable in many wireless communications applications due to their limited broadband response, high-Q ESA systems can potentially prevent or decrease coupling caused by external radio frequency (RF) threats. This paper explores this potential, as well as the difficulties associated with creating matching networks for antennas with low radiation resistance and a high reactance.

articleTitle: On a Fast Solution Strategy for a Surface-Wire Integral Formulation of the Anisotropic Forward Problem in Electroencephalography
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work focuses on a quasi-linear-in-complexity strategy for a hybrid surface-wire integral equation solver for the electroencephalography forward problem. The scheme exploits a block diagonally dominant structure of the wire self block— that models the neuronal fibers self interactions—and of the surface self block—modeling interface potentials. This structure leads to two Neumann iteration schemes further accelerated with adaptive integral methods. The resulting algorithm is linear up to logarithmic factors. Numerical results confirm the performance of the method in biomedically relevant scenarios.

articleTitle: A Planar Patch Antenna Array for 5G Millimeter Wave Extender
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A low cost, simple to fabricate, multi-layer printed patch antenna array that can be used as the outdoor antenna system in the 5G Millimeter wave Extender. The antenna is designed to operate in the n258 (24.25 GHz-27.5 GHz) and has a size of 2.3λx2.3λ. The antenna shows 94% efficiency with typical gain of 15.5 dBi with only a 0.6dB gain variation in the band of interest.

articleTitle: Bi-functional Saltwater-based Structure as UHF Antenna and EMI Shielding Window
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a transparent saltwater in glass structure working simultaneously as a UHF antenna and EMI shielding window. The proposed structure has high transparency (> 91%), which is achieved through the use of salt water as a conductive medium held between two clear glass layers, allowing its use as an optical window. On one hand, the saltwater in the glass structure functions as an EMI shielding window, with a shielding effectiveness above 20 dB. On the other hand, the proposed structure works as a transparent UHF antenna by adding only a feeding port.

articleTitle: A Minimal Realization of Delay Rational Macromodel of Multiconductor Transmission Lines Based on Gilbert’s Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a minimal state space model of delay-rational Green’s function-based macromodel for multiconductor transmission lines. The proposed method makes an order reduction on original model and guarantees that there is no redundant state variables converted from matrix-transfer functions during synthesis. Based on Gilbert realization’s construction, the formulation of minimal representation is developed for real poles, as well as conjugate poles. The equivalent circuit is generated optimally and SPICE netlist contains less elements, improving computational efficiency in time-domain simulation. The numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method can decrease the CPU time and memory consumed in standard simulation environment.

articleTitle: A TM31 Mode Circular Microstrip Patch Antenna with a Reduced Eigenvalue
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized TM31-mode circular microstrip patch antenna is presented. The patch is loaded with six symmetrically-placed radial slits, inspired by the surface current distribution of the mode. This will in turn facilitate elongating the current path and accordingly reduce the eigenvalue of the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf> mode. In particular, the realized eigenvalue is comparable to that of a conventional dominant TM11 mode antenna, resulting in about 72% reduction in the patch area.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Olive Tree Dielectric Properties Characterization by Using an Open-ended Coaxial Probe
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we propose a characterization of the dielectric properties of olive tree trunk and branches in a nondestructive way, by using a custom-designed open-ended coaxial probe. This research represents a first step in filling a knowledge gap due to the lack of dielectric characterization of similar structures. In particular, by dynamically observing the variation of the dielectric properties, the hydration status as well as other tree pathologies may be detected in the early stages, improving the plant productivity. The main advantage of the introduced methodology is the capability to detect permittivity and conductivity in a wider frequency band; furthermore, the small probe aperture diameter allows to accurately measure water content even in the smaller diameter branches. We measured the living olive plant dielectric properties for 5 days consecutively, in a controlled environment. A substantial difference was found between the more peripherical branches and the trunk, allegedly due to a different water content.

articleTitle: Topological insulator metamaterials based on transmission line networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Topological insulators play important role in recent academic research for their unique features, including bandgaps in the dispersion diagram, and robust edge mode propagation. Most of the designs that have been presented so far are based on coupled-resonators, resulting in limited bandwidth. In this paper, a topological insulator based on a dual lattice of differential transmission lines is presented. The operation principle of the proposed unit cell along with the related results for infinite and truncated lattice are presented to verify that the structure has topological property. Furthermore, potential applications in phased antenna arrays and nonreciprocal devices are outlined.

articleTitle: Safieddin (Ali) Safavi-Naeini – Innovative and Pioneering Contributions in Antennas and Computational Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: I had the privilege of knowing Prof. (Ali) Safavi-Naeini for over 26 years. He was my teacher and thesis supervisor during my Master’s and PhD studies but, beyond that, he was my champion and greatest supporter in many ways, an inspiring mentor, a true friend, and a remarkable yet humble human being. His deep and broad knowledge as well as his extraordinary insight in almost anything related to electromagnetics, had a profound impact on many areas in this field. In this talk, I will briefly summarize some of his innovative contributions in the areas of antennas and computational electromagnetics.

articleTitle: Out-of-Band Isolation Enhancement in RF Circulators With Embedded Filtering Functionality
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This manuscript explores design methodologies to enhance the out-of-band isolation (IS) bandwidth (BW) of RF co-designed components that exhibit the co-located functions of a bandpass filter and circulator (BPFC). These methodologies are validated at 3.1 GHz for a BPFC with the following characteristics: passband insertion loss: 3.4 dB, fractional bandwidth 6.5%, IS at f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cen</inf>: 20.6 dB, lower (> 20 dB) out-of-band IS BW: 2.66:1, upper (> 20 dB) out-of-band isolation BW: 1.48:1.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Conformal Hybrid HIS based Antennas Performance in 5G band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A low profile hybrid mushroom antenna (Hybrid-HIS) has been presented for the 5G and Wi-Fi system. The HHIS antenna design of overlapped 2x2 array of 4 element Unit Cells with corner and center elements shorted to reduce the mutual coupling by making elements exclusive. The HHIS is then conformed and its response variation is analyzed for its usage as a conformal element. The Conformed antenna array has response drop of 12.5% and 37.5% from the Planar antenna for radius of curvature, r=100 mm and r= 50 mm, respectively. The 2 modes are observed at different frequencies but close enough to contribute into more bandwidth and the difference in response due to curvature is more evident away from the two mentioned modes.

articleTitle: Wideband and Dual-polarized Transparent Antenna-on-Display using Via-less and Single-Layer Topology for mmWave Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new class wideband dual-polarized Antenna-on-Display (AoD) at mmWave spectrum. The proposed AoD is designed to achieve wide bandwidth and beam steering feasibility despite the limitations of the process. The optimized prototype exhibits a wide impedance bandwidth ranging from 26 – 40 GHz for |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < -10 with supporting dual-polarization. Moreover, the maximum beam scanning angle of ± 38° at 28 GHz and ± 40° at 39 GHz are confirmed.

articleTitle: Remembering Prof. Tapan Sarkar: A Wonderful Colleague and a Dear Friend
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: It is an honor to present this invited talk in the special session of the IEEE-APS-URSI Symposium dedicated to the scientific life of late Prof. Tapan Sarkar (1948-2021). I knew Tapan for nearly five decades and had many fruitful discussions with him on all kinds of EM topics including rapid evaluation of the Sommerfeld Half-Space Integral, Integral Equations, and MoM, Near Field Measurement Techniques, etc. What I vividly remember was his keen interest to constantly explore out-of-the-box solutions in dealing with advanced numerical techniques and their practical implementations for solving antennas and scattering problems. Ironically we shared some similar experiences by participating in enormous numbers of national and international conferences and presenting papers in the same sessions and contributing to many committee meetings together and the list goes on and on. We not only lost an exceptional researcher but also a dear friend.

articleTitle: The Road to Smart Electromagnetic Environments: The Future of Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The Smart Electromagnetic Environment (SEME) is a revolutionary paradigm that will definitely change how a wireless communication system is nowadays conceived, designed, and deployed. It is based on the driving idea that the propagation environment must play a key-role in enhancing the overall quality-of-service (QoS) in order to meet the ever-growing needs for ubiquitous connection, extreme throughputs, and high reliability foreseen in the next generation communications standards. The goal of this work is to provide a review of some of the most recent advances in such a very active research field.

articleTitle: SIW Interposer for Cost-Effective RF-Integration and Packaging of Active-Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A transition between grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) and substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) to form an interposer using ball gridded array (BGA) technology is presented for the first time. It allows for possible efficient and cost-effective 3D integration of multi-channel RFIC beam former into active-phased array antenna modular architecture. The interposer’s transition consists of embedded metallic via in SIW, and BGA used to couple RF-power between the SIW and GCPW structures. It is found that the two propagating modes, TE10 and Q-TEM in SIW and GCPW, respectively can be matched by properly optimizing the transition parameters. Simulation results are demonstrated in this paper.

articleTitle: A Numerical Method to Analyze Electromagnetic Fields on Semiconductor Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A coupled system of volume integral and two-fluid hydrodynamic equations is solved to analyze electromagnetic field interactions with non-local dispersion effects on semiconductor nanostructures. This coupled system, where the hydrodynamic currents and the electric flux are the unknowns, is discretized using Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson basis functions. Numerical results obtained using this solver show the presence of so-called acoustic modes at the frequencies lower than the resonance frequency of localized surface plasmon (LSP) mode. These modes cannot be identified if a Drude-like model or the single-fluid hydrodynamic equation is used to represent the electrical properties of the semiconductors.

articleTitle: A non-Reciprocal Waveguide Using Spoof Plasmon Polariton Coupling to a Magnetized Plasma
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We demonstrate non-reciprocal (one-way) waveguiding in a microstrip tailored to support the propagation of spoof plasmon polaritons with a resonance near f = 7 GHz. Time-reversal symmetry is broken by coupling the microstrip fields to a gyrotropic magnetized gaseous plasma column thereby exciting non-reciprocal interfacial plasma-vacuum surface plasmon polaritons. The magnetic bias breaks the symmetry of the magnetoplasmon resonances, resulting in a breaking of the bi-directionality of the wave propagation in the microstrip. A suprising feature is the presence of non-reciprocal response over the entire 2-7 GHz region of the spectrum. This broad response is attributed to the non-uniformity of the plasma, as the wavefield tuning to higher frequencies excites plasmon polaritons that move towards regions of high plasma density closer to the center of the plasma column.

articleTitle: Focusing Properties of Time-Reversed Electromagnetic Waves in a Rotating Metal Wire Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the focusing properties of time-reversed electromagnetic waves in a rotating metal wire array are investigated. Firstly, a single antenna model is established for theoretical analysis, and then the system simulation is carried out. The simulation results show that the time reversal channel changes when the metal wire array rotates, which has a great influence on the focusing effect. The simulation results are in good agreement with the theoretical analysis results.

articleTitle: A GSTCs Enhanced vectorial DGTD Scheme for the Modeling of Nonlinear and Conformal Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Metasurfaces are one of the most popular synthetic materials in optical and microwave fields in the past decade. Modeling and simulating the metasurfaces is one of the vital steps in metasurface design. Here a new scheme is proposed to simulate metasurfaces, based on discontinuous Galerkin time-domain method and generalized sheet transition conditions. Compared to the previous numerical methods for metasurfaces, the new scheme has the advantages in broad-band/transient/nonlinear response analysis, conformal geometrical approximation and vectorial basis functions for electromagnetic field. Two examples are presented to validate the newly proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Aperture-Level Self-Interference Cancelation for Full-Duplex Phased Arrays by Phase-Only Transmitting Beamfoming
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An effective phase-only transmitting beamforming method is proposed for aperture-level self-interference cancelation (SIC) in full-duplex phased arrays. The transmitting gain pattern and self-interference coupling power are calculated by the active element patterns and scattering parameter between the transmitting subarray and receiving subarray. Focusing on achieving good trade-off between transmit-receive isolation and transmitting gain loss, a non-convex multi-objective optimization problem corresponding to phase-only transmitting beamforming is established. By the introduction of iterative idea, the non-convex optimization problem is converted into solving a sequence of convex problem, and the phase excitations in transmitting subarray can be efficiently achieved. The simulated results as for X-band 8×8 transmitting subarray and receiving subarray show that the proposed method achieve around 29.3 dB averaged isolation improvement with only 0.2dB transmitting gain loss.

articleTitle: A Novel, FSS-Enhanced, Pop-Up Card Inspired Corner Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a corner reflector antenna with a reconfigurable radiation pattern. The the corner reflector uses a frequency-selective surface (FSS) as has a variable folding angle. The inclusion of the FSS in the reflector design causes nulls to appear 73° from the direction of maximum radiation on both sides. As the folding angle is decreased from 90° to 60°, these nulls deepen, and the difference between the gain at the nulls and the maximum gain increases. The cause of this may be that the FSS is better at reflecting radiation at the resonant frequency than a solid metal reflector.

articleTitle: Ultra-Robust Air-Filled Multiband Antenna for Smart Surface Integration
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A low-cost and highly efficient multiband antenna, operating in the SRD860 (863–870 MHz), 2.4-GHz ISM (2.4–2.4835 GHz) and LTE-7 (2.5–2.69 GHz) frequency standards, is proposed for deployment in smart surfaces. It exploits the electromagnetic shielding of a ridged air-filled cavity with completely metallized sidewalls, to enable extensive integration opportunities. Measurements demonstrate the excellent antenna robustness in several integration scenarios, indicating a great compatibility with a wide range of superstrates, as well as a strong isolation from supporting and surrounding materials.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Tripling of Triangular Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a frequency pulling technique (FPT), inspired by the band-pass filter synthesis, is proposed for increasing the bandwidth of symmetric-shaped antennas. Namely, by simultaneously feeding a triangular patch antenna by three symmetric points, we are able to triple its bandwidth compared to its traditional single-fed counterpart. To feed our patch, a three-way power divider that applies a consecutive phase difference of 90° at each input port is printed under the triangular aperture as the FPT requires. With this design methodology not only we significantly increase the bandwidth of our antenna, but we also keep its aperture size invariant, unlike other design methodologies found in literature.

articleTitle: Hybrid Dielectric Resonator Antenna: Innovations Over the Decades and State-of-the-Art Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) will complete 40 years since its inception in 1983 and has accumulated several novel techniques and designs to serve various applications. ‘Hybrid DRA’ is one of them, conceived more than 20 years ago. This paper is aimed to portray all kinds of Hybrid DRAs explored in the last two decades including some state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: Beam-Scanning Metalens Antenna using Prior-Knowledge-Guided Machine-Learning-Based Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A metalens antenna with beamscanning performance is designed using a proposed prior-knowledge-guided machine-learning-enabled (PK-ML) synthesis method. The algorithm of conditional deep convolutional generative adversarial network (cDCGAN) is utilized in the proposed method to generate pixelated metacells with high degrees of freedom. Prior knowledge, including well-known fundamental electromagnetic theorems and experience in antenna design, are purposely applied in the proposed method to guide and speed up the synthesis. Triple-layer metacells are generated using the proposed method for the design of the metalens antenna with improved gain bandwidth. The proposed metalens antenna of area of 13.2 × 13.2 wavelengths realize the gain of 29.4 dBi at 12 GHz with 1-dB bandwidth of 13.5%, 52.2% higher than the reference metalens antenna.

articleTitle: On the Efficient Evaluation of the Dyadic Green Function for Anisotropic Conductive Surfaces in Planarly Layered Uniaxial Media
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The efficient evaluation of the electromagnetic dyadic Green function of infinitely extended anisotropic conductive surfaces in uniaxial layered media is investigated. The proposed formulation and numerical method can be utilized to analyze surface plasmonic waves excited on conductive surfaces or meta-surfaces, and resolve numerical inefficiency due to highly oscillatory integrands and surface-wave modal singularities.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Assisted Active Base Element Modeling Based on Virtual Subarray Approximation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) method serves as one of the most inspiration techniques in both antenna and antenna array designs. Conventionally, the computational expenses of building ML models and predicting using these models are negligible when compared with those utilized to construct training data sets using full-wave simulators. However, in antenna array pattern synthesis, both radiation pattern magnitudes and phases covers all concerned angles and frequencies serve as characteristics for various kinds of array allocation and geometry designs, which creates much bigger data sizes when compared with antenna design problems. Therefore, unbearable computational cost are needed for array synthesis problems if conventional pure data-driven methods are used. In this paper, a novel ML-assisted active base element modeling method for practical array synthesis applications considering both mutual coupling and platform effects are proposed based on virtual subarray approximation methods. By introducing knowledge-based methods, the computational cost of both the ML training and predicting processes are greatly alleviated. A linear microstrip antenna array is introduced and utilized to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of a Tunable Non-Foster Circuit Using the Normalized Determinant Function Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A tunable non-Foster circuit is analyzed for stability using the normalized determinant function (NDF) method. The circuit is teamed with a wideband resistively loaded dipole antenna to improve signal reception at the low end of the operating band. Network stability is examined and the circuit is shown to be stable.

articleTitle: Aperiodic Space-Time Modulation for Antenna Array Beam Steering With Suppressed Sideband Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Recent advances of time-modulated antenna arrays (TMAs) have provided a new "time" degree of freedom to achieve high-precise beam steering. However, traditional periodic space-time modulation techniques face the difficulty of suppressing the harmful sideband radiations, which significantly prevents the application of TMAs in modern electronic systems. To address the above problem, we propose an aperiodic space-time modulation technique in this paper. An aperiodic time modulation sequence and its design procedure are discussed. By applying the proposed aperiodic space-time modulation technique, continuous steerable beams are synthesized, while sideband radiations are effectively suppressed to a satisfied sideband level (SBL < –30.0 dB). Several numerical simulations are carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed aperiodic space-time modulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Multilayer Reflectarray Unit Based on Second-Order Minkowski Fractal Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel multilayer unit of reflectarray antenna based on a modified second-order Minkowski fractal structure is proposed. The antenna is working at the frequency of 10 GHz and can improve the phase range effectively. A bending delay line is used so that a sufficient phase shift can be obtained by adjusting the length of the phase delay line. Also, the final phase response is wider than two cycles and reflection loss is better than 0.28 dB. Furthermore, a surface area reduction of 23.7% is achieved compared with the traditional rectangular patch. The reduced surface area can ensure a decreased mutual coupling and better ohmic losses. Simulation result shows that the phase response presents a good linearity.

articleTitle: Planar and Compact Ferrite Isolator in Ku- band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and fabrication of a compact, planar ferrite isolator in Ku-band. A completely filled Rectangular Wave Guide (RWG) isolator using an inset-fed micro strip transmission line is demonstrated. Size of the isolator is ~ 9mm x 9mm x 0.5mm (length x width x thickness).Method of feeding has considerably reduced the size of the isolator. The bias is applied transverse to the ferrite substrate. Isolation band from 16 GHz to 18.8 GHz is obtained. A maximum peak Isolation of around 40 dB is measured at 18.6 GHz. The device along with bias mechanism weights less than 20 gms. All the measurements are verified by simulations using a full wave 3D-electromagnetic solver. (CST MicroWave Studio(CST MWS)).

articleTitle: Direct Antenna FSK Modulation with Time Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An innovative time-modulated array (TMA) approach capable of simultaneously performing direct antenna frequency-shift keying (FSK) modulation and beam steering (BS) is proposed. Conventional binary FSK (BFSK) modulators are based on the commutation of two carriers and, to perform BS, a standard phased array with variable phase shifters (VPSs) is needed. Alternatively, the proposed TMA approach jointly performs BFSK modulation by transmitting each symbol over a different harmonic frequency, and BS by adjusting the on-off instants of the periodic binary sequences which control low-complexity 2-bit VPSs.

articleTitle: Printed Circular Antenna Arrays for Direction Finding Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A comparative study of the performance characteristics of a printed 8-element V-shaped circular antenna array with two director elements to obtain a V-Yagi based array operating at 5.8 GHz for vehicular direction-finding applications is presented. The array performance was improved as compared to [1] in terms of operating bandwidth and directivity. A director is added to the V-shaped antenna elements and a modified GND plane is considered for such improvements. The arrays were fabricated on FR-4 substrates with 0.8mm thickness. Both antennas show wide bandwidth of over 1.2GHz and gain values for all elements range between 2.1-3.1 dBi at 90 degrees elevation.

articleTitle: CNN-Based Propagation Loss Modeling Based on a Series of Images in Urban Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Propagation loss modeling is considered to be important for the efficient planning of any wireless communication system. We present a novel convolutional neural network (CNN)-based propagation loss modeling based on field measurements in urban scenarios. We consider bird’s-eye images as input data that include the information of buildings, intersections, and roadways. Each image represents a different spatial segment of main propagation paths between a transmitter and a receiver. Multiple feature extraction layers based on CNNs are used. The proposed model shows its superior performance compared with the COST 231 Walfisch-Ikegami model.

articleTitle: Frequency Controllable Triband Reflective Type Linear Converter With High Angular Stability in C/X/Ku Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper shows a compact reflective type linear cross polarization rotator with triple band operations in C/X/Ku frequency bands of the microwave spectrum. The unit cell of the converter consists of three open loop square ring resonators (OSRRs), supported by a metal backed single layer dielectric. The converter achieves above 90 % polarization conversion ratio (PCR) over the frequencies of 7.27-7.47 GHz in C band, 10.53-11.4 GHz in X band, and 13.89-14.26 GHz in Ku band. The unit cell is arranged periodically in the x-y plane with a size of 11.6 × 11.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Reflection from the proposed metasurface shows stable cross conversion at different high oblique angles, with PCR > 80 % is maintained up to an incidence angle of 40° for TE mode and 35° for TM mode. The designed converter has the ability to reduce the radar cross section (RCS) by > 18 dB, offering its practical applicability in stealth technology.

articleTitle: Cloaking Synthesis Based on Exact Re-analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel synthesizing procedure is introduced and employed to extract locally-optimal cloaking devices. Their performance is compared with fundamental bounds found using a convex optimization approach. The optimization method is based on a method-of-moments paradigm utilizing rank-1 updates of the structure iteratively performed based on a greedy algorithm. This approach produces locally optimal shapes and its incorporation into a global search strategy is described and applied. As compared to classical topology optimization schemes, no post-processing is required. Two canonical problems are solved and presented.

articleTitle: Design Algorithm of Near-Field Multi-Focus Array: Studies in Robustness against Array Element Failure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: With the rapid development of short-range communication and powering in 5G and beyond system, near-field multi-focus array received attention recently as it can offer designated power pattern on multiple target or regions with high efficiency. And the NFMF array is prone to adopt large-scale array to fulfill the focusing requirement for communication and powering, which may suffer failure of array elements for long-term use. Therefore, the studies in robustness of design algorithm against array element failure is proposed and discussed both in theory and experiment, then conclude the stability of NFMF array under various of focusing situations.

articleTitle: 2.4GHz Antenna for Deep Sea Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A 2.4GHz out-of-line series feed slot antenna is designed, manufactured and tested for deep sea communication link. The antenna was designed to perform under the extreme high pressure in sea water.

articleTitle: A Wideband Dielectric Resonator Antenna Fed by Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a design of a wideband Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) with a stable high gain is proposed. The antenna design covers 14 GHz of bandwidth (S11<-10 dB) for the frequency range from 26 GHz to 40 GHz while delivering a high gain of 6.8 dBi at broadside (at 36.5 GHz).

articleTitle: End-to-End Testing of Low Frequency Antennas in Highly Reflective Environments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: End-to-end measurements of the radiation performance of low gain antennas where the phase is not accessible, like on small space platforms, are challenging at low frequencies like 20-100 MHz because of the poor reflectivity of the measurement environments. To compensate for the non-ideal test scenarios, echo reduction schemes like modal filtering and time gating can only be applied to classic passive measurements, where the phase information is available. Moreover, such techniques are barely effective at such low frequencies because of reduced electrical size of the measurement environment. In this paper, a probe array working as plane wave generator is proposed to perform end-to-end characterization of low-frequency devices. The technique is based on a suitable optimization of complex coefficients of the probe array elements, generating a far field condition (i.e. approximate plane wave) over a finite testing volume called the quiet zone, while reducing the illumination of the chamber walls, and the hence the reflections.

articleTitle: Angular Response Analysis of Broadband RCS Reduction Checkerboard Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper examines the bistatic radar cross-section (RCS) reduction bandwidths of four checkerboard metasurfaces: a square-circle pair and a Jerusalem cross pair designed on Taconic TLY-3 substrate, another Jerusalem cross pair, and a simple cross-slotted cross pair designed on FR4 substrate. This is done by using simulations for various angles of incidence/scattering – from normal to 30°. The performance of each of these structures seems to be stable till 10° angle of incidence/scattering, with the square-circle pair being the only structure that is able to maintain a good fractional bandwidth up to a 30° angle of incidence. The other structures show a substantial reduction in bandwidth beyond 10°.

articleTitle: Combined Machine Learning- Inversion Scheme for Super-Resolution 3-Dimensional Microwave Human Brain Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: To realize three-dimensional (3-D) super-resolution whole brain imaging with a low high efficiency and computational cost, a new machine learning based-inversion method with the resolution enhancement technique is proposed in this work. This method consists three parts: a parallel semi-connected back-propagation neural network (SJ-BPNN) scheme, a U-Net scheme and a modified Akima segmented cubic Hermite interpolation (MASCHI) scheme. The parallel SJ-BPNN scheme is employed to map the measured scattering field data to the initial electrical properties distribution of human brain, firstly. Then, U-Net is used to improve the quality of preliminary reconstruction results obtained from SJ-BPNN. Finally, MASCHI scheme is adopted to greatly improve the resolution of reconstruction results with a very low computational cost. Numerical examples of normal human brain and human brain with abnormal scatterers show that the proposed model can achieve accurate human brain imaging with 1024×1024×1024 voxels resolution with a very low computational cost.

articleTitle: How Allen Taflove’s Left-Handed FDTD Code Helped Revolutionize Bioelectromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method has become a mainstay in bioelectromagnetic simulation. This paper is a tribute to Dr. Allen Taflove, describing the impact of FDTD on the bioelectromagnetics revolution.

articleTitle: Pattern Matching Approach for the Synthesis of Sub-Arrayed Linear Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel pattern matching-based methodology for the synthesis of subarrayed linear antenna arrays. A multi-step procedure that combines the k-means algorithm for defining the array partitions and the iterative projection method to find the best subarray excitations is proposed. A representative numerical result is discussed in order to highlight the improvements with respect to the state-of-the-art excitation matching-based approach.

articleTitle: A Discontinuous Galerkin Scheme for Transient Multiphysics Simulation of Organic Electrochemical Transistors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A time domain discontinuous Galerkin (DGTD)-based framework is developed to analyze three-dimensional organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs). The proposed framework uses a local DG scheme to discretize the (non-linearly) coupled system of the Poisson equation (in electric potential) and the drift-diffusion (DD) equations (in charge densities) in space. To reduce the computational requirements, a dual-mesh scheme, which uses a dense mesh for the DD equations and a much coarser mesh for the Poisson equation, is used. Furthermore, an implicit-explicit time integration scheme, which allows for a significantly larger time-step size, is utilized to efficiently account for the extremely long response time of OECTs. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the applicability and accuracy of the proposed solver.

articleTitle: Compact and Low-Profile Dual-Polarized Reconfigurable Antenna for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual polarized reconfigurable antenna for IoT applications is presented. The antenna can provide both vertically and horizontally polarized radiation thanks to the integration in the same structure of a segmented loop antenna and a wire-patch element. The compact and low-profile antenna structure, as well as the easy-to-control reconfiguration mechanism make the proposed antenna suitable for IoT applications.

articleTitle: A UWB Vivaldi Antenna for Time-Domain Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a UWB tapered Vivaldi Antenna for time domain radar applications. The proposed antenna has a hyperbolic cosine aperture profile which produces a smoother transition between the feeding slotline and the curved profile of the taper. Measurements results show that the impedance bandwidth is 0.8-9.93 GHz for the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> < 10 dB with an average peak gain in the end-fire direction greater than 3 dBi. These results are in good agreement with those obtained in simulation.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Modular Electromagnetic Skins for Multiple Blind Spot Coverage in Urban Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The importance of low-energy and sustainable solutions to improve the capacity and the quality of service in next-generation wireless communication systems has led to the introduction of the Smart Electromagnetic Environment (SEME) paradigm. One way to implement this concept is based on the use of electromagnetic skins (EMSs) that constitute completely passive devices able to redirect the electromagnetic (EM) signal from a base station towards the "blind-spots" in an urban scenario where the coverage would otherwise be limited or absent. To simplify the EMS manufacturing and installation, the EMS is composed of multiple independent tiles. The pairing of the EM field reflected from a specific tile towards a blind spot is carried out by means of a multi-objective genetic algorithm in order to optimize its layout and offer a set of trade-off solutions with coverage performance and EMS complexity.

articleTitle: A semi-analytical approach for FSS modelling in reverberating environments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This article proposes a semi-analytical model for the transmission parameter through a frequency selective surface (FSS) based on equivalent circuits. The circuit parameters are extracted from full-wave simulations. This article then proposes an evolution of those parameters as a function of the incident angle and the polarization. Finally, a model defining the mean transmission through an FSS in reverberating environment is proposed. The incident angle dependency of circuit parameters is well-modelled and in good agreement with full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Construction of Lumped Circuit Models from Full-Wave Simulations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A procedure for constructing lumped-element circuit models from a MOM simulation is outlined. The lumped element circuit topology is derived from port admittances computed in a MOM model by matching coefficients in the power series expansions of the circuit and MOM port admittances. The procedure is frequency-independent and stable. The resulting circuit model correctly captures both electric and magnetic field effects over a range of frequencies, including very low frequencies.

articleTitle: A Novel Broadband Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter Based on Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, two broadband symmetrical C-shaped linear-to-circular polarization converters (LCPC) are proposed. The reflection converter is composed of two metal layers separated by a dielectric substrate in the middle. The transmission converter consists of three metal layers which are separated by two dielectric substrates in a sandwich style. The surface metal layers of both converters have the shape of two C’s placed anti-symmetrically. The circularly-polarized (CP) wave can be obtained through the reflection or transmission converter excited by a linearly-polarized (LP) wave which has a tilted angle of 45° relative to the +x axis. The simulation results show that the converters have a good performance with a wide 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth and a low cross-polarization rate.

articleTitle: Mm-wave 3D-printed DRAs for Cost-effective Emerging 5G- and SatCom Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a demonstration for low cost dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) manufacturing, using 3D-printing technology for mm-wave applications. DRAs are high-efficient radiators, as compared to metallic antennas, especially at high frequency applications. Moreover, 3D-printing technology facilitates DRA machining and positioning on the printed circuit board. Two DRAs, designed at 20 GHz, and 30 GHz, are 3D-printed, and measured realizing good performance.

articleTitle: A Compact Filtenna for C-band applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a low profile filtenna designed for C-band applications. The proposed device exploits a rectangular patch antenna with parasites and directly connected to a compact filter, realized etching out properly designed spirals from the patch feeding line. The proposed structure is suitable for signals between 5.6 GHz to 5.8 GHz, such as DSRC at 5.8 GHz, rejecting WAVE at 5.9 GHz

articleTitle: A New Class of Multifunctional Reconfigurable Antenna With Continous Beam Steering Capability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new class of multifunctional reconfigurable antenna (MRA) technology that provides continuous beam steering capability at individual antenna level with low power consumption. A prototype MRA operating in the 28 GHz band that uses varactor diodes as interconnecting switches between its parasitic elements was designed by full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations. Simulated results demonstrate the continuous beam steering capability of the designed MRA. This new MRA technology has a simple architecture and consumes low power, thus it holds the potential to satisfy the antenna array performance requirements of fifth generation (5G) and beyond wireless systems with low cost and low power.

articleTitle: Compact Millimeter-Wave Antenna Operating in 28/38 GHz Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a compact wideband antenna operating in the 28 GHz and 38 GHz millimeter-wave spectrum. The proposed antenna is designed on the Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate. The proposed antenna has a simple geometry and compact dimensions of 17 mm × 12 mm × 0.79 mm. The antenna design is simulated using the ANSYS HFSS software. The features of the proposed antenna are also compared to similar designs from the literature, to demonstrate the potential of our antenna for use in the targeted frequency band. The results in the present paper indicate that our design is a good candidate for use in future wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Patch-Based Matrix-Free Time-Domain Method in 3D Unstructured Meshes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we propose a new time-domain method for solving Maxwell’s equations: Patch-based Matrix-Free Time Domain (P-MFTD) method, in unstructured meshes. This method is free of matrix solutions regardless of the element shape used for discretization. Meanwhile, it avoids the use of higher-order 3-D vector basis functions, and hence significantly reduces the number of unknowns required to solve the same problem. Moreover, its time-domain stability is guaranteed featuring real-valued eigenvalues despite an unsymmetrical numerical system. Numerical experiments have validated its accuracy, efficiency, and stability.

articleTitle: Non Invasive Glucose Detection with Rectangular Dielectric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (RDRA) has been designed for the non-invasive method of glucose checking. This antenna sensor uses an Alumina Ceramic dielectric resonator fed by a 50-ohm microstrip line. In this proposed sensor, the thumb will be placed on the dielectric resonator which causes changes in input impedance which is proportional to the change of the blood permittivity on different glucose concentration. When we placed the thumb on the sensor there will be a shift in the resonance frequency. The sensor was simulated on the CST simulation software. The 3D electromagnetic model of thumb has also been simulated using a Cole-Cole model. A shift of the resonant frequency is observed as the concentration of glucose gets higher. The size of the sensor is 60X60x1.75 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> which make it suitable for the handheld use.

articleTitle: A Robust Approach for Electromagnetic Simulation of S-parameters of Microstrip Circuits and Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a general-purpose and robust approach for extracting the S-parameters of microwave circuits and antennas. A key feature of the proposed technique is that it is robust, being independent of the nature of excitation and choice of matched termination. The paper describes the approach and presents results for test geometries to illustrate the efficacy of the technique.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Nano-Optical Isolators Based on Irregular Arrangements of Dielectric Rods
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Design and optimization of efficient and compact nano-optical isolators based on irregular arrays of dielectric rods are presented. These designs allow electromagnetic waves to propagate in single direction and prevent them from propagating in the opposite direction. This way, high forward transmission is achieved, while the main source is protected from reflected waves. Effective optimization algorithms are integrated with the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA), a fast and accurate full-wave numerical solver, to design efficient isolators composed of different arrangements of dielectric elements with controlled forward and backward transmissions.

articleTitle: Gain and Directivity Enhancement for Multiband Metasurface Antennas for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A method to enhance gain and directivity of multiband microstrip antenna is proposed using periodic metasurface on the ground plane. The closed form relations are derived and verified via 3D electromagnetic simulation. The antenna performance has been studied by changing periodic metasurface structure using SRRs on the ground plane. It has been shown that the proposed method enhances the gain and directivity of the multiband antenna structure. It is also observed that the periodic metasurface structure can be used as a knob to adjust the bandwidth of the antenna at the frequency of interest.

articleTitle: Spatial Maps of Reactive Energy Density around Antenna Arrays: An EM Lagrangian Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present an EM Lagrangian based approach to quantify the distribution of reactive energy density around generic antennas, specifically multi-port excited arrays. FDTD-computed electric and magnetic field values are first used to obtain EM Lagrangian density in the antenna near-field, which is further time-averaged to obtain spatial patterns of capacitive/inductive reactive energy density. We demonstrate the significant alterations in reactive energy density distributions for thin-wire dipole based arrays, considering different port-excitation conditions and use of parasitic reflectors/directors.

articleTitle: High precision monitoring system by satellite signal reflector
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In conventional geological disaster monitoring, the contradiction between the cost and precision has always been a concern. In this paper, we propose a remote monitoring system by a reflector. Concretely, a reflector is designed to transmit the satellite signals received from the monitored site to the stationary base station through the wireless transmission. Then uses signals from different antennas to establish a double-difference model. So as to realize low-cost remote monitoring. The experimental results show that when the reflector signal transmission distance is 0.2km, the monitoring accuracy of the system is within 3cm.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Transmit and Receive Technology for Radar Cross Section Reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Radar cross section (RCS) reduction using a simultaneous transmit and receive technique is discussed. The comparison between freestanding dipoles and dipole arrays to dipole arrays backed by a ground plane is used to demonstrate the benefits of this approach. The technique uses a feedback-based beamformer to radiate part of the received signal in the monostatic direction with a phase and amplitude shift to reduce monostatic RCS. Additionally, a study is conducted to determine the sensitivity of this technique for all dipole configurations. It is found that there is a tradeoff of radiation efficiency for RCS reduction bandwidth and field-of-regard.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual Circular-Polarized Shaped-Beam Reflectarray Antenna Using SVR
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the design of a shaped-beam reflectarray working in dual circular polarization (CP) with an isoflux pattern for global Earth coverage. The dual-CP capabilities are achieved using a unit cell based on a linear polarization (LP) Jerusalem cross plus an integrated LP-to-CP polarizer. Surrogate models based on support vector regression of the unit cell for several angles of incidence are trained and used in a direct layout optimization to obtain the design of the reflectarray that produces the desired shaped beam.

articleTitle: Enhancements of BST Thin Film Varactors with SmScO3 Buffer Layer on Sapphire Substrate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This study analyzes the effects of adding a SmScO3 (SSO) buffer layer to the sapphire substrate for barium strontium titanate (BST) thin film varactors. The varactors are fabricated on SSO buffered sapphire substrates at two different electrode and BST thicknesses. The devices are tested from 0 to 40 GHz, applying a DC bias. capacitance vs voltage, and Q vs voltage were obtained from the swept frequency scattering parameters. The study also demonstrates an overall higher tuning ratio and competitive Q for the SSO buffered devices.

articleTitle: Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna for Tri-Band Array Environment with Radome
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A multi-layer Fabry-Perot cavity antenna (FPCA) for increased boresight directivity is proposed for a high-band (HB) (3.4 – 4.2 GHz) array in a tri-band array environment with dielectric radome. Upon excitation of the HB dipoles in the baseline design, the radome behaves as a partially reflecting surface (PRS) which introduces reflected waves that destructively interfere with the incident wave at boresight at 4.1 GHz and 4.2 GHz. The superposition of these waves results in unacceptable boresight attenuation, leading to a reduction in the boresight directivity. The proposed FPCA reduces the boresight attenuation at 4.1 GHz and 4.2 GHz, thereby increasing the boresight directivity. The proposed technique shows a peak improvement in boresight directivity at 4.2 GHz from 10.3 dBi to 14.0 dBi, a 3.7 dB improvement, and a reduction in cross-polar radiation.

articleTitle: Balanced Near-Field Applicator for Controlled Microwave Tissue Exposure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a near-field applicator for monitoring microwave exposure of tissue samples on an inverted microscope also used for optical studies of these samples. The applicator operates at X-band (8-12 GHz) and employs low-cost fabrication technology such as printed circuit board (PCB) and 3D printing. Using a symmetrical dual-horn antenna, an almost-identical near-field distribution can be achieved on both ends of the applicator. With a diode detector array observation board on the control end, we can estimate and monitor the power at the tissue surface under exposure by symmetry. Measurement results of the initial prototype show agreement with simulations within 0.9 dB.

articleTitle: An Electronically-Controlled Frequency-Tunable Antenna Element Based on LTCC
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A 12-layer liquid crystal antenna element is proposed based on the Low-Temperature Co-fired Ceramic (LTCC) technology. The antenna element consists of fractal patch antenna combined with a slot-coupled feeding form and electronically-tunable liquid crystal. Simulation results show that it can effectively work in the frequency range of 17 22 GHz with a center frequency of 19.25 GHz and its tunable−frequency range is more than 2.0 GHz. Also, the return loss is greater than 15 dB during the tuning process, indicating a very good impedance matching. By controlling the radiation of elements, the gain of array can be adjusted conveniently and efficiently.

articleTitle: Self-Decoupled MIMO Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array Using Higher-Order Mode
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a self-decoupled circularly polarized (CP) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array is implemented using the higher-order mode. Specifically, the orthogonal TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">113</inf>(x) and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">113</inf>(y) modes are excited in the active DRA by a crossed slot to generate a CP field, while the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">112</inf>(x/y) modes are excited in the adjacent passive DRA due to the near-field coupling of the active DRA. In this case, the energy cannot get to the receiving port of the passive DRA through the slot because the field intensity of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">112</inf>(x/y) modes is rather weak there. As a result, a high isolation level of 47.1 dB is achieved without requiring any additional decoupling structure.

articleTitle: Dual-band, Aperture-Sharing Matching Network consisting of Separated Ground Layers and Via Posts for millimeter-wave Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes an aperture-sharing, dual-band matching network for patch antennas which exhibits near-identical far-field radiation characteristics at both frequencies. The patch antenna topology resembles that of a rudimentary single-resonance structure. The separated ground layers and connecting via posts introduce an additional L-shaped impedance matching circuit, enabling independent adjustment of resonant frequencies without using lumped components. The dual-band operation of the proposed dual-band patch antenna is ascertained experimentally, achieving the realized gain of 5.2 dBi (28.0 GHz) and 5.4 dBi (39.0 GHz). Beam scanning capabilities of 1×4 phased array antennas are verified with the integration of mmWave beamforming circuits. This investigation is expected to applicable in low-profile and highly-integrated mobile devices where the allocated antenna volume is extremely restricted.

articleTitle: Volume Equivalence Formulation of Characteristic Modes in One-Dimensional Inhomogeneous Media
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Characteristic modes of layered dielectric media are studied using a volumetric integral equation formulation. Power conservation predicts only two radiating characteristic modes in this class of problems. Example calculations illustrate the characteristic mode behavior of an oblique-incidence quarterwave transformer and a symmetric graded index layer. Results indicate correlation of reflection properties with modal degeneracies, rather than modal resonance.

articleTitle: An Early History of the Design and Development of the Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Almost 40 years after the initial development of the dielectric resonator antenna, a large number of variations based on the original design have been proposed, and some recently integrated into modern telecommunications equipment. As a class of radiators, they have been shown to be efficient at high frequencies with relatively large bandwidths. An early history of the design and development of this antenna is presented to document the processes which led to the original innovation.

articleTitle: Preconditioned Potential-Based Surface Integral Method for Modeling Lossy Conductors From DC to High Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A potential-based integral equation formulation is presented for accurately modeling the skin effect from DC to high frequencies. A preconditioning strategy is developed for the efficient iterative solution of the resulting system of equations. Realistic numerical examples demonstrate (a) the accuracy of the formulation, and (b) the effectiveness of the preconditioner for a wide range of frequencies and mesh densities.

articleTitle: A Broadband and Dual-Polarized Base Station Antenna with Absorbing Structure for LTE/5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband and dual-polarized antenna with absorbing structure for LTE/5G base station applications. The radiator of the proposed antenna is composed of two pairs of crossed printed dipoles, which are fed by Y-shaped baluns. Designing four absorbing structures are used to improve the front-to-rear ratio of the antenna. The proposed antenna has an overall size of λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> × λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> × 0.257λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> is the freespace wavelength at 3.0 GHz). The simulated results show that the bandwidth of this antenna achieves 47% (2.36~3.77 GHz) for S11/S22<-10dB and S21<-28dB, and a half-power beam width (HPBW) is 84±10 during the working bands. The antenna gain attains 7.55±0.35 dBi with a good stable radiation pattern. Therefore, the designed antenna is suitable for future LTE/5G base station antenna systems.

articleTitle: AoA effects in outdoor V2I parking environments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: As millimeter wave (mmWave) communication systems become an alternative solution to achieve higher transfer rates and lower latencies, they also induce channel degradations associated with their implementation. In this work, vehicular density impact over multipath contributions in a parking lot scenario is analyzed. The horizontal angle-of-arrival (AoA) information is presented and its relationship with five different vehicle densities is extracted. The angular dispersion is assessed by means of the AoA standard deviation and key representations of the channel characteristics are examined.

articleTitle: Dielectric Constant Estimation Using Calibration-Free Reflected Voltage Measurements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a waveguide-based dielectric sensing technique for the measurement of the relative permittivity of planar low-loss materials is presented. The material under test (MUT), assumed to be thicker than one half of wavelength (λg/2), is sandwiched between the waveguide’s aperture and a matched load. The reflected voltage magnitude is measured at the waveguide’s input port by relying on a custom-built reflectometer. The measured reflected voltage values are then used to calculate the dielectric constant of the MUT over the waveguide’s operating frequency range. The proposed method offers a major advantage of not requiring pre-calibration. This technique is tested on multiple material samples where accurate estimates of their respective dielectric constant values are obtained.

articleTitle: On the Effect of Scaling an Array of Complementary Split Ring Resonators (CSRRs) in the Ground Plane of a Single Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Recently, there has been a significant amount of research on the use of split-ring resonators (SRRs) for their implementation in wave guides, antennas, and transmission lines for filtering, miniaturization, and sensing. In the design of the split ring resonators in transmission lines and antennas, there is not a clear technique that directly equates the dimensions of the SRRs to the equivalent circuit shown in literature. This paper investigates the change in S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> of a patch antenna when the ground plane of the antenna is defected with an array differently sized split ring resonators.

articleTitle: Passive and Active Metasurfaces Enabling New Functionalities for Smart EM Environments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The aim of this contribution is to review some recent applications of metasurfaces and cast them in the scenario of next-generation wireless systems. In particular, we show their potentialities in overcoming some detrimental effects presented by the environment in wireless communications, and discuss their crucial role towards the practical implementation of a smart electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: Efficient Evaluation of Volume Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present the application of the simplex-product quadrature method to the singular interaction integrals found in the Galerkin discretisation of volume integral equations. We will show the benefit of a significantly reduced assembly time while still achieving the same level of accuracy when using the simplex-product quadrature compared to classical quadrature.

articleTitle: Toward a Fully-Coupled Semiclassical Model of Transmon Control Dynamics: Classical Case
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In superconducting circuit quantum systems, transmon qubits are typically controlled through applying classical microwave pulses on a transmission line capacitively coupled to the qubit. In order to design a pulse that achieves the desired result, modeling the coupled dynamics of the transmission line and transmon is necessary. Existing models consider the dynamics of both portions of the system, but often fail to account for effects such as the back-action of each subsystem on the other. This work begins to study this effect using a 1-D finite element time-domain solution to the equations governing the transmission line flux and transmon phase in a fully classical treatment, which will be extended to a full-wave semiclassical model in a future work.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Bluetooth Low Energy AoA Estimation System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation system based on Bluetooth low energy (BLE) using a uniform linear array (ULA). In the implementation, we first propose the phase compensation algorithm and the phase prediction method to reduce the phase offset caused by the signal frequency offset (SFO). Next, we use the super-resolution algorithm combined with the direct path identification algorithm to obtain an accurate AoA estimate of the line-of-sight (LoS) path. Experimental results show that the system can achieve a median AoA error of 2.7° in an indoor environment.

articleTitle: Digital Metasurface Reflectarray Antenna for 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A high gain digital metasurface reflectarray antenna for 5G applications is proposed using a single layered one bit digital metamaterial unit cell. The unit cell is a split square with a pair of metallic strips connecting the outer ring. The unit cell provides the two quantized phase states with 180 phase shift and low insertion loss resulting in one bit digital phase profile. This one bit digital phase distribution is employed to design a 9.7 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> × 9.7 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</inf> metasurface surface reflector. The digital metasurface reflect array is centrally feed by the source antipodal Vivaldi antenna to design high gain digital metasurface reflector array antenna. The designed reflect array antenna achieves a broadside gain of 18.7 dBi at 38 GHz with a low cross polarization level of less than -18 dBi respectively.

articleTitle: Compact Two-Stage Origami Horn Antenna for Terahertz CubeSat Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of high-speed satellite communication networks enabled by dense constellations in space, CubeSats are expected to be more compact than ever while maintaining large bandwidth operation. A candidate enabler for high-data-rate CubeSat constellations is the terahertz (THz) band (0.1-10 THz), which supports both compactness and large bandwidth.
