These two come at the cost of high propagation losses and impose the use of very high gain directional antennas, which on their turn drastically impact otherwise simple tasks such as neighbor discovery and broadcasting with nearby satellites. To simultaneously alleviate the challenges of neighbor discovery while overcoming the high path losses in long links, a THz origami horn antenna utilizing commercially-available WR4 waveguide is presented. The proposed antenna has two stages supporting phases of neighbor discovery and high-data-rate communication. The two stages demonstrate gains of 15.7 dBi and 30.7 dBi, respectively, at 218 GHz. The horn antenna is explored as a solution for enabling CubeSat swarms at terahertz frequencies.

articleTitle: Printed dipole MIMO pair for mobile platforms in mm-Wave communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A MIMO dipole pair is designed for mobile devices in mm-Wave communications by extending a single dipole antenna. Two of such MIMO dipole pairs are proposed and studied to maximize the diversity performances of the mobile devices in terms of envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) and mean effective gain (MEG).

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable 28/38 GHz Omni-directional Antenna Design for Future 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a simple and compact reconfigurable monopole omni-directional antenna operating at 28 and 38GHz for 6G applications. The proposed antenna has a wideband with dual-band operating characteristics. Two monopole antennas are printed on a substrate and connected through a PIN diode to achieve a dual-band operation. By changing the biasing of the PIN diode, different operational frequencies 28GHz and 38GHz bands are achieved. The proposed antenna is simulated using two different electromagnetic solvers, where an excellent agreement between both simulated results is achieved.

articleTitle: Study of Unbalanced MACKEY using Inverted F Antenna as feed element
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: ACKEY, which is sufficiently robust to metal objects, has been developed [1]. Here, an unbalanced MACKEY with an inverted F antenna for the part of the feed element using the dipole antenna of a conventional MACKEY is proposed.

articleTitle: High Gain Beamsteerable Metasurface Lens Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A compact high gain phase-gradient metasurface lens (MSL) antenna with end loaded cross dipole slot as unit cell is proposed for millimeter-wave beamsteering applications. The proposed unit cell is transmission-type and is insensitive to polarization and oblique angle of incidence. A MSL is designed using 25 × 25 array of unit cells having an overall size of 7 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 7 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.23 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The steered beams at 0°, ±15°, and ±30° is achieved by exciting the MSL using three different feed sources at an offset of 0 mm, ±7.5 mm and ±15 mm from the center along ± x-axis. The feed source is kept at 20 mm focal distance beneath the designed MSL having a f/D ratio of 0.27. Full 3-dB spatial beam coverage of 60° (± 30°) is achieved with a gain tolerance of 1 dB and a maximum gain of 18.4 dBi in the broadside direction showing a gain enhancement of 11.9 dB.

articleTitle: Advanced Antenna Modelling Tool for Performance Verification and Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A development project of a new software tool for uncertainty quantification (UQ) of an antenna’s performance caused by the stochastic behaviour of design variables of the system has been performed within the ESA Contract No. AO/1-10116/19/NL/AS. The mathematical algorithms implemented in the tool allow for a very general formulation, where uncertainty can be added to both geometrical and electrical parameters of the system. An application case is given and the results are compared to reference solutions.

articleTitle: Deployable Tightly Coupled Dipole Reflectarray for Small Satellites
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An origami-based, dual-polarized, ultra-wideband (UWB) tightly coupled dipole reflectarray is presented for small satellite applications. The reflectarray is designed on a multilayer, rigid-flexible substrate for seamless and efficient unfolding during deployment. The presented concept takes advantage of the UWB performance offered by tightly coupled dipole arrays (TCDAs) while eliminating the need for feeding networks and coaxial cables. In this manner, complexity and weight are decreased. Notably, the design employs horizontal dipoles connected to meander delay lines to achieve a low-profile. Overall, the proposed unit cell design provides stable phase delays across the 0.7-2.25 GHz (3.2:1) band while maintaining VSWR< 2.

articleTitle: A Study of Beam Scanning Scheme for IRS-Assisted 5G Millimeter-Wave Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting Surface (IRS) is a promising technology to reduce coverage holes of millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications in the fifth-generation mobile communication systems (5G). By reflecting incident signals from a base station (BS) toward a user in coverage holes, the IRS enables to increase the received signals power of the user, which requires an appropriate selection of the passive beam of the IRS. In this paper, the beam scanning scheme for IRS-assisted 5G mmWave networks is proposed to earlier determine the best beam than the exhaustive scanning scheme based on the conventional 5G beam management. The proposed scheme scans the coverage of the BS and that of the IRS based on the ratio of the area of the coverage of BS to that of IRS. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme determines the best beam for the user in the coverage of IRS earlier than exhaustive scanning scheme.

articleTitle: A 4x4 Planar UWB-MIMO Antenna with Dual Linear Polarization for WLAN/5G/WiFi/X-band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a 4 × 4 planar ultra-wideband multiple-input multiple-output (UWB-MIMO) antenna with a compact size of 29.28 mm × 29.28 mm × 1 mm. The antenna employs a defected ground structure-assisted bandwidth improvement approach for achieving ultra-wideband operating bandwidth. Within the frequency range of 4.7 to 22 GHz, the isolation level of the proposed antenna is less than 20.5 dB. The envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is good enough, less than 0.0027 with the diversity gain (DG) being nearly 10. All scenarios were simulated using CST Studio 2020. The proposed antenna was manufactured and tested. The test and simulation results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Wide-Incidence Angle and Polarisation Insensitive Transparent Metasurface for 5G Outdoor to Indoor Coverage Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wide-incident angle and polarisation insensitive transparent metasurface is presented for 5G outdoor to indoor coverage enhancement. In order to predict the structural geometry of the unit cell, the Genetic Algorithm (GA) has been applied. The proposed unit cell is arranged in a periodic structure to construct the transmission surface consisting of tow transparent layers of Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) mounted on both sides of Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) substrate. The proposed transmission metasurface can be simply coated on a glassy windows to empower the outdoor to indoor 5G signals.

articleTitle: Ultra Thin Dual-Polarized Flexible Patch Antenna for the 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: a flexible dual-polarized patch antenna with an extremely low-profile design, operating at 28GHz is presented for millimeter wave mobile communication. This patch antenna design is using a capacitive feed and parasitic element to improve the bandwidth and gain, and it is only 202 um thick. The single element patch antenna covers 26.6-28.5 GHz and exhibits almost the same boresight radiation pattern over the entire bandwidth with an average gain of 6.5 dBi and 12.3 dBi for the array antenna. The array element shows a -10 dB reflection coefficient with a wide bandwidth that covers a 2.4 GHz bandwidth from 26.6 GHz to 29 GHz. The results prove that proposed antennas have high potential in the fifth generation (5G).

articleTitle: 3-D Printed W-band Substrate Integrated Waveguide Filter Using a Dam-and-Fill Process
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a new approach to fabricating substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filters. The method relies on additive manufacturing (3-D fabrication) using aerosol-jet printing (AJP). The design of a W-band bandpass filter is presented to demonstrate the strength of the proposed process. The SIW structures are fabricated using an AJP by printing dielectrics (Polyimide and Benzocyclobutene) and conductors (Silver). The proposed process allows for the fabrication of single and multi-layer SIW structures. Here, the design of a single layer bandpass filter with a center frequency of 81 GHz and bandwidth of 6% is presented, along with details of the dam-and-fill process.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhanced Equal-Split Planar Knochel-Mayer Power Divider Capable of High Power Handling for Antenna Feed Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A planar 2-way equal-split in-phase power divider/combiner with broadband characteristics and capable of high power handling is presented in this paper. The proposed design uses a modified Knochel-Mayer structure to enable heatsinking and design flexibility of the isolation resistors, while extending the bandwidth of the design. A 2-way power divider/combiner prototype operating in the S-band is designed and fabricated in microstrip, exhibiting a bandwidth of 50% and an average power handling capability of 10 W. The measured results of the prototype show good agreement with full-wave EM simulation and the power handling capability was experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Radiation Beam Steering Using A Microfluidically Reconfigurable Metasurface Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A fluidically reconfigurable metasurface (MSF) is presented in this paper in order to achieve radiation beam steering with enhanced gain. A simple square ring resonator structure is used as the unit cell for the superstrate layer and a probe-fed microstrip patch antenna is used as the radiator. The microfluidic channels are implemented inside a 3D printed polylactic acid (PLA) substrate and gallium liquid metal alloy (LMA) is injected in the microfluidic channels to switch the radiation pattern in the elevation plane from broadside to ± 20°. The proposed metasurface antenna exhibits a constant fractional bandwidth greater than 7.5% in all states of reconfiguration. The maximum realized gain remains greater than 7.2 dBi. The simulated gain and bandwidth of the proposed structure are greater than those of a conventional patch antenna, making it a good candidate for certain 5G, cellular base station, and satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: MmWave channel propagation modeling in 5G high-dense wireless networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In a near future perspective, fully connected ubiquitous smart environments will involve numerous wireless communication systems operating simultaneously in heterogeneous networks. This paradigm will require fast, reliable, and secure user services and applications, accessible anytime and anyplace, regardless the devices, networks, or systems they use. For that purpose, adequate, efficient, and effective millimeter wave channel propagation modeling for 5G high-node scenarios is pivotal, in order to prevent communication limitations such as coverage, capacity, or channel interferences due to channel restrictions at these frequency bands. In this work, the densification impact characterization of 5G FR2 communication systems operating in an indoor complex heterogeneous environment is analyzed, by means of deterministic simulation techniques and empirical validation. These results and the proposed simulation methodology can lead in an adequate millimeter wave channel characterization, which provide suitable information for the overall network performance in complex heterogeneous high-node context-aware environments.

articleTitle: Antenna Array for Wireless Power Transfer to Deep-Brain Implants
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Implantable medical devices, enabled by continually reducing the size of integrated circuits, offer therapeutic solutions to many intreatable disorders. Yet, the large battery size and short lifetime remain a major challenge. In this work, we present a microwave transmitting array (4×4) operating at 2.1 GHz that focuses propagating fields inside the brain tissue. This mode of transmission enables reaching deep in the brain. Analytical derivation of the efficiency is used to conjugate-match the phase of TX elements. A high power transfer efficiency of 0.91% is achieved when a 2×2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> implanted power receiver is located 5 cm away from the TX array.

articleTitle: Novel Ka-Band Phase Shifter Design Based on Vanadium Dioxide Switches for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel design for a phase shifter at Kaband on silicon and in coplanar wave guide (CPW) is presented. The proposed design incorporates a novel configuration of vanadium dioxide (VO2) switches. A set of two shunt and two series VO2 single pole single throw (SPST) switches are configured to be controlled via a single thermal actuator. The proposed design reduces the number of thermal actuators by a factor of four. Ultimately, the proposed design demonstrates a low maximum insertion loss of 6.5 dB with 32 selectable phase shifts and consistent phase response over the range of 37-40 GHz.

articleTitle: Measurement and Modeling of Millimeter Wave Channel in Indoor Scenario at 26 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an 8*8 phased array antenna is used to conduct measurement campaigns in the 26GHz frequency band in an indoor scenario. Based on the measured data, the typical channel parameters such as delay, power, angle of arrival, and angle of departure are clustered. The measurements captured the spatial properties of millimeter-wave (mm-wave) propagation with a center frequency of 26 GHz. After analyzing the data using K-means clustering algorithm, A CDL model was built for the indoor scenario, which is useful for the design and performance evaluation of Millimeter wave wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Averaged Adaptive Cross Approximation with Schur Complement Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A modified form of the adaptive cross approximation (ACA) was proposed for certain structured matrices for which the original ACA fails. The formulation of the modified ACA algorithm is reconsidered, and a new inversion method based on the Schur Complement decomposition is presented.

articleTitle: Design of a Conical Spiral Antenna with 3D Printing Enabled Cavity and Radome
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A cavity-integrated conical spiral antenna is designed for instantaneous operation in the 2 to 8 GHz range. The antenna has stable unidirectional radiation with high front to back ratio, axial ratio < 2 dB, and efficiency greater than 75%. A hemispherical radome and conical RF grounding post with internal bundle feed are added to ensure the antenna is representative of and ruggedized for in-field use. The antenna is designed for manufacturing with 3D printing.

articleTitle: SIW-based Concurrent Triple Frequency Active Integrated Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based triple frequency active integrated antenna (AIA) has been proposed. Firstly, by incorporating a defected structure on a SIW section, a narrow two-pole bandpass response is obtained, and this technique is fundamentally followed for designing a triplexer. By simple modification of the triplexer geometry i.e., with the formation of three distinct radiating edges, a self-triplexing antenna is formed. This triplexing antenna is used in feedback with active transistors to give rise to concurrent triple frequency oscillation, thereby forming the concurrent triple frequency active integrated antenna structure. This type of active integrated antenna is suitable for multi-frequency radar or sensor applications.

articleTitle: Numerical Dispersion Compensation for FDTD via Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A hybrid deep neural network consisting of convolutional layers and LSTM structures is developed for compensating for the numerical dispersion error in FDTD. The proposed network is designed for the wideband computation of S-parameters of planar microwave circuits at coarse meshes. Without dispersion compensation, the accuracy of these computations is severely compromised. We show that deep learning can restore the accuracy to the level obtained by dense mesh simulations.

articleTitle: TM Polarized Plane Wave Scattering by a Window on a Thick Conducting Wall
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Kirchhoff approximation has been applied to analyze a plane wave scattering by a rectangular loaded hole on the thick conducting wall. The scattering fields can be derived as radiation fields from equivalent magnetic currents on a virtually closed aperture of the hole. This formulation may be used for estimating the scattering by a window glass and the effect has been discussed.

articleTitle: Analytical Comparison of Electromagnetic Pulse Propagation in Normal and Malignant Breast Tissues
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Experimentally measured dielectric data for normal and malignant breast tissues, which are represented by respective single pole Cole-Cole models, are utilized in an asymptotic analysis of the propagated field in chirped Gaussian pulse propagation. The accuracy of the obtained asymptotic description is compared and verified with purely numerical results. This asymptotic approach provides increased analytical insight regarding the dependence of the propagated field dynamics on the input field and breast tissue parameters and upon the propagation distance. Moreover, it enables an analytical comparison of the electromagnetic response of healthy versus cancerous breast tissues.

articleTitle: Wideband Miniaturized Multi-Port Correlator for 5G Applications at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel symmetric multi-port correlator using 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> circular hybrid couplers is proposed at the center frequency of 28 GHz. The work is focused on designing the multi-port circuit on a low thickness and low dielectric constant substrate (Rogers RT/Duroid 5880). The circuit is suited to realize a low-cost architecture and integrate with antennas for mm-wave applications. Due to the structure, this design can be implemented without any additional off-chip components. Moreover, the octagonal structure minimized the overall size of the circuit while providing enough space to solder 8 connectors. The performance of the designed structure is assessed via full-wave computer simulation technology (CST) and Advanced Design System (ADS). As simulation results show the proposed compact size multi-port network has a good fractional bandwidth of 28.6% from 24 to 32 GHz and superb phase resolution at four output ports.

articleTitle: A Fast AWE-Augmented Wideband Discontinuous Galerkin Frequency-Domain Method in Solving Electromagnetic Wave Equations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this research, a discontinuous Galerkin frequency-domain (DGFD) method is proposed to solve the electromagnetic wave equations. Different to the explicit time-domain analysis, the electric-field and magnetic-field in frequency-domain wave equations are coupled together implicitly, thus the established matrix equation is globally coupled, which is computational expensive if solving it directly. To address this issue, a Block-diagonal preconditioner and a restriction operator are applied to the matrix equation, which splits the global matrix into a number of small local matrix systems pertinent to each subdomain. Then, a direct solver can be employed to solve them with a FETI-like procedure. Besides, to further speed up the wideband analysis, the asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) is implemented into the DGFD solver, which only needs to calculate a few frequency points in a broadband. To benchmark the proposed algorithm, a SIW filter is investigated.

articleTitle: Reflectarray Power Handling Capability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The work surveys power breakdown effects that are relevant for reflectarray antennas used for wireless power transfer and proposes methodologies to analyze a reflectarray design for them. The effects the paper considers are the multipactor effect and electrical breakdown ionization effect of air (i.e. the corona discharge). These effects are analyzed using the commercial solver SPARK3D for a reflectarray unit cell using a split-ring resonator. The paper also presents a flux analysis to translate the unit cell results to the output feed power.

articleTitle: A Meander Line-Based Frequency Selective Surface for Strain Sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) are periodic arrays of conductive elements that have distinct reflection and transmission responses. In this work, an FSS sensor designed to operate in Ka-band to measure a wide range of uni-directional strain using a meander line-based unit cell is presented. Specifically, the proposed unit cell of the sensor consists of a convoluted meander line geometry designed on a thin dielectric substrate. Strain sensing is achieved by monitoring the change in the resonant frequency of the FSS when under strain that is parallel to an interrogating signal linearly polarized and aligned with the convoluted dimension of the meander line element. Simulation results of strain measurement over two ranges, small- (0% - 0.5%) and large-scale (0% - 5%), are presented. The simulated results indicate that the sensitivity of the sensor to small-scale strain is 21 MHz/0.1% strain and 230 MHz/1.0% strain for large-scale.

articleTitle: Design of A Novel Reconfigurable WBH Film Bulk Acoustic Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel reconfigurable film bulk acoustic resonator (FBAR) based on crystallographically oriented W-type barium hexaferrite (WBH) BaZn<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16-x</inf>Sc<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">27</inf> thin film is proposed. The structure is based on three-stage series capacitors and the total capacitance is changed by controlling the static bias voltages. The FBAR is simulated, manufactured and measured. Based on the measured results, the proposed FBAR has achieved the resonant frequency in the Ka frequency band. The proposed FBAR can be applied in the millimeter wave region of the 5G communication circuits and systems.

articleTitle: Microwave Profiling of Multiple Buried Scatterers with Arbitrary Curvilinear Shapes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The quantitative microwave profiling of buried dielectric objects with arbitrary curvilinear cross-sections, is addressed in this paper. As the problem is highly non-linear, the Covariance Matrix Adoption Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES), as a global stochastic optimization algorithm is implemented. Having the limited amount of measured data in these scenarios, it is very vital to reduce the number of problem unknowns, especially for modelling the curvilinear shapes. Here, the cubic-spline expansion is utilized to model the scatterer shape, using few numbers of unknowns. Moreover, an initialization step using diffraction tomography method is used to approximately detect the permittivity values and locations of scatterers and as a result reduce the search domain. The numerical results show that the proposed algorithm can acceptably retrieve two closely located high-contrast objects, using fewer number of unknowns, compared to previously reported partitioned search space techniques.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of RFID System for Detecting and Sorting Baggage in Airports
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a radio-frequency-identification (RFID) system which can accurately detect the position of moving baggages and sort them on the conveyer belts of airports. The system mainly consists of the chipped tag, reader, and signal processing algorithm with a machine learning based classifier. To improve the transmitting and receiving efficiency and the coverage range of the tag, the antenna is designed as a winding around the chip in the center and it is also circularly polarized. Since there exist interference and noise in signals, the support vector machine (SVM), decision tree, and neural network are used for signal processing so as to enhance the accuracy and reliability of the system. The system is extensively tested by experiments and its good performance has been validated.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Monitoring Using Electromagnetic Sensors – A Tribute to the memory of Professor Safieddin Safavi-Naeini
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a brief overview on the research about non-invasive blood glucose monitoring using electromagnetic sensors conducted at the Centre for Intelligent Antenna and Radio Systems (CIARS) at University of Waterloo. Professor Safieddin Safavi-Naeini was the founder and director of CIARS since 2004 till he passed away in October 2021. Under his leadership and vision, a variety of non-invasive sensing techniques were developed for reliably monitoring the blood glucose levels of clinical relevance to diabetes using the non-ionizing electromagnetic radiations of no hazards when penetrating the body. The sensing structures and devices introduced in this research were designed to operate in specific frequency spectrums that promise a reliable and sensitive glucose detection from centimeter- to millimeter-wave bands. Particularly, three different technologies were proposed and investigated: Complementary Split-Ring Resonators (CSRRs), Whispering Gallery Modes (WGMs) sensors, and millimeter-Wave Radars.

articleTitle: Developments on Imaging and Velocimetry of Dynamic Two-Phase Flows with Electrical Capacitance Tomography Sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Electrical capacitance tomography (ECT) based imaging and velocimetry methods are demonstrated for two-phase dynamical flows involving gas-oil and air-water mixtures. We consider two extended ECT modalities in particular. Electrical capacitance volume tomography (ECVT) is applied for electrically non-conducting flows such as gas-oil, whereas displacement-current phase tomography (DCPT) is applied for conducting flows such as air-water. In addition, gas flow rates are calculated from the reconstructed image and velocity profile, and compared to the actual gas flow rate.

articleTitle: A Frequency Shift Key Radar Approach for the Reconstruction of Flexible Phased Array Geometry
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new method for determining inter-element spacing in flexible phased arrays is presented here. Specifically, a Frequency Shift Key (FSK) radar approach is combined with a single-frequency phase shift measurement. When tested with two probe-fed patch antennas, the method estimates the distance between elements within 12% of a wavelength for all tested distances and within 0.8% for antenna spacing over half a wavelength. This paper can serve as the foundation for future investigation into FSK and phase-based geometry reconstruction techniques.

articleTitle: Investigating the Optimal Quadrature for Recovering the Full Steradian Scattering Pattern with MIDAS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In the present paper, we investigate the optimal quadrature to retrieve the full-direction scattering behavior of a realistic arbitrarily-shaped ice particle, from a limited number of pre-calculated incident directions. Our motivation is to enable accurate recovery of single scattering properties of realistic hydrometeors at any incident direction, or equivalently particle orientation, from scattering databases that have been built with our 3D full-wave model MIDAS, at a reasonable computational cost, both in terms of calculation time and storage. Finding the optimal trade between accuracy and compute-storage cost will confirm the comprehensive superiority of MIDAS over existing DDA-bases codes, and make it a compelling method for solving the EM scattering problem involving complexly-shaped realistic hydrometeors.

articleTitle: A Low Cost Implementation of Unconstrained Anisotropic hp-Refinement for CEM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The Finite Element Method (FEM) is a powerful and commonly used tool within the domain of Computational Electromagnetics (CEM). It is used to model Maxwells Equation’s with high fidelity over arbitrary geometries with arbitrary material properties; however, it can be difficult to arrive at solutions efficiently. Thus, it is common to start with a course discretization of a model, and slowly introduce more Degrees of Freedom (DoFs) through mesh refinements. This paper discusses an implementation of an FEM code which supports anisotropic h- and p-refinements while avoiding some common difficulties associated with implementing a continuous Galerking FEM code which supports h-refinement over quadrilateral or hexahedral elements.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Near-Field Beam Steering with a Flanched-Cross Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Near-field metasurface based beam steering are finding many applications. However, the traditional cells designed for such metasurfaces cannot produce all the required phase shifts with high amplitudes, ultimately contributing to high steering error. This paper presents a cell geometry, Flanched-Cross, that provides more accurate phase shifts with higher amplitudes than the traditional square patch cells. Simulation results verify that the Flanched-Cross cell produces a higher number of phase shifts with the error between 0.04°−1.2° only as compared to a square patch cell with an error between 0.1° − 2.2° for the design of a beam-steering metasurface.

articleTitle: Design of ESPAR Antenna Array for High Gain Communication Services
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Nowadays, the high gain directional antennas are very essential for any wireless communication system to reduce interference. In this paper, a new Electronically Steerable Parasitic Array Radiator (ESPAR) array antenna is presented for high gain communications and sensing. The antenna array (1x2) consists of two single ESPAR antennas with an optimum distance. The peak gain of the array antenna is 11.40 dB whereas the minimum gain is 9.95 dB. Approximately 3 dB gain increases as compared to the single ESPAR antenna (8.17 dB). The designed antenna could operate at the ISM frequency band of (2.40~ 2.50) GHz. The distance between the active and parasitic elements is chosen as λ/4 for optimum performance. To reduce the mutual coupling, the space between the two ESPAR antennas is selected as λ/8. This proposed array design of ESPAR antenna could be applied in many personal communications, ECG (electrocardiogram) monitoring system, Weather tracking, and in many others Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) applications.

articleTitle: Coherent Jamming with 1-Bit Time Modulated Digital Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A coherent jamming system to suppress the fundamental component with 1-bit time modulated digital metasurfaces has been proposed in this paper. With dynamically controlling the reflection phase coefficient of the elements, the energy of fundamental component of the jamming signals can be significantly suppressed, which can effectively reduce the exposure risk of the factual position and improve the jamming performance. The simulated result verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual Ku-Band Dual-Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna Fed by Substrate Integrated Coaxial Lines
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The design of a dual-band dual-polarized (DBDP) Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) is presented. The antenna is designed for a Ku-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) application. The DRA features two distinct polarization ports operating on two frequency bands and is fed by Substrate Integrated Coaxial Lines (SICLs), providing robust power handling and a high level of isolation. Realized gains of 3.9 dBi at 13.5 GHz and 6.5 dBi at 17.25 GHz are measured for a single element. This design allows a shared coupling aperture for both polarizations, hence maximizing the compactness of the antenna.

articleTitle: Circular Split Ring Resonator Asymetrical CPW-fed Dual Port MIMO Antenna for Wireless and Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The dual-port, multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna having very less designed footprint of 25×25mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> operating in WLAN/X/Ku band is reported for wireless and Satellite applications. By using an inverted Z-shaped radiator connected to a circular split ring resonator excites the three resonant frequency modes at 2.5, 9.45 and 12.3 GHz which covers the WLAN, X and Ku band. Further a vertical line consisting of several slant parallel stubs of size 2×0.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> placed at a distance of 1.9mm from each other acts as an isolating element is placed in between both the antenna elements. This entire structure generates bandwidth of 10.73 % (2.38 – 2.65 GHz) in F1 band, 27.20% (8.10 – 10.65 GHz) in F2 band and 34.86% (11.39 – 16.20 GHz) in F3 band along with minimum mutual coupling of -18dB, gain better than 1.5dBi, efficiency 70%, Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC)~0.01, diversity Gain (DG) ~10dB and Total Active Reflection Coefficient (TARC) below -10dB in the entire band of interest.

articleTitle: A Multi-Feature Based Machine Learning Approach for Ground-Moving Radar Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning method for radar ground moving target detection in unknown ground clutters. Several features such as clutter proximity feature, block size, and bending energy are extracted from the radar data in the angle-Doppler domain. They are then applied to a classifier that is trained by target and clutter data for slow-moving radar target detection. The simulation results of the proposed approach validate its effectiveness and demonstrate it is applicable in real ground clutter environments.

articleTitle: Snowflake Measurement and Analysis System (SMAS)
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a novel system for measurement and analysis of snow particles in free fall, constituting the Snowflake Measurement and Analysis System (SMAS). The SMAS features seven high-resolution cameras placed in a 3D fashion for 3D visual hull reconstruction of particle shapes and particle fall speed measurements. The SMAS data enable particle scattering computation, studies of snow habits, analysis of microphysical characteristics of particles, and hydrometeor classification.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Multi-Dimensional Parameters Estimation for Device-Free Human Tracking using WiFi Signals
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Recently, indoor localization in a device-free manner is important since it does not require any devices. Due to the wide application of multi-subcarrier and multi-antenna devices, joint estimation of multi-dimensional parameters can improve passive localization and tracking accuracy. So, in this paper, we propose an improved four-dimensional parameter estimation based on a two-stage algorithm. Specifically, we first use the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) for coarse estimation and then conduct parameter refinement using space-alternating generalized expectation-maximization (SAGE) to improve the parameter accuracy of the weak human-induced reflection path. We conduct experiments in a real indoor environment, and experimental results show that our proposed method can improve the accuracy of parameter estimation and then obtain a better tracking performance.

articleTitle: De-Embedding Unwanted Radiation from Phased-Array Systems in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we analyze for the first time antenna-efficiency measurements of a mm-wave phased-array antenna for smartphone applications by use of the reverberation-chamber-based three-antenna method. We measure the efficiency of the total system (array including an RF beamformer), and we introduce a new method to de-embed radiated emissions by other parts of the system from the efficiency result. We compare the measured result to a simulation model and conclude that the reverberation-chamber approach can yield accurate results when unwanted radiation is properly accounted for.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarized dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is investigated and discussed. The probe and microstrip feed line excite linear polarization (LP) and broadside circular polarization (CP), respectively. These different radiation patterns are obtained 43 % overlapping bandwidth. The measured results show that the antenna provides 43 % bandwidth, excited by probe feed line that produces linearly polarized and 74 % impedance bandwidth using microstrip feed line with the 18 % circularly polarized. The total overlapping bandwidth is 43 % starting from 8.65 GHz to 13.44 GHz. The antenna gain is between 3.4 and 5.2 dBi for linear polarized and between 2.8 and 5.1 dBi for circularly polarized patterns in the whole covered range.

articleTitle: Experiment-based risk evaluation for a stratospheric VLF antenna system
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Between 2014 and 2021 a series of seven test light-balloon stratospheric flights took place, with the objectives to test various aspects of vertical electric antenna systems for the Very Low Frequency range. These missions helped to define important risks associated with free-flying large antennas and create effective ways to mitigate them, allowing the successful implementation of a stratospheric VLF transmitter.

articleTitle: An Augmented Y-parameter Method for Macromodeling Electromagnetic Structures in the Presence of Plane-Waves
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel modeling approach to characterize microwave structures in the presence of external electromagnetic waves. The method relies on augmenting traditional network parameters such as Y-parameters with an increased number of columns to account for the inclusion of Vector Spherical Wave Functions (VSWFs) in the voltage vector. Once extracted, the proposed augmented Y-parameter model can then be used for real-time computation of port currents corresponding to numerous parametric changes that can alter the incident wave, thereby aiding in rapid circuit design and optimization exercises.

articleTitle: Chiral Nonlocal Metasurfaces for Frequency-Selective Wavefront Shaping
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We propose, design, and experimentally demonstrate a nonlocal metasurface with frequency-selective, wavefront shaping capabilities and at the same time polarization-selective chiral response. This operation requires the implementation of bi-layer metasurfaces with engineered nonlocal response, wherein each layer controls locally a specific linear polarization, while the coupled system supports arbitrary polarization states. We demonstrate that this platform enables unprecedented control over wavefront manipulation, including frequency-selective, spin-selective reflection with arbitrary geometric phase. We observe a highly chiral response with record-high reflectance efficiency over a narrow frequency window, both for a uniform metasurface and for one with tailored phase gradient for anomalous reflection. Both devices provide an efficiency well above the theoretical limit of 25% for conventional single-layer devices. Our work opens exciting opportunities for augmented reality and enhanced secure wireless communications.

articleTitle: CTS Antenna Array Optimization using Passive Corrugated Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the usage of passive corrugations to improve the performances of continuous transverse stub (CTS) arrays is investigated. Corrugations are employed as a secondary radiation source to reemit surface energy and to modulate surface waves at the antenna surface. Thanks to this effect, we demonstrate that the number of radiating slots of the CTS array can be halved maintaining the electrical performances unchanged (gain, bandwidth, and radiation pattern). The new array has a simplified feeding network, is more compact and lighter than the original configuration. Besides, the manufacturing complexity and cost of the new configuration are significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Enhanced Deep Subwavelength Direction-of-Arrival Sensing Using Time Modulation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We develop and analyze a model for a deep-subwavelength direction-of-arrival (DoA) sensor with enhanced performance and sensitivity, by incorporating time-modulation into the sensing system. We formulate the problem, derive an analytical model and equivalent circuit models, discuss the physical mechanisms responsible for the enhancement. We show that time-modulation enables a new degree of control over the operation frequency, and that incorporating the currents from higher generated harmonics into the sensing scheme allows us to extract more accurate information about the impinging wave.

articleTitle: A Checkerboard Metasurface Based on Staggered Triangular Arrangement for RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a checkerboard meta-surface that efficiently reduces radar cross section(RCS) using phase-cancelling units arranged in staggered triangles. Firstly, a metasurface unit with phase cancellation is constructed by Pancharatnam-Berry(PB) phase concept, and the phase cancellation is achieved by the linear relationship between the unit rotation angle and the reflection phase. The metasurface cell structure realizes 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup>reflection phase difference in a wide band, and uses a staggered triangular arrangement to combine the elements. The reflection metasurface realizes the RCS reduction from 9.56GHz to 20.0GHz larger than 10 dB. The structure can be not only effectively reduced in the broadband, but also helpful to the reduce RCS to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Joint Mutual Coupling Compensation and Direction-of-Arrival Estimation in Sparse Arrays using Evolutionary Optimization Techniques: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Structured sparse arrays, such as minimum redundancy array (MRA), nested array, and co-prime array, have non-uniform spacing between consecutive elements, and can achieve a similar performance in direction of arrival (DOA) estimation with a smaller number of physical elements as compared with standard uniformly spaced arrays. In practical sparse arrays, however, mutual coupling effect should be included in the optimization process for accurate estimation as it introduces a mismatch in the model and errors in the estimated directions since the mutual coupling matrix (MCM) may not be known exactly and should be included as unknown in the estimation process. This results in a challenging nonlinear optimization problem with a large number of optimization parameters. In this work, we apply various evolutionary optimization algorithms, which have previously been used in a diverse set of electromagnetic problems, and compare their performance in the joint estimation of the mutual coupling matrix (MCM) and direction of arrivals (DOAs) of sparse arrays. The numerical examples for the MRA case are presented.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Coupling for Wide Angle Impedance Matching of Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new technique to improve active impedance match of phased arrays over wide scan range is proposed. It is demonstrated that manipulating coupling asymmetrically can mitigate the impact of couplings on active impedance without causing extra cost or manufacturing complexity. The proposed technique is flexible and can be applied to the most of phased array structures.

articleTitle: A Generative Method for Antenna Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The key to rapid antenna design is to improve the optimization of design parameters by simplifying the modeling of antenna geometric structures. We propose a flexible geometric modeling scheme that can be formed into any arbitrary shape by simply connecting nodes. We also propose a machine learning based generative method for high dimensional design parameter problems. It consists of discriminators and generators. The discriminators predict the performance of geometric models and the generators create new candidates that will pass the discrim-inators. Further, an evolutionary criterion approach is applied to update the discriminators and generators. The eﬃciency of the new design methodology is illustrated by a dual resonance antenna design example.

articleTitle: Wireless Brain Implant for Dopamine Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Motoric symptoms in Parkinson’s disease (PD) patients are caused by low level of dopamine (DA) concentration in the brain. Facilitating daily real-time and portable DA monitoring can improve the life quality of the patients. Miniaturized wireless brain implant can accommodate this purpose. The realization of this device requires compatible design on DA sensor, signal processing, and the wireless technology. For the sensor, the electrochemical method, Fast Scan Cyclic Voltammetry (FSCV), enables the sub-millisecond DA concentration measurement. Coupling this sensing method with RF technology and wireless power transfer can increase the device miniaturization and implantability. From our numerical analysis, the FSCV electrode with planar area approximately one square centimeter can accommodate the low-level DA concentration detection.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Learning for Hallway Gait Analysis using FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We propose a novel corridor or hallway gait monitoring system based on radar signal processing, unsupervised learning, and an association method. Unlike some of our previous works where we designed an in-package lens antenna to sharpen the beam of a commercially available radar system, our algorithm proposed in this paper could be paired with any type of MIMO FMCW radar without need for radar antenna alteration to capture human gait in a highly cluttered environment. We validate the improved system functionality through accurately capturing the spatiotemporal gait values (e.g., speed, step points, step count, step time, step length, and cadence) in a long hallway.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile CPW-Fed Circularly Polarized Antenna for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In telemetry applications, biomedical antennas perform a critical function. This study describes a small-profile, low-profile, circular-polarized biomedical antenna operating at a frequency of 2.45 GHz. To keep the antenna size small, it is provided via modified coplanar waveguide technology (CPW). To produce the circularly polarized antenna at the desired frequency range, the radiant monopole comprises of a grooved rectangular patch with a slit at a 45-degree angle and a tiny, truncated patch at the left end of the CPW ground plane. To obtain the bending capacity, RT5880 (εr = 2.2, tan = 0.0009) with a typical thickness of 0.254 mm is used. The planned antenna has a total volume of 21mm 13.5mm 0.254mm. The simulation also examines the flexible study along the (x & y) axis. This antenna has been scaled down and is an excellent candidate for biological applications.

articleTitle: A hemisphere dielectric lens for high directivity with narrow beam and low side lobe level
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work proposes a hemisphere dielectric lens aiming at high directivity with a narrow beam and low side lobe level (SLL). The proposed lens is constructed by several dielectric sections with different permittivities, providing a wave transformation from a spherical wave to a plane wave. For achieving an easy and low-cost fabrication, liquid crystal display (LCD) printing is utilized to fabricate the entire lens. To modify permittivities of a commercial printable dielectric, air and Al2O3 fine powder are added. The lens is designed at 24 GHz and fed by a WR-42 waveguide excitation. The size of the entire lens is 2.66 λ0 × 3.02 λ0× 3.02 λ0. Simulated results show that at 24 GHz, the proposed lens exhibits a high directivity of 21.8 dBi with 12.2° and 16.3° half-power beamwidths (HPBWs) in E- and H-plane, respectively. It also provides a wide bandwidth of 41.7%, from 20 GHz to 30 GHz. Keywords— dielectric lens antennas; modified permittivity; radiation pattern; wideband antennas

articleTitle: Grating Sidelobe Suppression in Single-Layer Center-Feed Waveguide Antenna Array at 38 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we optimize the width of a slotted waveguide to minimize the distance between the adjacent diagonal slots for grating sidelobe suppression. By solving the tradeoff between the waveguide width and the guided wavelength. We find the waveguide with a width of 5-mm has optimal performance. Furthermore, by shrinking the waveguide width to 5 mm, we obtain a perfect single-peak radiation pattern in E-plane and an extremely high antenna efficiency (89.4%). Finally, the corresponding directive gain can be increased to 27.9 dBi.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Sensing Evaluations by Using a Passive Magnetic Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a non-destructive sensing technique exploiting a response-controlled passive magnetic metasurface, excited by an active RF coil placed in its near-field region. We numerically designed a magnetic metasurface, working at 3 MHz, able to synthetize arbitrary magnetic field distributions, by modulating the currents (amplitude and phase) flowing on the metasurface unit-cells and on the exciting RF coil. In particular, the proposed configuration comprises a 5×5 matrix whose unit-cells are made of an 8-turn planar spiral coil, covering a 19 cm × 19 cm area. By performing accurate full-wave simulations, we demonstrated that by designing the metasurface so as to produce a focused field distribution, it is possible to detect and spatially identify a 1 cm radius ferromagnetic inclusion, in spite of the low-frequency herein employed. The findings suggest that response-controlled magnetic metasurfaces could be used in non-destructive sensing, also exploiting real-time reconfigurability to sequentially scan the region of interest.

articleTitle: The SWO Box, a Portable Resonant Source for High-Power Electromagnetic Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Experimental results of a portable and compact high power electromagnetic, mesoband radiator, working in the lower-UHF band, are presented. The radiator is a self-contained unit, comprising a quarter-wave switched oscillator (SWO), antenna, high-voltage source, pneumatic system, and battery bank. The TEM horn antenna acts a mechanical support and partially houses the components of the system. The bounding box of the system is 0.44 λ at the central frequency of operation. Measurements of the radiated electric field are presented, and the overall performance of the system is discussed.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Reactive Loaded Miniaturized Catheter Antenna for Microwave Ablation in Deep Tissue Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A passive reactive loaded catheter antenna working at 0.8 GHz with peak gain 1.65dBi is designed for microwave ablation application in deep tissue environment. The proposed structure is 61% miniaturized with respect to an equivalent unloaded quarter wavelength monopole designed to work at the same frequency. The input impedance of the proposed catheter antenna can be practically engineered using series L-C loading in order to achieve good impedance matching at a desired miniaturization level with respect to an arbitrary source impedance without the need for external matching networks. The proposed catheter structure exhibits 38.7 dBm radiated power at around 0.8 GHz when inserted in deep tissue environment with 40dBm (10 W) of input CW power.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Metal-Insulator-Metal Capacitors using a High-K Dielectric Paste
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new fabrication method for metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitors. Micro-dispensing is used to realize the additively manufactured (AM) passive devices on a Kapton tape. These 3D printed capacitors are fabricated using Dupont CB028 to form the conductive layers and Creative Materials 128-49 as the dielectric layer. A 0.55 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> capacitor is realized and shows a value of 7.12 pF with the self-resonance of 6 GHz and Q factor of 103. This capacitor could be embedded into large area RF and microwave systems.

articleTitle: A SPICE Compatible PEEC Model with Curvilinear RWG Basis Functions for Electromagnetic Simulation of Lossy Flex Circuit
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel SPICE compatible PEEC model with curvilinear RWG basis functions is proposed for the electromagnetic simulation of flex circuits with losses under non-PEC boundary conditions. This method discretizes surfaces of interest through curved triangular cells for geometric modeling and curvilinear RWG basis functions for current modeling. Then, the quasi-static method of moments (MoM) solution to surface electric field integral equation (EFIE) is derived by introducing conduction loss, and the equivalent RLC circuit network is obtained by the partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) method. Finally, the network is imported into the SPICE solver for calculation. A numerical example is provided to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the approach.

articleTitle: Multimode Coupled Slots for Wideband Circularly-Polarized mm-Wave All-Metal Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: All-metal compound radiating elements able to radiate a circularly-polarized field over a wide bandwidth are presented. Such elements comprise an active waveguide-fed slot which couples to a backshorted slot. When this coupled slot supports the propagation of several modes by bending its shape, a remarkable wide polarization bandwidth can be achieved. As an illustration, an optimum H-shaped all-metal radiating element reaches a 1-dB axial ratio bandwidth around 25%.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Optimization of a Metasurface-Based Directly Modulating Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A directly modulating antenna using metasurfaces is optimized using the surrogate model assisted differential evolution for antenna synthesis (SADEA) method and simulated. Metasurface modulation holds promise as an energy efficiency transmitter technology, but suffers from modulation distortion and many differing parameters, making achieving good designs difficult. The algorithm used here, SADEA, obtained a design that shows improvement over conventional design techniques, producing amplitude variation of 1.8 dB over 360° and an average efficiency of 65%, up from 50% obtained by the standard model.

articleTitle: Design of a Multiple Beam Wideband Antenna Using 8x8 Butler Matrix Beamformer for 5G NR Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wideband Butler matrix beamformer is combined with a 1x8 linear array consisting of wideband U-slot antennas on conventional microwave substrate. The resulting eight beams allow beamforming between ±56°. A 19.86% bandwidth was achieved for the U-slot antenna. A peak realized gain of about 15.97 dBi was observed at the center frequency of 2.62 GHz. This design can be used for 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation new radio (NR) frequency bands N7, N38, and N41, N53.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave Scanning Array with Fine and Coarse Phase Shifters Realized by Using U-Section Meander Feed Lines and Varactor Diodes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: It is well known that conventional microwave phase shifters become both lossy and expensive when we attempt to scale them to operate at millimeter wavelengths. The objective of this paper is to present a scanning-array design which realizes the requisite phase shifts in both discrete as well as fine steps to scan the array. The discrete phase shifts are achieved by using meander lines with switches for the feed networks of the radiating elements, while varactor diodes are employed to realize phase shifts in a continuous manner by varying the bias voltages of the varactors, and to enhance the range of the realizable phase shifts. A Ka-band array of rectangular microstrip patches has been designed to demonstrate the scan capability of the designed array, which is expected to find potential applications in portable millimeter wave devices for 5G systems.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of 3D Meta-Volumes for Complementary Phases Enabling Wide Field of View RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Conventionally, the design of coding metasurface unit cells focuses on the performance at normal incidence. The traditional design process has been confined to working within the paradigm of two-dimensional planar or multilayer structures which inherently possess a limited field of view (FoV). Here, in a fundamental departure from this paradigm, a pair of three-dimensional unit cells are simultaneously optimized using a multi-objective genetic algorithm in order to firsthand design the unit cells for maximum performance at oblique incidence angles. These unit cells were then configured into a diffuse array for the purpose of RCS reduction. The surface reduces the bistatic, specular RCS (radar cross section) by 90% (10 dB) over a worst-case 63% bandwidth for oblique incidence of 70 degrees at H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> polarization and by 80% (7 dB) over a worst-case 70% bandwidth for oblique incidence of 45 degrees at E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> polarization.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Loss Printed Ridge-Gap-Waveguide Crossover for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A low-loss 0-dB crossover for millimeter-wave (mm-wave) beam-switching network applications is designed in this paper. It is mainly composed of two cascaded 3-dB hybrid couplers based on printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) technology operating on the quasi-TEM mode. The proposed crossover can be considered a good candidate to develop feeding beam-forming antenna systems designated for future 5G and 6G applications. The simulated results show that the designed crossover achieves better than -10 dB for both return loss and isolation. The insertion loss is about -0.5±0.1 dB over the whole operating bandwidth from 26.5 to 29.5 GHz.

articleTitle: An Ultra Wide Band Quad Horn Antenna with Different Ridges Profiles
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this article, an ultra-wideband quad ridge horn antenna, covering two full successive bands, specifically K and Ka bands is introduced. The proposed antenna can carry vertical and horizontal signals simultaneously with a deep matching level over the entire band. The introduced antenna shape is proposed based on a mathematical formulation that minimizes the discontinuity between the feeding structure and the horn. The presented work has a stable gain characteristic to facilitate the utilization as a reflector feeding.

articleTitle: Curl-Conforming Vector Bases for Hybrid Meshes: A New Paradigm for Pyramid Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A simple procedure for obtaining hierarchical curl-conforming pyramid bases has been obtained by shifting to a new paradigm that requires the mapping of the pyramidal cell into a cube and then directly imposing the conformity of the vector bases with those used on adjacent differently shaped cells (tetrahedra, hexahedra and triangular prisms). This summary discusses and generalizes some features of the new construction method recently published elsewhere.

articleTitle: Machine learning based tandem network approach for antenna design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce novel machine learning based techniques to design multi-band microstrip antennas as per user specifications over a broad range of frequencies. The approach involves the design and training of a neural network for approximating the electromagnetic simulations of antennas, the so-called ‘forward’ problem. Here, the antenna is parameterized in terms of a checker-board pattern of metallic sub-patches. Additionally, a second ‘tandem’ neural network is also designed, which takes the user specification of a desired return-loss spectrum and returns an antenna structure. We explore the various machine learning innovations that are required in order for this approach to succeed. Our approach makes way for rapid designs of multi-band antennas, which is otherwise known to be a tedious task requiring vast domain knowledge.

articleTitle: A Quad-Band Slant 45° Dual-Polarized Butler-based Omni-Directional MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of the compact quad-band slant 45° dual-polarized Butler-based omni-directional MIMO antenna working at the frequency band of 0.69-0.96 GHz (LB), 1.69-2.69GHz (MB), 3.3-4.2 GHz (C-Band), and 5.15-5.93 GHz (HB). The LB array of the proposed antenna consists of three elevation (EL) panels of slant 45° dual-polarized dipoles and two Butler-based azimuth beam formers. Through replacing traditional T-splitter type azimuth beam formers by the Butler matrix 3x3, the omni-directional 6x6 MIMO antenna at LB band can be realized without increasing the size of the antenna.

articleTitle: Comparison of NF and FF Automotive Antenna Measurement in DSRC and C-V2X Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Comparison of near-field and far-field data is important to verify measurement accuracy and study limitations of relying on only near-field data in automotive antenna measurement. In this study, near-field data extracted from FEKO full-wave simulator for three distances of 3m, 6m, and 9m, between the measurement surface and a monocone antenna mounted on the roof of a car, are compared to the far-field data. The frequency of the simulation and measurement is 6 GHz, for CV2X and dedicated short range communication (DSRC) services. Average gain is the parameter used for the comparison. The results provide a good benchmark to determine whether NF-FF transformation is required in the given applications and test scenarios.

articleTitle: Miniature RFID Tag Antenna with Low Profile and Wideband for Human Healthcare Monitor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work proposed a novel, cost effective miniatur RFID tag antenna for human healthcare monitor. To achieve the conjugated input impedance match between antenna structure and Monza-4 chip (7.17—j74.22 Ω at 915 MHz), the proposed antenna was optimized by coarsely controlling the positions of vias and fine-tuning the gap of coupled patches. To further reduce the height or the size of antenna, the design method based on the 3D-dipole current distribution was presented. Consequently, the proposed tag not only was miniaturized but also got a stable long read range (> 5.0 m) and a wide bandwidth of 71 MHz, regardless of different placed locations of tag on the human body. Adequate agreement between the simulation and measured results was verified experimentally.

articleTitle: A study of materials and additive manufacturing techniques for a novel 2D Luneburg Lens
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, characterization and manufacturing of a non-homogenous stackable 2D Luneburg lens, using additive manufacturing techniques is presented. The paper discusses the material characterization process, followed by the design, construction, and finally the prototype construction. It was found that ABS printed using SLA technology, produces the most promising results for the desired application.

articleTitle: Learning Antenna Radiation Patterns Through Gaussian Process Regression
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Knowledge of an antenna system’s radiation pattern is important for the optimal deployment of radio systems in the field. However, while an antenna’s radiation pattern can be measured in an anechoic chamber, in real-world applications, the radiated signal can also be attenuated by the environment in a manner that is angle dependent. For directional antenna systems, in order to properly steer radiated energy in desired directions, the behavior of the radio system in the real world must be characterized. In this work, we propose a method for using Gaussian Processes regression to learn the deviations of an antenna’s array pattern due to its signal’s interactions with the environment. We evaluate this approach on publicly available benchmark datasets collected on antenna systems at 2.4GHz.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Joint Inversion Using Successive Deep Perceptual Constraints
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Using joint inversion to reveal subsurface structures has drawn considerable research attention to reduce inversion uncertainties and improve resolution. In this abstract, a novel joint inversion workflow is proposed by using the deep neural network (DNN) combined with the traditional separated inversion process to improve the result for multi-physics data. Deep perceptual constraints are added when training the networks to enforce the structural similarity. The whole workflow is executed in an iterative way to guarantee the reliability of inversion results. Numerical examples demonstrate our method can achieve more accurate inverted property values and better structural features compared to traditional separate inversions and cross gradient-based joint inversion.

articleTitle: Surrogate Modeling for Designing and Optimizing MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This papers presents the design and optimization of multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) antennas through intelligent methods namely as: surrogate modeling. The optimization process is performed automatically with the combination of Microwave Studio (Dassault Systèmes) and MATLAB numerical analyzer. The proposed optimization method aims to find the optimal solution for the total active reflection coefficient (TARC) specification, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> by using shallow neural network. This methodology leads to efficiently size the design parameters of MIMO antenna and to optimize S-parameters and TARC specification jointly. To validate the proposed method, an ultra wideband MIMO antenna in the frequency band of 3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz is designed and optimized.

articleTitle: A Numerically Efficient CEM Tool for Modeling RF Circuits and Antennas for 5G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel hybrid approach to simulating RF and microwave circuits, as well as antennas and arrays, which may be mounted on complex platforms. We focus on developing CEM modeling techniques in the context of 5G and beyond. We describe how the proposed approach is incorporated in an existing CEM code, and present numerical results which demonstrate the enhancement of the computational efficiency of the embellished code.

Author Keywords: 5G antennas and circuits for millimeter waves

articleTitle: Array Control Via Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel machine learning architecture is proposed for control of a phased array. Two convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are assembled in tandem to determine the number of active elements when given a desired radiation mask, and to determine the phase weights that steer the beam to the desired direction. The dual-CNN design and training are described and demonstrated for a 2.4-GHz patch array of sizes ranging from 2x2 to 8x8.

articleTitle: A Low Coupling Broadband MIMO Antenna for 5G Using Meta-surface Decoupling Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A low coupling broadband multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is achieved by loading a single layer Meta-surface (MTS) under the antenna. The proposed MTS is formed by “I” shaped metamaterial with orthogonal opposite planes arranged according to the periodic structure. Through the investigation and evaluation of HFSS, the simulation results gives that a -10-dB fractional bandwidth of 46.47% from 3.21 GHz to 5.38 GHz has been realized for the designed CPW MIMO antenna loading MTS, which can cover the two operating bands of 3.3 GHz to 3.6 GHz and 4.8 GHz to 5 GHz for 5G applications. In addition, the coupling between the MIMO antenna elements is less than -15 dB within the operating frequency, and the lowest coupling can reach –26 dB. Simultaneously, the stable radiation characteristics also mean that the constructed MIMO antenna has a great prospect for 5G application.

articleTitle: Resonance Behavior of a Conducting Wire Object Below a Halfspace
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
