abstract: The resonance scattering phenomena of an object buried below a dielectric halfspace has been studied with potential applications such as unexploded ordnance detection and breast tumor screening. These studies adopted a theoretical approach where the resonant frequencies are numerically determined via a complex root searching procedure from the impedance matrix obtained from an integral equation formulation. The practically of retrieving these resonant modes from transient responses under different excitation aspects, though is crucial for subsurface target detection application, has not been well studied. In this paper, the resonant frequencies and the corresponding residues are extracted from the transient responses of a metallic wire object below halfspace. We found that the same set of resonant modes is extracted in most cases, but the residues vary significantly as the incident angle.

articleTitle: Generating High-Harmonic Optical Vortex Beams from Photonic Bound States in the Continuum
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we study the high-harmonic optical vortex (OV) generation from an α-Si photonic crystal (PhC) slab supporting the guided resonance associated with bound states in the continuum (BICs). We show that the topological charge of the nth-harmonic OV beams is determined by both the polarization charge of the BIC and the circular polarization state of the nth-harmonic signal relative to that of the fundamental waves.

articleTitle: Polarization Reconfigurable Circularly Polarized Antenna for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a polarization reconfigurable omnidirectional circularly polarized (OCP) antenna for Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications is presented. The circular polarizaton (CP) is due to the combination of two geometries that can provide vertical and horizontal polarizations, respectively. The antenna is fed by a single port. The simulated results show a CP bandwidth covering 19 MHz from 859 MHz to 878 MHz and an axial ratio of 2.5 dB at 868 MHz, which are maintained in both the antenna states thanks to the symmetry of the antenna geometry.

articleTitle: Coherence-Distance Estimation of Non-Linear Mode-Stirring Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: One of the main sources of uncertainty when measuring antenna characteristics in a reverberation chamber is correlation. Current methods of determining correlation between mode-stirring positions, such as autocorrelation, are constant over absolute stirrer positions. This work shows that the coherence distance can vary over position using the Pearson-correlation method to determine the coherence distance of mode stirring mechanisms. From this, it will be shown that the autocorrelation method underestimates the actual coherence distance. Using this method, stirring sequences can be optimized, and thus antenna measurements inside a reverberation chamber can be improved.

articleTitle: Leading Edge Synthetic Phased-Array (SPA) Antenna and Smart Multi-beam Antenna Sensors for Massive MIMO Mobile-Wireless Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Coordinated and spatially-distributed Synthetic Phased-Array Antenna and Smart Multi-beam Antenna Sensors will enhance the performance of the modern Wireless Network Systems i.e. 5G, beyond-5G and forthcoming 6G Communication Technology. Developing based on the concept of interfacing with the ever-expanding massive MIMO mobile-wireless network to meet the design goal of high spectral efficiency, stringent latency, and steady through-put connectivity. They are very efficient for mobile structures such as drones, unmanned automobiles and other rescuing robotic devices. The Operation of these sensors at extreme inclement environments (for example, severe weather conditions) to maintain network connectivity requires the enclosure of modern hi-tech radome materials for damage protection and performance sustainability. The main issues are channel fading, blind spots and various forms of radiation interferences. When deploying such advanced phased-array sensors for the modern communication networks, it is necessary to evaluate the RADHAZ (radiation hazards) impact for the wireless network at various level of radiation. Particularly the detection of the "hot-spot." It is very important to be aware of the dangerous radiation zones for the good of the general public.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfiguration of Microstrip Antennas by Controlling Slots in Its Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a pattern reconfigurable antenna with improved pattern diversity is proposed. The antenna is formed by placing a circular ring around a circular microstrip patch antenna and excited by using two feeds. The in-phase and out-of-phase excitation of these feeds provides conical beam and broadside radiation, respectively. Slots are introduced to the ground plane of the antenna to steer the main radiation direction in broadside radiation mode and to obtain asymmetric radiation in conical beam mode. Consequently, the pattern diversity of the two-mode antenna is improved.

articleTitle: Wideband Isolated Dual-Polarized Array Feeds
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A 3.5-21 GHz dual-polarized fixed-beam antenna array system with two isolated feed networks of 32 H-polarized and 32 V-polarized Vivaldi elements is presented. The feed network is comprised of an LTCC package that hosts two novel isolated radial combiners connected via a BGA transition to an organic interposer that is in turn attached to the 64-element Vivaldi array. The dual-polarized planar feed is low-profile, 0.26 wavelengths tall at highest frequency, and is mostly confined under the array footprint. Through diligent full-wave simulations, it is found that the feed loss is approximately 1 dB with -15 dB worst case isolation. The full system with the Vivaldi antenna maintains an input VSWR less than 2.5 over the 6:1 bandwidth while having a total efficiency between 75-90%.

articleTitle: A Center-Fed UHF Near-Field RFID Reader Antenna with Large Interrogation Zone
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel ultra-high frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) reader antenna is introduced in this paper. To achieve strong and uniform magnetic field distribution over an electrically large interrogation zone, this design adopts four tapered double-side parallel striplines to feed four segmented loop structures. The measured results show that this antenna achieves the good impedance matching over the frequency range from 850 to 1050 MHz, and it produces strong and uniform magnetic field distribution with an interrogation zone of 320 mm × 320 mm. The maximum reading distance is more than 300 mm with 30 dBm input power. Moreover, the antenna can achieve more than 95% read percentage within the height of 75 mm.

articleTitle: Linearization of 2D Inverse Scattering Problems Based on Reduced Order Models
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: By discretizing the 2D spatial differential operator and the wave parameters together, we prove that the sub-diagonals in the sparse matrix are linear with the wave parameters. With the reduced order model approach, this linearity can be used to improve the accuracy and robustness in solving inverse scattering problems. Numerical exaxmples validate this scheme and the results show a steady convergence and well-reconstructed images.

articleTitle: Near-Field Phase Transforming Structures for High-Performance Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A review of the state-of-the-art near-field transforming structures (NFTSs) for realizing high-performance antenna systems is presented. The NFTSs are primarily synthesized for near electric field phase transformation for various applications. They can operate from microwave to millimeter-wave bands. This study mainly examines the NFTSs reported for achieving high gain and passive beam-steering antennas with prototyping flexibility for low-profile and low-cost solutions. Furthermore, the optimal fabrication processes for various design concepts are discussed, highlighting a few of them.

articleTitle: Efficient Solution of Multi-Scale Problems with Localized Mesh Refinement Schemes and Huygens’ Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a framework composed by Domain Decomposition Method (DDM) that integrates a local mesh refinement scheme based on Huygens’ equivalence principle and the integration of multibranch basis functions for the efficient analysis of multiscale problems. The proposed method allows the improvement of the precision of the solution while the solving time is reduced via the decomposition of the problem.

articleTitle: A 36 port Dual Polarized High Gain Sub-6GHz Multibeam Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of the dual-band dual-polarized high gain sub-6GHz multibeam base station antenna for wireless communications at the frequency band of 3.3-4.2 GHz and 5.15-5.93 GHz. Based on the required specifications such as gain, the azimuth beam coverage, the cross-over point between beams, and the side lobe level, a 36-port dual-band dual-polarized multibeam antenna has been designed, implemented, and tested.

articleTitle: High-Resolution Quartz Transmitarray Antenna for Sub-THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A high resolution (4-bit) anisotropic transmitarray (TA) for sub-THz applications is presented here. A simple numerical model is employed to design efficiently the TA unit-cell. A 50×50 element TA optimized at 280 GHz is designed. The antenna achieves a peak gain of 28.0 dBi with 53.7% aperture efficiency at 290 GHz. The effectiveness of the design methodology is demonstrated by the reduced gain loss (only 0.5 dB) with respect to the value achieved by an ideal lens for the same configuration.

articleTitle: Polarization Effect on Feature Extraction and Object Classification by Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper reports the polarization impacts on feature extraction and object classification from ultra-wideband ground penetrating radar (GPR) by deep learning. Three different models are trained by the same convolutional neural network (CNN) to compare the effects of the polarization on the feature extraction and classification accuracy. It is shown that the quad-pole images have some inclusive features compared to single-pole ones. Moreover, the classification accuracy improves by 13.3% due to the inclusive feature of the quad-pole images.

articleTitle: A Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain Method to Simulate Metasurfaces using Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) are incorporated into a discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method to efficiently simulate metasurfaces. The numerical flux for GSTCs is derived for the first time using the Rankine-Hugoniot jump conditions. This numerical flux includes time derivatives of fields and therefore explicit time integration schemes that are traditionally used with DGTD do not yield a stable time marching method. To alleviate this bottleneck, a new time marching scheme, which solves a local matrix system for the unknowns of the elements touching the same GSTC face, is developed. Numerical results, which validate the accuracy of the proposed method against analytical solutions and demonstrate its applicability to the simulation of curved and space/time-varying metasurfaces, are presented.

articleTitle: Design of Very Low Profile V/UHF Directional Metamaterial Antenna for Airborne FOPEN Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a very low profile cavity backed planar V/UHF antenna, which has been introduced for possible intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) applications, namely for airborne foliage penetration radar. Multiple line slots on each half of the bow-tie and metamaterials inside the cavity are proposed for the wideband operation in the V/UHF band. The antenna operates in the frequency range of 240 MHz – 420 MHz with VSWR < 2.0:1 while maintaining positive realized gain with a maximum value of 4.5 dBi. The overall size of the proposed antenna is 0.36λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</inf> x 0.36λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</inf> x 0.04λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</inf>, only 5 cm in depth instead of a quarter wavelength, corresponding to 85% size reduction.

articleTitle: Effective Predictions of Snow Scattering Characteristics Using Neural Networks and The Quasi-Crystalline Approximation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Prediction of snow scattering characteristics is critical to active and passive microwave remote sensing of snow. In this paper, we combine the quasi-crystalline approximation (QCA) scattering model and a neural network to effectively predict the scattering parameters of snow. These include the effective permittivity, the scattering coefficient, the absorption coefficient, and the phase matrix. The physics driven neural network is shown to outperform a purely data-driven neural network. The developed framework significantly speeds up the computational efficiency compared to the QCA scattering model.

articleTitle: Design of EM Skins for Windowed Building Facades by Means of Non-Radiating Currents
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a synthesis strategy is proposed to design Static Passive Smart Skins that match the desired reflection pattern and can be installed on building facades presenting one or more windows. Thanks to the profitable exploitation of Non-Radiating (NR) currents, the proposed approach enables decoupling the field-matching requirements from the geometrical constraints and addresses them separately. The potentiality of the proposed approach is demonstrated in a simple illustrative example.

articleTitle: A Deep-Learning Characteristic Modes Classification Model for Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a deep-learning surrogate model is developed with the objective to predict the characteristic modes of any general geometry. Namely, a physics-based correlation function is introduced capable of classifying the modal currents of different geometries. These currents are used in turn to train our image-based supervised deep neural network. To generate the desired number of arbitrary geometrical shapes, Gielis’ supershape formula is utilized. As a proof-of-concept, our algorithm is tested on patch antennas that have shapes of perturbed rectangles. Our results show that our deep neural network has good predictive ability.

articleTitle: Transition Matrix in Characteristic Modes Theory
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This abstract presents the versatility and computational effectiveness of characteristic mode decomposition based on the transition matrix. The described treatment is valid for all lossless and linear material distributions and is independent of the numerical method used to resolve a particular scattering scenario.

articleTitle: Conformal Irregular-Grid Metasurfaces Comprising a Dense Array of Free-Standing Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: For large or infinite metasurfaces, a design technique for a dense array of subwavelength resonators on an irregular grid is presented. For a given incident wave, the desired induced dipole moment distribution determines the local electric field that excites individual meta-atoms. The interaction field that accounts for mutual coupling is evaluated via a combination of discrete coupling from nearby resonators and continuous sheet current coupling from far-separated resonators. Meta-atoms placed on an irregular grid can be treated, greatly enhancing the flexibility in surface profile in practical conformal metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Screen-Printed, Compact, Flexible ISM Antenna for Wrist Wearability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Wearables have been gaining popularity in the current decade, which needs a wearable antenna design that adheres to certain requirements including human tissue compatibility, flexibility, and low cost. In this work, a printed, compact, and flexible patch antenna is proposed for wrist wearables applications. The proposed antenna has compact dimensions of 36mmx44mmx0.5mm with a full ground plane of 50mmx100mm to be wrapped around the wrist. Although bending and human tissue proximity affect the bandwidth, the resulting bandwidth is 72MHz at the 2.4GHz ISM band. Meanwhile, the realized gain of the antenna at the center frequency is 1.65dBi and a specific absorption rate (SAR) of only 0.06W/kg.

articleTitle: Transient Port Parameter Extraction for Analysis of Coupled Linear EM and Nonlinear Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The ability to extract temporal port parameters from the interface between a coupled EM-device system is highly desirable for a number of applications, particularly in high-frequency systems involving strongly nonlinear devices. Among the manifold advantages are computational benefits, reuse of port parameters to incorporate any device, and potential integration with other physical models. While port extraction methods are commonplace in Fourier methods, constructing them in time domain was, until recently, untenable. The objective of this paper is to construct and validate a general transient port extraction method that is flexible to device models and can stably evaluate complex nonlinear systems. We present a number of numerical results that validate the method and demonstrate the proposed benefits.

articleTitle: Research on Time Domain Crosstalk Between Twisted Pairs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the time-domain crosstalk between twisted pairs is solved for the first time by using the Two Step Crank-Nicolson Finite Difference Time Domain (TS-CN-FDTD) algorithm previously proposed by the authors. It combines the Crank-Nicolson (CN) difference and two-step FDTD to propose a new unconditionally stable method with high accuracy. A set of uniform five-conductor transmission line models are established where both the disturbing lines and disturbed lines are also twisted pairs, and the time domain crosstalk of the model is solved by the TS-CN-FDTD algorithm. The correctness of this method is verified by comparing the time domain crosstalk results of single line and twisted pairs in the existing literature. Finally, the time domain result of voltage and current between the twisted pairs is obtained.

articleTitle: Holographic Inversion for Millimeter Wave Imaging Based on Range Stacking and Coherence Factor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the recently indigenously developed general holographic imaging (HI) algorithm based on linear frequency modulation (LFM), namely GHI-LFM, for millimeter wave imaging (MMWI), is further improved by using range stacking (RS) and coherence factor (CF), called HI-RS-CF. While avoiding the traditional time-consuming interpolation operation by using RS, the imaging accuracy is further improved by using CF. Consequently, both the imaging efficiency and accuracy are apparently improved. It is validated by imaging using both synthetic data of benchmark objects and real data.

articleTitle: Low-profile inductive metasurface for surface wave excitation in L-band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a low profile inductive surface for High Frequency Surface Wave Radars (HFSWR). The long-term operating frequency band considered is High Frequency (HF). In this paper we will only discuss L-band in order to simplify the manufacturing phase and the proof of concept. A compact thin 2D Super Inductive Surface (SIS) based on printed metal rings excited by an L-band monopole (1.1 GHz) is proposed to significantly increase (10 dB at the extremity of the SIS and 7 dB one wavelength further) an electric field in TM polarization (electric field normal to the air/sea interface) required to excite a surface wave. The proposed SIS thickness 10.26 mm ($\frac{\lambda }{{30}}$), is approximatly three times thinner than a recent 3D SIS developed both in L-band and HF-band ($\frac{\lambda }{{10}}$ ) which makes it possible to consider surface wave launchers of much lower height in the HF-band in the future. A 2D L-band prototype with a bandwidth of 130 MHz was manufactured and ElectroMagnetic Infrared measuRements (EMIR) confirmed simulated SIS performances.

articleTitle: Microwave Head Imaging Based on On-Body Matched Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A microwave head imaging system for intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) detection is proposed in this paper. The system is based on an 8-element antenna array, in which each antenna element is an on-body matched differentially-fed magneto-electric (ME) dipole. The antenna element with compact size operates in a wide bandwidth from 0.45 GHz to 2.4 GHz and exhibits unidirectional near-field radiation patterns with high front-to-back ratios (FBR) and stable main beam, which all contribute to good detection capability for the proposed imaging system. The reconstructed two-dimensional images inside the head model demonstrate the successful detection and localization of the small circular bleeding area (radius=5 mm) by the system in experiments, and it has the capability to detect multiple bleeding areas inside the human brain, which indicates the head imaging system has the potential to be used in clinical trials.

articleTitle: Rotational Magnetic Field Generated by Metasurface for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Conventional WPT systems suffer from angular misalignment of the receiver position. This paper proposed metasurface-inspired resonator which can generate rotational magnetic field. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed transmitter can achieve WPT efficiency of 68% and it remains almost constant for any rotational angle of the receiver. This result paves the way for potential applications in consumer electronics.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-based Antennas for On-Chip Applications in the Millimeter-Wave Range
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present the design of metamaterial-based antennas for on-chip applications using the Jerusalem Cross metamaterial structure to improve the radiation and electrical properties of three types of antennas: Monopole, dipole, and Vivaldi. The enhancements were derived from full-wave simulations. The central frequency of these antennas is 78.5 GHz. The three topologies were designed on a high resistivity silicon wafer and a silicon dioxide insulation layer. The frequency range, and materials used for the design are suitable for on-chip applications such as vehicular radar systems as well as other E-band applications.

articleTitle: Accurate Modeling for Electromagnetic Interaction with Plasma Mass Based on Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The re-entry capsule of space craft will produce a high temperature due to its strong friction with air when it re-entries the atmospheric layer and this will produce a plasma sheath which surrounds the capsule and prevents the propagation of electromagnetic (EM) wave. The interaction of EM wave with such a plasma sheath has not been well addressed. In this work, we use the integral equation method to solve the problem by establishing a model. The EM characteristic is described by volume-surface integral equations (VSIEs) and the Nyström method is used to solve the VSIEs. A numerical example about the EM scattering by a metallic sphere surrounded by a plasma-like medium is presented and the good performance of the proposed approach has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Design of an Electrically Small, Folded Dipole Antenna for Wireless Electromyography Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An electrically small, folded dipole antenna is proposed for use in wireless electromyography systems with operation frequencies within the ISM band (2.4 GHz to 2.5 GHz). Using miniaturization techniques, full coverage of ISM band is achieved while keeping an electrical size, kr, of 0.65, a physical diameter under 1 inch, and a 2-dimensional design with no added thickness. The proposed antenna design achieves a -10-dB impedance bandwidth of 0.114 GHz covering from 2.391 GHz to 2.505 GHz and has a fractional bandwidth of 4.65%. This achieves full coverage of all channels presented by the ISM band with a minimum radiation efficiency of 98.9%.

articleTitle: Non-Conforming Direct Domain Decomposition Methods (D3M)
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A direct domain decomposition method (D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>M) for non-conforming finite element electromagnetic computations is proposed. This method extends the applicability of the conforming D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>M in [5] to domains with non-matching unstructured triangulations across domain interfaces, while retaining symmetry, minimal size and sparsity of the interface matrix. The method relies on a novel integral equation (IE) based coupling. This coupling offers markedly improved accuracy and reliability over the more conventional Dirichlet transmission condition nonconforming coupling. Numerical results confirm the accuracy of the proposed non-conforming D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>M on complex and realistic structures.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient Power Transmission-Conversion Chain For a Wireless and Battery-Free EEG Cap
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The goal of this study is to introduce practical state-of-the-art considerations for designing a highly efficient power generation, transmission, and conversion chain system, PGTCC, to power up the front-end’s electronics that acquire satisfactory EEG signal acquisition in a portable wireless and battery-free EEG cap. Several solutions, strategies, and unique configurations have been presented to reach this goal, including, a highly efficient and compact resonance-inductive link, multi-resonator power transfer, use of magnetized materials to improve power transmission efficiency, closed-loop power transmission, and a highly efficient power conversion chain. The proposed design has the potential to significantly improve the total efficiency and supply stable power for the front-end units that include the EEG signal, filtering, noise cancelation amplification units, processing units, and transceivers.

articleTitle: Analysis of Circularly-Polarized Millimeter-Wave Antennas for Rotatable Wireless Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A 135–170-GHz circularly-polarized antenna for rotateable contactless millimeter-wave (mm-wave) interconnects is designed and analyzed. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time circularly polarized antennas with wide bandwidth are proposed for mm-wave wireless interconnects. To evaluate the performance of the proposed antennas for wireless mm-wave interconnects, time and frequency domain performance metrics such as fidelity factor and group delay are investigated. Results demonstrate that the proposed antennas feature fidelity factors of more than 98.94% and a linear variation of transmission coefficients phases with group delay variations less than 0.01 ns.

articleTitle: A Broadband Reflectarray with Independently Controlled Dual-Beams
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A broadband 1-bit independently dual-polarized dual-beam reflectarray antenna (RA) based on a magneto-electric dipole (MED) unit cell is proposed. This unit cell employs four stubs, which can be short-circuited (SC) or open-circuited (OC) to independently control two orthogonal linearly polarized beams. The proposed unit cell exhibits a very wide reflection phase bandwidth from 31.5 to 54 GHz (54.1 %). The radiation characteristics of the RA are obtained analytically, using the aperture field approach. The proposed reflectarray achieves a 1.5dB gain bandwidth of 35 % from 32 to 45.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Ka-band Reflectarray Antenna for Broadband LEO Satellite System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents design of a high gain circularly polarized Ka-band reflectarray antenna for Starlink LEO broad band services. A pentagon shaped patch is chosen as reflecting element to enhance the required circular polarization. Dual polarized conical horn antenna is used as a CP feeding for the proposed design. The proposed reflectarray antenna is simulated and the gain is estimated at 18 GHz to be 18 dBi,

articleTitle: A Differential Aperture-Coupled Laminated Resonator Antenna with High Common-Mode Suppression
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a differential aperture-coupled laminated resonator antenna (LRA) with high common-mode (CM) suppression for the first time. Based on low-cost PCB technology, a single microstrip line is adopted to feed the proposed LRA through a coupling slot. Under differential-mode (DM) excitation, an efficient coupling can be established from the feedline to the LRA resonating at TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf> mode. Then, unidirectional radiation is obtained. Under CM excitation, the LRA cannot be excited due to its in-correct signal phasing so that a high level of CM suppression can be achieved. For verification, a prototype antenna is simulated, fabricated and measured. Experimental results exhibit that the proposed differential aperture-coupled LRA features high level of CM rejection, high radiation efficiency, low cross polarization and symmetric patterns.

articleTitle: A New Microwave Imaging System for Dielectric Characterization of Highly Organic Arctic Permafrost Soil
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-band microwave imaging system that operates at P- and L-bands for the quantitative dielectric reconstruction of organic soil with various saturation levels. Multi-band operation and miniaturization were achieved by introducing slots in the radiating edge of a microstrip patch sandwiched between a substrate and supersaturate layer. The geometry and location of the soil sample container were designed to be in the center of the imaging cavity to simplify the inverse scatting reconstruction algorithm. Preliminary reconstruction of synthetic objects obtained through Born Approximation showed the promising performance of the system to reconstruct a realistic range of dielectric constants of soil samples. The antenna array and the imaging system were fabricated, and preliminary measured results of antenna performance showed good agreement between design and fabrication. This work is of particular interest in physics-based radar retrieval of highly organic arctic soil properties, where the dielectric models of soil are needed in the forward-inverse scattering framework.

articleTitle: High-gain Dual-pol Conical Dielectric Resonator Antenna Fed by a Cavity-Backed Slot
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A conical dielectric resonator antenna fed by a rectangular cavity-backed slot is proposed. The design consists of a conical dielectric antenna lying on a cavity-backed slot excited by a coaxial probe. This design aims to block the undesired radiation and enhance the antenna radiation quality to obtain high gain and support exciting high-order modes. Compared to that of other high gain antennas, the proposed design can provide high gain at a lower cost with easy fabrication for dual-pol capability.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Circular Ring Slot Patch Antenna for Low Frequency Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A study of a miniaturized square microstrip antenna design for low frequency applications is proposed. The rationale of the design is accomplished by adding circular ring slots at the top of the antenna patch to acquire a unique lowest operating frequency range and the dimension reduction. Two small parasitic patches are coupled to the edge of the radiating aperture to improve the antenna impedance bandwidth. This design is later adapted to a layer of metasurface superstrate structure loaded over the antenna, which effectively shifts the antenna operating frequency to a lower level range. The design is optimized for a relative impedance bandwidth of 41.4% extending from 0.46 to 0.7 GHz with a good performance of the realized gain up to 7.31 dBi.

articleTitle: Stability Control of Unsymmetrical Time-Domain Methods
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Unsymmetrical numerical methods in time domain have become increasingly important. However, the stability of an unsymmetrical system is generally unknown and difficult to control. In this work, we propose a theory and develop an efficient method to control and enforce the stability of unsymmetrical methods. The proposed method is then applied to analyze and control the stability of a matrix-free time-domain method in unstructured meshes, whose underlying numerical system is highly unsymmetrical. Numerical experiments have validated the proposed method for the stability control and enforcement of unsymmetrical numerical methods without compromising accuracy.

articleTitle: Multipath Assisted Single Base Station Positioning for NLOS Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multipath assisted single base station positioning technology in NLOS environment. Firstly, a scattering model is constructed according to the spatial layout near the base station. Secondly, the parameters of multipath signals are processed by a joint clustering algorithm, which are used to establish positioning equations with the help of the spatial layout information of the scattering area model. Finally, particle swarm algorithm based on natural selection (NPSO) is utilized to solve the objective function to acquire the target position. Simulation results show that the NPSO algorithm has better positioning accuracy compared with Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm and this method can be used in single-station positioning in an outdoor non-line-of-sight (NLOS) environment.

articleTitle: Method to Obtain Structures in Multi-port Cavity Based on Physics-Informed Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a method to obtain structures in multi-port cavity is proposed. The time-reversal method is applied to obtain a rough physical topology of the intracavity structure. Further, a U-net is introduced to extract the final device structure. In addition, networks based on adversarial autoencoder with physics constraints have been proposed for multi-port device design with better results. Both methods achieve a better means of initial value construction, which will provide an initial solution for the iterative optimization method of the multi-port devices inverse design, and is even expected to be an alternative method.

articleTitle: Antenna Designs for CubeSat-Borne Continuous-Waveform Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: CubeSat-borne radar has many potential applications in space exploration, including tracking, imaging, and weather prediction. A continuous-waveform radar has advantages of compact size and low power consumption, making it suitable to implement on small platforms such as CubeSats. This paper presents power budget analysis that sets the required isolation between the transmitter and receiver. The presented approach is to integrate oppositely polarized antennas on two deployed solar panels to minimize the interference. The prototyped antennas are tested on a 6U CubeSat frame and the results show more than 40 dB isolation, satisfying the power budget requirements.

articleTitle: Prof. Sarkar’s contribution to Antenna Diagnostics and NF-FF Transformation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This contribution summarizes one of the numerous contributions to electromagnetics of Prof. Sarkar. In particular, it is focused on the equivalent currents-based techniques for antenna diagnostics and Near-Field to Far-Field (NF-FF) transformation. First, the theoretical background is briefly presented, followed by a review of the main works developed by Prof. Sarkar in this field. Finally, the importance and impact of Prof. Sarkar’s work on this topic is highlighted.

articleTitle: A Ku band Waveguide Horn Array with Sidelobe Suppression
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a novel high gain waveguide horn array with sidelobe reduction using a shifted and twisted septum technique. A Prototype 64 element waveguide array antenna is constructed for test. A final weigh reduced antenna will be built using additive manufacturing.

articleTitle: Suppression of Mutual Coupling in Dual Differentially Fed Microstrip Patch Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, mutual coupling suppression in a dual differentially fed microstrip patch antenna array with polarization diversity is studied. The investigated antenna is an array of two square patches and each patch is fed with two differential pairs to generate multiple polarization. A metamaterial absorbing wall is placed between the patches to isolate the patches in both E and H planes. The absorber wall comprises of an array of split ring resonators (SRR) printed within a dielectric substrate to decouple the patches. The introduction of the absorber wall results in an isolation enhancement of 15 dB and 5 dB in the E and H-planes respectively over a frequency bandwidth of 9.33-9.45 GHz.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Double-Layer Transmitarray Antenna Based on Split Cross Dipole Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A double-layer dual-polarized transmitarray antenna (TA) using the split cross dipole elements is proposed for millimeter-wave applications in this paper. The elements consist of two layers of identical split cross dipole printed on a dielectric substrate. Metal vias are employed to augment the transmission magnitude of the element. The phase shift is controlled by varying the length of the dipole. A 14X14-element TA is designed, fabricated, and measured. The measured results show a peak gain of 25.92 dBi at 30 GHz, together with an aperture efficiency of 43.1%. The maximum peak gain reaches 26.36 dBi at 30.7 GHz, and the 3-dB gain bandwidth is 11.5%.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Magnetoelectric Dipole for 3G/LTE/Sub-6GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new ultra-wideband magnetoelectric (ME) dipole antenna is proposed as a dual-polarized base station antenna for 3G, LTE and Sub-6GHz 5G wireless networks. Double layers of ME dipoles with different sizes are combined to expand the bandwidth, and the orthogonal placement of ME dipoles enables dual polarization radiation. Simulation results reveal that the proposed base station antenna achieves 133.3% fractional bandwidth and satisfying radiation characteristics, including high front-to-back ratio (FBR) (>14 dB), high cross-polarization levels (>20 dB), and stable gains about 5-10 dBi in 1-5GHz.

articleTitle: Wireless Information and Power Transfer Systems in Biomedicine: A New Perspective on High-Speed Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The near-field wireless information and power transfer system that can support high data rate applications presented in this paper. It was developed by coupling dual-band resonators (DBRs) oscillating at the practical frequencies of 433 MHz and 900 MHz. In turn, the required DBRs were designed applying the slotted ground plane technique. Furthermore, when two 20×20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> DBRs are separated by 18 mm, the power transfer efficiency was measured to be around 60% for both operating bands. Finally, the obtained bandwidth of 9 MHz at the data transfer band allows allocating several resource blocks.

articleTitle: Genetic Programming for Advanced Metamaterial Design: A Legacy of a Perfectionist
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this presentation we celebrate Professor Tapan Sarkar’s legacy and outstanding contributions to the electromagnetic community by drawing parallelisms between his innovative and longstanding contributions to the electromagnetic technologies.

articleTitle: RF Sensing for Smoking Detection at Oil Fields
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband (UWB) Radar sensor is used to detect human gestures while smoking or vaping in potentially dangerous areas such as an oil field or a gas station. Existing smoking detection systems are primarily camera-based, which has a number of drawbacks, including poor illumination, training issues with longer video sequence data, and major privacy concerns. The data collected from a UWB Radar is represented in the form of spectrograms. Three classes are considered, namely cigarette, vape and when the subject is not smoking. InceptionV3, VGG19, and VGG16 deep learning algorithms are used to extract spatiotemporal information from the Spectrogram. Finally, by classifying the Spectrograms into the considered gestures, the smoking and/or vaping is accurately identified. The simulation results show that InceptionV3 can achieve a maximum classification accuracy of 90.00%.

articleTitle: Investigating The data rate of Intelligent Reflecting Surface Under Different Deployments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is capable to control the scattering, reflection, and refraction characteristics of the electromagnetic signals. The IRS is usually deployed near the distributed users for the purpose of enhancement the local coverage which is completely different from that for the active relay, almost placed in the middle of the transmitter and receiver for balancing the signal to noise ratio (SNRs) of the two-hop links, that process and amplify the source signal before forwarding it to the receiver. We have studied the deployment of IRS for different locations in SISO wideband system with single antenna at the AP and each user. We used the communication setup considered in the IEEE signal processing Cup 2021 to investigate the user data rate enhancement under different IRS deployments. Simulation results have shown that the data rate improved when the IRS is placed either near the users or the AP. However, the data rate has been reduced when placing the IRS in the middle between the AP and the users.

articleTitle: Optimizing DCIM for Layered Green Functions for Quasi-Electrostatic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A method for optimizing the DCIM approximation for the spatial domain layered Green function for low-frequency quasi-electrostatic analysis is presented. The method is based on a novel decomposition of the spectral Green function. The proper DCIM parameters of these terms are found by optimizing the Matrix Pencil method solution for the discrete residues and poles. The method has been found to provide at least six digits of accuracy for layered medium with highly disparate layer thickness and material constants.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Partially Reflective Surface based Beam-Steering Antenna with RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a beam-steering (BS) antenna based on reconfigurable partially reflective surface (PRS) with a wideband probe feed is proposed. The PRS and feed antenna form a Fabry-Perot resonance cavity, which leads to the improvement in the radiation characteristics of the beam. The abosrbing structure can scatter electromanetic waves propagating externally, and thus reduce the antenna radar cross section. The phase of PRS unit changes with electrical parameters of loaded diodes, thus achieving beam-steering. The beam tilting angle can be deflected to 0°, ±8° and ±16° in elevation when resonating at 5.5 GHz, and the peak gain up to 11.1 dBi is noted.

articleTitle: Leaky Surface Waves Suppression Using Simple Planar Patch-type AMC Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes the usage of planar artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) structures in place of traditional pin/via-based electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures to suppress leaky surface waves in waveguides. Compared to conventional mushroom-type / pin-based elements, planar structures allow for ease in the scalability of radio frequency (RF) devices to the sub-THz frequency band using the existing manufacturing technique. A square patch-type AMC element is considered for simplicity. The periodic AMC structure is applied in a groove gap waveguide type structure in place of pins to study the effectiveness of the structure. An approach to optimize the performance of the AMC is also shown using simulation results.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of Phased Array Antennas for ST Radar Operating at 53MHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work discusses the design of an atmospheric radar using active phased array comprising three element Yagi Uda antennas and high-power amplifiers. The radar operates at 53MHz and will help to understand the atmospheric turbulations in the Indo-Gangetic plain wherein land sea interactions play an important role in framing the atmospheric processes. The associated challenges in system design and antenna characterization is discussed.

articleTitle: Utilization of Characteristic Modal Analysis for the Antenna Design Needed for an AFIT Satellite
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Antenna design is a pervasive knowledge base for electrical engineers. As the number of new materials and techniques increase, so too do the demand and requirements pushing forth new innovative ideas to expand the capabilities antennas can achieve. Characteristic Modal Analysis (CMA), originally credited to Garbacz and Turpin [1], is a leading edge analytic technique that is one of these ideas. CMA breaks down the current distribution along a structure in a way that can offer great insights into how that structure operates as an antenna. This technique has great merits in post design analytics and can be integrated into the design process. This paper applies the techniques of CMA to create independent designs for a single antenna problem involving a AFIT Satellite. The results are three different designs that meet the requirements proving the utility of CMA in the antenna design process for this specific application.

articleTitle: A Circular Polarized Antenna with Fine Tuning Parameter for Dual Band Operation in C-band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual band patch antenna for operation in C band. The design of the antenna is based on the modal degeneration mechanism applied to a circular patch. The patch is gap-coupled with two pairs of parasitic reactive elements, which are the key of the dual band operation.To achieve adequate control of the two operation frequencies, the coupling is implemented as a distributed inter-digit capacitor. This feature permits the fine tuning of the coupling resulting in a higher control of the two resonances.

articleTitle: Channelized Frequency Synchronization Using Consensus Averaging for Distributed Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We demonstrate a novel channelized consensus frequency synchronization approach that enables separate radio-frequency wireless systems to converge at a consistent operating frequency, enabling distributed phase-coherent wireless operations. The approach is based on decentralized averaging, which is a consensus-based coordination approach. Nodes transfer their frequencies to neighboring nodes and calculate the average of their frequencies and their neighbors’ frequencies. The approach is decentralized, thus there is no single point of failure as in typical centralized approaches, and the consensus frequency is tolerant to adding nodes, dropping nodes, and drifting oscillator frequencies. We use a channelized approach where nodes transfer their frequencies on designated subcarriers, supporting full-duplex operation. We analyze the algorithm convergence through a proof-of-concept microwave wireless testbed using software-defined radios, demonstrating consensus frequency operation between four separate radios.

articleTitle: Bands in 3D Periodic Structures with the Broadband Green’s Function-Multiple Scattering Theory
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We apply the BBGF-MST (Broadband Green’s function-Multiple Scattering Theory) to calculate Band Structures and Band Field Solutions in periodic structures A feature of BBGF is that the lattice Green’s functions are broadband and are calculated rapidly for many frequencies for speedy calculation of the determinant of the KKR (Koringa-Kohn-Rostoker) equation. Using BBGF-MST, a low order matrix eigenvalue equation for the bands is derived. Previously, the method was applied to 2D problems. In this paper, we have extended the method to 3D problems. For the first two bands, the dimension of the matrix equation is only 9 by 9. Numerical results of the band diagrams are illustrated.

articleTitle: Performance of Array Decomposition Method with Higher-Order Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The performance of the Array Decomposition Method for finite regular antenna arrays with arbitrary identical elements using higher-order basis functions is investigated. We demonstrate how using higher-order basis functions results in significantly reduced simulation time for a 10×10 (22λ×22λ) circular horn array, without the need for approximations.

articleTitle: Array Scanning Method-Macro Basis Function for Connected Arrays of Printed Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a fast finite array analysis technique based on the Infinite Array solution. The developed technique is the extension of the Array Scanning Method-Macro Basis Function (ASM-MBF) approach to the layered medium, applicable to antennas that are printed on a substrate backed by a ground plane. This method has been validated for the connected array case for which other types of MBF methods require specific treatment and have practical difficulties. Results are validated for the port currents in a large connected antenna array.

articleTitle: Surface Wave Wavefront Formation with Photonic Graphene and Topological Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We propose a printed circuit board (PCB) metasurface that can construct surface waves with uniform wavefronts and large beam apertures within a sub-wavelength-long region. The effect stems from the "pseudo-diffusive" resonance that happened at the corners of the first Brillouin zone of graphene-like photonic crystals (PhCs), where the energy propagates omnidirectionally while the phase velocity is locked at a single direction. Valley-constrained photonic topological waveguide plays an important role in this design to properly couple the energy into the desired diffusive mode. The design can be potentially used to build new PCB-based microwave devices such as miniaturized horns.

articleTitle: Optimization of mean inter-element distance in aperiodic sparse linear phased array antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Sparse linear arrays are attractive when high directivity and low cost should be simultaneously achieved, when near field coupling must be avoided, or when physical constraints limit the minimum separation between elements. However, uniformly distributed sparse arrays present strong side lobes that may cause severe interference and security faults. Thus, the non-uniform arrangement of elements has been extensively proposed to reduce the side lobe level (SLL). In this paper, we present numerical results revealing that when a minimum inter-element separation is considered, there is an optimum mean distance that minimizes the SLL of the array.

articleTitle: Meshed Conductor Considerations for Optically Transparent Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Transparent antennas are a uniquely enabling technology permitting antennas to be hidden in windshields, disguised in consumer electronic displays, and even utilized in dual-use optical-RF apertures. The key enabling technology for transparent antennas is the transparent conductor. Their primary challenge is balancing optical and RF performance, which typically tradeoff performance. The manuscript presents the practical performance limitations of these conductors with evidence from the published literature. Additionally, insights into transparent conductor fabrication methods and extensions toward their use as antennas are presented. Furthermore, key parameter threshold considerations when designing transparent antennas with a meshed conductor to achieve optimal antenna performance are described in terms of radiation performance and transparency.

articleTitle: Bagley Polygon Power Divider using Simplified Composite Right/Left Handed Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a Bagley Polygon power divider using Simplified-Composite Right/Left Handed (S-CRLH) transmission line (TL) is presented. Bagley Polygon power divider provides possibility of selecting the desired phase in the third port in one or two bands by using metamaterial transmission lines or conventional lines. The proposed design supports two frequency bands at 2.4GHz and 5.2GHz with a compact size of 55mm x 55mm. The results of the CRLH and S-CRLH structures are also compared. It is noted that S-CRLH as compared to CRLH exhibits small dimensions of the structure, including optimal bandwidth and lowest return losses.

articleTitle: RF-induced heating evaluation for patients during MRI breast imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the radiofrequency (RF)-induced heating for patients undergoing Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) breast imaging. One supine and three prone posture models are developed based on the posable female adult model. The electromagnetic fields inside these four posture models are evaluated numerically. The simulated results show that the peak averaged specific absorption rate over 1 gram has no substantial difference among the four posture models. However, the electric field distributions in the coronal slice for the prone posture models are higher than from supine posture model. It is observed that there is no evidence indicating the RF-induced heating hazards for patients during MRI breast imaging. However, higher electric field distributions in the spinal region can potentially lead to RF-induced heating concerns for patients with spinal implants.

articleTitle: Dual-mode antenna for sub-GHz terrestrial and space IoT communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A dual-mode antenna structure with the capability to generate a wide beam RHCP pattern or an omni-directional radiation pattern with a vertical polarization is proposed at 910MHz . The structure suits perfectly to future hybrid IoT terminal compatible with terrestrial and space network.

articleTitle: Planar, Lossless and Scan Angle Enhancing Lens for E-band Automotive Radars using Ray Transfer Compensation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new method to realize a planar lossless scan angle enhancing metasurface lens (SAEML) for automotive application is discussed and proposed. The method uses ray transfer matrix and ray-tracing analysis to extend the scan range and minimize the scan loss. A lens-prototype designed using the proposed method is designed at 76.5 GHz, fabricated, and measured. The prototype features an extended scan range of 54° with a maximum gain loss of 1.4 dB, highlighting this to be the first-reported planar, lossless lens at millimeter-wave spectrum.

articleTitle: An Angularly Stable Triple-band Reflective Polarizing Surface Using a Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Linear-to-circular polarization converters with wide- and multi-band capabilities can simplify antenna systems where circular polarization is desired. Multi-band solutions are attractive in satellite communication systems, which commonly have the additional requirement that the sense of polarization is reversed between bands. However, the design of these structures using conventional methods is ad hoc and relies heavily on empirical methods. Here, we employ a data-driven approach integrated with a generative adversarial network to explore the space of polarizer unit cells thoroughly. A triple-band reflective surface with stable performance over incident angles up to and including 30° is proposed.

articleTitle: A Novel Design of X-band Microwave Absorber Based on Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a metamaterial microwave absorber with a shape of rotating open square double ring is proposed for X-band frequency. The absorber has a unit cell with a size of 0.1λ × 0.1λ × 0.072λ at 10 GHz and consists of a resonant layer, substrate, and metal ground. By adjusting parameters of the resonant elements, high absorptivity in the X-band is achieved. The simulation results show that the absorptivity is higher than 94% in the X-band range and has two distinctive absorption peaks with the absorptivities of about 99% occurring at the frequencies of 8.44 GHz and 11.10 GHz, respectively. Also the absorber is insensitive to both the polarization and incident angle of incident wave.

articleTitle: On Objective-Aware Adaptive Methods in Computational Electromagnetics: Comparing Error Estimation and Indication Approaches for Problems with Singular Solutions
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We summarize the application of goal-oriented adaptive methods in computational electromagnetics (CEM), that, as opposed to methods based purely on indicators, tailor discretizations in accordance with a collection of objectives, namely the accurate computation of certain quantities of interest (QoIs). When the accuracy of the goal separates from the properties of an underlying indicator (e.g., the jump in some functional of the solution), numerical results (and the predicted accuracy of those results) may subsequently diverge, rendering undetectably unreliable simulations. In the presence of singular, or otherwise burdensome solution behavior, which requires many degrees of freedom (DoFs) to model with acceptable accuracy, neglecting the objective in the refinement procedure may yield particularly poor results in addition to refinement inefficiencies. To elucidate these connections, we compare a goaloriented error estimation approach with a pure indicator methodology for the Maxwell eigenvalue problem, with a focus on an eigenpair with a singular eigenfunction. Driving ineffectual refinements, refinement based on indicators disconnected from the accuracy of the goal quantity can deliver poor convergence behavior in comparison to equivalent goal-oriented adaption.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement Using Corrugated Horn Feed for Optic Lens Antenna Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A high gain and high efficiency optic lens antenna is presented. The antenna gain is enhanced by using an optimized corrugated horn as the optic lens feed, and moreover, the radiation patterns are improved with reduced sidelobe level. The simulated return loss is better than 15 dB from 80 to 90 GHz. A high gain of exceeding 43.5 dBi is realized and the sidelobe levels in both E and H planes are lower than -32 dB. And aperture efficiency of better than 45% is achieved over the operating frequency band. It is suitable to design high-gain and low sidelobe antennas in millimeter wave and terahertz bands.

articleTitle: Dual Slot Two Element MIMO Antennas for Multi-Band Frequency Agility
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A frequency diversity multi-band MIMO antenna is presented in this paper. The 2×1 MIMO antenna consists of two identical radiating elements each having a rectangular slot with a hexagonal slot being placed in the inner conducting element. A 50 Ω microstrip feeding line has been placed on the other side of the substrate and being optimized for impedance matching. Each radiator contains a varactor diode with a variable capacitance characteristic based on the applied inverse biasing voltages that are ranging from 0 – 15 V. The proposed antenna exhibits a quad frequency band of operation (2.32 – 2.44), (2.88 – 3.16), (4.32 – 5.25), and (5.21 – 5.71) GHz with the ability to tune the center frequency within each band based on the varactor biasing voltage. Several parameters have been investigated such as the diversity gain (DG), ECC for an efficient view of MIMO features.

articleTitle: Antenna Technologies for Ubiquitously Connected and Immersive Future
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents opportunities and challenges of antenna technologies for mobile network-based connected future and immersive applications.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Scanning Liquid Crystal Infrared Reflect Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a new reflectarray technology capable of scanning in two dimensions. The device is a reflective semiconductor chip composed of small two-stage phase delay cavities filled with electrically biased liquid crystal. The scanning is enabled by changes in the AC electrical bias, which modifies the effective dielectric constant of the liquid crystal. This enables each cavity to delay the fields in each stage by as much as 360 degrees. As a result, the two-stage cavity allows nearly independent scanning in two orthogonal planes. The structure operates at a wavelength of 1550nm and is manufactured using a standard damascene process.

articleTitle: High-Precision Localization of Multiple Passive Intermodulation Sources Based on Frequency-Extended Compressive Sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: High-precision localization of multiple passive intermodulation (PIM) sources is an interesting and challenging problem in electromagnetics. In this article, we present a method based on frequency-extended compressive sensing to solve this problem. Compared with the direct passive intermodulation localization, the frequency-extended compressive sensing method is effective in localizing more sources with high accuracy. The effectiveness of the method is verified by several numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Characterization of Nonlinear Electromagnetic Systems using the Koopman Operator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Wideband multi-carrier and multi-channel receivers are powerful communication system architectures for their high spectral efficiency, flexible bit-rates and data constellation format used by the dynamically selected sub-carriers. These systems, when augmented with MIMO (multiple input – multiple output) capabilities, further improve spectral efficiency and increase the number of users. However, the architectures that allow these performance benefits are also responsible for harmonic distortions, inter-channel crosstalk and inter-modulation products introduced by the nonlinear components of the receivers and nearby transmitters. The use of traditional analog linearization methods results in fairly complex and in many cases inadequate solutions. In addition, most time domain methods employed for electromagnetic modeling are either limited to linear systems or systems with known nonlinearities behavior. This paper introduces a time-domain method based on the concept of the Koopman Operator and describes its application to the characterization of dynamic systems with nonlinearities which are either unknown or difficult to mathematically describe.

articleTitle: A Coupled Integral Equation / Foldy-Lax Multiple Scattering Formulation to Characterize Topological One-Way Edge States
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The coupled integral equation - Foldy-Lax multiple scattering method is applied to compute the reflection-free topological one-way edge states induced by wave interactions with the interface between gyromagnetic scatterers and a PEC boundary. The scattered field of gyromagnetic scatterers is represented in terms of the exciting cylindrical wave coefficients and its scattering T matrix. The PEC boundary is also regarded as a scatterer and its scattered field is linked to the excitation fields with a surface integral equation discretized by method of moments. This multiple scattering formulation directly couples the scattered field of PEC wall with gyromagnetic scatterers. This method needs to compute the T matrix of gyromagnetic scatterer only once and significantly reduces the number of unknowns. Field results are compared with results from COMSOL simulations. The comparisons confirm the accuracy of the proposed method and show that it is far more efficient than COMSOL. The proposed approach can be a useful tool for topological wave device analysis and design.

articleTitle: Leaky waveguide with mecanically-controlled radiated power
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This article presents the topology of a leaky waveguide with mechanically-controlled radiated power allowing to radiate at each aperture the same amount of power. To do this, the number of opened slots is modified. Its design and radiation performances on the ISM band at 2.4 GHz are detailed. Achieved gain variation goes from 12.7 % up to 90 % of the incident power.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel Reconfigurable Waveguide Filter using Liquid Crystal in 5G Millimeter Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel reconfigurable waveguide filter using liquid crystal is proposed for the 5G-FR2 millimeter wave band applications. The influence of the liquid crystal under different bias voltages has been analyzed. The designed filter is based on the fourth-order Chebyshev prototype. The filter is fabricated and is measured using a vector network analyzer. The measured results show that the passband frequency of the filter can be tuned from 26.7 GHz to 28.8 GHz by controlling the voltage values of the static electrodes V1~V8. The filter can be applied to the three sub-bands of n257, n258 and n261 in the 5G-FR2 millimeter wave bands.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Boundary Condition Optimization applied to Nanoscale IR Antenna Structure Simulations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We explore the use of best fit impedance boundary conditions (IBCs) for use in electromagnetic structure simulators in realms where IBCs are not readily applicable. In particular, we apply the technique to the development of a on chip infrared antenna fabricated using a damascene process. The best fit IBC are synthesized by choosing the impedance values that best match the solution of a volumetric simulation on a small representative portion of the structure. These impedance values can then be applied to the entire structure to greatly reduce simulation time and facilitate design optimization.

articleTitle: Rapid Viral Detection Using Microwave Sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The electromagnetic field (EMF) of biomolecules can be utilized for detection and identification purposes. This paper is presenting a preliminary proof-of-concept experiment for rapid virus detection using an improved complementary split-ring resonator of mutually-coupled cells. Spectral responses of the sensor prototype have reliably indicated the presence of an Adeno-Associated Virus (AAV) in the hosting medium. Besides, two isolates of a fish virus were differentiated when tested in the near-field of the sensor. Promising results would revolutionize the space to develop an inexpensive, reusable, rapid EM testing technology for lab-on-chip virus detection to help combatting future pandemics.

articleTitle: Angular Stable Single/Dual/Triple Broadband Metamaterial-Based Reflection Type Polarization Converter For Terahertz Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new compact unit cell of reflection-type linear co to cross-polarization converter for terahertz applications which can be optimized easily for single wideband as well as dual and tri broadband polarization conversion. The unit cell of size 128 × 128 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> consists of asymmetrically oriented dual semi-circular trident shaped resonators, and converts a linear polarized incident wave into cross polarization over the frequency range of 0.57 to 0.74 THz (170 GHz) with polarization conversion ratio (PCR) > 90% and angular stability > 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> both for TE and TM modes. The modified structure exhibits polarization conversion between frequency ranges of 0.67-0.81 and 1.65 -1.90 THz for dual band, and 0.68-0.85, 1.57-1.71 and 2.09-2.15 THz for triple band respectively over PCR > 90%. The single band design shows nearly 100% polarization conversion from frequencies 0.61-0.68 THz while dual band shows the same at 0.75 and 1.84 THz.

articleTitle: Broadband Terahertz Meta-surface Absorber Based on Multi-layer Resonances
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a near-perfect terahertz absorber is proposed. Based on the multi-layer resonances, the meta-surface has obtained absorbing rate of more than 90% from 2.7THz to 4.38THz. Since the strict center symmetry of the structure, the same absorbing rate and bandwidth can be maintained for any polarization angle. In addition, while the incident angle is 40 degrees, the structure can hold the original bandwidth, and the absorbing rate is approximately maintained above 80%.

articleTitle: 1-bit Multipolarization Reconfigurable Metasurface for Dynamic Focusing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The reconfigurable metasurface improves the flexibility of the metasurface and solves the problem that the characteristics including the focus and focal length cannot be changed after the traditional focusing metasurface design is completed. Combining the metasurface with active phase shifter such as PIN diode to form a reconfigurable metasurface, the resonant status of the element can be changed by switching the diode. However, the flexibility of element polarization is often required in practical applications, which needs to be achieved by increasing the number of diodes. In this paper, we propose a 1-bit multipolarization reconfigurable metasurface element containing two diodes and one DC bias line. The 1-bit phase shift is achieved within 180°±20° at 5.56~6.38 GHz. Then a 20*20 array is formed to verify the dynamic focusing function, and the simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
