articleTitle: Design of an Ultra-Thin Metal-only Endfire Array Antenna Using Continuity of the Cross-Polarized Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An ultra-thin metal-only endfire array antenna is designed in this paper. The proposed endfire array antenna element consists of a metallic sheet with a split-ring slot, which is asymmetric along the x- and y-axes. Thanks to the geometric asymmetry of the proposed element, the endfire radiation of the endfire array antenna can be realized by utilizing the continuity of the cross-polarized electric field. Furthermore, a 16 × 16-element bidirectional endfire array antenna is designed by using the proposed 1-bit phasing element. For realizing unidirectional endfire beams, we change the endfire array antenna element spacing and incident angle of the plane wave to satisfy the Hansen-Woodyard (HW) condition. Finally, the simulation results show that the proposed endfire array antenna can be used to generate stably the bidirectional endfire and unidirectional endfire beams within the 11.6 GHz – 12.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a 1-Bit Broadband Low-Cost Metal-Only Reconfigurable Reflectarray with Polarization Transforming Capability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 1-bit broadband low-cost metal-only reconfigurable reflectarray (RRA) is designed at X-band. The 3-D spiral ladder element consists of a square base, a circular turntable and three ladders with different heights. By rotating the proposed 3-D RRA element mechanically, the 1-bit reflected phase and orthogonal polarization transforming are achieved. Then, a 26×26 metal-only RRA is designed and fed by 20° offsetting corrugated horn. The simulated gain of the pencil beam is 27.7 dBi @10.0GHz with aperture efficiency of 27.5%. And the −1 dB gain bandwidth is 24%, it shows that proposed RRA has a broadband characteristic. Compared with the RRA printed on the multilayer substrates which adjusts phase by switching RF switches, the proposed metal-only RRA has simple structure and no additional RF loss.

articleTitle: Investigation on Atmospheric Gradient to Establish the Seasonal Forecasting Criteria for Rainfall
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Rainfall forecasting using GPS signals has been an emerging field of research in recent decades. Several researches have been conducted on rainfall prediction based on the accumulation of water vapor. On the other hand, atmospheric gradient has gained the attention of the scientists in recent years, mostly for the application in point positioning. In this paper, we have investigated the behaviour of the gradient for different monsoon seasons in Singapore before precipitation. The variation in gradient angular estimates during both precipitation and non-rainy hours for all the four seasons provides a rainfall forecasting criteria for the tropical island Singapore. The gradient is mostly aligned with the direction of wind flow. The results bolster the fact that gradient can be a crucial parameter for the rainfall prediction along with Precipitable Water Vapor (PWV).

articleTitle: Design of a 5.8 GHz 1-bit Reconfigurable Slotted SIW Antenna Array with Four Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The design and simulations of a flexible beam-scanning slotted SIW antenna array is presented. The proposed element consists of two rectangular slots with opposite electric field directions on the metal surface. By turning on or off one of the two switches located in the center of the slots and making the other switch in the opposite state, one of the slots is excited, thus achieving 1-bit quantization phase with 180 ° phase difference. The simulated reflection coefficient at both phase states is -35.1 dB at 5.8 GHz. A 1-bit 4-element beam-scanning antenna array with the length of 128.0 mm is simulated. The -10 dB simulated impedance bandwidth of the 0 ° beam is 8.6%, the peak gain at 5.8 GHz is 11.6 dBi while the aperture efficiency is 70.4%, the beam scanning is ranged from -56 ° to +56 °.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Slot-Coupled Two-Layer Hemispherical Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Air-gap
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, a microstrip slot-coupled two-layer hemispherical dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with an air-gap between two dielectric layers is analyzed, that is particularly relevant to the design of multilayer DRA configurations. The Green’s function for the structure is formulated using the generalized reflection coefficient. The variation of the TE111 mode resonant frequency and Q-factor with the air-gap for the configuration is investigated. The effect of the air-gap on the input impedance / reflection coefficient along with radiation characteristics for the antenna configuration are also analyzed.

articleTitle: RF-Analog Hybrid Circuitry Emulating Pyramidal Cell Neuronal Behavior
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Classical neuron models have inspired decades of research and development for in silico hardware and AI software. McCulloch and Pitts developed one such model that relies on Hebbian's synaptic reinforcement principle. Today, we know that pyramidal cells, the most important excitatory neurons in the brain, include nonlinear NMDA-based dendritic integrations. Also, their synapses are reinforced in accordance to an asymmetric spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) principle. Energy efficient realization of these non-linear models in millions is very challenging. In this paper, for the first time, we present a novel RF-analog hybrid energy efficient equivalent model with a feedback mechanism to represent the non-linear behavior of L5 PCs.

articleTitle: Radio-Frequency Characterization of Thermally and Electrically Conductive Adhesives for Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The RF behavior of Thermally and Electrically Conductive Adhesive (TECA) material has been investigated for high-frequency applications through measurements that are documented in this paper. TECA materials are typically used to provide conductive bonding between substrate layers in high volume planar designs like antenna arrays. This study compared the performance of a copper microstrip transmission line with a TECA material, called COOLSPAN, which is a conductive epoxy based silver filled adhesive film. The adhesive was laminated onto the substrate to function as the conducting signal trace in a microstrip line configuration and was compared to a more typical copper trace. The S-Parameter measurements for the two transmission lines closely agreed below 9 GHz. Therefore, the use of thermally and electrically conductive adhesives can be used in multi-layer, substrate integrated antenna designs for the lower GHz ranges. This will greatly simply the fabrication process providing a reliable conductive pathway, while also enabling thermal management within the entire RF module.

articleTitle: A Radial Bi-focal Binary Fresnel Zone Plates Dielectric Lens Antenna at 24GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a design of a radial bi-focal dielectric lens antenna is introduced for 24GHz radar systems based on Binary Fresnel Zone Plates (BFZP). The aim of the design is to use a single lens for both of radar’s transmitter and receiver in order to achieve a more compact, reliable and mechanically stable radar system while maintaining the high gain, scanning angle and performance achieved by using two separate lens antennas for each block. The design was created and simulated using Ansys HFSS and the results show acceptable gain of 26.5dB for a 10cm separation distance between transmitting and receiving antennas.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Radome Design for a Millimeter-Wave Helical Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The design of an additively manufactured radome for a millimeter wave helical antenna is considered. The radome provides environmental protection of the helix and is engineered for fabrication using the stereolithography. The considered antenna is also 3D-printed, albeit with the direct metal laser sintering. Helix has relatively wide bandwidth spanning parts of K and Ka-bands and is monolithically integrated with a coaxial feed and hybridly with a 2.4mm connector. Due to the careful design of the radome that included the near-field distribution around the helix, the minimal impact on the far field pattern shape is obtained. Measured results of the baseline antenna validate the computational model and indirectly the simulated performance upon integration of the radome.

articleTitle: A Wideband Slotted Monoconical Antenna with a Broad-beam Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We propose a wideband monoconical antenna with broad-beam radiation pattern for airborne application. The proposed slotted structure in a monoconical radiator forms a rotating current distribution. The proposed antenna forms E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</inf>- and E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ϕ</inf>-components from the rotating current flow that can achieve circular polarization characteristic. In the proposed design, the null-filled pattern over 1:12 impedance-matched frequencies, while the size of the reference monoconical antenna is maintained.

articleTitle: Continuous Full-Azimuth Beam Steering using Mode Synchronization in Dual-Mode Circular Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new concept for beam steering using a dual-mode circular waveguide is proposed. Two antennas are designed using this concept to achieve full-azimuth beam steering over a narrow bandwidth. The idea is to use the first two non-degenerate circular waveguide modes (TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>) and synchronize them to achieve a desired interference pattern on the waveguide cross section. Slots are then introduced into the waveguide to allow radiation along the azimuthal direction where the two modes add constructively. Using an orthomode transducer, the polarization of the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode is rotated, by modulating the amplitude of the two signals at each port, to achieve full-azimuth beam steering. This technique is therefore fundamentally different from the traditional methods of beam steering that use mechanical control or phase control.

articleTitle: A Transmissive All-Dielectric Metasurface-Based Nanoantenna Array for Selectively Manipulation of Thermal Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this study, a wavelength-selective thermal nanoantenna emitter based on metamaterial design with heat radiation signature management and radiative cooling property is proposed. The design can be considered as a multifunctional window by reducing the heat signature and releasing the heat energy within the non-atmospheric window. The approach relies on the indium tin oxide cubic-shaped unit cell coated on a flexible and transparent substrate (polystyrene). The spectral behaviors of the proposed structure are obtained using the finite difference time domain method, where the power calculation model is utilized to demonstrate the radiative cooling efficiency and low power detection on infrared cameras.

articleTitle: Inverse GRIN Lens Design Using Artificial Neural Network and Geometrical Optics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient artificial neural network for inverse design of GRIN lens antennas. A fast ray tracing method based on Geometrical Optics (GO) is implemented to numerically generate sufficient datasets for training. A simple artificial neural network is built for inverse design. A demonstration shows such a network can realize good mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) between the desired and predicted geometrical variables. The training and testing MAPE are 3.42% and 4.38%, respectively. Radiation patterns of a test lens and its prediction are presented to show the GO method and network accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimum Parameters of an Infinite Phased Array of Printed Dipoles with a Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We study the relationship between parameters of a large-size phased array of printed antennas with a superstrate and its optimal operation conditions. Design trends that simultaneously ensure high radiation efficiency, wide scan angle, efficient matching to the external network, and practical superstrate thicknesses are discussed.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Isolation Magneto-Electric Dipole MIMO Antenna for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wideband high-isolation magneto-electric dipole multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is proposed for terahertz applications. The four-port MIMO antenna consists of four magneto-electric dipole elements which have merits of wideband radiation, high gain, and high front-to-back ratio. The conductive slabs between antenna elements are applied to reduce mutual coupling and thus high isolation can be realized. The proposed magneto-electric dipole MIMO antenna can cover the 0.75-1.1 THz frequency range of the standard WR1.0 rectangular waveguide and the maximum realized gain is 11.5 dBi at the frequency of 991 GHz. The isolation between antenna elements are better than 25 dB.

articleTitle: Smart EM Environments Enabled by Optimal Planning of Low Cost Building Skins
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Within the Smart Electromagnetic Environment (SEME) paradigm, the optimal planning of low-cost and passive building skins (PBSs) is addressed. A set of passive reflective skins are installed on the building facades to improve the received power within selected regions-of-interest (RoIs). Towards this aim, an innovative instance of the System-by-Design (SbD) paradigm is proposed to find the optimal PBSs deployment in a real urban environment. An illustrative example is reported to show the effectiveness and the potentialities of the proposed PBSs planning technique.

articleTitle: Modeling extreme fields of nano-plasmonic modes excited by dense particle beams
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Plasmonic modes that are excited in conductive nanomaterials sustain electromagnetic (EM) fields which can be confined over a few nanometers. Our work has demonstrated that collisionless transfer of energy from a charged particle beam to plasmonic surface modes can lead to excitation of ultra-strong focusing fields. These ultra-strong focusing fields rapidly focus the beam and increase the energy density of the beam as well as the plasmonic modes. Because plasmons can sustain fields at the nanoscale, the energy density continues to increase through this plasmonic focusing effect over nanometric spatial scales. The increase in energy density of plasmons and rapid field enhancement drive the plasmons into a nonlinear regime. While linear perturbative plasmonic modes can be modeled with purely EM computational codes, nonlinear plasmonics additionally requires particle tracking to incorporate various effects. It is critical to model this multi-scale problem over collisionless and longer timescales. We utilize the collisionless particle tracking simulations to model the interaction. The extreme fields sustained by plasmonic modes hold the promise to open novel possibilities.

articleTitle: Dual-band Split-ring Antenna with High-gain Endfire Radiation Characteristics for 5G mm-wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A dual-frequency band high-gain split-ring antenna is proposed for 5G mm-wave applications. The antenna consists of three split ring resonators (SRRs), one is the main SRR which radiates at the first resonant frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>=24.5 GHz). The other two resonators are parasitic SRRs which act as directors to get end-fire radiation characteristics for the proposed antenna at f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>. In addition, the two parasitic SRRs are fed by capacitive coupling with the main SRR to radiate at the second resonant frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>=28.5 GHz). The antenna has better radiation characteristics. It has high gain values of 7.9, and 7.5 dBi with radiation efficiencies of 92% and 95% at f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, and f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, respectively. The proposed antenna is a good candidate for MIMO array at 5G frequency bands utilizing the antenna high gain to improve the system performance.

articleTitle: MIMO Antenna with Hexagonal Split Ring Resonator for LTE, Wireless LAN, and Wi-Fi 6 Services
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The two-port multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna incorporating Hexagonal Split Ring Resonator (HSRR) for Long Term Evolution (LTE), Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) and Wireless Fidelity (Wi-Fi 6) is proposed and analyzed in this research work. The antenna consists of a modified Psi-shaped radiator along with a hexagonal shaped split ring connected on the left arm of the modified Psi shaped structure engraved on compact and low-cost FR-4 substrate. Further an "I-shaped" decoupling structure of size 25×1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is placed in such a manner that it acts as an isolating element and at the same time connects the two partial ground plane on the back side of substrate. This complete structure induces bandwidth of 20.49 % (2.19-2.69 GHz) in F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> band and 29.44% (5.88-7.91 GHz) in F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> band along with minimum mutual coupling of -15dB, gain better than 2.5dBi, efficiency 70%, Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC)~0.01 and diversity Gain (DG) ~10dB in desired band of interest.

articleTitle: Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy at mmWave for Bio-Sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Chronic skin wounds resulting from burns, diabetes, ulcers, and other medical conditions can overwhelm the skin’s regenerative capabilities, leading to persistent infections and even amputations in severe cases. Over 10 million patients with chronic wounds are treated yearly in the United States, with an estimated cost of more than US $ 40 billion in annual spending for treatment. Even with the latest advancements in IoT-based connected health, smart bandages can only aid in drug release to prevent infections. However, a smart bandage that can non-intrusively diagnose or monitor the burn wound’s state does not exist. To address this shortcoming, in this work, we present a non-intrusive, affordable, real-time wound assessment device, that employs mmWave patch sensor for burn wound prognosis through electrical impedance spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Field Focusing for Implantable Telemetry Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Implantable medical devices (IMDs) have many applications where implantation of smaller IMDs are desirable. For these smaller IMDs (potentially only a few mm in dimension), antennas for communication and power transfer will need to be smaller, as well. Expanding on previous research using biopolymer focusing rods to focus the fields, this research simulates a focusing system for implantable antennas. With this field focusing transmission into and out of the body is shown to improve with addition of focusing rods for both dipole and loop antennas. This paper offers a potential solution for electrically small antennas in IMDs and suggests further research on the topic.

articleTitle: Simulation Investigation of Base Station Deployment Scheme of the Wireless Train Communication Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Wireless train communication network (WTCN) is a promising technology to improve the intelligentization level of the high speed train (HST). To achieve reliable radio coverage of WTCN inside the HST and avoid mutual interference between adjacent HSTs, radio coverage distribution inside and outside of HST is simulated. The simulation results of base station with omnidirectional antenna and directional antenna are comparatively analyzed. The comparative analysis results show that the base station with directional antenna scheme is suitable for wireless train communication networking.

articleTitle: Quasi-Optical Beamforming using Dielectric Slabs at mm-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Beamforming at higher frequencies is one of the critical components for any communication network; e.g., IoT and 5G/6G backhaul system as well as for various types of sensing systems. A state-of-the-art quasi-optical technique is introduced and demonstrated in this paper. 3 element antennas are used along with dielectric slabs to form 3 simultaneous partially overlapping beams, improve efficiency and enhance gain. The proposed method can be extended to 2-dimensional arrays to form multiple partially overlapping beams. Full wave simulations in Ansys HFSS are provided to support the proposed techniques of beamforming using quasi-optical (lens type) structures and validations are done in CST microwave studio.

articleTitle: A low-cost and fast resonant cavity watercut meter using amplitude measurement
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Replacing the expensive and bulky network analyzers and moving toward stand-alone measurement equipment is a live topic of research for resonant cavity-based watercut meter sensors. In this paper, we distinguish the cavity’s resonant frequency using transmitting signal amplitude. This frequency is proportional to the watercut of water-oil or water-gas in multi-phase flows. To prove the concept, a resonant cavity sensor (RCS) was fabricated. To improve the transmission coefficient of RCS, an impedance matching circuit was also implemented. Since there is no feedback in the sensing chain, this method is very fast. Moreover, reducing the number of elements leads to a lower cost.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Millimetric Inclusions Detection Through a Spiral Contactless Sensor for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the experimental results of a novel sensor for non-invasive millimeter inclusions detection are presented. The hardware configuration, working at 570 MHz, has been originally designed for air bubbles detection in hemodialysis, but it is suitable for several cases of target detection as well. The proposed microwave radiating system comprises a microstrip self-resonant spiral coil, inductively coupled to an external concentric and coplanar probe loop. An approach aimed at Q-Factor maximization has been followed to precisely achieve the spiral resonant design. In the proposed experimental set-up, we reproduced the blood tissue by using an Agar (2% w/v) solution, in which various millimetric PLA particles are embodied to simulate air inclusions. In particular, the inclusion detection is achieved by observing the external probe loop input impedance amplitude and frequency shift variation through VNA. Theoretical assumptions were validated by experimental results, encouraging future research into the sensor’s potential usage in biomedical applications. Indeed, the sensor might be employed to detect and real-time monitor the air inclusions and blood clots presence during a hemodialysis treatment, making the procedure safer for patients.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of a Compact Beam-Tilted Circularly Polarized Slotted Waveguide Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents design configuration and performance analysis of a compact and thin beam-tilted circularly polarised (CP) radial line slot array (RLSA) waveguide antenna. In conventional CP RLSA beam-tilting method, the aperture efficiency degrades significantly due to sparsely distributed slots throughout the aperture. In this paper, we have presented a new design configuration by utilizing the most effective aperture of the antenna, and eliminating the least effective area. Using this method, an antenna was designed at 18 GHz with a beam tilt angle of 30° and a total aperture of 10λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The antenna has demonstrated a directivity of 25.9 dBic and a realized gain of 25.6 dBic at 18 GHz with a tilt angle of 30°. The far-field radiation pattern has shown a side lobe level of less than -21 dB.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Self-Assembled (Sub)Millimeter-Wave Helical Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We evaluate realizable self-assembled axial-mode helical antennas for (sub)millimeter-wave applications. To enable a direct comparison between these candidates and the feasibility of fabrication, they are simulated at the fixed length of 6.4 mm and in the same volumetric envelope of a conical ground shield. We present the realized gain, impedance bandwidth, axial ratio, and sidelobe level for several helical configurations. The proposed designs are suitable for fabrication using recently reported self-assembly of helical nanomembranes.

articleTitle: WiFi coverage planning and router position optimization using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a regression based supervised learning algorithm Mels (Modified Extensible Lattice Sequence) combined with Global response search method (GRSM) optimization routine is used for (i) design of a WiFi antenna for IEEE 802.11 WLAN protocol, and (ii) radio coverage planning and optimization of number of routers to maximize coverage using the designed antenna for an office space. A dual slot antenna is designed to operate at 5.2 GHz (S46 or S54 band) with a gain of 6 dBi and used as a representative router antenna for coverage planning. Using machine learning, the number of routers is optimized such that maximum coverage with at least a minimum date rate of 13 Mbps is achieved over a 15000 square foot office space.

articleTitle: Online Examination and Self-Assessment Tool for EM Teaching
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In the framework of modern electromagnetic (EM) education, a showcase of the most recent advances in the development of E-XAM, an online examination and self-assessment web platform created by the teaching staff of the ELEDIA Research Center of the University of Trento, Italy, is provided.

articleTitle: Photothermal Meta-surface Absorber with Ultra-low Profile Designed for Terahertz Micro-bolometer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a broadband terahertz meta-surface absorber which is designed to be the radiation coupling module of terahertz micro-bolometer. The unit cell of proposed compound meta-surface consists of several basic square unit cells, specifically, 36 basic square unit cells of three different sizes are arranged in an array, perform chessboard-like layout to form a compound unit cell. Simulated absorbing rate of the proposed meta-surface absorber is higher than 80% from 4.46 to 5.76THz (25.4% fractional bandwidth) with a thickness of merely 1.1μm (0.018λ). Since the symmetrical layout of compound unit cell, the absorbing rate keeps stable for incidence with different polarization angles. Moreover, the photothermal response is 8.5K∙mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/W by multi-physics simulation, which shows great potential to improve the terahertz micro-bolometer.

articleTitle: Dielectric Properties Extraction using Complementary Metamaterial Sensor with Enhanced Performance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a modified Complementary Split ring resonator is presented with enhanced accuracy. This is a single resonator based sensor with deep notch in S21. The sensor is designed to have a resonance frequency of 4.96GHz. This sensor comprising of a unit cell CSRR can be represented as a narrow band reject filter. This compact sensor is designed on the commercially available RO4003C material. The dependence of resonance frequency based on structural parameters is simulated in CST Microwave studio. After parametric analysis this sensor is optimized to give a deep notch in C-Band. S-parameters simulation shows that this resonator can be utilized as high accuracy sensor for dielectric constant and loss tangent measurements.

articleTitle: A Compact Polarization Selective Surface (PSS) for Dual-Band Wi-Fi and Wi-Max Shielding Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This article reports on a compact, single layer, and angularly stable Polarization Selective Surface (PSS) for dual-band Wi-Fi and Wi-Max shielding applications. The unit cell consists of a square loop loaded with stubs and rectangular loops. Unlike conventional FSS, the proposed unit cell generates two stopbands by rotating it 90° without the use of any active components for polarization selective operation. A finite prototype containing 20 × 16 elements is fabricated and tested for verification. Measured results show good agreement with the simulations. The performance of the proposed PSS establishes its application as polarization converters and in wave generators.

articleTitle: FDTD Formulation for Nonlinear Two-Port Networks using their X-Parameters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An updating formulation for finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation was developed to simulate nonlinear components by means of their X-Parameters. Time-domain electric fields surrounding the device are updated as a function of the device’s frequency-domain X-Parameters and the electric and magnetic fields present on the device ports. Agreement was shown between this model and an existing FDTD nonlinear model based on the Ebers-Moll transistor model. The proposed formulation expanding the repertoire of available FDTD device models.

articleTitle: The Influence of the Size of Square Dipole Probe Array Measurement on the Accuracy of NF-FF Pattern
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to illustrate the influence of the size of the measurement plane on the accuracy of the far field pattern result using the near field square dipole probe array measurement to far field transformation approach. We are expecting that the larger size of measurement we choose, the more accuracy result we will get, so the question is what the relation between the accuracy and the size of the measurement plane is so that we can make a smart choice to get the accurate enough result efficiently. Sample numerical results are presented to illustrate how accurate it can be and what the relation between the size of the near field measurement plane and the accuracy of the final result is.

Author Keywords: Planar near Field to far field Transformation

articleTitle: A 2-18 GHz Hemispherical Vivaldi Array for Wide Angle Scanning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We report a conformal ultra-wide band (UWB) array on a doubly curved surface for wide angle electronic scanning. We use a quadrilateral mesh as the basis for systematically arraying UWB radiators on arbitrary surfaces. A 52 element, dual-polarized Vivaldi array prototype on a 181 mm diameter hemisphere is developed. The antennas and connectors are metal 3D printed. Measured realized gain is within 2 dB of the theoretical value from 2-18 GHz and scan angles θ < 90°.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Wearable MIMO WiFi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band textile antenna on denim fabric substrate is proposed. The antenna has a conductive layer in the back which reduces the back radiation, improves the gain, and stabilizes the performance when the air gap between the textile and the body is changed. The performance of the antenna for various MIMO settings was examined in an indoor scenario.

articleTitle: A Low Profile Ultra-Wide Band Fractal Monopole Conformal Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low profile ultra-wideband (UWB) array based on fractal monopole antenna is proposed. In order to extend impedance bandwidth, the elements are etched with two iterations Sierpinski-like fractal patch and defective ground. The performance and the manufacture feasibility are fully considered and optimized. The developed monopole antenna can be used for conformal arrays in many ultra-broadband applications where very compact size and light weight is required. The experimental results agree well with the simulation, and high average radiation efficiency in whole band is obtained.

articleTitle: Analysis of Ultra-Wideband Double-Ridge Open-Ended Waveguide Antennas for Millimeter-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A comprehensive study is performed to evaluate the performance of ultra-wideband double-ridge open-ended waveguide antennas (OEWAs) at millimeter-wave (mm-wave) regime. Specifically, two double-ridge OEWAs with 15–40-GHz and 40– 110-GHz bandwidths are designed and fabricated. Each antenna demonstrates |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|<–10 dB and stable and symmetric radiation patterns across 15–40 GHz and 40–110 GHz with aperture sizes of 9.47×5.79 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 3.78×2.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, respectively. To evaluate the performance of the proposed double-ridge OEWAs for ultra-wideband millimeter-wave communications, time and frequency domain performance metrics such as fidelity factor and group delay are investigated for face-to-face and side-by-side orientations. Results indicate that the proposed antennas feature fidelity factors more than 86.33% and a linear variation of transmission coefficients phases with group delay variations less than 0.25 ns.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effects of Point Electrode and Variation of Muscle Thickness in the Assesment of the Electrical Impedance Myography Through Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Electrical impedance myography (EIM), an electrophysiological technique, is recently proposed as a painless, non-invasive technique for assessing neurological disease status. In EIM, bio impedances such as resistance, reactance, and phase are measured over the muscle or muscle group of interest. However, this EIM data depends on several anatomic and nonanatomic factors, such as muscle grith, subcutaneous fat thickness, and electrode configuration. This study has been conducted to explore the effect of variation of muscle thickness on EIM data by applying point electrodes' placement. To our best knowledge, this is the first time we have developed a point electrode configuration placed over the muscle or muscle group of interest to better understand the EIM's ability to access muscle health. In this study, a finite element model (FEM) of the human arm is developed based on the anatomic data. The result shows that of the three major EIM parameters-resistance, reactance, and phase, resistance is least sensitive to the alternation of the muscle thickness in point electrode configuration placement on the FEM model. For example, a 66% increase in muscle thickness resulted in a 50% change in reactance at 50 kHz but only a 13% change in resistance. These exciting findings are a significant augmentation for further study in EIM research.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Dipole-like Antennas for Differentially-Fed IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The implementation of Printed Circuit Board (PCB) antennas for the Internet of Thing (IoT) base station application is a co-design of the antenna size, shape, position, and board/ground layout. This paper investigates the radiation features of a typical PCB antenna combined with a dipole-type structure. A circularly polarized (CP) antenna for differential feeding is proposed and experimentally verified. By taking the advantage of the PCB antenna radiation and working principle of the dipole element, it is shown that CP radiation could be achieved for differential-fed signals. The proposed antennas demonstrate good radiation performance in terms of efficiency and bandwidth.

articleTitle: Benefits and Limitations of Beam Widening in GNSS Satellite Antenna for SSV and Beyond Users
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The space exploration and moon colonization is becoming an attractive goal for many companies and government agencies. A precise and reliable navigation system is essential to provide a satisfying positioning accuracy in space missions. In this paper the authors present benefits and limitations of GNSS space antenna beamforming to support space navigation in the Space Service Volume (SSV) and beyond.

articleTitle: Two-Stream Feature Fusion Convolutional Network Based Target Recognition for Entangled Light Quantum Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: To address the problems of blurred contour and missed local image information of the entangled light quantum image, which leads to poor recognition performance, this paper proposes a target recognition method of entangled light quantum imaging based on a two-stream feature fusion network. Specifically, we first prepare the entangled photon pairs via spontaneous parametric down-conversion to achieve quantum imaging. Then, we design a two-stream feature fusion convolution network to recognize the target of the reconstructed quantum image. We test the MNIST handwritten digit images to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Co-Simulations for Transmit Broadband Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents analysis of octave-bandwidth transmit electronically scanned arrays (ESA), through full-wave, circuit and system co-simulations. The analysis is showcased on a 6–12 GHz four-element array of electrically-small flared horns fed with microstrip-to ridge waveguide transitions, cascaded with 2-W commercial GaN MMIC power amplifiers (PAs). The corporate feed network contains ideal phase shifters. The results show effects of PA nonlinearities on phased array active antenna impedance, EIRP and overall efficiency, across a wide bandwidth and as a function of scan angle.

articleTitle: Augmented Power Pattern Synthesis Through the Use of Space-Time Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Herein, we present a procedure for the design of a space-time metasurface which can produce a desired far-field power pattern. We also demonstrate how the additional functionalities of space-time metasurfaces allow for an augmented power pattern synthesis (spatial and spectral tailoring) by also desiring a change in frequency with respect to the incident wave. The approach is shown to be valid through the use of a finite-difference time-domain simulation.

articleTitle: Terahertz Photomechanical Detector Based on Meta-surface Absorber and Enhanced Cantilevers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Terahertz focal plane array imaging system has attracted much attention nowadays, this paper proposes a photomechanical terahertz detector, which is ideal for forming the focal plane array. The detector works at room temperature, and a meta-surface absorber is used to couple the incident terahertz radiation, so that a coupling efficiency higher than 90% can be obtained from 2.7 to 3.46THz. The bi-material cantilevers will produce a deformation corresponding to incident power, and the responsivity of detector is R=12.2μm/μW with a response time of 90ms. Thermal isolation between pixels is also considered and realized by introducing heat-insulating cantilevers.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Quadratic U and Inverse Quadratic U Sum-Difference Beampatterns
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work examines and compares the radiative behavior of the quadratic U and vertically-inverted quadratic U distribution, both unique convex quadratic functions for the application of distributed antenna arrays. The comparison of the two analogous distributions demonstrated that the beamwidth of the random array relies on how the element population is either clustered or dispersed. Furthermore, this behavior occurs for both characteristic modal solutions in which element radiators are used independently to deliver both sum and difference beams. The quadratic U distribution raises sidelobe levels, and its inverse lowers sidelobe levels. By the same token this applies to a tapered aperture distribution where energy is seen to be removed by the mainbeam, increasing sidelobe levels or oppositely lowering sidelobe levels, but increasing mainbeam width. Thus, a trade-off applies to mainbeam width and its corresponding sidelobe levels. Simulated results for the quadratic U and inverted quadratic U with comparison on beamwidth and sidelobe levels conclude this paper.

articleTitle: Microwave Data Inversion With a Model Compression Scheme Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a nonlinear model compression scheme based on deep learning for microwave imaging. Permittivity models are described by the latent parameters of a trained variational autoencoder (VAE) neural network. The latent variables are taken as the unknowns to be inverted through minimizing the data misfit function with the Gauss-Newton method. By decoding the inverted parameters, features extracted from the dataset can be incorporated into the imaging process, which effectively mitigates the ill-posedness of the inverse scattering problem.

articleTitle: Cross-talk Mitigation Using Left/Right-Handed Circularly-Polarized Antennas for Multi-Lane Millimeter-Wave Wireless Interconnects
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the feasibility of reducing cross-talk for multi-lane millimeter-wave (mm-wave) wireless interconnects using left/right-handed circularly-polarized antennas. The obtained results demonstrate that the proposed antenna system can effectively (>14.6 dB) decrease the cross-talk in both near- and far-field scenarios in comparison with the antenna system with identical polarization.

articleTitle: Angle-of-Arrival Estimation Using Null-Steering Antennas for Simplicity and Accuracy Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes an antenna system for straightforward and accurate angle-of-arrival (AoA) estimation. The proposed system applies power-based direction finding using a null-steering antenna to enhance simplicity and accuracy in determining AoA. The accuracy enhancement is achieved by the antenna that scans a deep null over −30 dB. Furthermore, the estimation accuracy in the system is evaluated by triangulation. The result reveals that the conventional antenna array produces a maximum estimation error of 8.0 m due to shallow null depths, while the proposed one significantly reduces it to 0.5 m.

articleTitle: Reversed T-matching in RFID Tag Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze a reversed T-matching used in UHF RFID tag antennas. We investigate similarities and differences between T-match and reversed T-match using EM simulations and an equivalent circuit approach applied to a generic 70 x 14 mm RFID tag antenna for M700 IC.

articleTitle: Feed Analysis of a Proximity Coupled Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The performance of microstrip patch antennas is strongly dependent on the feeding techniques such as coaxial, microstrip line, and proximity coupled feeds. Proximity coupled microstrip patch antennas have been investigated for various applications but research on the positioning and length of the proximity coupled feed is limited. In this paper, the length of the feedline in a proximity coupled microstrip patch antenna was investigated. It is found that the length of the feed line has a direct influence on the resonant frequency and that the antenna resonates at a higher frequency when the length of the feedline is increased.

articleTitle: A Very Compact Dual-Polarized Antenna Array Topology Supporting Multiple 5G Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a very compact dual-polarized antenna array topology that allows for operation in the 26 GHz, 28 GHz, 37 GHz and 39 GHz bands designated for 5G uses. Four1 × 4 sub-arrays, namely low-band horizontally polarized (LB H-pol) array, high-band horizontally polarized (HB H-pol) array, low-band vertically polarized (LB V-pol) array and high-band vertically polarized (HB V-pol) array, are designed on a 12-layer laminate with total dimensions of 25 mm×6 mm×0.97 mm. The LB arrays achieve reflection coefficients of less than -10 dB from 24 – 30 GHz, and the HB arrays can operate from 37 – 43 GHz. Special techniques are used to reduce the mutual couplings between elements and enhance the array gain. Each sub-array features peak gain of more than 9.7 dBi at its center frequency. The 3-dB beam scanning ranges for the H-pol and V-pol arrays are ±45° and ±56° at 27 GHz, and ±42° and ±28° at 40 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Excitation of Traveling Wave on Metal Casing Using Folded Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Multiple antennas have been installed on mobile devices, and miniaturization of antennas is required. In addition, high-frequency bands are used with the development of communication technology, and the size of the platform becomes relatively larger than a wavelength. It becomes difficult in antenna design to approach from the standing wave on the platform which resonates such as a half-wavelength dipole. This paper proposes the traveling wave antenna with a platform on which the surface wave propagates and radiates. The proposed antenna is expected that the radiation can be changed by changing the characteristics of the platform surface where the surface waves propagate.

articleTitle: Bi-directional Leaky-Wave Antennas with Independent Beam-Scanning Laws
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A bi-directional periodic leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is presented for the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) band with suppressed stopband and independent beam-scanning laws for top and bottom sides of the antenna, respectively. The bi-directional slot-pair antenna is designed to radiate out-of-plane beams along two directions on each antenna face. The operation of this antenna is verified using full-wave simulations at a design frequency of 28 GHz. The antenna can be engineered to point high gain beam along specified angles, and can be adapted to provide precision control of the independent output beams in various frequency bands.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Compact UHF RFID Tag Employing Slow-Wave Structures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Smart connected things that can sense, interact, and share data have a huge potential in enabling a smart environment. Due to the rising interest in realizing the internet of things to provide smart services in smart cities, there is a requirement of vast deployment; therefore, things/tags need to be low in cost and compact in size. Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) is one of the technologies that can enable sensing and wireless communication between things. In this paper, additive manufacturing is used to minimize the cost of RFID tags while slow-wave structures (SWS) are explored to make them compact. The largest element of RFID tags i.e. antenna is initially taken as a standard half-wave dipole then folded to employ SWS along the parallel conductors. The process of folding and SWS loading have been carefully performed to ensure decent radiation efficiency and read range. To fabricate the proposed RFID tag, silver nanowires-based conductive ink is employed while the substrate is 3D printed. The overall tag size is 54 x 56 x 0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (ka=0.71), and it has a read range of 6.4 m at 867 MHz.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Multi-Mode OAM Reflectarray Synthesis With Reduced Number of Active Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach to synthesize reconfigurable multi-mode reflectarrays (RAs) or transmitarrays (TAs) with the minimum required number of active elements is presented. Namely, we strategically tune the progressive phase delay required for each mode of operation to reduce the corresponding phase errors below a pre-set threshold. Only the unit-cells whose phase error exceeds this threshold are replaced with active elements while the rest use passive elements, thereby reducing cost, complexity, and losses of the system. The performance of the proposed method is studied analytically by synthesizing a multi-mode orbital angular momentum (OAM) RA capable of generating three modes (l = +2, +3, and +4). The RA exhibits high directivity (> 30 dBi), low SLL (<−10 dB), low divergence angle (< 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup>), and high aperture efficiency (> 56%) in all three modes of operation, while requiring only 36% of the elements to be active.

articleTitle: Optimization of Single-sideband Time Modulated Array for Wideband Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An optimization method of low sideband level for wideband communication system based on single-sideband time modulation array is proposed in this paper. By significantly reducing the sideband level within the beam’s range with optimizing the modulated pulses, the proposed method can effectively reduce the in-band interference caused by harmonics’ spectrum aliasing and improve the system’s bandwidth. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method for wideband communication, which enhances the application scope of time modulated technology in a wideband system.

articleTitle: Microstrip line Loaded High Dielectric Constant Slab phase shifter using Piezo- Bender Actuation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the simulation and measurement results of ka-band microstrip line (MSL) loaded high dielectric constant slab phase shifter is presented. The phase shifting states are controlled by changing the gap between dielectric slab and MSL by using a piezo bender actuation mechanism. The measured result shows a phase shifting range of more than 360° over 1 GHz bandwidth, with average insertion loss less than 3.65 dB and loss variation less than 1.2 dB is achieved.

articleTitle: WPT Enabled SP3T Switch for Broadband Antenna Switching Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a battery-less single pole triple throw (SP3T) switch enabled through wireless power transfer (WPT) for a frequency range of 0.5 - 6 GHz. A set of three rectifying circuits, each connected to their independent antenna elements (rectennas) were designed. These rectennas were designed to operate at 2.3 GHz, 2.45 GHz, and 2.6 GHz, respectively. Different frequencies were used to avoid any interference between received signals. The three RF output ports of the switch were biased using each rectenna. A minimum of 1.8 V is required to actuate each RF port that was rectified when the input power ranges from 0-2 dBm with RF-to-DC power conversion efficiency (PCE) which is around 50% for each rectifier. The proposed battery-less SP3T switch paves the way to reconfigure microwave devices and antennas for a broad range of applications.

articleTitle: Wideband Beamforming Network Design Using Gradient Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This article presents an advanced technique in designing beam-forming network (BFN) for conformal antenna arrays using gradient optimization. In this application, high isolations between ports and equal electrical paths to common power receiver are desired for BFN performances. Rather than employing complex/expensive digital beam steering/forming designs, this application focus on low-cost analog power combining. The optimized multistage Wilkinson BFN with gradient based algorithm offers fast computation, scaling capability, and wideband performance for microstrip BFN structures which are easy to fabricate. In this paper, the performance of an ideal Wilkinson BFN at S-band and a gradient-optimization based BFN at C/X-band will be shown to illustrate the methodology.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Reflectarray Antenna for Polarized Division Multiple Access
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Dual-beam reflectarray antenna for polarized division multiple access is presented with a reflective unit cell using coupled delay line. The unit cell, designed at 11 GHz using a simple patch structure with two substrate layers, can be made to generate two states with 180° phase difference and 0.3 dB reflection loss. Three reflectarray antennas were fabricated to demonstrate that they could form two independent beams. The reflectarray antennas have beam-forming within ±30 range and are obtained with a aperture efficiency of 10.2 % at 11 GHz.

articleTitle: Modified Butler Matrix Operating in Three Frequency Ranges for Multibeam Antenna Applications With Efficient Aperture Utilization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A concept of a feeding network that can be used for achieving multibeam radiation pattern in three-frequency ranges is proposed. The presented feeding network is based on a concept of a Butler matrix that smoothly changes its order from 2 x 2 to 8 x 8 across two-octave frequency range. As is shown it is possible two design a Butler matrix which operates at f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> as 2 x 2 Butler matrix, subsequently it changes into 4 x 4 at 2f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, and finally changes into 8 x 8 at 4f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. It is also theoretically shown that such a network, when connected to broadband radiating elements spaced by 0.5 λ at 4f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> allows for achieving multibeam radiation pattern over the entire two-octave frequency range. Moreover, at the three discrete frequency ranges, i.e.: f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, 2f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and 4f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> it provides classic two, four and eight-beam radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Enforcing Continuity Condition on the Open PEC-Dielectric Interfaces for the Solution of Volume-Surface Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In the solution of volume surface integral equation (VSIE) for composite objects, how to enforce the continuity condition (CC) of electric flux on the open perfect electric conductor (PEC)-dielectric interfaces to reduce volumetric unknowns is investigated. It is found that to correctly enforce the CC, the equivalent surface current on both faces of the PEC should be distinguished. For this purpose, the combined field integral equation (CFIE) is proposed to model the open PEC part. Numerical experiments show that compared with the traditional application of the CC, the proposed method gives more accurate results.

articleTitle: Two-Element Implantable MIMO Antenna with Sensing Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-port implantable MIMO antenna is proposed for high-data-rate communication and sensing inner state of tissues. To achieve compactness in the proposed design, a high dielectric substrate, reactive slots and shorting pins are adopted. Accordingly, the suggested antenna maintains a compact geometry. Both elements of the antenna operate at 915 MHz with a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 6.95% and isolation of 21.77 dB. The results demonstrate good communication performance as well as sensing capability. The suggested antenna has fair radiation patterns, gains, impedance matching and bandwidths for all dielectric properties of human tissues. Furthermore, it maintains consistent MIMO parameters over the wide range of human tissues. Therefore, the proposed antenna is suitable for high-data-rate communication and monitoring pathological changes of tissues.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna Based On Liquid Metal Switch
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a pattern reconfigurable antenna based on a liquid metal switch is proposed. The antenna is mainly composed of a printed three-element Yagi-Uda antenna whose reflector is loaded with a slot in the middle. A microfluidic channel, filled with a movable liquid metal post and applied as a manipulating switch, is attached to the surface of the reflector. Due to the coupled connection between the radiating arms and liquid metal post, the slot can be shorted or opened by moving the post, leading to changes in the lead and lag of phases between the radiating elements. Thus, the radiation pattern of the antenna can be adjusted. The simulated results achieved by CST Microwave Studio® indicate that the direction of the maximum radiation can be changed by about 180°, and the antenna can operate at 2.4 GHz at two working states.

articleTitle: Bi-Layered Patterned Phase-Gradient Metasurface for Refraction in Ku-Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A bi-layered patterned phase-gradient metasurface design for refraction of normal and oblique incident waves in Ku band is proposed. A bottom-up design strategy for the metasurface’s unit-cell and super-cell is introduced and applied to design two refractive metasurfaces; one for normally incident illumination and one for obliquely incident illumination. The refraction phenomenon is validated by full-wave simulations in Ku-band at 15 GHz.

articleTitle: A Technique for an Array to Generate Switchable Linearly Polarization with High Polarization Purity Using Circularly Polarized Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method is presented to obtain switchable linearly polarized phased array antenna (LPPAA). The LPPAA is designed with right and left hand circularly polarized (CP) elements. Sequential rotation technique (SRT) is applied to achieve linear polarization (LP). Results show the proposed LPPAA not only exhibits low scan loss with wide-angle scanning, but also have very low cross polarization. This revealing a concise and reliable method for polarization reconfigurable array design for wide angle scanning system.

articleTitle: Effect of Low Frequency Surface Plasmon-Like Standing Waves on Frequency-Scanned Structured Metal Surfaces with Plasmonic-Like Reconfigurable Subwavelength Rectangular Groove Gratings Using Periodically Photoinduced Plasma
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper theoretically presents effect of surface plasmon-like standing waves on scattering characteristics of structured perfect electric conductor (PEC) surfaces with subwavelength rectangular groove gratings periodically filled with photoinduced plasma, using mode matching technique. And, the control of the high order diffracted waves using the surface plasmon-like waves is theoretically discussed for application to novel opto-electronically reconfigurable reflector antennas.

articleTitle: Knot as Antennas: A Brief Review
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper reviews the applications of different structures of knots in terms of their unique radiation properties. The various knots as a radiating structure discussed in this paper are classified in terms of a monopole antenna, linearly polarized unidirectional antenna, pattern diversity antenna, conical beam and broadside circularly polarized antennas.

articleTitle: Measurement and Characterization of Winter Precipitation at Wallops Island Snow Field Site
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present our ongoing studies of physical and scattering properties of ice particles in winter precipitation combining delicate optical, electronic, and mechanical surface instrumentation and state-of-the-art radars. We outline integrated field measurements, followed by analysis, at the NASA Precipitation Research Facility Wallops Island, Virginia. Accurate measurements and characterization of snowflakes and snowfall are crucial for advancement of numerical weather prediction models and in the correct interpretation of data from the national network of weather radars.

articleTitle: Channel Selection of Hybrid Communication Systems using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Commercial and military free space communication needs are growing at a remarkable pace. The requirements for free space data transfer have increased as the technology increased, and now engineers are considering higher frequency bands for free space, including W/V, millimeter wave and optical bands. Laser communications can offer much higher data rates than traditional radio frequency (RF) systems and have the added advantage of not being regulated by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). This along with typical hardware being much smaller in size, weight and power (SWaP) make optical communications a desirable solution for high-rate communication systems. W/V band systems also have the advantage of higher data rates and less frequency congestion than traditional RF systems, as well as the advantages of being able to link through clouds. As the need for "data on demand" increases, the likelihood of users moving to hybrid systems is very high. Today, multiple users in both commercial and government sectors are looking to integrate both laser communication (lasercom) and RF solutions onto their platforms. The goal of this work is to use machine learning on a hybrid communication system, to determine which system will give the highest performance for a given satellite mission.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Direct Digital Modulation with Time-modulated Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A simple reconfigurable direct digital modulation system with time-modulated metasurface is proposed and verified. Instead of baseband transmitting chain, baseband complex symbols of multiple users are mapped into the harmonics of control signals and load to the radio frequency (RF) carrier by the metasurface with only 1-bit phase-adjusted resolution. Theoretical analysis and simulations are provided to verify its feasibility. The reconfigurable harmonic modulation method, low complexity hardware and minimum requirement for metasurface indicate its potential applications in large scale multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) transmitters.

articleTitle: Additive Manufactured Antennas on Automotive ABS Using Intense Pulsed Light Sintering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Antennas for automotive communications are developed using additive manufacturing techniques on temperature sensitive Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) substrate. Different Intense Pulsed Light profiles are used on the devices in order to optimize the sintering process without destroying the substrate. The conductivity of part of the antenna reaches 3.3% of bulk silver. The maximum realized gain of the antenna at 857.5 MHz is 0.81 dBi and at 5.9 GHz is 7 dBi.

articleTitle: Maximizing RF Switch Usage Efficiency in Electronically Reconfigurable Unit Cells: A Design using Binary Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: RF switches are the key components in many electronically reconfigurable reflect-/transmit-array antennas. From a practical standpoint, the number of RF switches that can be implemented per unit cell is limited because of the associated cost, loss, and complexity. This paper presents a workflow to design reconfigurable unit cells that generate the maximum number of phase states with a given number of switches, thereby maximizing the RF switch usage efficiency. We demonstrate the design of a 19 GHz reflectarray unit cell that achieves 2-bit phase resolution with two switches. The unit cell utilizes a pixelized element designed by binary particle swarm optimization.

articleTitle: Parametric Design and Simulation of a Biconical Antenna: Admittance, Directivity, and Far Field Radiation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to respond directly to the Project Authorization Request (PAR) for developing P2816: Recommended Practice for Computational Electromagnetics Applied to Modeling and Simulation of Antennas. A biconical antenna model provided as the specific example is simulated by Ansys HFSS electromagnetic solver based on Finite Element Method (FEM). HFSS is a full wave electromagnetic simulation tool available in ANSYS Electronics Desktop (AEDT) and can be used to predict how complex real-world geometries will perform as designed. The simulation results of this paper are compared to previously published and accepted theoretical analysis of a spherical capped biconical antenna.

articleTitle: A Compact CP Wearable Antenna backed by AMC Array for WBAN/WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a simple and compact wide-slot circularly polarized antenna backed by a 2×2 artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) array is presented for 5.8 GHz wireless body area network (WBAN) applications. An inverted T-shaped parasitic strip at the open end of a microstrip line extension and slot modification was applied to attain wideband CP. The total footprint of the proposed antenna is only 30.9 × 30.9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> board of semi-flexible Rogers RT-Duroid 5880 substrate. Full-wave EM simulation results have been presented in numerous studies, both in free space and in proximity to the human body. The integrated design provided an impedance bandwidth |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| ≤ -10 dB of ~9.41-percent (5.57-6.12 GHz) and an AR bandwidth ≤ 3 dB of 9.8-percent (5.24-5.78 GHz). Furthermore, over a gap of 3 mm from the human body, the final design achieved peak gain and total efficiency enhancements of 8.5 dBi and 91.4%, respectively. A very low specific absorption rate, compact size, and high gain make the proposed design a good candidate for most off-body wearable applications.

articleTitle: A SIE-PDE Formulation with Non-conformal Meshes for Electromagnetic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A hybrid surface integral equation partial differential equation (SIE-PDE) formulation with non-conformal meshes is proposed to solve the electromagnetic problems. An equivalent model with only the electric current density is first constructed for piecewise homogeneous media, which is then enforced into the Helmholtz equation as an excitation. A connection matrix is carefully constructed to couple the SIE and PDE formulations without any additional requirements upon the boundary conditions and meshes. Therefore, non-conformal meshes are fully supported, which is extremely flexible to model complex structures. Numerical results show that it is accurate, efficient and flexible to solve electromagnetic problems.

articleTitle: Resonance Behaviors of Time-Varying Spherical Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Quasi-analytic methods are used to examine the coupling of incident fields, up-converted harmonics, and internal resonances in systems composed of time-varying resistive shells. Results demonstrate that, in certain regimes, single mode resonant coupling leads to predictable behavior based on the internal resonances of perfectly conducting spheres and up-converted harmonic frequencies. This predictability degrades as losses are increased and modal bandwidths overlap.

articleTitle: Nyström Solution of Volume Integral Equations by Using Elements with Different Materials
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) problems with inhomogeneous penetrable media are formulated by volume integral equations (VIEs) in the integral equation approach. Traditionally, the VIEs are solved by the method of moments (MoM) with Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson (SWG) basis and testing functions which are defined over conforming tetrahedral elements. The conformity does not allow individual meshes to stride across material boundaries or one element cannot include different materials, leading to much inconvenience of geometric discretization. In this work, we use the Nyström method to discretize the VIEs and develop a scheme that can allow meshes to step over material interfaces. The numerical example shows that the approach is effective and robust.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Method to Estimate the Resonant Frequency in mmWave Microstrip Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses a new, straightforward and accurate method to calculate the resonant frequency of the dominant mode for microstrip patch antennas, considering the conductor foil thickness on the patch. This method aims to extend the applicability of existing microstrip-antenna models to millimeter wave frequencies. The proposed method predicts the resonant frequency with errors less than 1 % for frequencies up to 300 GHz, and for substrates with foils up to 35 µm thick.

articleTitle: On a Constrained Pseudoinverse for the Electromagnetic Inverse Source Problem
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Inverse source approaches have shown their relevance for several applications in the past years. They rely on the solution of an ill-posed problem where near-field/current data is reconstructed starting from far-field (or less informative field) information. Standard strategies, including the physically constrained ones using Love conditions, result in linear systems to be pseudoinverted which are still ill-conditioned due to the lack of information from the evanescent fields. In this work we present a generalized pseudoinverse for those problems that allows the inclusion of extra constraints from the evanescent field space, when available. This is obtained by dropping some of the standard Moore-Penrose (MP) requirements and using the resulting degrees of freedom to obtain a generalized pseudoinverse that shows favorable performance in several cases of practical interest.

articleTitle: A Multi-trace Surface Integral Equation Solver to Analyze Electromagnetic Field Interactions on Graphene-based Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
