abstract: A multi-trace surface integral equation (MT-SIE) solver is proposed to analyze electromagnetic field interactions on graphene-based devices. This solver decomposes the computation domain into an exterior subdomain (the background medium where the device resides in) and an interior subdomain that represents the device’s dielectric substrate. The infinitesimally thin graphene sheet partially covers the interface between these two subdomains. On the graphene surface and the rest of this interface, resistive Robin transmission conditions (formulated for the first time in this work) and the traditional Robin transmission conditions are used to "connect" these two subdomains, respectively. In each subdomain, the electric and magnetic field equations are used as the governing equations. Various numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and the applicability of the proposed MT-SIE solver.

articleTitle: Dual-mode Antenna Using Permittivity Gradient for S-band CubeSat Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact dual-band S-band antenna with an isoflux radiation pattern Cubesat applications. It consists of a probe-fed square microstrip patch antenna placed on top of a 3D printed ABS substrate. In order to obtain a dual-band behaviour, a permittivity gradient is achieved by controlling material porosity. A peak realized gain of 5.3dBi and 2.6dBi is simulated respectively at 2.02GHz and 2.17GHz.

articleTitle: Implan table Radio Frequency Identification Tags for Patient Data Recognition
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a biocompatible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tag designed for long term implantation and resonance in the ultra-high frequency (UHF) band is presented. The antenna is designed to be implanted subcutaneously and read from within 20 cm for patient data acquisition. Preliminary computer-simulated results from ANSYS HFSS analysis are presented and further experimentation is discussed.

articleTitle: The Need for Narrow Beamwidth in Ridged Horn Antennas for UAV-Based In-situ Measurements of Radars and Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a lens-integrated wideband ridged horn antenna is presented for UAV based in-situ characterization of radars and communication systems. The proposed customized antenna operates from 2 GHz to 12 GHz covering the commonly used radar bands for weather and defense applications. Compared to the narrowband and bulky horn antenna, the proposed lens-integrated ridged horn antenna is wideband, low weight, and compact in size that make it suitable for UAV based measurements. Using a single wideband probe for outdoor in-situ measurements gets rid of installing and re-calibration of multiple probes for meteorology measurements. The main limitation of the commercially available ridged horn antenna is, it suffers from wider H-plane beamwidth performance at low frequencies. The proposed lens integration technique reduces the beamwidth in the H-plane by 67% (for instance at 3 GHz), that also helps in achieving near-symmetry in the patterns.

articleTitle: A Guided Random Search Approach for Synthesis of Sparse Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Grating lobes in sparse arrays can be removed by using aperiodic element spacing, however, the traditional random sampling methods cluster some of the elements too close together, making fabrication impractical. We present a new constraint based design approach using guided random search. Numerical results are presented and we show that our approach is capable of removing the grating lobes and reducing the sidelobe level while keeping the elements from being too close together with an organized distribution within the aperture.

articleTitle: Vehicle-Mounted Antenna with Full-Duplex and Beamforming Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In-band full-duplex (IBFD) systems can be utilized to facilitate spectrum-sharing in vehicle-to-everything (V2X) applications. Vehicle-mounted antennas should ideally provide omnidirectional radiation patterns to cover all angles around the moving platform, which has been demonstrated with the use of arrays and circular mode phasing schemes. This paper introduces and presents the simulation of a novel antenna design that integrates that phasing concept with the ability to perform adaptive beamforming on receive. This added benefit provides an IBFD system with the capability to estimate a signal’s direction of arrival, which can improve communication-link performance for V2X and other applications.

articleTitle: Time Domain Analysis of an UWB Electrically Small Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the pulse transmission capability of an ultrawideband (UWB), coaxial probe-fed, electrically small, microstrip patch antenna has been examined. The designed antenna, which covers a 2:1 VSWR bandwidth of 54.94% (2.5-5 GHz), is subjected to a narrow Gaussian type pulse. A detailed investigation of the pulses, received by an identical antenna, in face-to-face and side-by-side orientations, has been performed in the far-field region. The study concludes that the proposed ESA is capable of transmitting narrow pulses, especially in face-to-face configuration, with good fidelity factors (> 0.9), and has uniform group delays over the frequency band of operation, rendering it suitable for various pulsed UWB wireless applications.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of an In-house Developed Characteristic Mode Analysis Tool
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, performance evaluation of an in-house developed software tool for the characteristic mode analysis is presented. A Python-based interactive graphical user interface is developed for the 64-bit Windows environment. The developed program can be used for the characteristic mode analysis of metallic structures and can be controlled through scripting as well as user arguments. The simulated results obtained through the in-house developed code for the CM analysis is compared with the commercially available EM simulation software having the capability to perform CM analysis. It was observed that the results obtained from the in-house CMA tool are in good agreement with the commercially available software.

articleTitle: A mm-Wave High-Order Mode Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present the design of a novel mm-wave leaky wave antenna (LWA), which operates at the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> high-order mode. While typical LWAs operate at their fundamental mode, e.g., TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>, our proposed TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> high-order mode LWA takes advantage of its modal distribution, thereby coupling more energy to free-space through appropriately designed slots. Due to the latter, our TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mm-wave LWA achieves 1.47 3.24 dB more gain over a bandwidth of 5 GHz (from 35 GHz to−40 GHz) when it is compared to a traditional LWA of the same electrical dimensions that operates at the fundamental TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>-mode.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Impedance Metasurfaces for High-Accuracy Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable surfaces that dynamically control the reflected beams can play a vital role in the next generation of wireless communications. In this paper, we present a method to design varactor-loaded metasurfaces that precisely control not only the angle of reflection, but also the reflected beam characteristics. Optimization of the varactor capacitances based on a rigorous Method of Moments formulation allows the realization of different far-field patterns. Scanning of a Taylor-pattern with −20 dB sidelobe level is demonstrated up to 45° off-broadside through full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: A Versatile Shape Generation Method for 3D Meander-line Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a custom method for the design of 3D meander-line antennas with arbitrary geometries. This technique, used in conjunction with multi-objective optimization and 3D printing, enables the creation of antennas with unintuitive geometries which have enhanced performance over traditional designs. As an example, we employ this method to design two quadrifilar helix antenna (QHAs). One of the antennas has a dual-band behavior with different radiation characteristics in each band. The second antenna has wide bandwidth, high broadside gain, and compact size.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Dual-Linear Polarization Transmitarray Unit Cell for Ka-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel dual-band transmitarray (TA) unit cell based on the Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technology is proposed in this article. The TA cell provides orthogonal linear polarizations for the two frequency bands while sharing the same radiating aperture. A dual-band, single-layer, frequency-selective surface (FSS) that generates a wave rotated of 90° to the incident one in one of the two bands, maintaining unchanged the polarization in the other is used. For each band, the proposed element and its mirror image can provide 0° and 180° phase shifts with 1-bit phase quantization. The proposed element can be easily fabricated as a single layer PCB with a standard manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Influence of Terminal Dimensions on Bandwidth and Efficiency Bounds of Small Printed IFA Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a study of the influence of the terminal dimensions on the bandwidth and efficiency bounds of small antennas suitable for IoT or 5G applications. The antenna considered in this study is a printed Inverted-F Antenna (IFA). The obtained results clearly show that the dimensions of the terminal have a strong impact on the maximum total efficiency that can be achieved, whereas the bandwidth bound is less impacted.

articleTitle: Practical FSS-Based Sensor Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Frequency selective surfaces are a periodic array of unit cells that, when illuminated externally, have a specific frequency response that depends on element geometry, spacing, and substrate properties. Theoretically, FSS is assumed as an infinite array of unit cells with a plane wave excitation. However, in practice, an FSS is finite and hence, due to edge effects, the limited number of unit cells, and non-uniform illumination, the response will deviate from the theoretical. As it relates to FSS-based sensing in particular, a localized illumination is often used in order to improve the sensing resolution. However, due to the aforementioned factors, the sensitivity of the sensor may suffer as a result. Hence, the effect of these factors is studied on the FSS sensor response. Then, taking strain measurement as an example, the degradation in the sensor sensitivity to strain is evaluated in comparison with that of a theoretical FSS. The simulation results show that a finite FSS with non-uniform illumination has reduced sensitivity to strain. This degradation in sensitivity of reduces as the number of illuminated unit cells increases. However, the sensitivity of a finite FSS with uniform illumination is nearly constant with respect to the number of illuminated unit cells.

articleTitle: Joint Sensing and Communication via Superposition of Spectrally-Sparse Radar and BPSK Signals
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present an approach to joint wireless sensing and communications by adding a spectrally-sparse radar waveform to a communications signal. Two-tone radar waveforms achieve near-optimal range accuracy, and occupy very small fractional bandwidths by concentrating their spectral energy at the ends of the system bandwidth. We explore the concept of adding such a waveform to an existing communications signal, the latter of which is minimally impacted due to the spectrally-sparse nature of the two-tone waveform. We furthermore use the communication signal as a coarse range estimate to disambiguate the two-tone radar response, resulting in an unambiguous, high-accuracy approach for simultaneous sensing and communications. We demonstrate the approach in software-defined radios by adding a two-tone waveform with a 6 MHz bandwidth to a 2 MHz binary-phase-shift-keying (BPSK) signal centered between the two tones at a 4.5 GHz carrier frequency. We show measurements demonstrating the ability to track a walking person in an indoor setting while fully recovering the transmitted data.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach for the Fast Isolation Assessment of Co-located 5G Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Deployment plans of Base Stations depend on the maximum number of antennas that can be installed on the same infrastructure and their separation distances is strictly related to the isolation assessment. In fact, closely spaced antennas can lead to an increase in electromagnetic coupling with consequent degradation in the performance of the overall radio system. In this work, we propose a novel approach to speed up the calculation of isolation value among co-located antennas on the same 5G cell tower; the methodology here presented allows us to overcome the current limitations of commercial software or long measurement campaigns.

articleTitle: A Low Back-lobe Miniaturized Circular Polarized Antenna with Spiral Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to decrease back-lobe radiation of the small Circular Polarized (CP) antenna. The proposed CP antenna is composed of four antenna elements arranged in a rotational symmetry at 90 degrees on the ground, which are excited with the same amplitude and 90 degrees phase difference. Each antenna element is formed by a spiral antenna branched from the near the middle of an inverted-L antenna. From the result of simulation, backward radiation of the proposed CP antenna can be decreased by 13 dB due to the addition of the spiral elements.

articleTitle: A Comparative Investigation of Conventional and Dual Differential-Fed 2×2 Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a comparison between conventional 2×2 phased array and dual differential-fed 2×2 phased array is presented from the perspective of system effective reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>), axial ratio (AR) for both circular polarization (CP) and linear polarization (LP), and directivity. It is shown that S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> can be a useful tool to evaluate the combined effects of single element ports isolation, individual port matching, and mutual coupling between the patch elements. When reducing the mutual coupling by increasing elements spacing, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf> can be improved while limited by single element ports isolation. Isolation levels beyond -60dB are shown for the proposed dual differential-fed phased array, which is superior to the isolation level of the conventional 2×2 phased array. Moreover, the AR of the proposed dual differential-fed phased array is almost 0dB for CP and nearly 60dB for LP, and its AR is immune against mutual coupling.

articleTitle: Recent Progress on Full-duplex and Armband Textile Wearable Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Wearable technologies have become ubiquitous in our daily lives, providing unprecedented degrees of freedom with the aim of improving quality of life, especially for health monitoring. Wearable antennas offer the potential to realize large SWaP (size, weight, and power) reduction over conventional antennas for their ability to achieve comparable or even superior functionalities in ultrathin and flexible packages. This study presents the most notable works and advancements in this field while placing a significant focus on antennas with explicit practical applications in the emerging areas of wireless body area networks (WBAN) and Internet-of-Things (IoT). As illustrative examples, we primarily focus here on a discussion of the benefits and drawbacks of three textile wearable antennas including a full-duplex antenna, an omnidirectional armband antenna and an end-fire leaky wave antenna.

articleTitle: Utility-Based Beam Selection Algorithms for Sub-6 GHz Backhauls
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Small cell is a growing technology that enables Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) to deploy sites in strategic locations offering smaller coverage with higher capacities, using licensed and unlicensed wireless spectrum. The most problematic and restrictive element carriers face when deploying a small cell network is backhauling. Finding a site for deploying a small cell can be a painstaking process. Beam management is a procedure that correctly selects the beams to overcome strong path loss attenuation. In this paper, a beam tracking solution for sub-6 GHz is proposed. Together with the path-loss information of all the serving hub beams, its serving hub shares this path-loss map with the other co-located hubs at the same cell/site. The remote backhaul module uses the sum-utility-based algorithm to pick the hub beam that maximizes the sum utility of the link.

articleTitle: ‘Narrowband’ PUMA Arrays – A Simpler Alternative to Broadband Patch Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A simplified ‘narrowband’ planar ultra-wideband modular antenna (PUMA) array with 30% fractional bandwidth is presented as a competitive alternative to patch antennas of similar build complexity. The new topology integrates the dipole elements and the PUMA plate on a single metal layer enabling double-sided printing on a single FR-4 type core. To benchmark the performance, infinite array simulation results are reported and compared to a dual-polarization probe fed patch array, of similar manufacturing complexity. They suggest that a simple ‘narrowband’ PUMA array achieves better orthogonal port isolation and cross-polarization levels than the probe fed patch array. The proposed design has a predicted VSWR < 2 at broadside and less than 3 at θ = 45° and orthogonal port isolation better than -15 dB in a 45° scan cone. Realized co-pol radiation efficiency is better than 85% at broadside and 70% at the worst-case scan plane in a θ = 45° scan cone over the 15-21GHz (30%) frequency band.

articleTitle: Recent Trends on Unconventional Phased Array Architectures for Communication, Sensing and Wireless Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Next-generation communication and sensing systems are driving the antenna technology towards cost-effective phased array solutions. This work presents a review of the recent advancements in the design of unconventional array architectures, collecting and discussing the most significant contributions on sparse, thinned, clustered, and modular phased arrays for communication, radar/sensing and wireless power transfer applications.

articleTitle: On the Design of PDMS Based Miniaturized Ultra-Wideband Antenna for Compact Flexible Electronics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized UWB antenna for compact size devices is presented in this article. The antenna is designed using on PDMS substrate, well known for flexible nature. The antenna offers a wide impedance bandwidth covering UWB spectrum along with small overall size of 10 × 15 × 1.524 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. CPW fed antenna was modified using slots and stubs to achieve a compact size flexible antenna having simple geometrical configuration. Presented studies are carried out using Electromagnetic Solver, High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS).

articleTitle: Beam Steering for Adhoc Mesh Network Wireless Power Transfer at 2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present beam steering module for wireless power transfer system with our ad-hoc mesh network modality. The system comprises of 4×4 butler matrix and 4 1 × 4 patch antenna array operating at 2.45 GHz and provides total azimuthal coverage of 107.3°. This module is then paired with our wireless power transfer system.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Multilayer SIW Cavity Backed Differential Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a differential dual-band three-layer substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed antenna. The SIW has three cross-shaped slots and two shorting pins to facilitate radiation and improve impedance matching. The measured fractional bandwidth of 1.2 and 2.06%, peak gain of 5.67 and 6.99 dBi, radiation efficiency of 79.75 and 92.78%, and cross polarization level more than 37.94 dB have been achieved at resonating frequencies of 10.66 and 11.64 GHz, respectively. The proposed antenna is suitable for X-band application by comparing its output parameters with the previously reported results

articleTitle: Shaped-Beam Pattern Synthesis using Flat Lens Based on the Generalized Law of Refraction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A Beam shaping flat lens (BSFL) has been designed to shape a primary beam of a patch antenna into a desired pattern of a flat-top beam. Magnitude directivity functions of primary and desired beams are applied to calculate the required phase gradient profile using equation of the Generalized law of refraction (GLR). Resultant phase profile is practically implemented using a multilayer phase shift structures (PSS) radially distributed along the surface of the lens. Fifteen unique PSSs are arranged to create a flat lens of dimensions 75 x 75 x 3.35 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with F/D ratio of 0.5 at 30 GHz. A flat-top beam of 60º beamwidth with ripple level of ± 1dB is achieved with good transmission properties.

articleTitle: Mechanically Tunable Broadband Omnidirectional Infrared Absorption by Dielectric Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: New designs of mechanically tunable broadband and omnidirectional mid-infrared absorbers are proposed and theoretically analyzed. They utilize periodic dielectric metasurfaces embedded in an elastic material, i.e., polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Their tunable performance can be further improved when crumpled metallic substrates are used to terminate their structure. When stretched, the period of the dielectric metasurfaces increases while the thickness of the PDMS decreases, resulting to a rapid reduction in the total absorption. This dual elastic mechanism leads to a high degree of continuous absorption tunability over an ultrabroad wavelength range in the mid-infrared spectrum. The presented omnidirectional absorption tunability is expected to have important applications in emerging thermal management phenomena, such as radiative cooling of solar panels or spacecraft.

articleTitle: Research on AH-FDTD method based on improved UPML boundary condition
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an improved uniaxial anisotropic perfectly matched layer (UPML) absorption boundary method based on the Associate Hermite polynomial finite-difference time-domain (AH-FDTD) is used to analyze transient response of electromagnetic field in time domain. The method uses AH basis function to extend Maxwell’s equations, and uses Galekin principle to eliminate time variables, and separates time and space variables, so that the method is not restricted by Courant-Friedrich-Levy (CFL) conditions. The improved UPML absorbing boundary adds a new attenuation factor and improves the attenuation effect of low-frequency wave group. The FDTD method, Alternating Direction Implicit FDTD (ADI-FDTD) method and AH-FDTD method are used to realize the improved UPML absorbing boundary, and the absorption effects of the three methods are compared from two aspects of 2 norm error and infinite norm error. Simulation results show that the improved UPML based on AH-FDTD method has better absorption effect for low-frequency wave groups.

articleTitle: Non-Foster-inspired Two-transmitter System based on Coherent Current/voltage Sources
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: It is well-known that non-Foster-based transmitting systems comprising electrically small antenna suffer from stability problems. This problem could be overcome by recently proposed two-transmitter antenna feed arrangement, which effectively mimics the operation of non-Foster element. The drawback of this approach is technologically complicated hardware that assures wideband quadrature signals. Here, we remove this difficulty by transmitting system based on coherent voltage/ current sources.

articleTitle: Two Resonator based Approach to Extend the Tuning Range of Negative Resistance Oscillators in Active Integrated Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A switched dual-band oscillator using two resonators is proposed in this paper for application in the design of active integrated antennas. In this oscillator, two independent resonators are placed in parallel which is connected to a single transistor. For the resonator to work one at a time, surface mounted (SMD) trimpots are used to emulate switches by varying the resistance from high to low. The transistor acts as a negative resistance device for two resonators independently by using two different positive feedback elements which are then switched using trimpots. Two bands of oscillation, one from 1.123 GHz to 1.505GHz and another from 1.493 GHz to 1.758 GHz are obtained by this design approach. A Wilkinson power divider is integrated with the single port oscillator circuit using an output matching network. This allows the integration of two antenna elements to form a two-element active antenna array.

articleTitle: Octave-Band Three-Beam Antenna Array With Broadside Beam Fed by Broadband Butler Matrix
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel concept of a three-beam antenna array operating in an octave frequency range is presented. In the proposed antenna array stable radiation patters across such a broad bandwidth is ensured by a frequency-dependent feeding network based on a broadband Butler matrix composed of tapered-line directional couplers. To achieve appropriate signal distribution across the desired frequency range additional directional filters have been implemented. Moreover, taper excitation across the antenna array has been ensured to lower the resulting sidelobes, what has been achieved by an increased number of radiating elements and additional power dividers. The developed concept has been verified by measurements of the antenna array operating in 2 – 4 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Towards Non-Invasive Monitoring of Human Bio-physiological Parameters Using an RF-Panel
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel RF-panel to monitor multiple human physiological parameters non-invasively and accurately without requiring any complex arrangements. The proposed panel consists of three resonators coupled with a transmission line. A finger model was placed on and in between the resonators and the responses of the resonators were observed. The results indicate that there will be a clear correlation between the responses received and different physiological aspects intended to be measured. This outcome also helps envision that the incorporation of smart sensing materials and machine learning based analysis will make this RF panel capable of sensing physiological parameters by just placing a finger on any position of the panel.

articleTitle: Two-Way Long Short-Term Memory Architecture for Non-Contact Hand Gesture Identification
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This study proposes a novel method for the classification of hand gestures using a frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar. A two-way long short-term memory (TW-LSTM) architecture is introduced to categorize the movements recorded by an FMCW radar into 12 standard types of hand gestures provided by IEEE DataPort. The TW-LSTM method initially segments the physical displacement features of 4,600 movements into smaller frames. It then applies intra- and inter-frame temporal operations on the data to identify the type of movement. Experiments on four different subjects report an F1 score and an average accuracy of 84.02% and 84.0% for the classification of hand gestures respectively. It is also demonstrated that the true positive rates for all subjects fall within the range of 71.0%-91.0%, showing excellent consistency between predicted and true labels of hand gestures.

articleTitle: SDR Platform Implementation of DoA Detection Algorithm for Wireless Security Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A cost-effective system for detection and estimation of direction of arrival (DoA) for wireless transmitters is implemented on a software-defined radio platform (SDR), using beamforming algorithm and digitally controlled microwave switch for antenna selection. The system configuration and parameters are discussed and its detection capability is demonstrated at 2.45 GHz. The system is affordable and simple to operate and reproduce, hence it provides a robust and appealing practical educational platform.

articleTitle: Non-metallic Scanning Antenna System for ELF Magnetic Imaging Through Conductive Barriers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Recent work has shown that imaging through highly conductive barriers can be performed using radio waves in the extremely low and very low frequency bands (ELF/VLF 30 Hz–30 kHz). Specifically, the detection of hidden metallic and ferromagnetic objects inside a conductive container is possible under illumination by a near-field magnetic source. Illumination with a magnetic field normal to the conductive barrier results in a measurable depletion or enhancement that is used to produce images. A specialized automatic non-metallic scanning system is developed to improve the speed and accuracy of images produced. The main case investigated is a metallic object hidden inside a thin-walled aluminum cube. Frequencies of 50 and 200 Hz are demonstrated to effectively inspect the hidden object.

articleTitle: Scattering of a PEC Wedge in Anisotropic Media: Wiener-Hopf Model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The study of electromagnetic wave in interaction of Perfect Electrically Conducting (PEC) wedge in anisotropic media is of great interest in propagation models, GPR technologies and aerospace applications. In this work we present a general method based on the application of an extended version of the Wiener-Hopf (WH) technique for the analysis of the electromagnetic scattering and diffraction. This method is part of the semi-analytical spectral methods that allow physical interpretation of the solution in terms of field components.

articleTitle: Dynamic RCS Estimation of Drone Using Method of Moments Ignoring Coupling Between Propellers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We proposed a method for quickly estimating the dynamic radar cross-section (RCS) of a drone in various motions to train a classifier. The method of moments (MoM) is used with far-field approximation and mesh-element rotation. In this method, first, the impedance and admittance matrices of a single propeller are generated only once. Next, instead of rotating propeller, the position information of the mesh elements is rotated using a Rodrigues 3D rotation matrix. Finally, by using the mirror-image symmetric characteristics of drone propellers and the far-field approximation, the backscattered field of multi-propeller can be computed from the superposition of the propeller individual backscattered fields. Dynamic RCS estimation was performed at 3 GHz and 9 GHz. In addition, dynamic RCS was converted to spectrogram and Cadence-velocity diagram (CVD). As a result, it was difficult to obtain the rotation frequency at 9 GHz, whereas it was easier to find the rotation frequency at 3 GHz.

articleTitle: Loaded Microstrip Network Transmision-Line Metamaterials on an Irregular Grid
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A planar loaded microstrip network metamaterial on an irregular grid for modeling 2-D electromagnetic environment in TE polarization is presented. The technique is applied to a Luneburg lens example toward printed circuit implementation and verification.

articleTitle: Lead-Specific Transfer Function Validation Strategy for MRI RF Heating Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A lead-specific transfer function validation strategy for active implantable medical devices (AIMDs) radiofrequency (RF) heating model under Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is presented in the paper. This lead-specific validation strategy uses a selected sets of trajectories to achieve high signal to noise-ratio with low correlated incident electric fields during the model validation. Based on all possible validating pathways, both temperature rises and the field correlations can be estimated quickly. A commercially available AIMD used in this study to demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Nonlocal Effective Medium Theory for Time-Varying Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We introduce an effective medium theory for time-varying metamaterials based on a rigorous multascale approach. We show that nonlocal effects and artificial magnetism can emerge in certain parameter ranges, and we highlight similarities and differences with respect to the spatial counterparts. Finally, we show that the effects associated with a nonlocal temporal boundary can be harnesses so as to perform elementary analog operations on an impinging wavepacket.

articleTitle: Wideband Design of a Triple-Band Multi-Ring Microstrip Antenna Fed by an L-probe with Stubs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents wideband design of a triple-band multi-ring microstrip antenna (MR-MSA) fed by an L-probe with stubs. The proposed antenna consists of a quadruple-layered dielectric substrate. Three square ring patches are situated at the first to third layers from the top of the substrate for triple-band operation. A feeding L-probe to excite the three patches is arranged in the bottom layer with a large thickness for wideband design. In order to realize wideband operations for three bands, the structural parameters including the thicknesses of the layers of the substrate are tuned by using the numerical simulation with Mentor IE3D. Furthermore, the L-probe with stubs is used to improve the reflection characteristics. The design frequencies of the proposed antenna are around 3.6 GHz, 4.6 GHz, and 6.0 GHz. The simulated results reveal that fractional bandwidths of the three bands less than –10 dB reflection are 5.3%, 3.9%, and 14.3%, respectively. It is also confirmed by the simulation that stable unidirectional radiation patterns are obtained for the three bands.

articleTitle: An Effective Sequence of VNA Experiments for a Junior-Level Electromagnetics Course
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: There is a need for incorporating practical high frequency measurement experiences into an undergraduate electrical engineering (EE) program. This paper presents a sequence of experiments that develops student capabilities in vector network analyzer (VNA) measurements and component specifications formation. Students have demonstrated the effectiveness of this approach by constructing a datasheet for an unspecified RF/microwave filter as a summative experience.

articleTitle: Radiation from aperiodic reflectarrays using optimized NUFFTs
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We deal with one of the computationally most critical steps of the Phase-Only synthesis of aperiodic reflectarrays, namely, the fast evaluation of the radiation operator. We present an approach exploiting the use of a fast numerical algorithm using 2D Non-Uniform FFTs (NUFFTs) of NED (Non-Equispaced Data) type and of parallel processing on Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). A fast GPU-implementation of the NUFFT routine is achieved by exploiting a polynomial representation of the spatial and spectral windows and using the Horner polynomial calculation scheme.Numerical result highlight the performance of the developed approach.

articleTitle: A Broadband Pattern Diversity Metasurface Antenna With High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A low profile broadband pattern diversity antenna with high isolation based on metasurface is proposed. The proposed a nonuniform metasuface which consists of 5×5 patches. To achieve pattern diversity, the domain mode which have broadside pattern and high order mode which have bidirectional patterns of the metasurface are selected. The size of patches are optimized to obtain desired modal performance. A centrally placed slot is used to excite the domain mode. Two slots which are placed under the edge of the metasurface are used to excite high order mode. Due to differentially fed structure, the proposed antenna has infinitely high isolation in theory. Simulated results demonstrate that the proposed antenna achieves a wide bandwidth of 36% ranging from 5 to 7.2 GHz. The port isolation is higher than 60 dB over the whole impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: Accelerated Inversion of Short Offset Transient EM Data Using Supervised Descent Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Traditional gradient descent inversion for the short offset transient electromagnetic method (SOTEM) is inefficient, since the computation of the forward modeling and Jacobian matrix is more complex and time consuming than the conventional TEM with the loop source. In this paper, the application of the supervised descent method (SDM) for accelerating the SOTEM inversion is studied. During an offline training stage, the average descent direction can be learned by a set of training models. In an online predicting stage, the inversion process is accelerated by directly using the learned descent directions instead of computing the Jacobian matrix. Numerical examples verify the feasibility and efficiency of SOTEM inversion with SDM.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Reflectarray Antenna Unit Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper focuses on the application of a tunable square microstrip unit cell to the design of a wideband reconfigurable reflectarray antenna. The design utilizes the concept of varactor-loaded stubs to provide a wide tuning range with sufficient phase range. A parametric study on the unit cell is performed, including the effect of incidence angle of the incoming wave. On that basis, the parametrically optimized unit cell is predicted to achieve a tunable phase range of more than 300° over a 20% frequency tuning band.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Simulation of a Biconical Antenna with Spherical End Caps using Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A biconical antenna with a half cone angle of π/4 bounded by a sphere with radius of 2.4 cm to form spherical end caps was simulated in FEKO using Method of Moments. The critical aspects of this simulation is the presence of a finite but necessary feed gap to excite the antenna. We simulated the antenna with 2 nm, 10 nm and 356.65 nm feed gap length and noted that the maximum error in simulated directivity is no larger than 1.2% when compared to the theoretical model. Conversely, the errors grow large for the imaginary component of the input impedance. Discounting errors near the zero crossing of the imaginary component, the maximum errors are 546% and 34% for feed gaps of 356.65 nm and 2 nm respectively.

articleTitle: Optimal Swarm Size for Efficient Design of Nonuniform Helical Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Design of nonuniform helical antennas is a challenging task due to highly nonlinear relations between design parameters. The choice of the optimization setup is crucial for efficient finding of the best solution. Therefore, in this paper we investigate the influence of the swarm size for the particle swarm optimization with the main goal of finding nonuniform helical antennas that achieve the highest partial gain for the considered circular polarization.

articleTitle: Active Janus and Huygens Sources: Achieving Near-field and Far-field Directionality Control
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Active Janus and Huygens sources are proposed to investigate the directional properties of their EM fields. We use a twin current filament model to construct active Janus and Huygens sources. Particularly, a realistic active Janus source is proposed for the first time. Simulation of this source in a parallel plate waveguide (PPW) environment shows that the Janus and Huygens sources achieve similar far-field performance as their equivalents in 3D space. Investigations in the near-field show the PPW sources possess directive coupling properties in agreement with earlier works featuring ideal Janus and Huygens sources. This work paves way for the practical generation of the Janus source and its use in directive near-field coupling, with applications to multifunctional device design and near-field energy transmission.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering from a Magnetized Plasma Discharge Tube
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We study the electromagnetic (EM) scattering from a heterogeneous gyrotropic plasma rod using an analytical model, numerical simulations, and experiments. The plasma tube is represented as a 3-layer cylindrical structure composed of a plasma column core and quartz shell, separated by an unionized gas layer. The analytical model of the angular dependence of the scattered power is in excellent agreement with simulations. Both are in good qualitative agreement with experiments and selecting plasma conditions in the simulation that provide quantitative agreement with experiments affords a means of determining plasma properties.

articleTitle: Hardware-friendly Unsupervised Coding Scheme for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Based on Binary Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we study an unsupervised coding scheme for reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) based on binary neural networks (BNNs). Inspired by the difference map algorithm (DMA) that considers the beamforming of RISs as a search for the intersection of sets, the proposed coding scheme emulates the iterative procedure of the DMA by employing the BNNs to learn the parametric update rule. This scheme requires only the beam pattern masks to guide the learning process of BNNs, instead of labeled phase distributions, which enables the unsupervised training. The applications of BNNs reduce the computational load and make the proposed scheme hardware-friendly. The effectiveness of this scheme is further verified on a 1-bit RIS with 2304 unit cells.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit of OCS Negative Capacitor based on Linvill’s Floating NIC
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An open-circuit stable (OCS) non-Foster negative capacitor is frequently used for broadband matching of a short dipole. The most common implementation is based on Linvill’s floating negative impedance converter (NIC). Unfortunately, assurance of stable operation of such a system is a rather challenging engineering problem. It is usually solved by many cut-and-try development-fabrication cycles, often without clear understanding of the cause of instability. Here, we propose two simple equivalent circuits of an OCS negative capacitor that give clear insight into the influence of particular design parameters on instability and dispersion, enabling a simpler design.

articleTitle: Volume-Efficient Miura-Ori Reflectarray Antenna for SmallSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a deployable Reflectarray Antenna (RA) operating in K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band (38 GHz) is presented. A 80x80x25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> foldable RA, based on a Volume Efficient Miura-Ori Origami (VEMO) folding pattern, is developed to achieve high gain (36.1 dBi) and high volume packing efficiency (97.5%). The RA stows into a cuboid whose volume occupies just 16% of a 1U CubeSat. In its deployed state, the aperture produces a pencil beam with -18 dB side lobe level and 52.5% aperture efficiency.

articleTitle: A Thin Planar Ultra-wideband Antenna Element for Tightly Coupled mm-Wave Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The fast growing of mobile network technology towards 5G and 6G has led to interest in ultra wideband phased array antennas covering wide range of unlicensed mmWave frequencies specially the frequency range of 24 GHz-71 GHz. Existing antennas are either narrowband or very high profile and require complex fabrication methods. In this paper, a very thin (0.71mm) planar UWB antenna element in a tightly coupled array structure covering the whole frequency range of 24 GHz-71 GHz is designed and optimized for system on chip (SoC) applications where the size is of great importance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Deformed Antenna Array Based on Infinitesimal Dipole Model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The deformation of the array antenna will affect its radiation performance. In this paper, a method based on infinitesimal dipole (ID) equivalent array antenna elements is proposed to analyze the electrical performance of ideal and deformed array antennas. Numerical calculations are provided to demonstrate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of VHF/UHF Antennas for CubeSat using Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the application of the Characteristic Mode Theory for the design of CubeSat antennas in the VHF and UHF bands. It is shown that the addition of radial monopoles allows to obtain arbitrary directional patterns and polarizations, combining the degenerate modes appearing at the same frequency.

articleTitle: Europa Clipper X-Band Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Deep Space planetary missions require a set of robust antennas with varying radiation patterns in order to close the dynamic communications link over the mission life. This paper will focus on three such antennas, a Low Gain Antenna (LGA), a Medium Gain Antenna (MGA), and a Fanbeam Antenna (FBA). The LGA was implemented using a choke-ring cylindrical horn, the MGA was implemented with a dual-mode conical horn, and the FBA was implemented using a diplexed pair of waveguide fed helix arrays. All three antennas radiate circular polarization and operate over the International Telecommunications Union (ITU) Deep Space frequency band for Uplink and Downlink communications at X-Band. The implementation, analyses, and tests for these antennas to operate in the deep space environment will be detailed in this paper.

articleTitle: Uniform Near Magnetic Field Generated by Metasurface for Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The charging platforms capable of powering multi-receivers have attracted much interest in wireless power transfer realm. In this paper, we propose a metasurface-inspired resonator which generates uniform magnetic fields in the central working area of 30 cm × 30 cm. The maximum available power transfer efficiency of this area also reaches more than 90% suitable for charging a single receiver or multiple receivers in an office table.

articleTitle: Flexible Self-Alignment Reception for OAM-Based Large-Capacity Wireless Backhaul Links
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Due to the beam divergence of the Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) Radio Frequency (RF) waves, the transmission distance is quite limited. Considering actual engineering constraints, it is difficult and costly to deploy conventional coplanar arrays on the station towers to receive OAM beams. In this paper, a flexible self-alignment reception scheme with General Non-uniform Array (GNA) is proposed to solve this problem. The antennas are distributed around the propagation axis without strict coplanar and uniform requirement, so that the phase plane covered by this distributed array can be large enough to receive the divergent vortex beams. With credible analysis and experiments, it can be confirmed that the OAM-based long-distance wireless backhaul links can be acquired.

articleTitle: A Polarisation-Agile Phased-Array Antenna for Satellite and beyond-5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper a 8x8 stacked patch array is presented. The antenna elements are dual linearly polarised. By feeding the correct excitation for each antenna port, the array is capable of polarisation reconfigurability. The array is realised on a triangular lattice to simplify the system integration and packaging. An operating frequency range of 37 GHz to 42 GHz is achieved, which corresponds to a 13% fractional bandwidth at 39.5 GHz. The array is able to scan from -60° to +60° on all ϕ-planes while maintaining a scan loss below cos (θ)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.3</sup>. Moreover, the total active reflection coefficient is below -10 dB for the frequency range. The results show that the array operates on dual linear-polarisation mode or single circular-polarisation. For the circular polarisation the axial ratio is maintained below 2.7 dB for all the analysed frequency points and scan angles.

articleTitle: 2-Inverted U-Slot Integrated Rectangular Patch Antenna Array for S band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 2 inverted U-slot integrated rectangular patch antenna array is proposed that can be used for S band applications i.e., radar applications, communication and wireless networks. In the proposed antenna design 2 inverted U slots are introduced in the patch to improve bandwidth providing a bandwidth of 150 MHz and gain of 4.08 dBi resonating at 3.3 GHz. Furthermore, 4 X 4 antenna array is fabricated on 1.6 mm thick FR4 substrate with dielectric constant 4.4 providing a gain of 14.2 dBi. Ansys HFSS is used for antenna simulation and a prototype is fabricated and tested.

articleTitle: Characterization of Nematic Liquid Crystal using Complementary FSS in D-band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A multi-loop complementary frequency selective surface (CFSS) for characterizing the permittivity of the nematic liquid crystal (LC) mixture is proposed and investigated. By using the CFSS structure, the permittivity of a 10 μm thick LC layer can be effectively extracted. Furthermore, the quasi-broadband characterization is provided through the multi-loop structure. The proposed structure provides an inexpensive, compact and straightforward measurement method to extract the LC permittivity in the sub-THz band.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Enabled Full 360° Azimuth Surface-Level Beam Scanning Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of metasurface (MS) to enhance the scan range performance of the phased-array antenna for next-generation sub-6 GHz applications. The proposed system consists of a cylindrical Huygens' MS integrated with the source (phased array), and the MS steers the beam from the source towards the horizon. The metasurface's inherent symmetry also allows for full azimuth surface-level scanning. The proposed system achieves a gain of more than 15.5 dBi across the frequency range of 3.5-3.8 GHz.

articleTitle: On the Moisture-Resilience of On-Body Surface Wave Single Wire Transmission Lines (SWTLs)
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Radio Frequency (RF) surface wave transmission lines support low-loss on-body propagation, and have recently attracted significant interest for wearables. In this work, the effect of fabric moisture absoption on a surface-wave textile Single Wire Transmission Line (SWTL) is analyzed in the Ultra High-Frequency (UHF) spectrum from 0.5 to 4 GHz. It is shown that moisture can increase the losses (in dB) by four-fold. The 42 cm SWTL maintains an insertion loss around 15 dB up to at 2.4 GHz, when the substrate is covered fully in water. The measured response is compared to a printed textile microstrip line; the surface-wave SWTL exhibits a more linear response to the moisture content indicating its suitability for RF moisture sensing applications.

articleTitle: Calculating S-Parameters Using Only Port Voltages
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A method is presented for calculating the S-parameters of a multiport network using only the voltages evaluated at the port terminals with one port driven by a matched signal source and the other port(s) match loaded. The calculations can be performed using general mathematical analysis software; specialized RF software is not required. The goal is to make the topic of S-parameters more accessible to undergraduate students.

articleTitle: Frequency-Extended-Space MUSIC for Positioning PIM Sources
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Facing to the passive intermodulation (PIM) detection, this paper proposes the frequency-expanded-space multiple signal classification (FES-MUSIC) to break through the limitation of the sufficient antennas required in the time reversal (TR) imaging methods. The method provides only two antennas but to detect more PIM sources. Compared with the ultrawideband MUSIC (UWB-MUSIC), the proposed FES-MUSIC method performs more robustness and achieves much higher resolution.

articleTitle: Cloaking of Cylindrical Objects with Graphene-Metasurface Structures for Low-Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: It is a common practice for most of the theoretical studies to assume an ultra-high mobility and/or high value of chemical potential for graphene to realize its various functionalities such as perfect absorption, transmission, cloaking, etc. However, it is very difficult to actually fabricate such nano-patterned graphene structure, thus compromising its practical performance, despite the appeal of theoretical predictions. In this paper, we present a graphene-metasurface structure, taking inspiration from the design in ‘X. Wang and S. A. Tretyakov, IEEE Trans. Antenna Propag., vol. 67, no. 6, 2019'. When this specific metasurface is enveloped around cylindrical objects, the scattering width of the object reduces noticeably, thereby implying the cloaking effect. Our design utilizes extremely low values for mobility and chemical potential of graphene, making it highly desirable for practical applications.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Motion Tracking Methods: Magnetic Induction and HF RFID
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Human motion tracking has broad applicability, and currently, various approaches are available for its deployment. Wearable sensors and vision-based methods are among the most commonly used techniques that still face challenges in terms of accuracy, privacy, coverage, and cost. The magnetic induction (MI) system is a new approach based on inductive coupling, representing motions via variation in the MI signals. In this work, we present the performance analysis of the MI system and compare its accuracy with a high frequency (HF) radio frequency identification (RFID) system using experimental measurements in 3D motion tracking.

articleTitle: 330-500 GHz Waveguide-feed Tapered Slot Antenna on Micro-machined Silicon Substrate
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A corrugated Fermi tapered slot antenna (TSA) working at WR2.2 (330-500 GHz) is proposed in this paper. The proposed TSA adopts Fermi-structure tapering and corrugated edges to reduce the side lobes and improve the radiation patterns. It is fed by a microstrip line using a Marchand balun, and an E-plane probe is used as the power transfer between antenna chip and waveguide. The antenna is fabricated using SOI wafers with 15um thickness high-resistivity Silicon, and the partial substrate is etched to reduce the surface wave effect. The proposed antenna has -10 dB measured bandwidth at 330-500 GHz and 5-9.31 dBi measured gain. In addition, the simulated and measured E-plane and H-plane radiation patterns at 350 and 450 GHz are shown, of which the main lobe radiation patterns fit the simulation.

articleTitle: A Highly Directive D-Band Antenna Module comprising a Flat Discrete Lens and an Active Feed
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The design and characterization of a D-band active antenna for short-range communications are presented. An antenna-in-package, comprising a two-channel transmitter integrated circuit in 45-nm CMOS technology, a diplexer and a four-element patch array, excites a high-directivity transmitarray, i.e. a flat discrete lens. The lens is optimized to form a broadside beam and includes 2304 elements providing 16 different phase shifts. A standard printed circuit board process is used to fabricate the feed and the lens. The overall module achieves a high fractional bandwidth, operating between 139.4 GHz and 156.6 GHz, and a peak effective isotropic power of 17 dBm.

articleTitle: Low-complexity DoA Estimation method based on Space-Time modulated Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we present a novel metasurface-based Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation method. The proposed approach exploits the properties of space-time modulated reflecting metasurfaces to realize multiple beams in the scattered field, each of which propagating with a different frequency and wavenumber. In particular, the method makes use of the amplitude unbalance of the received fields at broadside at the frequencies of the two first-order harmonics generated by the interaction between the incident plane wave and the modulated metasurface. Here, we demonstrate that, breaking of the spatial symmetry of each order harmonic scattering pattern, it is possible to easily determine the DoA of a plane wave with extreme accuracy. Compared to conventional DoA estimation methods, the proposed approach simplifies the computation and hardware complexity, ensuring at the same time estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of a Reverberation Chamber for lyophilization: Finite-Element Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper examines the field intensity and uniformity inside a reverberation chamber for lyophilization processes. Simulation results, validated by experiments, show that double-ridge horn antennas outperform monocone antennas in electric field uniformity and intensity. Moreover, we also show that the angular position of the horn antenna has a significant impact on the electric field properties. These results demonstrate, for the first time, that significant improvements in terms of process uniformity are possible when RF waves are employed in freeze-drying of pharmaceutical products.

articleTitle: GCRO-DR Method for Solving Three-Dimensional Electromagnetic Wave Scattering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Many applications in electromagnetic engineering require the prediction of the current induced by a wide range of incident plane waves on a given object. This paper presents an efficient and accurate method for calculating the angular response of electrically large targets. Using the recently proposed Krylov cycle method GCRO-DR can effectively solve the matrix solutions of multiple RHSs. Numerical results are presented and compared with other iterative algorithm to verify the numerical solution and illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: General resonance-based design method for precise metasurface standard filters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a systematic method to design two-port metasurfaces with transmission spectrum matching standard filters with great accuracy. It relies on the system resonant modes, which can be computed easily by an eigensolver. Obviously, the resonant frequencies must match the required poles for the desired filter. More interestingly, we derive analytical conditions for the necessary ratios with which the resonant fields must couple to the two ports, in conjunction with a slowly varying background response, to also enforce the desired filter transmission zeros. The resulting conditions give a better optimization problem with respect to structural parameters that converges faster, compared to brute-force methods optimizing directly the transmission spectrum. The method applies to any length scale, including for wavelength-sized systems with overlapping resonances, where circuit models and coupled-mode theory typically fail. We demonstrate it by designing multiple RF metasurfaces configured for polarization-preserving transmission, reflective polarization conversion, or diffractive anomalous reflection, and exhibiting responses that precisely match standard bandpass or bandstop filters of various orders, bandwidths, and types (with focus on elliptic filters).

articleTitle: SFCW Software-Defined Radar using LabVIEW and USRP for Subsurface Sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we describe the experiment of a dual-channel stepped-frequency continuous wave (SFCW) radar system using LabVIEW and NI USRP N210. The step-by-step of the radar design is discussed, including the SFCW signal generation, the USRP-LabVIEW connection, and the transmit/receive process of the system.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Decomposition of Scattering Dyadic
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This abstract describes the decomposition of a matrix representing a scattering dyadic into characteristic modes. Scattering dyadic, as compared to conventionally used impedance matrices, are independent of numerical method used to compute them and the same characteristic mode formulation can be used for decomposition of composite and inhomogeneous materials. The utilization of scattering dyadic makes it possible to synthesize characteristic modes which are orthogonal over prescribed portions of the far-field sphere, or ex-post decomposition of measured data. The theory is demonstrated on a simple example and its features are discussed.

articleTitle: Multiple Scattering Effects of Trees on L-band Microwave Using a Hybrid Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The multiple scattering of electromagnetic waves in forests is studied using a two-step hybrid method. First, the T-matrix of a single tree is calculated based on its far-field computed with the full-wave simulations of the FEKO software. The T-matrix captures the multiple scattering caused by the tree structure. Second, the the interactions among different trees are considered using the T-matrices of the individual trees and the Foldy-Lax equations. The result of the two-step hybrid method is validated with FEKO by solving scattering from two trees directly. The multiple scattering effects are illustrated by the field solutions.

articleTitle: On the Optimum Substrate Selection in a Wideband Microstrip Patch Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper provides a general guideline to reduce surface wave (SW) excitations in a microstrip patch antenna, while maintaining wide impedance bandwidth and a stable gain performance. The design approach involves efficient selection of substrate parameters, viz. $h\sqrt {{\varepsilon _r}} /\lambda $, such that only a lower magnitude of the dominant TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> mode is excited, while restricting the excitation of all higher order SW modes. Results from the proposed design approach show that very wide antenna bandwidth, reduced E-plane coupling and stable boresight gain can be obtained.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Sub-6 GHz MIMO Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper examines a hybrid coupler fed cylindrical dielectric resonator (CDR) at sub-6 GHz band for 5G applications. With 50 ohm termination of the isolated port, and modification in the through port and coupled port, an axial ratio bandwidth of 11.6% ranging from 3.3 – 3.7 GHz is observed. The impedance bandwidth ranging from 3.11 – 4.22 GHz is observed which covers the n78 band of 5G. The proposed 5G multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna shows good isolation of -22dB with high radiation efficiency of 92 – 97 %. Also, the average gain achieved if 5 dB.

articleTitle: Power Handling of Varactor Diode-Based Frequency Agile Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Power handling of varactor diodes (varactors) is a significant limitation on reconfigurable antennas. In this paper, the power handling of antennas that are frequency reconfigurable using varactors was quantitatively investigated. This was accomplished by fabricating a Ring Resonator End Loaded Slot Antenna (RRELSA) and measuring its behaviour under high input powers. This paper shows that the nonlinear behaviour of the varactors becomes problematic well before physical power limitations. This work confirms that this nonlinearity pollutes the spectrum through radiation, and goes on to demonstrate significant degradation in impedance match.

articleTitle: Last advances in freehand sensing for mmWave imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This contribution presents the last developments of freehand systems for electromagnetic sensing, focusing on millimeter-wave (mmWave) freehand imaging systems. In particular, the impact of positioning errors in the quality of the obtained electromagnetic images is discussed, emphasizing the importance of using tracking systems that can be embedded in the freehand device. In addition, several challenges faced by freehand systems to achieve a higher scanning speed and a reduced computational burden towards fully autonomous portable systems are summarized.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of HRRP with missing data and noise
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper applies a recently developed technique for Bayesian reconstruction of Fourier pairs to reconstruct the impulse response (or the High Range Resolution Profile-HRRP) of a stepped-frequency radar target assuming missing data (backscatter), and assuming additive Gaussian noise corrupting the data. This technique is very successful at recovering HRRP of a target with significant amount of backscatter missing. The reconstructed data is used for target identification with performance nearly close to the optimal classifier.

articleTitle: On the Study of a Low Profile Triple-Band Meander Line Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact microstrip meander line antenna has been presented with a size of 36×30×1. 524mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed antenna resonates at three different frequency bands which include 4.48-4. 529 GHz radio communications, 5. 037-5. 098 GHz Wi-Fi applications, and 5. 821-5. 876 GHz WLAN applications. The antenna geometry comprises of a well-built vertically and horizontally coupled slotted structure at the trace plane with a continuous reference ground plane to achieve the desired applications bandwidths. The proposed design has demonstrated a satisfactory antenna return loss, gain, along with directional radiation patterns in both fields at all three frequency points thus making itself suitable for various wireless applications.

articleTitle: Compact Bandwidth-Extended CRLH-TL based Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A compact bandwidth extended Composite right/left-handed transmission line (CRLH TL) based monopole antenna is presented in this paper. The antenna's higher order resonant mode is merged with the zeroth-order resonant (ZOR) mode and other multiple resonant modes (created by the shunt inductor’s connecting arm). The antenna is designed on a lossy FR4 substrate with a compact foot print of 33 mm × 40 mm. The proposed antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth of 57.1 % (2.3 GHz to 4.14 GHz) and covers major applications like WIFI, Bluetooth, SHF RFID, WIFI (802.11b, g, & n), WIMAX (2.5 GHz –2.69 GHz, 3.4 GHz –3.69 GHz), CBRS.

articleTitle: Reflectarray-based Intelligent Reflecting Surface to Improve mm-Wave 5G coverage in outdoor scenarios
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the use of a reflectarray panel as an efficient and low-cost solution to improve millimeter-wave coverage in 5G scenarios. A dual-polarized shaped-beam is designed to radiate a flat-top beam to cover a blind zone without coverage. The design is carried out using a phase-only synthesis considering the beam specifications for the outdoor scenario. Then, a single-layer reflectarray element is used to perform a design at 27.7 GHz. This element provides an angularly-stable phase response at the operational frequency with an independent phase control in each linear polarization. The reflectarray panel shows a stable gain and a low both side-lobe level and cross-polarization within 1 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: Wearable Logo Textile Directive Antenna for IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new logo textile directive antenna useful for IoT applications has been presented. The antenna consists of two resonant elements mounted on a jean material and capacitively fed by proximity with transmission lines placed behind it. A progressive design has been used to achieve the logo antenna proposed. The structure has been excited with a power divider yielding good impedance matching (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> < −10 dB) from 2.1 GHz to 3.6 GHz with maximum directivity around 4.84 dBi, and a stable radiation pattern in the range frequency.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized and Wideband Orthogonal Dipole Antenna for LTE/5G Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a simple dual-polarized and wideband orthogonal dipole base station antenna for LTE and 5G sub-6 GHz communication systems. The proposed is composed of the radiator, reflector, absorbing structures and a pair of crossed Y-shaped baluns. A pair of orthogonal dipoles are fed by microstrip baluns coupling and used to obtain dual-polarization. Four absorbing structures are used to achieve high front-to-rear ratio.
