The proposed antenna has an overall size of ${\lambda _L} \times {\lambda _L} \times 0.257{\lambda _L}$ (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> is the free-space wavelength at 3.0 GHz). The simulated results show that the bandwidth of this antenna achieves 53.3% (2.3~3.63 GHz) for S11/S22<-10dB and S21<-26dB, and the gain is 7.6 ± 0.4 dBi within the operational bandwidth. With this features the proposed antenna is suitable for LTE/5G base station communication applications.

articleTitle: Azimuth-Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An azimuth-pattern reconfigurable antenna (APRA) based on dipoles is proposed in this paper. The antenna consists of four dipoles, two strips, and two square patches. By switching over four PIN diodes, the dipoles can switch between driver and reflectors, resulting in four different operating modes. In each operating mode, the beam direction of the proposed antenna is always opposite to the reflectors and the pattern covers more than a quarter of the azimuth plane. As a result, four steerable beams which are capable of covering the entire azimuth plane can be obtained. Simulated 3 dB beamwidth in the elevation plane is switchable from 138° to 206°. Moreover, due to its compact size, the proposed antenna can be applied to various communication application scenarios, e.g., RFID readers, subway, and railway communications.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface with Substrate Integrated Waveguide Configuration
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology has been widely explored in the design of frequency selective surface (FSS) for improving the selectivity. However, reconfigurable FSS based on SIW technology was rarely investigated due to its complicated geometry for bias network design. In this work, a reconfigurable FSS based on SIW configuration is proposed. The device exhibits a narrow transmission band that can be tuned by controlling the capacitance of a varactor diode as well as the dielectric constant of liquid crystal filled within the cavity of dielectric layers. The proposed FSS exhibits a transmission band that can be tuned from 5.56 GHz to 4.6 GHz when the capacitance of varactor is tuned from 0.025 pF to 0.19 pF and the dielectric constant of liquid crystal is tuned from 2.42 to 3.2.

articleTitle: A Triple-Band Antenna for Indoor 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a Triple-band antenna for 0.7/3.5/28 GHz is proposed and studied for 5G operations. The antenna consists of a folded monopole, C-shaped monopole and four patch arrays to generate three resonant modes for triple-band operation. The folded monopole which is fed by S-shaped strip generates a frequency band at 700 MHz. By couple-feeding of C-shaped monopole through and C-shape strip, a frequency band can be generated at 3.5 GHz. These two elements have an omnidirectional pattern, and they cover the sub-6 GHz band for 5G application. The four patch arrays have a resonance frequency of 28 GHz with a directional radiation pattern. The antenna is designed on a RO-5880 substrate with a total area of 135 mm x 50 mm. Plots of the return loss and radiation pattern have been presented and discussed to show the suitability of the design for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Restoration of Antenna Radiation Pattern Using Conditional Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A deep learning model based on the conditional generative adversarial network (c-GAN) is proposed to accelerate the measurement of radiation and scattering patterns. Recently, GAN has been proposed to effectively restore an image from its fragments and blank areas. Here, we further leverage the GAN model to fully restore the antenna radiation pattern with sparse solid angles, thus greatly saving the characterization time and cost. We envision that the proposed GAN-assisted measurement method may be beneficial for various applications, including radar, remote sensing, and optimal deployment of 5G/6G networks.

articleTitle: A Pattern Reconfigurable Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new design of a reconfigurable antenna based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) antenna parity mode switching is proposed. The antenna just uses one PIN diode realize the switching between omnidirectional radiation pattern and directional radiation pattern. For simplicity, a metal block is added in the simulation to simulate the conduction of the PIN diode, and the metal block is removed to simulate the disconnection of the PIN diode. The simulated results show that the antenna works on the omnidirectional radiation pattern within 5.52GHz-5.62GHz by switching the PIN diode off. When the PIN diode is on, the endfire radiation pattern can be obtained and its operating frequency is 5.46GHz-5.6GHz with the maximum gain 5.77dB.

articleTitle: Wideband MIMO Antenna Array Design With High Isolation by Using Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metasurface to enhance the isolation of the dual-element wideband MIMO antenna array. The metasurface is consists of conventional cross-shaped periodic units. The reflection of the space waves from the MS has the same amplitude and opposite phase, which can enable cancellation with the direct coupling component of the antenna array. Based on the decoupling mechanism, the isolation of the antenna array can be improved from 15 dB to more than 25 dB within the bandwidth of 4.13-4.89 GHz. Since the cancellation in the normal direction, the radiation of the array has a slight deterioration.

articleTitle: High-gain and Wideband Fabry-Perot Resonator Antenna based on a Pixelated single PRS layer for Ku-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband and high-gain Fabry Perot Resonator Antenna (FPRA) is proposed. It is based on a synthesized compact, single partially reflective surface (PRS) layer acting as a superstrate to a slot-coupled feed antenna, which acts as a radiating source element for the proposed design. The PRS uses a 2-D printed unit cell, where the lower part is a simple circular-ring Frequency Selective Surface (FSS), incorporated with a synthesized FSS unit cell. This latter acts as the upper part of the proposed PRS layer and provides a positive phase gradient. It is almost perfectly resembles that of the optimum PRS over the desired frequency range, with a relatively high reflection magnitude, making it an efficient superstrate candidate for wideband and high gain FP resonator antennas. The proposed design achieves important performance in terms of impedance bandwidth ranging from 11.9 to 17.6 GHz (38.64 %). In addition, the 3-dB gain bandwidth is 39.11 % from 11.6 to 17.24 GHz, with a maximum peak gain of 14.21 dB achieved at 16 GHz. Consistent and almost invariant radiation patterns are achieved over the Ku-band frequency band of interest.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Ridged Horn Performance in Lieu of Stereolithography Required Modifications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Impact of release holes on the phase center stability and 10 dB beamwidth of wideband millimeter wave (36-90GHz) horns is studied. Shape and size of the holes are studied in the context of material release that enhances quality of additive manufacturing and enables more uniform plating. Results show that using elliptical shaped holes in general allow for lower phase center deviation and less pattern distortion. Identifying these deviations in the horn characteristics allows for future study of the mechanisms causing them as well as potential solutions for enabling 3D-printing of millimeter-wave horn antennas.

articleTitle: Printed Metasurfaces for Wearables
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A metasurface designed for anti-jamming was direct-write printed on nylon fabric. Free-space measurements of the textile metasurface were conducted, confirming a rejection center frequency around 5.95 GHz, consistent with simulations. The printed metasurface demonstrates longevity with minimal change in performance over 120 days. Anti-jamming properties were tested in the presence of radio frequency interference (RFI) and showed full recovery of a transmitted signal. This work demonstrates the viability of wearable metasurfaces for protection against jamming at industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) frequencies.

articleTitle: Optimization of 5G Infrastructure Deployment Through Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The application of machine learning for optimal deployment of 5G infrastructure, such as the position and the orientation of the antenna that help achieve the best signal coverage, is investigated in this paper. This avoids the need to perform on-site measurements or extensive software simulations. Multivariate Regression (MR) and Neural Network (NN) models were applied to predict the signal coverage in an indoor environment. The results showed that the average prediction error using NN for the case investigated is 7 dB for a 60-GHz operating frequency, whereas the error using the MR technique is lower than 6 dB. The unique aspect in our work is the integration of the clustering algorithm and the NN machine learning model for predicting indoor signal coverage.

articleTitle: Full Azimuth Beam Steering by Means of Radiation Pattern with the Narrow Beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, it is attempted to illustrate a procedure in generating and steering the radiation pattern with a narrow beamwidth, roughly seven degrees. The proposed structure includes 64 radiating elements surrounding a cylinder. Each time, every 16 elements are placed in the active section and engender the required pattern leading to full beam steering in the azimuth plane. The feeding network and the excitation coefficients are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Design of a Conformal Ultra-thin Metasurface for Broadband RCS Reduction of Radar Targets
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A Conformal Ultra-thin Radar Absorbing Metasurface (CU-RAM) is designed in this paper, which is characterized by the broadband RCS reduction ability and can be applied in optical transparent targets. To broaden the reduction bandwidth, the polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) and frequency selective surface (FSS) are introduced to design and analyze the CU-RAM. The former is concentrated to converse the EM beams, and the latter needs to dissipate the EM energy transmitted into the CU-RAM. For X-band and K-band, the CU-RAM can realize a reasonable RCS reduction of better than -5 dB with ultra-thin thickness, that is applicative for the conformal metasurfaces attaching to radar targets. All the preliminary results verify that the proposed CU-RAM provides a novel approach to design stealth metasurfaces for further flexible three dimensional radar targets.

articleTitle: Array-Fed Ring-Focus Reflector: Synthesis Methods for Annular Sum and Difference Patterns
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Three different methods to synthesize annular sum and difference patterns, produced by an array-fed ring-focus reflector (RFR), are presented. In the first method, an ideal planar source associated with the maximum possible gain is placed near the reflector’s aperture, and then from its radiated fields the source distribution of the feed array is determined. In the second method, the ideal planar source is projected directly onto RFR’s surface and the radiated fields of the "non-planar" source is employed to synthesize the feed array source distribution. In the third method, a direct optimization is invoked to determine the array source distribution. For the difference beams, Gram-Schmidt’s orthogonalization is employed. The numerical results for sum and difference beams are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-polarized UWB Antenna for UAV Based Low-Frequency Software Defined Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarized ultrawideband antenna for a software-defined radar (SDRadar) mounted on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) with various modes of operations is proposed. The antenna consists of two perpendicularly combined double slot Vivaldi antennas (DSVA) to achieve a reasonable gain over a wide bandwidth and is compact enough to meet the UAV payload size requirement. An antenna operating in the range of 0.25 − 2.5 GHz is designed and ready for fabrication. The simulated reflection coefficients of the antenna is shown to be better than −10 dB within the design frequency range. The antenna is low-profile with a total height of 300 mm and lateral dimensions of 230 mm × 230 mm. This design allows the radar system to operate in multiple modes, including ground penetrating sounding and imaging modes. This article details the design process and simulated results for the DSVA antenna element of the dual-polarized antenna.

articleTitle: Coupled Mode Theory as a Unifying Concept in Multi-Mode Patch Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Coupled Mode Theory (CMT) is a classic model that addresses many diverse problems in physics and electrical engineering. Although CMT is well-established in areas such as filter and directional coupler design, its significance in antenna engineering is less well-recognized. Recently, Characteristic Mode Analysis has shown how CMT quantitatively models a wide variety of broadband, multi-mode patch structures. In this paper, we review these results and discuss the similarities and differences between these radiators through the lens of CMT. With these principles in mind, multi-mode radiators may be designed in a straightforward manner and new ideas for broadband, multi-mode patches are stimulated.

articleTitle: A Conjugate Gradient Algorithm with Analytical Expressions for Compact Metasurface Pair Design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: For the design of compact metasurface pairs using an existing design approach, a conjugate gradient (CG) algorithm with analytical expressions for the CG direction, step length, and the initial guess is developed. This is done in an attempt to fully automate this design approach.

articleTitle: Measuring Impedance with Spread Spectrum Time Domain Reflectometry
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Spread spectrum time domain reflectometry (SSTDR) can be used to measure circuit impedances similar to those measured by a vector network analyzer (VNA). We describe a measurement setup and calibration method to compare VNA and SSTDR measurements of a complex load from 0.1 MHz to 100 MHz for the former and near DC to 96 MHz for the later. The impedance for the SSTDR measurements closely match the VNA and ideal impedance magnitude values from 10 MHz to 65 MHz, where the SSTDR signal has enough spectral power to create an accurate reflected signal. These initial measurements show the feasibility of using the SSTDR approach to measure impedance.

articleTitle: A Curvature Based Shaped Reflector Antenna Design Method for Contoured Beam Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new shaped reflector antenna design technique based on surface curvature for a continental US coverage (CONUS) beam synthesis is presented. An approach based on representing a reflector surface as a set of curves where its shape is modified by altering the curve profile. Instead of directly optimizing the curves, we first evaluate their curvature and represent it using B-spline polynomials. The spline control points are defined as optimization variables, which generates a new curvature profile at each iteration of the optimizer. From the optimized curvature profiles, the reflector surface is generated using an iterative algorithm proposed in this work. The major advantage of this work is that the surface constrains on curvature can be imposed directly in the optimizer, without the need for additional design variables as required in TICRA’s POS software. The validity of this method is confirmed by an application example and its advantages are compared with a reflector surface represented using a traditional technique based on modified Jacobi polynomials.

articleTitle: Definitions and Measurement Procedure for the Receiving Efficiency and Noise Figure of an Active Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: For complex active array receiver systems, losses are distributed across multiple elements, making it difficult to define and measure common antenna figures of merit. Previous methods for finding the noise figure of active arrays are based on combining the parameters of individual components of the system and fail to define noise figure in terms of the system-level properties of the array. We use the array isotropic noise response and receiving efficiency to give a rigorous definition and a technique for measuring the noise figure of an active receiving array.

articleTitle: Revision of IEEE Std. 1720-2012: Recommended Practice for Near-Field Antenna Measurements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The IEEE Std 1720™ "Recommended Practice for Near Field Antenna Measurements" was approved in 2012 as a completely new standard by the IEEE Standards Association Standards Board (SASB). After being active for ten years, the standard will expire in 2022. A revision is required to update the document to incorporate new developments and technologies that have matured during the past decade. Following approval by IEEE SASB of the project for minor revision, a working group (WG) of the Antennas and Propagation Society Standards Committee (APS/SC) was formed. The WG is transversal, with users and experts of the near-field measurement systems. It consists of about fifty dedicated volunteers from industry, academia, and government. This paper provides an update on the ongoing activities and discusses the suggested changes to the standard.

articleTitle: A Method for Fast and Accurate Analysis of Attenuation and Phase Aberrations of Waves Propagating in Random Media
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces the S-matrix method for fast and accurate analysis of both dense and sparse random media. In the method, the random medium is divided into slabs and the relation between outgoing and incoming waves are described by a matrix (S-matrix). Similar to the network theory, the S-matrices can be cascaded and used to find the response of the random medium to arbitrary sources and incoming waves. The performance of the method is shown in analysis of the attenuation and phase aberrations of waves propagating in rain.

articleTitle: K/Ka-Band TX/RX Phased Array Antenna System for Two-Way Mobile SATCOM Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a very brief overview of an extensive research and technology development that was led by Safieddin (Ali) Safavi-Naeini on the K/Ka-band mobile satellite communication (SATCOM). The developed system is based on modular scalable architecture. It consists of two 32×32 (1024) element active-PAA panels for transmit and receive. It allows for establishing both reliable uplink and downlink communication with GEO satellites. Preliminary over-the-air measured results show good performance. The antennas’ main beam can be steered electronically over scanning range ± 70 deg.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of Lossy Media using Improved 3-D HIE-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient lossy media implementation using the improved hybrid implicit–explicit finite-difference time-domain (HIE-FDTD) method. Various schemes, including a forward-backward scheme, are formulated for the proposed implementation. The efficiency of formulated schemes are validated through numerical results and compared to the efficient alternating-direction-implicit (ADI)-FDTD and the conventional FDTD methods.

articleTitle: 3D beam steering cylindrical antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: 3D beam steering antennas are a current topic for improvement of wireless applications in many fields, such as radar, multi-user or low-power wireless networks. In Wireless Sensor Networks, piloting an antenna in elevation shows interest for deployments when energy-constrained nodes lie out of plane. We propose an upgrade of a cylindrical Switched Beam Antenna to add steering in elevation. The simulation of the stacking of the former structure with proper Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) cell configuration shows a beam gain of 11.6 dBi at elevation 0° and the possibility of a discrete steering in elevation of 22° and – 22° with a beam gain of 9.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna Using Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We propose a circularly polarized dielectric resonator antenna fed by a printed ridge gap waveguide inverted microstrip line, the antenna achieves a 13.2-dBi peak gain. The radiation characteristics of the proposed antenna is improved significantly by the use of a dielectric ring.

articleTitle: Safieddin (Ali) Safavi-Naeini—Advancing Fundamental Research and Industrial Impacts of Terahertz Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Prof. Safieddin (Ali) Safavi-Naeini was our Ph.D. supervisor, a great mentor, a kind supporter and above all our role model. He had a vast knowledge and wide experiences in his field of expertise, was a great educator, an extremely supporting mentor, and a visionary academic/industry leader. In this talk, we would like to focus on Prof. Safavi-Naeini’s pioneering research on terahertz (THz) technology and his significant contributions to this field. He has had profound impacts on many graduate students, postdocs and research associates who have been trained and graduated from his group in this field and other fields of applied electromagnetics.

articleTitle: Angle of Arrival and Angle of Departure Analysis in Scattering Environment for THz Wireless Links
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) spectrum is taking center stage in achieving 1 Tb/s high data rate wireless communication. At THz frequencies, the wave propagation characteristics witnessed in a scattering environment scenario seem quite complex. Previous works interpret the electromagnetic wave scattering phenomenon from real surfaces utilizing mainly scattering models of Rayleigh-Rice (R-R) and Beckmann-Kirchhoff (B-K). However, these presume surface topographic irregularities of a random rough surface (RRS) in statistical terms, thus disregarding the physical nature of the irregularities. Contrastingly, the real 3D surfaces randomly vary in time and space, whereby not only the amplitude and phase of the waves fluctuate rather the angles of arrival and departure are also impacted. In this paper, we therefore endeavor to study multipath propagation taking into account R-R approach and real 3D surfaces at 300 GHz carrier frequency. The comparative study is carried out in a realistic simple office environment with different surface roughnesses for both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions.

articleTitle: Calculating the Energies of a Pulse Radiator with Marching-on in Time Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the numerical technique to calculate the three parts of the electromagnetic energy of a pulse perfectly electrically conducting (PEC) radiator with marching-on in time (MOT) scheme.

articleTitle: Optimization of Aperture Efficiency of Reflectarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Reflectarray aperture efficiency (h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>) is usually analyzed first to predict the performance of a reflectarray antenna. Aperture efficiency is dependent on spillover efficiency (h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>) and illumination efficiency (h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>) which in fact is a function of the f by D ratio, where ‘f’ is the distance between the feed and reflectarray, and ‘D’ is the length of the reflectarray antenna. In this paper we take a numerical approach to accurately estimate the aperture efficiency for varying f/D and comparing with an existing analytical solution. The full-wave analysis of the reflectarray proves that the aperture efficiency obtained from the numerical approach is more accurate than the analytical solution. Furthermore, we discuss about intuitively modifying the input parameters of the analytical solution to accurately estimate the aperture efficiency.

articleTitle: A Thin Dual-Mesh Transparent Metamaterial Unit cell for Millimeter-Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This article presents meshed wire-based transparent metamaterial unit cell for millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequencies. Thin copper wires are used to from meshed conducting ring patches on a 0.254 mm thick Polyimide substrate material in order to obtain transparency. Closely spaced metallic wires are placed in such a way that the structure exhibits negative effective permeability, effective permittivity, and refractive index at the magnetic resonance frequency of 28 GHz with 85% transparency. Nicolson-Ross-Wier (NRW) and direct retrieval methods are used to obtain the metamaterial characteristics. The performance of the metamaterial unit structure is evaluated mainly using scattering parameters, the surface current density and effective dielectric parameters. The performance of the unit cell indicates that it is a suitable candidate for use in next-generation 5G mmWave communication devices.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Passive Reflector for Radar Detection of Road Markings
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces the design of a passive reflector which presents a relatively large radar cross-section to forward-looking automotive radars. The reflector’s low-profile configuration facilitates integration into roadway infrastructure by embedding into painted asphalt. Thus, the reflector may be used for detection and identification of road markings in low-visibility weather conditions. The reflector is designed for operation at the 79 GHz automotive radar band, and exhibits a simulated cross-section of -12.7 dBsm at an 85° incidence angle.

articleTitle: Efficient Near-Field Meta-Steering Systems for Connectivity-On-The-Move Applications using Hybrid Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work we provide an elaborate discussion on Near-Field Meta-Steering systems with hybrid metasurfaces. The steering efficiency of the system is increased by using different types of highly transmitting cells in the design of metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Reducing Mutual Coupling Between Directional and Non-Directional Antennas by Using Metamaterial Screens
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper compares influence of metamaterial screens on interaction between directional and non-directional antennas. It is shown that the metamaterial screens make it possible to reduce the mutual coupling between antennas of both types near natural resonant frequencies. The results obtained are used to provide the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of compact radio-electronic equipment groups.

articleTitle: W-band Dielectric Characterization of Automotive Paint
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A rectangular waveguide sample-holder is proposed for characterization of dielectric constant of thin sheets, where the sample is mounted in the longitudinal direction. This is a desired configuration as it provides higher sensitivity in measurement of complex dielectric constant and ease of sample preparation for WR-10 waveguides. Unlike conventional rectangular waveguide techniques, this technique relies on the resonance behavior of the reflection coefficient from the sample to accurately estimate the dielectric constant of the sample under test. A rectangular waveguide sample holder was fabricated, and different samples were characterized. The estimated dielectric constant values were verified using a CPW resonator technique.

articleTitle: Using Genetic Programming to Achieve High Broadband Absorptivity Metamaterial in Compact Radar Band (1–11 GHz) without Lossy Materials
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In the modern age of metamaterial absorbers (MA), many implementations are generally in the C and X microwave bands. Genetic programming (GP) software is used to generate new 3D designs for metamaterial absorbers with multilayer dielectrics to achieve high broadband absorptivity in the compact radar band (CRB) (1–11 GHz) without lossy materials. GP was previously used to create an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) with broadband capabilities in 225–450 MHz without magnetic or absorbing materials. Utilizing the capabilities of GP to create broadband structures, the GP software is modified to create broadband MAs. Two 2D patterned structures with multilayer dielectrics were generated with above 90% absorptivity peaks around 3 and 5 GHz. The preliminary use of GP to create broadband MA structures shows excellent potential for creating a structure that broadens the whole CRB.

articleTitle: Harmonic Beam Steering Along Both the Cardinal Planes Using a Dual-polarized Space-Time-Coding Digital Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a space-time-coding digital metasur-face is proposed for harmonic beam steering along both the cardinal planes. With respect to the harmonic frequencies, the metasurface steers a TE- (or y-) and TM- (or x-) polarized incident wave along xz- (ϕ = 0°) and yz- (ϕ = 90°) plane, respectively, upon reflection. To maintain the main lobe magnitude at the same level and the first side-lobe levels (SLL) 10 dB below the main lobe maximum for all the harmonic orders, an artificial neural network (ANN) routine is used to find out the required space-time-coding patterns for both the polarizations. A 1-bit coding digital metasurface is shown which can support the proposed idea.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Frequency Selective Surface Design Using Artificial Hummingbird Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, the design and optimization of an FSS device are presented for dual-band operation in the frequency bands of LTE-2600 and 5G-FR1 cellular communication net-works. The proposed FSS device is designed by utilizing a recently introduced swarm-based meta-heuristic, namely the artificial hummingbird algorithm. The obtained numerical results of the proposed FSS device exhibit resonances at the frequency bands of interest, and quite acceptable values of gain and efficiency. Its overall performance makes it a suitable candidate for a receiving module of a rectenna in RF energy harvesting applications.

articleTitle: New Design of Wullenweber Antenna for Secondary Surveillance Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: New design of the Wullenweber antenna for the secondary surveillance radar is proposed and numerically analyzed. The unbalanced fed ultra low profile inverted L antenna is used as element antenna. Three element phased array antenna mounted on the side of sixty-faced polygonal cylinder with its radius of 1,400 mm is studied at the design frequencies from 1.03 GHz to 1.09 GHz.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation of Xenograft Tumor Tissues Imaged with Pulsed Terahertz Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Pulsed terahertz (THz) spectroscopy has achieved promising results in differentiating cancerous tissue from healthy adipose tissue. However, quantitatively evaluating THz spectroscopy of freshly excised tissue and its correlation to pathology presents a significant challenge. The processes involved in obtaining a pathology image cause significant deformation of the tissue. Therefore, pathology images are largely decoupled from their corresponding pulsed THz images of freshly excised tissue samples. Lacking highly correlated pathology analyzed images brings challenges in generating reliable training labels for supervised segmentation models and evaluation between segmentation and classification methods. This work proposes a novel THz image process pipeline and adopts an unsupervised image-to-image domain adaption method to generate synthetic THz scans directly from pathology images. With the generated synthetic THz scans, we train a robust segmentation neural network that effectively classifies tissue types among real-world THz scans at the pixel level.

articleTitle: Efficient Data Generation for Stroke Classification via Multilayer Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to overcome one of the main problems of machine learning when it faces the medical world: the need of a large amount of data. Through the distorted Born approximation, the scattering parameters and the dielectric contrast in the domain of interest are linked by a linearized integral operator. This method allows to generate a large data-set in a short time. In this work, machine learning is exploited to classify brain stroke presence, typology and position. The classifier model is based on the multilayer perceptron algorithm and it is used firstly for validation and then with a testing set composed by full-wave simulations. In both cases, the model reaches very high level of accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of 3D Conformal Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A general synthesis technique for 3D conformal metasurfaces is presented which utilizes integral equation-based modeling techniques and rapid optimization methods. The metasurfaces considered consist of conformal impedance sheets above conformal ground planes. The metasurfaces are modeled using integral equations and RWG basis functions which accu-rately account for all mutual coupling and finite dimensions. A conformal metasurface is designed in two phases: a Direct Solve phase involving the solution of the governing integral equation via the method of moments to obtain an initial design with complex-valued impedance sheets satisfying the desired far-field beam specifications, and a subsequent Optimization phase to convert the complex-valued sheets into purely reactive sheets. To accelerate this step, the metasurface is optimized using an adjoint optimization method. A metasurface with sinusoidal curvature is designed using this approach.

articleTitle: Modified Coupling Aperture to Optimize the Power Transfer in a Fabry-Pérot Open-Cavity Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The push for the usage of higher frequencies (> 30 GHz) towards 5G and 6G is posing new challenges on the antenna design. One of the challenges concerns the dielectric materials used to design the antenna on-chip or in-package. The values of the relative permittivity and loss tangent of these dielectric materials are not always known and need to be characterized. A popular system to characterize these dielectric materials is the Fabry-Pérot open-cavity resonator. The accuracy of the measurement with this material characterization system is determined by its Q-factor. One way to improve the Q-factor is to optimize the design of the coupling hole, i.e. iris, between waveguide and open-cavity. This will lead to a trade-off between the maximum amount of energy coupled into the cavity and the minimum amount of energy flowing back into the waveguide. This article proposes a change in the shape of the iris, which has lead to 2.5 times more power coupled into the open-cavity compared to other known modifications.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Stethoscope for Continuous Assessment of Lung Water: Towards AI-based Data Augmentation and Prediction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Pulmonary edema (excessive fluid in the lungs) is a common pathway for acute and chronic conditions such as heart failure, acute respiratory distress syndromes, and kidney failure. Early detection of pulmonary edema is key to prevent the patients from deteriorating into these critical conditions. Previously, we have developed a prototype non-invasive wireless cardio-pulmonary stethoscope (CPS) and demonstrated its capability of estimating the change of lung water content and associated vital signs (e.g., heart rates, respiratory rates) for a cohort of 26 patients in a clinical trial. We aim to enable the wireless CPS to estimate absolute lung water content and expand its usage to a diverse population of patients. A promising approach to achieve these goals is to build a personalized machine learning model to estimate the absolute lung water content based on the sensor measurements (i.e., S-parameters) from the CPS. However, the hurdle is the lack of a comprehensive database of the S-parameters of the lungs with excessive fluid in a variety of patients. In this paper, we outline a roadmap of using AI-based data augmentation to build such a database. As a critical initial step, we propose an automatic workflow to convert computerized tomography (CT) scan images to 3D lung objects in high-frequency simulation software (HFSS), in order to obtain S-parameters of the lungs at different water levels. The proposed workflow allows us to utilize a large NIH database and establish personalized lung water assessment models for a diverse population of patients. Simulation results validate our concept.

articleTitle: Spatially Dispersive Zero Thickness Sheet Model of All-Dielectric Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A general polynomial expansion of the tangential susceptibilities with respect to the transverse wave-vector, k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">||</inf> is presented to properly describe a spatially dispersive zero thickness model of an all-dielectric metasurface via an extended form of the generalized sheet transition conditions. Tangential susceptibilities of a typical cylindrical dielectric puck are extracted from commercial full-wave simulators and expanded into multi-Lorentz spatial resonances. Results are validated using integral equations solvers and show that ignoring spatial dispersion deprecates the metasurface field scattering response under oblique incidence.

articleTitle: Nulling Level Minimization via Array Antenna With Desired Gain and Sidelobe Level
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of minimizing the nulling level (NL) given the desired minimum power gain and the desired sidelobe level (SLL) via a wide-beam array antenna. Different from the traditional approaches which solve the shaped beam pattern synthesis (SBPS) problem, the paper tries to further suppress the NL by solving the power gain pattern synthesis (PGPS) problem. We firstly sets up the mathematical model of the discussed problem, and then its non-convex structure is transformed into convex one via approximation scheme. As a result, the formulated problem can be solved effectively with available solvers. Numerical examples are provided to validate the performance of the proposed algorithm by compared with the existing SBPS-based algorithm, which validate the the proposed algorithm is able to further suppress the NL more than 10 dB.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Antenna Array Based on Substrate Integrated Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarized 1×4 slot antenna array is proposed supporting a millimeter-wave application. The dual-polarized antenna is excited with two microstrip lines based on Substrate Integrated Gap Waveguide. The simulated return loss for both ports achieves a sufficient matching level over 10% bandwidth and beyond 12 dBi Gain for both polarizations. The simulated isolation is better than 30 dB.

articleTitle: Near-Field Enhancement of Microstrip Antenna Using Engineered Superstrate for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The design of an engineered superstrate to enhance the near-field of the microstrip antenna at 60 GHz is presented for biomedical applications. The proposed superstrate uses 49-unitcells consisting of two metallic layers printed on both sides of a dielectric layer with a material commonly used in 3D printing technology. The total structure is simulated using a full-wave electromagnetic simulator and the results are compared in the case of a rectangular patch antenna with and without using the engineered superstrate. The near-field analysis inside the model of human body skin shows that using the engineered superstrate leads to 4.25-dB enhancement of the near electric field, from 1613 V/m to 2639 V/m, without disturbing input matching.

articleTitle: An Optically Transparent Antenna for Digital TV Reception Using Nanoweb Sub-micron Wire Mesh
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present measurement results of an optically transparent bowtie dipole antenna for watching over-the-air digital TV channels. It operates over the UHF band for digital TV, 475-800 MHz. The transparent conductive elements of the antenna are made of a silver sub-micron mesh (Nanoweb), fabricated on a polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate, laminated together with optically clear adhesives and protection layers. The Nanoweb layer and the antenna stack have over 95% and 82% optical transparency, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is one of the largest transparent antennas ever made, demonstrating reception of local free view channels.

articleTitle: Radome Characterization at millimeter-wave using Real-time Inverse Scattering Estimation (RISE) Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new methodology that can extract the electrical and physical profile of an unknown radome in real-time is proposed and studied at 76.5 GHz. Denoted as Real-time Inverse Scattering Estimation (RISE), this method utilizes the inversion of scattering matrix using minimal parameters. The accuracy of this method is maximized through a decomposed and weighted selection of the TE/TM polarization. Experimental investigation confirms that we can extract the permittivity and thicknesses of random radomes within 0.4%, 1.4% deviation, respectively. This method can be further instrumental for application such as high precision, rapid non-destructive diagnosis for sensing, flaw detection, and extensive analysis.

articleTitle: Computationally Efficient Semi-Analytical Model for Single Feed High Gain Antenna Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A semi-analytical model for a high gain antenna structure is presented. The model utilizes the uniform theory of diffraction to predict the gain performance of the antenna structure. The proposed model gives a physical insight about the structure radiation mechanism. The radiation mechanism can be analyzed by the use of edge diffracted fields. The use of edge diffracted fields allows the employment of array theory to further understand the structure behavior.

articleTitle: Band-pass Hairpin Filter Using C-shaped DGS With Wide-band Rejection
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A band-pass hairpin filter is proposed that is combined with two C-shaped defected ground structures (DGSs) to provide a wide rejection band. The top layer of the structure consists of a hairpin filter of 5th order, and the bottom layer has DGSs that introduce low-pass filtering. The proposed hybrid circuit has 5 dB of insertion loss and 13 dB of return loss at its center frequency of 1.98 GHz.

articleTitle: Novel coaxial transition for shaped coaxial horn antennas operating at millimeter wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel optimized design and analysis of a coaxial coupling structure for standard and shaped horn antennas operating at millimeter wave frequencies. A novel dielectric support structure for the inner conductor and a transition to a 2.92 mm K connector are proposed. The horn’s performance was evaluated through full-wave electromagnetic finite element method analysis performed on Ansys EM. The dimensions of the dielectric structure and transition were optimized using a multi-objective Genetic Algorithm to enhance the horn’s performance. The final design presented a frequency bandwidth greater than 45% (25–40 GHz) with a return loss exceeding 20 dB.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band Slot Loop Antenna for Wi-Fi Application Based on Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-band antenna for Wi-Fi application is presented by using characteristic mode analysis (CMA). The proposed antenna consists of a slot-loop structure based on a wide bandwidth, high-efficiency electromagnetic radiation structure (WHEMS). To realize effective dual-band requirements for Wi-Fi antennas, the modal significance and modal current distribution are utilized to facilitate the analysis and improve antenna structures. Then, a coplanar waveguide (CPW) feed is used to optimize the antenna with optimal feed position. The simulated results show that the operating bandwidths reach 35% at 2.4 GHz and 24% at 5.8 GHz, and the maximum gains at the frequencies of 2.4 and 5.8 GHz are 4.62 and 5.21 dBi, respectively. The results confirm that this slot loop antenna based on characteristic mode analysis can be well applied in the Wi-Fi application with competitive performance.

articleTitle: Time Domain Solutions of Transmission Line Crosstalk
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper uses the Associate Hermite polynomial-finite-difference time-domain method (AH-FDTD) to analyze and calculate the transmission line (TL) crosstalk for the first time. The proposed method expands the transmission line equation using AH basis functions, uses Galekin's principle to eliminate the time variable, solves the implicit equation in the AH domain and performs inverse changes to obtain the solution of the equation. Compared with FDTD, this method separates the spatiotemporal variables, is not constrained by the Courant– Friedrich–Levy (CFL) condition, and has a higher calculation rate when there are many discrete segments of the transmission line. Simulation results show that the proposed method has much lower CPU time and better accuracy compared to FDTD and Alternating Direction Implicit (ADI) FDTD, which has obvious advantages.

articleTitle: AI-Driven RIS Footprint Contouring - Towards B5G and 6G Smart Environment Control
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The possibility to afford multi-beam contoured footprint patterns with simple reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) is addressed within the Smart ElectroMagnetic Environment (SEME) framework. Towards this end, an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven design process is formulated within the System-by-Design framework. A preliminary numerical validation is shown to remark the effectiveness of the proposed strategy when dealing with advanced multi-beam contouring problems.

articleTitle: A Flush Mount Automobile 4-Channel Universal Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a flush mount compact vehicle antenna system that supports 4-channel MIMO operation of LTE, 5G sub6, WLAN, and C-V2X communications. Compared to its previous design [1], additional design features were added to cover 5G sub6 band (617-698 MHz). The new design is also recessed into a metallic cavity for supporting flush mount configuration below the roof of the vehicle. Each individual channel produces a directive pattern and the combination of all 4 channels produces a relatively uniform azimuthal pattern in the selection combining MIMO mode. The measurement results of a fabricated prototype are also presented.

articleTitle: Passive and Lossless Conformal Huygens’ Metasurfaces for Arbitrary Wave Transformation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We discuss a general framework for designing irregularly shaped passive and lossless conformal Huygens’ metasurfaces (HMS), derived from the theory of transformation optics. Through a conformal coordinate transformation, the physical space in which the HMS resides is mapped to a computational space, in which the surface geometry is significantly simpler. The mapping preserves the boundary conditions governing the field transformations, meaning any previously developed design methods for flat HMSs remain valid. Importantly, it also facilitates the identification of completely passive and lossless surface designs, which are usually sought-after for their ease of implementation.

articleTitle: Split-Ring Resonator Sensor for Detecting Water Content in Biological Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new method is proposed to determine the relative water moisture content in biological materials, based on a split-ring resonator (SRR) design. A microwave SRR utilizes capacitive coupling to create a focal point at which a resonance frequency is susceptible to modulation in the presence of a dielectric material. The SRR can transmit signals through a biological system, such as a juvenile tree stem. Then, the transmission data obtained can be used to calculate the relative permittivity of the tree by analyzing a resonance shift in the SRR sensor. This method is non-invasive and reduces measurement time compared to conventional methods. Relative water moisture content is standard practice to determine the amount of available water within a tree relative to its maximum hydration capacity. The results herein show that this sensor design can successfully track water content non-invasively via dielectric material characterization and can prove to be very useful in biological applications such as dehydration prevention.

articleTitle: A low-cost wide-angle multi-beam coverage Bruce rectennas for energy harvesting applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a low-profile, efficient and wide-angle rectenna array for energy harvesting and wireless power transmission in the 5G mid-band. Specifically, the device consists of a set of onboard Bruce-array antennas operating at the same frequency (5.8 GHz) but with different radiation angles, so as to achieve the radiative energy harvesting in the spatial multiplexing form. The Bruce-array antennas can efficiently receive RF signals with incident angles ranging from -60° to 60°, with a peak gain larger than 7.89 dBi. A suitable power management system is also proposed for this arrayed rectenna system. The rectenna panel can exhibit a conversion efficiency of 60 % at input power of -2.2 dBm over a wide range of reception.

articleTitle: Compact Stacked-Patch Antenna for Directional Modulation in Azimuth and Elevation Planes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work proposes a compact stacked-patch antenna capable of beamsteering in the vertical and horizontal directions. These characteristics are studied to realize directional modulation (DM) schemes in the vertical and horizontal planes, using a structure of 0.56λ diameter. The design offers a unidirectional beamsteering across the entire xy-plane, with a scanning range of 118° and 112° in the xz and yz-planes, respectively. A peak realized gain of 6.75 dBi is achieved, with an isolation better than 15 dB at the center frequency of 2.4 GHz. The directional modulation performance shows a beamwidth with Bit Error Rate (BER) < 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> of 33° in the horizontal plane, and 50° for the elevation planes. This performance is proposed to improve the secrecy and privacy of data transmission in the growing field of small Internet of Things (IoT) technology.

articleTitle: An error control high order Galerking method for integral equations in electromagnetism
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The method of boundary integral equation is commonly used in computational electromagnetics (CEM). Both Galerkin and Nyström are two possible schemes to discretize the resulting boundary integral equation. In both cases one can use low order basis functions or high order basis functions. In this paper we show a simple way of estimating the error given the solution obtained. The error is estimated by using a spectral analysis of the induced sources on the surface. This method can be used in case of highly adaptive discretization of the geometry.

articleTitle: Analytic Logarithm Integrals with Near-Machine Precision for Linear Source Cells
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Two-dimensional, electrostatic integral equation integrands are often the product of a logarithmic kernel and a polynomial basis. Analytic expressions for these integrals with monomial bases are derived for linear source cells. Results for the analytic integrations are compared against numerical quadrature results using an arbitrary-precision math library. Near near-machine precision accuracy is observed.

articleTitle: Near-Field to Far-Field RCS Prediction for Large-Scale Scatterers Based on Multi-Level Spherical Wave Expansion
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: For weapon systems, most RCS measurements are captured in the near-field area in anechoic chamber, considering the security requirements for the research process and high spatial costs. So, It is necessary to convert the scattered wave measured in the near-field region to the RCS value in the far-field region. Therefore, this paper proposes a near-field to far-field transformation algorithm based on multi-level spherical wave expansion for application in near-field RCS measurement systems. It was verified that faster and more accurate RCS prediction is possible by supplementing this via a multi-level technique.

articleTitle: A Blended Quadrature Approach for the Accurate Integration of the Gradient of the 3D Green’s Function
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a partially closed form and partially numerical method for the accurate integration of the singular integral related to the gradient of the 3D Green’s function. Verification examples are provided and compared with a brute-force integration using an arbitrary precision library.

articleTitle: Dual-band Decoupling Network for MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method to design a decoupling network (DN) to increase isolation between dual-band antennas. The DN design is based on the scattering matrix and optimized by the Genetic Algorithm (GA). The decoupling example shows that the DN offers impedance matching and high isolation within desired bands, verifying the concept.

articleTitle: A Contactless Feeding Network Design Using MetaCoax Coupler
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel contactless capacitively coupled PCB-to-PCB coupler is proposed in this paper. The coupler is used to couple a 2×2 element circularly polarized antenna array PCB to its feeding layer PCB and connectors. The simulated results of the antenna array alone and the antenna array with the couplers matches well, indicating the good performance of the contactless feeding network. The antenna array with the couplers has 18% bandwidth and a maximum gain of 11.15 dBi, which is only 4% and 0.13 dBi smaller than that of the directly excited antenna array.

articleTitle: Polarization Insensitive Phase Change Material-Based Nanoantenna Array for Thermally Tunable Infrared Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Thermal radiation management is an emerging application of metamaterials owing to their exotic electromagnetic radiative properties. Herein, a thermally tunable phase change material-based nanoantenna array is reported to manipulate electromagnetic waves for potential applications in radiative cooling and multispectral camouflage from thermal infrared detectors. The simulation results show that the proposed nanoantenna array possesses high reflectance exceeding at least 60% within the 3−5 µm and 8−12 µm wavelength ranges, indicating low thermal emissivity, while the reflectance value increases as the temperature rises. Additionally, the wavelength-selective nanoantenna emitter operates with high absorption and therefore emission within the non-atmospheric window (5−8 µm). The thermally tuning feature leads to further controlling the absorption and, therefore, the emission performance of the nanoantenna and corresponding infrared signatures detected by thermal cameras.

articleTitle: Biodegradable deployment apparatus for environmentally-friendly RFID-based sensors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Previous work on sensors has delved into the possibility of using passive RFID as environmental sensors. This work examined the possibility of a biodegradable antenna deployment system for this type of sensor. The deployment system was constructed of biodegradable materials so that the sensors would create minimal environmental impact while also eliminating the need for collecting used sensors.

articleTitle: Near-Field Conical-Helical Probe for Receiving Sensitive EM Backscattering Side-Channel Signals
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel near-field probe design that improves the sensitivity of backscattered electromagnetic side-channel signals. We present the design, simulation, and fabrication of our probe, as well as measurements illustrating its sensitivity for non-destructive hardware Trojan detection. We show a 25 dB improvement in received power and a 3 dB improvement in directivity over previous work.

articleTitle: A Multimode Ultra-Wideband Filter Based on Coplanar Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces and studies the design of a multimode ultra-wideband filter based on a coplanar waveguide (CPW) transmission line. The filter is composed of a multimode resonator consisting of two high and low impedance lines. Through the coupling between the input and output ports of the CPW transmission line and the multimode resonator, an ultra-wideband dual-mode filter is obtained. There are 2 transmission poles in the filter and it has a center frequency of 6.8 GHz, a bandwidth coverage of 3.1−10.5 GHz, and a relative bandwidth of 110%. The designed filter has the advantages of simple structure, compact size, easy integration, and good performance in CPW circuits.

articleTitle: A Novel Fluid-Based Pattern-Reconfigurable, Textile Antenna Array for Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The pattern reconfigurability of a textile antenna is investigated based on the fluidic selection for a 4-channel platform used as parasitic and phase shifters. A textile loop antenna is designed where the 4-channel platform is placed on top of the antenna to be used as a flat lens and a beam steering engine. Two fluidics namely distilled and sea waters were selected as actuators. Each channel was activated by one fluidic at a time and the radiation was evaluated. The loop antenna is designed considering conductive textile automatically embroidered onto denim fabric. The channel platform consists of 4 compartments made of polymer. The simulation suggests that, at 1 GHz, using distilled and sea waters, the elevation angle of the antenna is steered from -145<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup> to 139<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">◦</sup> and the amplitude of the realized gain varied from 1 to 15 dB. To the author’s knowledge, this is the first time a clothing-integrated, fluidically reconfigurable antenna is studied and reported. This result can be used as a design guideline for textile-based beam-steering antenna used for wearable applications.

articleTitle: Design of A Size-Reduced, Tunable Yagi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A Yagi antenna with frequency tunability using variable capacitance elements is investigated. This antenna is size reduced with the use of top loading to decrease the height of the driver and the two directors. Folding is used to decrease the spacing between the elements of the Yagi antenna. Then, varactors are added onto the bottom of each director to electrically tune the resonant frequencies of the two directors. The total frequency tunable bandwidth is increased by combining the tunable bands of each director. The total frequency tunable bandwidth of 19.8% is achieved.

articleTitle: A Possible Realization of Plasmonic Cloaking Using non-Magnetized Plasma Discharge Tubes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We propose a possible realization of the plasmonic cloaking technique for dielectric cylinders using non-magnetized plasma tubes. First, we analytically show how a homogeneous plasmonic layer can provide cloaking for dielectric cylinders. Then, we present a non-homogeneous, but practical representation to achieve effective and, more interestingly, tunable cloaking.

articleTitle: A Beam-Splitting Metasurface Designed by Optimization & Machine-Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Ideally, metasurface designers want to create a metasurface that satisfies given application-specific criteria, which can take the form of far-field criteria such as beamwidth, side lobe level, manufacturing constraints, etc. Designing the metasurface from this set of broad criteria is very challenging without the complete knowledge of the tangential fields. Moreover, determining the required unit cells to realize the required scattering often requires numerous iterative simulations. Here, the inverse design of a metasurface that splits the input wave from a horn antenna into two asymmetric beams is tackled using a combined end-to-end approach involving optimization and machine-learning. Experimental results of a prototype of the optimized metasurface are presented that corroborate the effectiveness of the inverse design approach.

articleTitle: Pixelated AMC Design Using Digital Microfluidics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 4.5 GHz pixelized artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) ground plane is dynamically reconfigured using digital microfluidics. The AMC ground plane comprises pixelized unit cells interconnected by liquid metal switches. Depending on the applied bias, these interconnects can be switched on or off, resulting in a change in unit cell geometry and consequently, operating frequency. Simulation results show that the AMC operating frequency can be switched among 2.24 GHz, 4.5 GHz, 4.6 GHz, and 5GHz.

articleTitle: On the H2 Representation of EFIE MoM
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An efficient way to construct a data-sparse ${\mathcal{H}^2}{\text{ - matrix}}$ representation of the Electric Field Integral Equation (EFIE) is proposed. The method is based on the physical properties of the EFIE, yet is fully algebraic. These insights are leveraged to construct a nested basis which can be used to compress admissible, i.e. non-near interactions of the EFIE Matrix in a multi-level fashion. The resulting ${\mathcal{H}^2}{\text{ - matrix}}$ is found through computational experiments to be error controllable with nearly $\mathcal{O}(N\log N)$ and $\mathcal{O}\left( {{N^{1.5}}\log N} \right)$ complexity in memory and setup time respectively for problems up to 32 wavelengths in all three dimensions. Moreover the matrix vector multiplication time is very fast and scales as nearly $\mathcal{O}(N\log N)$.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of bioinspired helical nano-antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work proposes helical antenna models inspired by biological structures. Single turn bifilar helical antenna is modeled from diameter and pitch of A-DNA and Z-DNA, while 310-helix and π-helix (protein structures) are used to model single turn monofilar helical antenna. The far-field of all the four structures are analyzed in Ansys High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). Radiation patterns, gains, and circular polarization are compared when simulated at six different wavelengths. The effect of conformational change (right-handed to left-handed) in monofilar helical antenna is also analyzed.

articleTitle: A Non-diffractive Radiating System for Safer Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Treatments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a radiative system for Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (TMS) able to accomplish a focused treatment with a lower electromagnetic field exposure inside the brain tissue is introduced. The proposed radiating system comprises five actively fed and properly loaded RF coils able to shape the magnetic field distribution into a non-diffractive Bessel beam. In this work, we evaluate the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR, W/kg) within the investigated biological phantom, comparing the proposed radiating system against a traditional single-coil arrangement, achieving the same magnetic field amplitude within biological tissues. The numerical results obtained through accurate full-wave simulations show a significant SAR reduction with the focused radiating configuration. In addition, the exposed phantom region is more confined, strongly reducing the overall potential side effects on human health. Therefore, the preliminary results encourage future works, suggesting the possibility to reduce the invasiveness on the patient and improving clinical effectiveness of TMS treatments.

articleTitle: Deep Learning with Attention Mechanism for Electromagnetic Inverse Scattering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new deep learning technique is investigated to improve the solution of electromagnetic inverse scattering problems (ISPs). The basic idea of this technique is to introduce the attention mechanism to U-Net. By doing this, the deep learning model can automatically learn to focus on target areas of the measured scattered field matrix. In this way, the proposed technique can offer higher accuracy and faster convergence compared with the traditional deep learning networks. Numerical results validate the efficacy of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Single-Antenna Blade Modulation Based 3D Direction Finding
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A top-hat antenna is developed for direction finding (DF) applications using blade rotation modulations, which is capable to achieve direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimations in both elevation and azimuth directions. Unlike conventional DF arrays using multiple antenna elements, a single antenna is required in the proposed DF system. Antenna performance might be influenced with the presence of rotating metallic blades. However, with the consideration of blade rotations in designing the single DF antenna, the antenna radiation pattern diversity is realized through blade modulations and the DOA estimations could be achieved. The incoming plane wave with different azimuth and elevation incident angles and linear polarization states is investigated. The 3D DF capability of the proposed single top-hat antenna with four rotating blades is demonstrated based on Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) calculations using the 3D complex antenna radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Framework for Evaluating Channel Estimators in Millimeter-Wave New-Radio Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A framework for evaluating the performance of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing channel estimators is developed. This framework builds upon previously published work to provide testing of millimeter-wave phased array architectures with realistic phased array hardware components and associated errors. The framework generates performance metrics to help optimize estimators for various array architectures and propagation channels without the need for time- and cost-intensive measurement campaigns. The verification process of the developed software is discussed to ensure correct operation through both analytical and empirical methods. Finally an example evaluation of a least-squares channel estimator is presented.

articleTitle: Penrose Super-Radiance in a Synthetically Rotating Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Super-radiant amplification of scattering in a rotating medium was predicted by Sir Penrose as an exotic astrophysics phenomenon. Here we demonstrate its electromagnetic analogue using spatio-temporally modulated metasurfaces that experience a form of synthetic rotation. We consider excitations with signals carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM), highly beneficial for multiplexed wireless networks that demand high data rate capacity. The metasurface efficiently couples and can amplify selected OAM orders based on a phenomenon analogous to Penrose super-radiance. We build, analyze, and simulate a single circuit element, modulated in time through varactors, that efficiently manipulates three OAM orders and selectively amplifies them. We then show the possibility of observing angular Doppler shift and amplifying selected OAM signals using an array of these elements forming a metasurface.

articleTitle: Analysis of Ground Plane’s Shape of Microstrip Monopole Antenna using Theory of Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The Theory of Characteristic Modes (TCM) is applied to analyze a finite-sized ground plane shape of a circular monopole antenna, providing physical insight into the effect produced by the ground plane. A circular monopole has been designed on FR-4 substrate on the rectangular and circular ground plane. The information yielded by the modal analysis reveals the close influence of the ground plane shape on the impedance behavior of the antenna. Information provided by TCM can help optimize the ground plane’s size and geometry by exciting the desired modes and suppressing the unwanted modes.

articleTitle: Broadband Single-layer Reflective Metasurface for Generating OAM Vortex Wave
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a reflective metasurface which is designed to generate orbital angular momentum (OAM) with a wider band and a smaller size. The metal pattern of unit cell adopts the winding-shape design to reduce the size, and the multi-resonant structure to increase the phase shift range and expand the bandwidth. By varying the length of the metal pattern of the unit, linear phase curves can be obtained in the working frequency range while maintaining high reflective coefficients. Based on this unit, scattering characteristics of the metasurface prototype using a horn antenna as a feed source is simulated. The measured results of the prototype demonstrate that the OAM vortex wave can be generated effectively at 7-12GHz, which prove the correctness and practicality of the proposed metasurface.

articleTitle: 3D-printed gear system for antenna motion in an MR environment: initial phantom imaging experiments
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We have developed a microwave imaging device for breast cancer imaging that can be used concurrently inside an MR imaging system. The microwave measurement system is comprised of a horizontal array of 16 monopole antennas that can be moved vertically for full 3D coverage of the breast.
