All compatibility issues have been addressed. The motion is achieved using a novel 3D printed gearing device. Initial results demonstrate that the system is capable of accurately recovering the size, shape, location and properties of a 3D shape varying object. This is a critical step towards clinical microwave breast imaging in the MR.

articleTitle: A Contrast-Source Inversion Approach Base on Projected Landweber-Kaczmarz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An updated contrast-source inversion (CSI) scheme is proposed in this work. The scheme minimizes the misfits of the contrast-source (CS) equations using the Landweber-Kaczmarz (LWKZ) algorithm. The step lengths were updated using the maximum eigenvalues of the Fréchet derivative matrices associated with the cost terms through each iteration. At the end of the iterative loop, a first-norm projection operator is imposed to satisfy the sparsity constraint. Numerical results illustrate the efficiency of the proposed approach both in image quality and reconstruction time.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of UWB Cavity-backed Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an improved version of cavity-backed UWB monopole antenna has been presented. An antenna showed a significant improvement in gain and bandwidth when corners of the conventional rectangular/square ground plane were rounded, and a circular cavity behind the monopole replaced the square cavity. Simulations were performed to verify the effectiveness of circular cavity and circular ground plane in antenna performance. The results indicate that the proposed antenna features an impedance bandwidth of 115% for 12.6 dB broadside peak gain. Hence, the updated version improved the impedance bandwidth by 25% and the peak gain by 2.6 dB.

articleTitle: Graphene-Based Terahertz Holographic Conformal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a conformal graphene holographic antenna designed for terahertz (THz) band is proposed. The radiation principle of the proposed pattern reconfigurable antenna is based on the holographic technology. The surface reactance modulation and pattern steering capability can be easily facilitated by a tunable DC-biased graphene patch array. Thanks to the super thin structure and excellent mechanical property of graphene, the proposed THz graphene holographic antenna can be designed conformal to required platforms easily. Besides, the equal size as well as same spacing of graphene patches make it easy to modeling and manufacture. To verify the proposed idea, an antenna conformal to a cylinder is designed and simulated. The results of full wave simulation software HFSS shown that the conformal antenna has great performance.

articleTitle: 5.2-6.2 GHz Dual-pol Hat-fed Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A dual linear polarization feed for a compact self-supported center-fed reflector antenna for the C-band frequency range of 5.2–6.2 GHz is presented. The main goal of the feed is to maximize the antenna efficiency and to minimize the sidelobe levels and cross couplings that are usually associated with a small F/D ratio of a reflector. The primary and secondary radiation patterns of the designed feed are presented, as well as antenna gain (efficiency) and scattering parameters of the reflector antenna.

articleTitle: Study on Thinned Array Leaky-Wave Antenna for Potential Use of Fixed-Frequency Beam Switching
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, thinned slotted array leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) based on rectangular waveguide are designed for potential use of fixed-frequency beam switching. The main beam angle can be controlled by changing slots spacing in periodic structure using genetic algorithm (GA). Using this proposed synthesis method, two 20-element thinned array antennas are designed, whose beam direction are pointing to -30° and 20° at 6 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: An Active Metasurface Cloak to Control the Scattering of a Conductive 3D Cylindrical Target
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work details the initial design of an active scattering cancellation cloak designed to hide a 3D target. Such a development is important, from a practical sense, as this method of electromagnetic cloaking has only been validated on either 2D or quasi-2D objects. The presented device is composed of an array of whip dipoles enveloping a 3D, conductive, cylindrical target. By configuring the input weights of these antennas, the array can radiate a field capable of cancelling any scattering which would arise when the target is illuminated by impinging electromagnetic waves. Initial performance evaluation is conducted in which the cloak is used to reduce the scattering of the target/cloak assembly when illuminated by a ridged horn antenna at 1.2 GHz. Overall, cloaking is found to be successfully achieved almost over the entire scan range with the greatest scattering suppression occurring within the shadow region formed behind the target.

articleTitle: Plug-and-Play Dual Polarized Phase Reconfigurable Waveguide Network for 5G Millimeter Wave Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a plug-and-play waveguide-based feeding network is presented to achieve steerable radiation by reconfiguring the phase shift between the corresponding output ports. The proposed structure is tailored to serve 5G millimeter wave systems with steerable radiation pattern capabilities. More specifically, a groove gap waveguide based feeding network is designed to split the circularly polarized signal at the input into four output signals with dual linearly polarized characteristics. Such splitting is accompanied with phase reconfiguration capabilities by reconfiguring the grooves’ distributions within the feeding network through a plug-and-play mechanism. Such mechanism maintains equal splitting with a wide phase range that extend beyond 230<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> for the span of frequencies between 28 GHz and 32 GHz. Such phase reconfiguration is distributed over 23 different plug-and-play configurations while ensuring stable phase response and high isolation factor between the various ports across the entire operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: An Improved Technique for the Incident-Wave Excitation in DGTD for Wideband Electromagnetic Scattering of Lossy Dielectric–Metallic Targets
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this communication, an improved technique for the incident-wave excitation of discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method is developed to analyze the wideband electromagnetic (EM) scattering problems of lossy dielectric-metallic targets. Compared with conventional total-and scattered-field decomposition (TSFD) technique which is widely used in the DGTD, TFTD and FDTD, the improved technique can effectively reduce the number of degrees of freedom (DoFs) and simplify the EM scattering modeling. Two examples about the EM scattering of lossy dielectric–metallic targets are used to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the improved technique for the incident-wave excitation.

articleTitle: Wide-angle Beam-steering with Electronically-scanned Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We discuss the design of a reconfigurable leaky wave antenna capable of one-dimensional wide-angle beam-steering. It has a simple architecture consisting of a microstrip line loaded with individually addressed varactors. The biasing scheme of the varactors is determined from a numerical optimization procedure inspired by the design of electromagnetic metasurfaces. The proposed design method can identify loading configurations that produce the optimal radiation pattern while accounting for non-ideal effects such as amplitude tapering or end reflections. It can also identify designs with optimal impedance matching, which helps to extend the effective scan-range of the antenna.

articleTitle: Figure of Merit for Objective Assessment of mmWave 5G Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Recently, considerable research efforts have been concentrated on the design of mmWave 5G phased array designs for base stations and small cells. However, it is difficult to compare the performance of different mmWave 5G phased array designs, as there are many design trade-offs, such as operational bandwidth, the number of elements, beam scanning range, realized antenna gain, polarization properties, and overall dimensions. Currently, there is no standard or figure of merit (FoM) for an objective assessment of the array performance. In this paper, we derive a FoM, which includes all the above factors to create a fair comparison of different mmWave 5G phased array designs. The proposed FoM is then applied to various mmWave 5G phased array designs from the literature to compare their performances.

articleTitle: A Fast and Precise Parallel Numerical Model Using PML for Maxwell’s Equations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we have designed a numerical model to solve a three-dimensional (3D) time-harmonic Maxwell’s equations appearing in biomedical applications when a perfectly matched layer (PML) is used to truncate the unbounded domain. Besides, we are using PML as transmission conditions at the interfaces between subdomains in a domain decomposition method. These two implementations of PML will result on one side in the improvement in the accuracy of the solution compared to the absorbing boundary conditions and on the other side will contribute to the acceleration of the computations.

articleTitle: Limit of an aperture-fixed MIMO system considering the Chu limit of antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: It has been proved that an aperture-fixed multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) system has a degree of freedom (DOF) limit, which is also referred as the limit of spatial electromagnetic (EM) modes or scattering channels. Typically, using more antennas can excite more spatial EM modes for enhancing channel capacity, while keep increasing the number of antennas would be useless when the available EM modes are fully occupied. Nevertheless, when the number of antennas is increasing, the accompanying decrease of antenna’s physical size will lead to a reduction of its maximum bandwidth (Chu limit). Therefore, there would be a trade-off between the DOF and bandwidth. Based on a physical channel model, we demonstrate the DOF and capacity limits with/without incorporating antenna’s bandwidth limit, which provides a fundamental bound on the performance of an aperture-fixed MIMO system.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Slot MIMO Antenna with Pattern Diversity for CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents a highly miniaturized folded slot-based multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna design for Cube Satellites (CubeSats) applications at UHF band with pattern diversity. A novel combination of meandered slot with folded structure and reactively slot loading with a discrete capacitor is used to achieve miniaturization. The antenna can operate over a wide-band from 430 to 510 MHz with pattern diversity over the entire band of operation. The overall board dimensions of the proposed antenna design used are 100×100 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed antenna design is highly suitable for small satellite applications, especially CubeSats.

articleTitle: Ring-loaded coaxial groove horn antenna for 12/14/20/30 GHz bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In order to achieve rotationally symmetric beam, low cross-polarization component, and small size in a wide frequency band, a new quad-band horn is proposed in this paper by using a coaxial groove structure loading a ring structure. As a design example, a compact horn antenna with a cross-polarization level of less than -30 dB in a specific quad-band, Ku/Ka-band, is presented.

articleTitle: A Novel Clothing-Based Nest-Inspired Resonator for Wireless Power Transfer and Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new topology for textile-based wireless power transfer and harvesting system is presented. it consists of a nest-inspired resonator that concentrates the electric and magnetic fields in the center and within the periphery of the nest, respectively for robust electromagnetic field presence to tackle the misalignment problem. The resonator was designed and simulated to operate at 433 MHz. This design enabled high power transfer efficiency (PTE) when the resonator was under the influence of lateral misalignment along the direction of the RF current. The results suggest a PTE of up to 82.5% within 10 cm of displacement. This is 10% improvement over the PTE of a single loop operating at the same frequency. The diagonal misalignment showed a PTE of up to 77.5% within 10 cm of misalignment. This is up to 20% of improvement over that of the single loop. A textile-based power harvesting circuit operating at 433 MHz with an RF-to-DC conversion efficiency of 82% at 500 mW is proposed to be integrated with the resonator. A combination of the resonator and power harvesting circuit will be implemented on an ad-hoc on-body charging solution.

articleTitle: A 220 GHz Electronically-Scanning High-Gian Reflector Antenna with a Small-Scale Array Feeder
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A 220 GHz electronically-scanning high-gain reflector antenna with a small-scale array feeder is presented in this paper. Multi-variables of the array feeder including the element spacing, defocused distance, and spatial tilting angle as well as the exciting amplitude and phase are optimized to achieve a multi-objective optimization including the beam coverage and scanning loss. Then, three independently 1×4 linear arrays are designed based on a 50-um quartz substrate to verify the scanning performance at 220 GHz. Simulation results present a good scanning performance with a –5.5° ~ 6.5° beam coverage, 40 dBi maximum gain, and 2.6 dB scanning loss, showing good prospects in applications of terahertz detection, inter-satellite communication, and next-generation wireless communications.

articleTitle: Hybrid Frequency Selective Rasorber Combining 2-D and 3-D Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized rasorber with an absorption-transmission-absorption frequency response is proposed. The rasorber has a broad absorption band and a middle pass band with low insertion loss. A three-dimensional (3-D) bandpass structure acts as a reflecting ground for the upper lossy layer and provides a high-transmission window. The resistor-loaded metallic meandered line on the top layer is applied to achieve a wide absorption band. The fractional bandwidth of reflection below –10 dB is 120% from 4.2 to 16.8 GHz. The 1 dB transmission window can be obtained from 9.8 to 12.2 GHz with a 22% fractional bandwidth, and the lowest insertion loss is 0.1 dB.

articleTitle: Wideband Compact Planar Metallic Lens and Antenna for Radiation of High-Power Microwaves
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A compact, dual-band high-power antenna system, operating in L and S bands is presented. The design consists of a dual-band corrugated horn antenna whose gain is improved by the use of two circular metallic lenses. Numeric simulations of the radiation pattern for the single and stacked lens are presented. The resulting system is smaller and lighter than a single horn with equivalent directivity.

articleTitle: Receiving Antenna Realized Gain Understood by the Poynting Streamline Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Antenna realized gain is generally defined and used to analyze transmitting antennas, but rarely for receiving antennas. In this paper, we use a direct way to model and understand the receiving antennas. The flow of electromagnetic energy around a receiving antenna is modeled by generating streamlines of the Poynting vectors. The realized gain can be described by a two-dimensional geometry, where the streamlines within this region are absorbed by the antenna load. Compared to the traditional equivalent circuit, this image provides a closer physical way to explain and understand the realized gain for the receiving antennas.

articleTitle: Path Loss Characterization for a Pulse-based Wireless Power Transfer System Using Ultrawideband (UWB) Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a path loss characterization of a wireless power transfer (WPT) network for deployment in unmanned aerial system (UAS) applications. The intended WPT system consists of two novel 4 × 4 phased array antennas of the same design integrated with a combiner/splitter network placed 1m distance apart. The path loss of the proposed system is characterized based on both simulation and measurement results which are presented in the paper. The antennas operate at ultrawideband (UWB) frequency ranges of 5.65−6.6GHz and 7.2−7.8GHz. The overall system achieves 22.7dB path loss with a maximum of 7.33% power transfer efficiency for 1m distance.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband 3D Tapered Aperture Antenna -3D Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A design concept for an ultra-wideband 3D tapered aperture antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna is designed for ultra-wideband applications close to 20:1 bandwidth. It has a relatively high gain values (vary from 3dBi to 13dBi) over the same bandwidth. The cross polarization is more than 60dB below the co-polarization along the aperture. The design features two exponential lines and spins it 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> in opposite direction to create 3D tapered aperture. The simulated results regrading return loss, gain, and far field are presented. Ongoing study is focused towards optimizing the aperture to increase the gain value at lower frequency band while maintaining the gain value at mid and high frequency band.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of a Metal-Only Reflectarray Based on the Phoenix Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a detailed analysis of the effect of the height of the 3D Phoenix Cell on the performance of Metal-Only Reflectarray Antennas. An improved design approach is proposed and a 18% bandwidth (for gain variations less than 1 dB) is obtained after the optimization.

articleTitle: A Novel Class of Dielectric Resonator Antenna Phased Arrays with Enhanced Beam-Scanning Capabilities for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The design and manufacturing of a novel class of dielectric resonator antenna phased arrays operating at K-band is discussed in this study. The proposed array features enhanced beam-scanning capabilities in terms of scan loss as compared to alternative solutions based on printed antenna technology. The design is also optimized for cost effectiveness in combination with an easy and reliable mechanical assembly process, while enabling improved thermal management. A 64-element array model configured for operation in the 24-GHz ISM band is used here to illustrate the developed design strategy and the relevant benefits in terms of beam-scanning capability.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Bio-inspired Planar UWB Antenna for Cognitive Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work presents the design of a compact ultra-wideband bio-inspired planar antenna, with a bandwidth starting at 0.76 GHz up to 11 GHz, applicable for cognitive radio technology. The structure was developed in a FR4 substrate of 1.6 mm height and occupying an area of 140 × 133 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The gain of the proposed antenna is between (2-8.2) dBi and presents 97.2% of maximum radiation efficiency at 1 GHz. The development of the flower-shaped bio-inspired antenna using the Gielis formula is presented.

articleTitle: Pattern Control for Reflector Antennas Using Electronically-Reconfigurable Rim Scattering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In prior work, we demonstrated sidelobe nulling for a reflector antenna system by electronic modification of the phase of scattering from elements located near the rim of the reflector. Applications for such a system include radio astronomy, where deleterious levels of interference from satellites enter through sidelobes. However the prior work was limited to placing single nulls with no constraint on main lobe characteristics, leading to gain which varies as a function of null direction. In this work, we consider simulated annealing as a means of placing nulls simultaneously with enforcement of a gain constraint. Using this method, deep nulls are possible even when element control is limited to discrete binary (i.e., 1-bit) phase-only control.

articleTitle: Analytical Design of In-phase/Quadrature Two Paths Space-Time-Modulated Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an analytical design of space-time-modulated metasurfaces with modulation elements composed of two paths, In-phase (I) and Quadrature (Q), is proposed. The analytical model realizes the space/frequency domain manipulations of first order harmonics by designing the dimension and time sequence of I and Q paths. In the specular reflection direction, an objective frequency shift of the reflected first order harmonic can be obtained. While, in other directions, the opposite first order harmonic can be easily controlled by changing the dimension of I/Q paths and the objective first order harmonic remains unchanged. Furthermore, with a small dimension of I/Q paths, the first order harmonic can be used for beam scanning by pre-designing the start time of the modulation element.

articleTitle: Wideband Miniaturized Planar Patch TX/RX Antenna Arrays For Microwave FMCW Doppler Radars
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Wideband miniaturized patch linear transmit and planar receive (TX/RX) antenna arrays are presented for microwave FMCW radar applications. RT/duroid 5880LZ laminate is used as the substrate to miniaturize the antenna elements and to provide the required FMCW short range radar system bandwidth. The resonance frequency and bandwidth are set to be 5.8 GHz and 400 MHz. The TX antenna is a 1x4 linear array while the RX antenna is a 2x4 planar array to improve the gain and SNR performance of the radar receiver. TX/RX arrays show pure radiation patterns with proper alignment and the gain of ~12.9/15.2 dB and 15.5/17.5 dB of front-to-back ratio, respectively while achieving a ~70 dB of TX-to-RX isolation.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Model for Varactor-Loaded Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) have gained a lot of attention due to its ability to perform low-cost beam steering for applications in emerging smart radio environments. An equivalent circuit model for a varactor-loaded microstrip RIS element, covering a wide tuning range and providing accurate physics-based circuit model for both reflection phases and magnitudes for a normal incidence is developed and presented. The circuit model facilitates system level study of RIS-based wireless communication networks with realistic analytical RIS responses as parameter inputs.

articleTitle: Low Profile Orthogonal Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna Using Halo Antenna with Short Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-profile orthogonally polarized antenna. The proposed antenna is composed of a sleeve antenna as a vertically polarized element and a Halo antenna with parasitic elements as a horizontally polarized element. The short element is loaded on the Halo antenna and the two parasitic elements, so that both polarizations have an omnidirectional radiation pattern in the horizontal plane. As a result of the simulation, it is found that the relative bandwidth is 5.2%, and the antenna diameter and height are 0.14λ0 and 0.47λ0, respectively.

articleTitle: A Generalized Approach to Real-Time Performance Estimation of Antenna Types Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Machine learning methods, such as deep learning, hold great potential in the study of electromagnetic (EM) structures as they excel at complex multi-dimensional modeling. In this work, we introduce a generalized method to predict antenna performance using deep neural networks. Specifically, we estimate the far-field radiation and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> of an antenna (e.g., rectangular patch antenna) in real-time by utilizing the near-field data using an artificial neural network (ANN). Our method is generalized as it can learn from a range of design parameters for various substrate materials and operating frequencies, and it can accurately predict all the required EM properties (e.g., near- and far-fields, S-parameters) of the desired antenna. When compared to numerical methods, we achieved acceptable antenna performance estimation, e.g., a mean absolute percentage error of 0.27% for an arbitrary antenna configuration.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized Ka-band radiating element unit-cell for SatCom wide-angle electronically steered phased arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulations of a circularly polarized cavity-backed patch antenna for a low profile active electronically scanned Ka-band array with a beam-scanning capability over a wide-angle range (+/- 60°). The proposed unit-cell devoted to aircraft SatCom applications is derived in two versions for both 18-20 GHz and 28-30 GHz bands. It comprises an upper patch coupled to a dual pin-fed lower patch, both separated by a metal grid spacer. By symetrically placing the two input feeds, a similar behavior for both polarizations can be achieved, attaining thus a low axial ratio over a wide-angle range.

articleTitle: Capacity-Oriented RIS Control Through a Genetic Algorithm with Learning Capability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This work addresses the issue of controlling a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) in real-time to maximize the network capacity. A RIS control strategy is proposed exploiting a Genetic Algorithm (GA) augmented with learning capabilities to achieve high computation efficiency and guarantee consistent network performance in highly-dynamic scenarios. The proposed strategy does not require knowledge of the channel between the RIS and the users, enabling the design of RIS without channel-sensing hardware. The proposed strategy is demonstrated in a small-scale numerical example.

articleTitle: Wideband Antenna Design for 5G mmWave Applications Using Enhanced Adaptive Differential Evolution
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Antenna design for 5G mmwave applications is a challenging task. Moreover, if the design specifications require wideband behavior the problem becomes more complex. In this paper, we address the above presented design problem by introducing a new modified E-shaped patch antenna that has an additional third slot. We present a design procedure based on Enhanced Adaptive Differential Evolution. The numerical results show that the obtained best design presents wideband behavior that covers the whole frequency range 2 (FR2) zone and expands up to 60GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Biconical Antenna with Embedded Band-Stop Resonator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A volumetric resonant structure is embedded inside an otherwise wideband (6–36 GHz) biconical antenna (bicone) to achieve band rejection within its wide instantaneous bandwidth. The parameters of this structure are chosen such a notch with a 3dB return loss is formed between 16.8 and 18.2 GHz. A parametric study is carried out to demonstrate the tunability of the band-reject region. A bicone is designed for fabrication with stereolithography followed by electroplating.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Pattern Dipole Antenna for Secure Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present the design and measurement of a switched dipole antenna for directional modulation in a single antenna via radiation pattern dynamics. The antenna is fed by a single port, the output of which is fed to two locations on the dipole. By switching between the two states, the complex radiation pattern is quasi-static within a secure region in the mainlobe, and dynamic outside of the secure region. We show that the complex pattern dynamics outside the secure region impart additional modulation onto the radiation pattern that will distort transmitted or received data. We present the design of the dynamic pattern antenna and measured radiation patterns of the two antenna states. We numerically characterize the secure wireless capability through calculation of the bit-error-ratio on various digital modulations in communications, demonstrating the ability to maintain a small secure region.

articleTitle: Design of A Wideband Low-Profile Cylindrical Conformal Array Antenna With Flexible Beam Scanning Capability
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband low-profile cylindrical conformal array antenna with flexible beam scanning capability is reported. The design consists of the semi-cylindrical band-pass array antenna and the semi-cylindrical band-stop array antenna, which are connected by radius of R = 31.8 (1.06λo) mm. Based on the frequency selective surface, the profile of band-pass and band-stop element is less than 0.15λo, meanwhile, both have the characteristic of easy to conformal. The band-pass element comprises top and bottom layer of square metallic patch and a middle layer of metallic square-ring slot, and its transmission loss is less than 0.9 dB within 8.0-12.0 GHz. The band-stop element consists of top and bottom square metallic patch, middle metallic square-ring slot loaded with square tube, and its reflection loss is below 1.5 dB within 8.0-12.0 GHz. And a wide-angle of 360° beams scanning is realized, by rotating the spatial position of scanning conformal array. Finally, the simulated results show that the proposed low-profile array antenna have the characteristics of wideband, low-loss, wide-angle beam scanning.

articleTitle: Inhomogeneous Dielectric Lens Antennas Design based on Clothoid Ray Paths
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper we present a novel approach for the design of inhomogeneous lenses based on clothoid ray paths. Among various possible choices, Clothoids are a type of curves which present the advantage to control their curvature. Given the illuminating and the target aperture distributions of the field on both sides of the lens, the proposed technique consists first in a "ray tracing" inside the lens volume; the exact ray paths can be adjusted to reach a minimum curvature ray congruence. Then, through a subsequent "phase tracing" algorithm, the wavefronts are traced inside the lens and refractive index distribution is finally retrieved. The lens design algorithm is presented in details and some inhomogeneous lens examples are given.

articleTitle: Slotted Waveguide for Industrial Heating Application
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A longitudinally slotted waveguide (LSWG) for use in high dielectric industrial drying is presented. Teflon radome of 5 mm, 7 mm, and 10 mm are considered. The radome thickness has a limited effect on the resonant frequency. Redesigning the LSGW for a high-dielectric environment increases resonant frequency from 2.44 GHz, 2.45 GHz, 2.46 GHz to 2.88 GHz, 2.89 GHz, 2.75 GHz for 5 mm, 7 mm, and 10 mm radome thickness. For the 10 mm radome the bandwidth increases from 57.4 MHz to 222.8 MHz when placed into the high dielectric surrounding.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of the Metamaterial-Based Beam-Steerable Huygens’ Box Antenna with Dramatically Reduced Phasing Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present an experimental demonstration of the Huygens’ metasurface enabled antenna for millimeter wave beam steering with very few phasing elements. We synthesize a propagating plane wave in the Huygens’ metasurface-based cavity, and couple the synthesized plane wave to directive radiation steerable in both azimuth and elevation directions by engineering the cavity wave travel direction and the refractive index of the cavity respectively. The result shows comparable radiation to what is obtainable from microstrip patch phased array of similar aperture size, but with tremendous reduction in the number of required phased elements.

articleTitle: Metasurface Cloaks for Reduction of Mutual Coupling in Slot Antennas at C-Band Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: With the intention of reducing the detrimental effect of mutual coupling between two slot antennas placed in very close proximity, designed to operate at C-band frequencies, we make use of the specifically designed metasurface cloaks, which employs the concept of mantle cloaking. In this paper, it is demonstrated that by encasing each edge of the individual slot antenna with the elliptical metasurface cloaks, we are able to achieve a significant reduction in the mutual coupling. This decoupling effect is evident in the plots for S-parameters of the slot antennas. Along with this, restoration of the far-field radiation patterns is also observed. Thus, these explicitly tailored cloaks enable each slot antenna to radiate independently, as if the antennas were functioning in an isolated environment.

articleTitle: On a Frequency-Stabilized Single Current Inverse Source Formulation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Several strategies are available for solving the inverse source problem in electromagnetics. Among them, many have been focusing in retrieving Love currents by solving, after regularization, for Love’s electric and magnetic currents. In this work we present a dual-element discretization, analysis, and stabilization of an inverse source formulation providing Love data by solving for only one current. This results in substantial savings and allows for an effective quasi-Helmholtz projector stabilization of the resulting operator. Theoretical considerations are complemented by numerical tests showing effectiveness and efficiency of the newly proposed method.

articleTitle: Physics-Embedded Machine Learning for Efficient Modeling of High-Frequency Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We propose the integration of analytical extension of eigenvalues (AEE) into neural network (NN) for efficient modeling of microwave circuits. By embedding the physics knowledge of lumped equivalent circuits, the proposed machine learning method allows us to build more generalizable relations between the input parameters of a circuit and its electromagnetic properties, showing a 10-fold improvement for input parameters outside the range of training set. The proposed model is also more data efficient in that it can achieve the same level of accuracy with fewer data compared with traditional NN-based circuit modeling.

articleTitle: Concept of Independent Reflection Magnitude and Phase Using an Electromechanical Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A simple concept to perfectly decouple the reflection magnitude and phase of a reflective metasurface is proposed. For a linearly-polarized illumination, a full 2π phase is achieved in reflection by physically displacing the unit cell normal to the surface, with respect to a fixed reference and source, while the reflection magnitude is independently controlled via an integrated resistive element inside the unit cell. This proposed concept is demonstrated using full-wave simulations, which is the first step towards an electromechanical metasurface with truly independent real-time amplitude and phase control.

articleTitle: Metasurface Reflector with Independent Polarizations Control using a Supercell Concept
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel supercell concept is proposed to control the amplitude and phase of a metasurface reflector, independently for the two orthogonal polarizations, and is numerically demonstrated. The supercell concept is based on a fundamental unit cell that operates on one linear polarization only, which when spatially rotated by 90°, can be used to respond to the other orthogonal polarization. By spatially combining the unit cell and its spatially rotated version, a super cell is formed which can impart a desired reflection amplitude/phase to each of the polarizations without affecting the other.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-polarized Notch Band Absorber with High Band Edge Selectivity and Broad Absorption Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A polarization insensitive notch band absorber (NBA) is presented. The proposed design offers a flat notch band with high band edge selectivity. Its |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| ≤ 0.2 dB notch bandwidth extends from 8.32-8.78 GHz, which is sandwiched between a lower and an upper 10-dB absorption band with fractional bandwidths (FBW) greater than 74.5% (3.62-7.92 GHz) and 46.27% (9.12-14.61 GHz), respectively. The performance of the designed notch band absorber is verified by comparing the numerically simulated results with the measurement results.

articleTitle: A Versatile Polynomial Model for Reflection by a Reflective Intelligent Surface with Varactors
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: An analytical model for reflection of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) using varactors to adjust the reflection phase of an incident plane wave is presented. The model results are compared to a full-wave RIS simulation for different varactor bias voltages. The model is intended to be analytical and simple enough, but related to a realistic RIS, to be inserted into MIMO wireless systems algorithms to estimate the propagation channel including the RIS.

articleTitle: Investigations on Biconical Antenna : Benchmarking Against IEEE P2816 Standard
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The IEEE Antennas and Propagation Standards Committee (APS/SC), sponsored by the Antennas and Propagation Society (AP-S), has taken a special drive for the benefits of the antenna researchers, engineers, faculty members, and students. The objective is recommended practice providing common guidelines for modeling and simulation of antennas (P2816). The biconical antenna is proposed as one of the possible benchmark candidates. The design and simulation of such a biconical antenna are presented in this manuscript.

articleTitle: A Pattern Reconfigurable Multi-Mode Antenna Based on Circular Disk and Ring-Shaped Resonators
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this study, a miniaturized, pattern reconfigurable microstrip patch antenna based on the excitation of different modes of multiple resonators is designed, fabricated, and measured. The antenna composes of a concentric circular patch and a ring-shaped resonator. To miniaturize the antenna, the ring-shaped patch is loaded by capacitors. To obtain different patterns, radiator sizes are adjusted to yield different TM modes. The ring part is excited by two probes, whereas the circular patch is parasitically excited. The beam is rotated continuously by varying phase differences between these two ports. Measurements support that the beam can be steered from -40<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> to 40<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>.

articleTitle: Comparison of Additive Manufacturing Methods for the Attachment of Bare Die to Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents two different methods for the additive/subtractive hybrid integration of bare die with conventional Printed Circuit Boards (PCB’s). Differences in fabrication, electrical performance, and sizing are discussed. One method involves attachment to a pocket milled into the dielectric of a copper laminate. Filet bridges between the chip and board are applied using a house-made photocurable dielectric ink, and aerosol-jet silver conductors are printed overtop. The second method is similar, but the die is instead attached to a copper ground plane on top of the laminate. Electrical measurements are taken using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA). The experiment is shown here with a 0dB attenuator die, and results using a Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) die will also be presented.

articleTitle: A New Image Based Regression CNN for Predicting V-band Power Attenuation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel application of machine learning and image processing for estimating mm-wave attenuation due to varying weather conditions is developed and tested. A deep learning approach is taken to analyze doppler weather radar images obtained from the NEXRAD radar system. Pairing the radar images with RF power data obtained from a 24 km, 72 GHz terrestrial link, the received power is estimated through a Convolutional Neural Network, tuned for regression, and the attenuating effects of clear skies and cloudy days are compared to experimentally measured results.

articleTitle: High EIRP Dielectric Lens Loaded Quad-Ridge Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A design of a dual-polarized quad-ridge horn (QRH) antenna operating beyond an octave of bandwidth is presented. The antenna is optimized for a very strict gain performance over a narrow field of view (FOV) and high-power operation. This resulted in a configuration with the QRH loaded with the dual-surface shaped lens and permittivity/loss tangent not found in the bulk. Cylindrical holes are therefore integrated with the host material to achieve necessary effective permittivity. Initial tests of QRH-only configuration show good agreement with simulations.

articleTitle: A 24-GHz Directional Button Antenna for Wireless Power Transfer on Human Arm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A directional button antenna working at 24 GHz of ISM band is proposed for Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) on human arm. It consists of the feed of microstrip line, the monopole antenna loaded dielectrics, and the AMC structure close to the feeding port. The WPT and communication antennas are placed on the real human arm model of a Chinese female, the interactions between arm and antenna are investigated, including the matching, the channel characteristics, the pattern, the specific absorption rate (SAR), and the transmission efficiency.

articleTitle: Switched Beam Steering Using Shared Aperture Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a method to steer the antenna pattern beam in multiple frequency bands using shared aperture antenna arrays. L and K band frequencies are being used in satellite and surveillance radar systems. Multiple antennas and mechanical rotation is needed to steer the beam towards specific target which makes those systems complex. Here, we proposed a low profile and mechanical rotational system free, shared aperture antenna system for both of the L and K band application. Both of the L and K band antennas are placed side by side on a single substrate while maintaining a low magnitude of crosstalk (<-30 dB). Simulation results confirm that this system is capable of steering the beam across upper hemisphere with <3 dB of loss of gain.

articleTitle: Design of Decagon Ring Two Port MIMO Antenna for Wireless Fidelity-6 Application in Next Generation Futuristic Wireless Devices
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The design of two port multiple input multiple output (MIMO) decagon ring with dual inverted T-shaped radiators functioning in Wireless Fidelity (Wi-Fi) 6 applications for next generation futuristic wireless devices is designed and analyzed. The two antenna elements are constructed on a FR-4 substrate with size of 42.5×19.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, thickness 0.8mm and excited using co-planar waveguide (CPW) fed technique to operate smoothly with frequency span of (5.88 - 7.57 GHz) fulfilling the bandwidth requirement of Wi-Fi-6 bands. In order to be the potential candidate for MIMO practical applications, the two CPW grounds are connected with each other along with an inverted-Psi shaped radiator embedded between two ground planes which also act as a decoupling structure to reduce the interference between antenna elements. Moreover, the proposed MIMO antenna generate bandwidth of 30.03% in Wi-Fi-6 frequency band at single resonating frequency of 6.7GHz, isolation >18dB, gain greater than 4dBi throughout the desired band. Finally, the MIMO parameters like envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) < 0.02 and diversity gain (DG) ~ 9.9dB are also achieved in Wi-Fi-6 operating bands.

articleTitle: Influence of Active Antennas on EMF Restrictions in 5G Base Stations Deployment
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a model to analyse the influence of active antennas on ElectroMagnetic Field restrictions in 5G base stations deployment is presented. The model (based on simulations via CST) allows for the computation of exposure in the vicinity of base stations with active 5G antennas in order to compute the respective exclusion zone that enables the safety of the population, taking realistic maximum power levels. Representative scenarios with co-location of antennas from several systems (from 2G to 5G) are analysed. For an urban scenario, the exclusion zone is reduced from 25.2 m to 16.4 m, when proper exposure conditions are taken into account.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Metasurface Beam Shaping Using Far Field Masks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic metasurfaces (EMMSs) have been an area of intense research in recent years owing to their low profile and reduced cost compared to existing phased-array solutions. EMMSs relate the tangential fields on one side of the surface to the other through their surface parameters. Unfortunately, there is no analytical relationship between the required tangential fields on each side of the EMMS and desired far field criteria in the form of upper and lower masks. Here we present a method for optimizing the EMMS surface parameters to satisfy a given far field upper and lower mask. This involves using the alternating direction method of multipliers to optimize a two-dimensional EMMS model constructed using the method of moments. This model incorporates important inter-cell mutual coupling along with edge effects. An example performing cosecant beam shaping is presented.

articleTitle: Quasi-Isotropic Antenna-in-Package with a Shielded Core and Wide Circular Polarization Coverage
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Given the dynamic nature of the Internet of Things (IoT) scenarios, peripheral devices’ radiation patterns must cover large areas to avoid disconnection in case of change of orientation relative to the base station. This broad coverage should be for both the power radiated as well as for the polarization of the electromagnetic wave, increasing the probabilities of a sturdy link between peripheral devices and the base stations. Current devices implement simple omnidirectional antennas that are linearly polarized and can be easily detuned due to the proximity of the electronics. This paper proposes an Antenna-in-Package design based on a microstrip patch volumetric array. The system consists of six circular patch antenna elements with perturbation segments. The patches work on the 2.4 GHz ISM band. Each element is placed on one face of a 3D hollow cube, and the internal walls are covered in metal, acting as a shielded core for the embedded electronics and ground for the patch elements. The design simultaneously demonstrates a 7 dB gain variation in 95% of the 3D sphere and a circular polarization coverage in 84%.

articleTitle: Laplacian Filters for Integral Equations: Further Developments and Fast Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper extends the concept of Laplacian filtered quasi-Helmholtz decompositions we have recently introduced to the basis-free projector-based setting. This extension allows the discrete analyses of electromagnetic integral operators spectra without passing through an explicit Loop-Star decomposition as previously done. We also present a fast scheme for the evaluation of the filters in quasi linear complexity in the total number of unknowns. Together with the fact that only a logarithmic number of these filters is required for solving the h-refinement breakdown of electric field integral equation, this results in an effective preconditioner that rivals Calderón strategies in performance without relying on barycentric refinements. Numerical results confirm the theoretically predicted behavior and the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Hybrid Genetic Programming Designed Laser-Induced Graphene Based Absorber
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Hybrid genetic programming (HGP) is applied to the design and optimization of a laser-induced graphene (LIG) based metasurface (MS) electromagnetic absorber. The HGP designed absorber has bandwidths of 115.4%and 56.5% for absorptivity above 70% and 80%, respectively. It is 5.1 mm thick, with a unit cell (UC) periodicity of 8.7 mm. The LIG is generated on a polyimide substrate. The MS absorber has copper ground plane backing.

articleTitle: A Local Current Recovery Scheme for Error Estimation in Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A simple and inexpensive current recovery scheme is proposed for local error estimation in connection with the numerical solution of integral equations. Results for several test targets show favorable performance compared to other inexpensive estimation schemes.

articleTitle: A Comparison Between Multiple Launch Angle Method (MLAM) and Single Launch Angle Refractivity-from-Clutter (RFC) Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Lower atmospheric ducts in ocean and littoral regions can be retrieved using sea surface backscattering. This technique is called Refractivity-from-Clutter (RFC). Improving currently available RFC techniques is an active area of research. The duct effects on an EM signal depends on the angle that the signal is launched. Hence, using multiple launch angles might be a good way to improve the RFC inversion technique. This paper is a theoretical study of how using multiple launch angles in RFC inversion can improve the duct estimation with respect to using a single launch angle.

articleTitle: Wideband Millimeter-Wave Horizontally Polarized Omnidirectional Antenna Using Machine-Learning-Assisted Optimization Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A wideband horizontally polarized omnidirectional patch antenna is presented. The antenna consists of a ring-shaped patch and 9 conductive vias shorting the patch concentrically. To reduce the computational expense of antenna optimization, the method of machine-learning-assisted optimization is introduced. The proposed antenna design covers a frequency band of 23.25-30.5 GHz, which serves as a great candidate for millimeter-wave wideband wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Dual Rampart Antenna for Radar Systems with Enlarged Field of View
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel antenna based on a dual rampart radiating structure whose main radiation lobe can be steered across a broad angular range by changing the frequency of the input signal. The antenna characteristics are controlled electronically using suitable single-pull double-throw switches. The design has been completed using a full-wave electromagnetic simulation tool. A field of view of 135 degrees over the frequency band from 7 GHz to 8.5 GHz has been achieved.

articleTitle: Design of Truncated Microstrip Square Patch Antenna for Terahertz Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the effect of truncation on each corner of a microstrip square patch that can be utilized for Terahertz (THz) communication. The truncated microstrip patch antenna has a bandwidth of 410 GHz (-10 dB impedance bandwidth from 3.48 THz to 3.90 THz). Moreover, the proposed antenna reveals a minimum reflection coefficient of about -29 dB, maximum gain of 5.01 dBi, directivity 6.06 dBi and a total radiation efficiency of 80.2% at 3.65 THz frequency. The proposed antenna is suitable for future Terahertz communication and imaging.applications.

articleTitle: Plow-Shaped Wideband Antenna for mm-wave 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a simple planar plow-shaped wideband antenna is presented for mm-wave 5G devices. The proposed antenna is designed on a thin substrate with an overall size of 10×12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The results show that the antenna offers 49.5% fractional bandwidth ranging from 22.2 GHz to 36.8 GHz. Moreover, the radiation efficiency of the antenna is >90% throughout the operating bandwidth, with a peak gain of 3.3 dBi. Through its simple structure and high performance characteristics, it can be observed that the proposed antenna can be termed as a potential candidate for future mm-wave 5G communication devices.

articleTitle: A Planar Multi-Mode Antenna Array with Enhanced Horizontal Scan Range for mm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A multi-mode antenna array with enhanced scan range and reduced scan losses is presented. The individual array element consists of a micostrip patch which is differentially fed through two capacitively coupled ports and a cylindrical dielectric resonator (DR) fed by a coplanar waveguide integrated in the middle of the patch. The radiation pattern of each array element can be reconfigured by changing the phase offset between the feeding ports of the patch and the DR so to excite two distinct radiating modes. When using a 8 × 4 planar array configuration, the achieved scan range extends from -70° to 70° along the horizontal plane, and from -20° to 30° along the vertical plane.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Fast Method for Designing Phase Shifting Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a method that enables the ulta-fast design of phase shifting surfaces (PSS) for various antenna applications. Traditional design approaches utilize full-wave simulations that are extremely time-consuming and computationally expensive. Our approach uses the multiplication property of ABCD parameters of cascaded networks to design N-layer PSSs, which consist of M different variations of conductive patches. Following the proposed approach for designing an N-layer PSS, we only need to perform N × M full-wave simulations instead of N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">M</sup> simulations, which must be performed when the traditional approach is used. Our method’s accuracy is studied and validated; specifically, it exhibits a total percentage error of less than 6% for both amplitude and phase.

articleTitle: Hyperparameters Tuning of Prior Knowledge-Driven Multilayer Perceptron Model Using Particle Swarm Optimization for Inverse Modeling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this article, a prior knowledge input (PKI) based ANN model, using a trained multi-layer perceptron (MLP) model, has been developed. The particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is utilized for the hyperparameter tuning of the MLP model. The proposed modeling technique has been validated using an ultra-wideband (UWB) band-notched antenna. The PKI model has been used for inverse modeling of the UWB antenna. For a comparative analysis, the genetic algorithm (GA) is also investigated for tuning the hyperparameters of the PKI model.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a transmit-array base station for mm-wave communications in the Fresnel region
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarized transmit-array is evaluated as an indoor base station antenna for mm-wave communications at 28 GHz. The antenna is designed to produce a constant field distribution in a specific area generating different spots wherein the devices are placed. The antenna is fed in a multi-feed configuration, radiating a different coverage area each feed. The design technique is based on a phase-only synthesis (POS) and a proper distribution of the feeds. The transmit-array is simulated and finally manufactured. The prototype is based on dielectric-only elements which provide a low-cost solution. The results show a high agreement with simulations. Moreover, the presented results validate the design technique as well as transmit-array antennas for this purpose.

articleTitle: Investigation of Coordinate System Rotation and Translation on Iteratively Reconstructed Truncated Antenna Field Patterns
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: One of the major limiting factors in full-sphere antenna pattern characterization is truncation. Pursuing the goal of full-sphere characterization via multiple truncated radiation patterns, this paper investigates the behavior of iteratively reconstructed truncated antenna field patterns and their corresponding spherical harmonic coefficients under rotation and translation of the coordinate system. The findings indicate that manipulation of such coefficients introduces pattern distortion, however, this distortion is contained in the region near the angle of truncation. This further implies that multiple truncated patterns with sufficient overlap have the potential of serving as a basis for stitching misaligned truncated patterns to achieve full-sphere characterization of an antenna.

articleTitle: Deep learning based higher-order approximation for multiple knife edge diffraction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We introduce an hybrid approach for computing multiple knife-edge diffraction attenuation. First, we show that the well-known Epstein-Peterson method can be considered as the first order approximation of the Vogler method. In the other words, the Vogler method is a combination of the Epstein-Peterson method and an higher order approximation. Then, we propose to learn the approximation based on deep learning methods. The key advantage of this approach is the significant reduction of generating training data to approximate the Vogler method while still offering a good accuracy and fast computation. Comparison to the state-of-the-art methods demonstrates the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized Dual-differential Co-located SIW Slot Arrays for Full-duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A new high isolation slot array antenna offering dual-polarization and high isolation for 5G in-band full-duplex (IBFD) applications is presented. The single-layer structure consists of series-fed SIW slot arrays oriented in a cross-shaped setup. Also, the proposed design exploits dual-differential feeding to achieve -10 dB matching from 23.2 GHz to 25.3 GHz and the isolation between activated and passive ports is around 70 dB. The maximum simulated realized gain is around 13.8 dBi while the simulated cross-polarizations are well below 30 dB or lower from the main beam maximum. To the best knowledge of the authors, no similar antenna configuration has been previously reported offering high isolation in the K-band, which can enable high-data-rate transfer for in-band full-duplex systems.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Modeling of High-Q Cavity Fields Using Dynamic Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: We present a data-driven reduced-order model based on dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) for analysis and prediction of resonating electromagnetic fields inside a cavity. The full-order model employs a rectangular finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) scheme to generate the high-fidelity data which is used as input to the DMD algorithm. DMD extracts the dominant spatial patterns and respective frequencies which corresponds to the resonance modes of the cavity. The DMD based reduced-order model (ROM) is then used to extrapolate the fields in time for long-term predictions. We demonstrate the method for a closed rectangular cavity made of aluminium. Such time-domain ROMs not only facilitate analysis of the cavity resonances, but also help expedite the time consuming FDTD simulations by predicting late-time fields.

articleTitle: A Ku-Band SIW Diplexer-Power divider
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, first, a novel compact configuration of a multi-layer diplexer is introduced for Ku-band applications. The proposed structures are based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. The main novelty of the proposed structure is to utilize an extended SMA instead of complex filters in a diplexer topology. The location of this SMA help provides two separated transmission paths for the RF signals. Then a new topology for integrating diplexers and power dividers is presented. Two SIW Y-junction power divider is efficiently applied to implement the diplexer-power divider. These junctions are directly connected to the proposed SIW diplexer.

articleTitle: Deterministic Synthesis Technique for Elliptically Shaped Conformal Aperiodic Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Conformal array pattern synthesis represents a challenging problem. In this paper, a deterministic design method for elliptical conformal arrays based on the auxiliary array pattern formulation is presented. This method, being semi-analytical in nature, is able to evaluate the location and excitation coefficients of each array element in just a few seconds using conventional computers which are currently available on the market, whilst accounting for either layout or beamforming network constraints.

articleTitle: A Compact Inkjet-Printed Wide-band Antenna for X/Ku/K/Ka-band and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a compact fully inkjet-printed wideband antenna on a flexible substrate. The proposed antenna incorporates a modified rectangular patch and a partial ground plane inkjet-printed using silver nanoparticle ink on a flexible Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) substrate. The 10-dB impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna covers a wide frequency spectrum ranging from 7.9 to 35.9 GHz. The antenna has a large bandwidth (BW) of 28 GHz and occupies X/Ku/K and Ka- bands along with the 24/28 GHz bands that are used for millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) 5G applications. A radiation efficiency of more than 83 % and a peak gain of 5 dB is also reported for the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured 24 GHz Circular Horn Antennas
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Three smooth-walled conical horn antennas have been designed simulated and additively manufactured and post-processed in three different ways, for operating at 24 GHz. This paper discusses these processes, as well as their characterization measurements, for obtaining the return loss, gain and radiation pattern of the antennas.

articleTitle: The Extension of the Spectral Projection Model for Electromagnetic Scattering
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: The spectral projection model (SPM) was introduced in 2019 as a fast and accurate method for analyzing scattering from two-dimensional surfaces [1]. SPM is based on the addition theorem for Bessel and Hankel functions. The constraints of the addition theorem limited the application of the initial model to surfaces that were nearly circular. In this paper, it is shown that by manipulating the addition theorem and translating the geometric origin, the application of SPM may be extended to describe scattering from conducting surfaces of any shape. The translation of the origin is implemented using the addition theorem to incorporate a convolution operation in the spectral projection process [2]. Simulations are performed for a variety of different shapes with both TM and TE polarization and compared with the results from the Method of Moments to study the accuracy of the method. A surface generation technique known as the vector-sum method is combined with the advanced SPM model to formulate the scattering problem for a variety of two-dimensional surfaces [2]. Simulations show that the results using this advanced form of SPM compare well with results generated by MoM.

articleTitle: Transparent, Cascaded-Sheet Metasurfaces for Field Transformations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: Integral equations are used to design transparent, cascaded-sheet, metasurfaces for arbitrary field transformations. Commonly used techniques such as the local periodicity approximation do not account for the inhomogeneity of the cascaded sheets. As a result, they impose restrictions on the separation between the sheets. In contrast, we use the governing integral equation to accurately design metasurfaces consisting of three cascaded inhomogeneous sheets separated by two dielectric spacers of arbitrary thickness. The integral equation, that is solved using the Method of Moments (MoM), accounts for all electromagnetic interactions between the inhomogeneous sheets. A design example is presented that shapes the field radiated from a line source into a collimated beam with a cosine tapered amplitude. The performance of the metasurface is verified using a commercial electromagnetics full-wave solver.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Electrically Small Huygens Dipole Antenna with Full Space Radiation Coverage
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable, electrically small Huygens dipole antenna (HDA) with full space (quasi-isotropic) radiation coverage is reported. One unique feature of the design is its uniform polarization across the entire space. The HDA consists of two metamaterial-inspired electrically small radiating elements: an Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) and a reconfigurable capacitively loaded loop (CLL), and a small driven dipole. The width of the top strip of the CLL is reconfigured slightly by controlling the on/off states of two PIN diodes located between a thin strip and the CLL. Because the coupling effect between the EAD and CLL is dependent on the width of the top strip of the CLL, the phases of the currents on the EAD can be changed by 180° by varying it. As a result of the Huygens radiation physics, such a phase change alters the radiation pattern between the broadside forward- and back-directed modes. Because of the extremely broad beamwidth of the ensuing Huygens patterns, quasi-isotropic radiation coverage is realized. Furthermore, the length of the short-driven dipole is also reconfigured by one PIN diode to maintain consistent impedance matching at 915 MHz in the ISM band for both modes. It is an ideal candidate for indoor wireless power transfer (WPT) enabled IoT applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Filtering Antenna with High Stopband Suppression for Ku-band Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a six-slits filtering antenna with high stopband suppression is designed for Ku-band satellite communications. In order to acquire a waveguide transmission line with good filtering characteristic, a set of stepped metal rods are introduced into the rectangular waveguide. The proposed antenna has a 10 dB impedance bandwidth from 11.79 GHz to 13.05 GHz, covering the downlink frequency band (from 12.25 to 12.75 GHz) of Ku-band SATCOM. It also has a stable gain around 15 dBi within downlink band. Meanwhile, this antenna obtains a high outband rejection more than 26.5 dB in uplink band (14 ~ 14.5 GHz) and can be expanded to a planar array easily.

articleTitle: Response Analysis of Varied Q-Power Values of Cosine Distribution In Spatial Correlation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of Q-power values of cosine distribution on the spatial correlation of cylindrical array using the maximum power of offset distribution. Our results showed significant mismatch between the simulation and theoretical coefficient for arbitrary Q-power values above ten(10) as compared to that of the Von Mises distribution. Even though high Q-power values are the key parameters for system performance, there is a need to carefully select arbitrary Q-power values above ten (10) to minimize errors in channel modeling.

articleTitle: 28 GHz Digital SIW Phase Shifter Using Embedded PIN Diodes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for designing of a controllable phase shifter based on integrated substrate waveguide (SIW) technology and PIN diodes for 5G millimeter wave wireless communication applications. The proposed phase shifter operates at 28 GHz with a wide bandwidth (14%) from 26 GHz to 30 GHz. The proposed geometry is designed and optimized by numerical simulation (HFSS) and results show a good agreement and a maximum differential phase of 99.99° at the central frequency (28GHz). The phase difference is provided by metal poles which are switched by PIN diodes and achieved a good performance regarding return loss and insertion loss.

articleTitle: A V-band Phased-Array Antenna for Millimeter-Wave-Based 3D Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact phased-array antenna for efficient and high-gain millimeter-wave-based 3D beam steering applications. The proposed antenna array consists of 2 × 2 unit cells and each unit cell is a sub-array comprising of 2 × 2 patch elements connected to microstrip lines that are co-fed by a single coaxial cable. Two 45° phase shifting lines are incorporated in each sub-array to facilitate the wide beamsteering range. The dimensions of the proposed phased array antenna are 24 × 24 × 0.324 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Simulation results show that the proposed phased-array antenna has a resonating frequency at 58.4 GHz with an operational bandwidth from 50.1 GHz to 77.5 GHz along with a high gain of 26.8 dBi. The array exhibits a maximum beam steering range of 105° in the elevation plane and 195° in the azimuth plane with a gain variation less than 0.9 dBi.

articleTitle: Switchable Beamsteering Antenna Array Using 3-bit Phase Quantization at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and USNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/URSI)
abstract: A novel beam-steerable 3-bit antenna array is presented for millimeter-wave application. The design operates at 28GHz and consists of a tightly stacked aperture feeding antenna with eight reconfigurable quantized phases which can effectively steer the beam from +50º to -50º. Three different configurations were fabricated and tested. The measured antenna is in good agreement with the simulation result. The measured broadside gain was 13.44 dBi with the gain threshold of 10dBi within the steering range (viz. 100º).
